story: The Horizon Line stretches flat across the desert; from its center a huge Meat Hook hangs down, its shaft gouging one straight furrow through the sand — the first STREET.
reading_story: Cho glides her broom low down the empty STREET at midnight, her wandtip sparking off every cobblestone.
issues: Minor coherence strain: the Meat Hook 'hangs down' yet gouges a furrow 'through the sand', implying unexplained lateral motion; not a gate failure (ordinary physical motion) but the drag could be made explicit.

story: The Falling Katana slices down the left, the Meat Hook hangs on the right, and the Horizon Line stretches between them; one Ink Droplet, coated in the hook's rust flakes, splashes everything RUST-COLORED.
reading_story: Tanner pulls a hide from his vat and groans — the tannin has stained it deep RUST-COLORED, the color of old iron.
issues: Minor: Ink Droplet is defined as glossy black ink, so the rust-colored splash depends on the 'coated in rust flakes' detail to stay consistent — acceptable physical interaction, but one extra inferential step.
Minor: droplet's central position inside the frame is implied rather than stated; left/right/between staging is otherwise explicit and faithful.

story: An Ink Droplet falls onto a clamped Pot Lid; a Fishhook twitches beneath it; a bending Vaulting Pole sweeps one long stride under everything, underlining THIS.
reading_story: The Sheriff jabs a gloved finger at the bounty notice, barks one clipped word — THIS — and the whole saloon goes silent.
issues: Imageability (graded, non-gating): the three clauses ('Ink Droplet falls onto a clamped Pot Lid', 'a Fishhook twitches beneath it', 'a bending Vaulting Pole sweeps one long stride under everything') are causally unlinked — no actor affects another, so it reads as a spatial inventory rather than the single vivid/striking image required by docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §2 Stage 2.

Meaning payoff is deictic rather than physical: 'underlining THIS' points at the whole scene instead of giving the keyword a concrete moment; passes gate 4 (terminal placement, matches meaning_placement 'end') but is a weak payoff.

Distinctiveness risk: 丶 (Ink Droplet) and 亠 (Pot Lid) are very high-frequency components, and a droplet landing on a lid is a scene likely to recur across many kanji; only Fishhook and Vaulting Pole carry discrimination here, and nothing emotional or unusual anchors it against neighbors.
The Fishhook 'twitches beneath it' with no reason for the twitch — a small missed opportunity to bind it to the droplet impact and convert the stack into one causal image.

story: DESTITUTION: a Falling Katana slashes down past one Ink Droplet onto a clamped Pot Lid; underneath, the scraped-bare pot holds only a Fishhook twitching in the emptiness.
reading_story: Bowie, in a threadbare Ziggy suit, busks on a subway platform, glitter smeared, coin cup empty, singing about beautiful DESTITUTION.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the Ink Droplet is only passed by, not interacted with - weakest-integrated component, most likely to be forgotten at recall.
Minor (non-blocking): slight coherence gap - the Pot Lid is 'clamped' yet the viewer sees 'underneath' into the pot; the katana slash is never stated to open it.
Minor (non-blocking): 'empty vessel / scarcity' imagery may interfere with neighbouring scarcity kanji that also use the Fishhook (乙) actor.

story: THE LATTER: a lone barbed Fishhook dangles at the very tail of the line, twitching, curling tighter — never the first thing down, always the one that comes after.
reading_story: An Otter surfaces twice — empty paws first, then a glinting hook clamped in its teeth. Everyone remembers THE LATTER.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the story's closing clause 'never the first thing down, always the one that comes after' is asserted abstraction rather than a visual; a concrete cue (e.g. a first hook already sunk above it) would raise concreteness.

story: A Lightning Bolt spears the riverbed, shattering the Soup Ladle at left and the Fishhook curling up on the right; between them the River Eel lies unscathed in its lazy S — whatever else dies, this one continues TO BE.
reading_story: Yah barks one clipped syllable in an empty dojo; the echo answers back, and suddenly there seem TO BE two of him.
issues: Spatial fidelity (graded, non-blocking): the story asserts 'Soup Ladle at left' and 'Fishhook curling up on the right', but 也 is a single fused stroke-shape — 匕 and 乙 are not laid out as left/right elements. The placement is invented staging rather than glyph geometry.

Actor physics nit: a 'worn metal soup ladle' shattering is slightly off-material (metal deforms rather than shatters). Ordinary enough to pass the persona gate, but 'flattening'/'buckling' would fit the registry image better.
Length is at the ceiling (39 words); any future edit has no headroom before breaching the ~40-word gate.
Distinctiveness risk: the 'lightning destroys all but the survivor' frame is a generic template likely to be reused across other N1 kanji sharing 乙/匕, raising interference odds.

story: A Swaddling Wrap curls over the top like a hooded head, hugging a Rice-Paddy Grid whose mud dikes tile the shell beneath, while a twitching Fishhook dangles below as the tail: TORTOISE.
reading_story: A clipped locksmith's Key turns once — kee — in the TORTOISE's shell, and the plates swing open like a strongbox lid.
issues: Meaning story is a static assembly tableau — actors are positioned, not doing anything to each other; no event or absurdity to anchor recall beyond the shape-match.

Interference risk: a Rice-Paddy Grid stacked over a dangling hook is also the lower half of 電/雷; only the Swaddling Wrap hood distinguishes 亀 from those neighbors, and it is the least visually loaded element in the story.
The Fishhook is reduced to 'the tail' — its barbed, twitching character does nothing in the scene, so the most distinctive actor carries the least narrative weight.

story: You lean over the Wellhead Grid — two pairs of timber beams crossed into a square frame — and drop a pebble through the opening; a cold echo splashes far below: this is the WELL.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage lowers his long beard into the WELL like a rope, hauling up a dripping bucket of icy water.

story: Across the top, Horizon Line runs dead flat. Below it, Railway Tracks clamp the Sun between their two rails, carrying its glow from desert edge to desert edge — one endless burning SPAN.
reading_story: Coe sprints across a mile-long bridge, stride stretching wider each step, finishing at the far pylon — one runner covering the whole SPAN.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric §3 item 11, graded not gating): 亘 stacks as line / 日 / line, but the story places Horizon Line 'across the top' and then puts Railway Tracks 'below it' clamping the Sun between their two rails — that renders as horizon, then two rails with the sun between them, i.e. the sun sitting below both top strokes rather than between the top and bottom line. Fix by splitting the rails: 'Horizon Line caps the top; the Railway Tracks' lower rail runs beneath, the Sun pinned between them.'

Distinctiveness of the reading story: 'runner sprints across a bridge' is the single most predictable image for the English word SPAN, and generic crossing imagery risks interference with other cross/extend kanji (渡, 跨, 涉). Coe on a bridge is not wrong, just low-uniqueness; anchoring him to the same desert/rails set as the meaning story would bind the two better.

Minor redundancy inherited from the record, not the candidate: the component list carries both 一 (Horizon Line) and 二 (Railway Tracks), so three horizontal-line concepts compete for two strokes. The candidate handles it about as well as possible, but the decomposition itself is worth checking upstream.

story: ASIA rises in welded steel: one colossal Scaffold Rack bolted across the whole continent, square and rigid, its middle crossbar missing so dawn light blazes straight through the gap.
reading_story: Ace the barnstormer threads his biplane through that empty middle gap, smoke-writing one word above the pipework: ASIA.
issues: Reading story does not cue the short/clipped vowel that defines the Ace persona (reading_actor note: 'clipped bare "a". Short.'); doc §1.2 calls vowel length the #1 reading error, so the brevity signal is a missed reinforcement (non-blocking).

'Ace the barnstormer' with a biplane invents persona detail not in the registry, which only fixes the name 'Ace'; risks inconsistency if other あ kanji give Ace a different occupation (non-blocking, no contradiction).

story: An Iron Nail rams into garden turf and a tea stand erupts around it: the Bedsheet Cover snaps taut into open side-walls, an Open Mouth bellows orders above them, the Pot Lid clangs down as the domed roof — PAVILION.
reading_story: Tay hangs paper lanterns along the lakeside PAVILION until the water glows, then falls asleep in a hammock strung between its posts.
issues: Keyword pre-empted mid-story: 'a tea stand erupts around it' (word 11) reveals the pavilion/restaurant sense before the components assemble, weakening the end-placed PAVILION payoff (rubric gate 4, 'keyword is the payoff... not buried'). Literal placement gate still passes.
'a tea stand erupts around it' is instant-assembly rather than a watchable physical action — the one vague beat in an otherwise concrete story.

冖 'snaps taut into open side-walls' repurposes a drape-cover as structural walls; physically plausible for cloth so gate 5 passes, but it stretches the registry image ('draped over something hidden, edges hanging down').
Reading story is generic postcard imagery (lanterns, lake, hammock) with no hook tying it to 亭 specifically — weakest link for interference with neighbours sharing 亠/口/冖.

story: Pot Lid pops off the shouting Open Mouth below it; the Bedsheet Cover slithers down off the Wishing-Well Legs. Nothing muffled, nothing hidden — the shout rings out CLEAR.
reading_story: Ryo, the hardboiled detective, drags his sleeve across the rain-smeared diner window, stares through the newly CLEAR glass, and names the killer sitting outside.
issues: Non-blocking: 'Nothing muffled, nothing hidden' is abstract commentary rather than a visual beat — it explains the payoff instead of showing it; the story would be tighter with a concrete substitute.
Non-blocking: the scene splits into two parallel uncoverings (lid off mouth, sheet off legs) rather than one striking image, which slightly dilutes focus per rubric item 13.
Non-blocking: Pot Lid's registry image specifies it clamped over 'an unseen pot'; here it caps a mouth. Consistent as ordinary physical placement, but a shade off the registry framing.

story: At the left edge of the field, villagers hang two loaves on the Scarecrow's stiff outstretched arms; each dusk the hungry quietly come and take them — BENEVOLENCE.
reading_story: Jin empties his pockets after every concert, pressing warm coins into cold hands — pure BENEVOLENCE.
issues: Non-blocking: reading story's generic charity image (coins into cold hands) risks mild interference with other kindness-themed N1 kanji (e.g. 恵, 慈); the glyph story carries the distinctive load.
Non-blocking: 'each dusk' frames a recurring habit rather than a single frozen frame, slightly softening imageability.

story: At the left foot of Mountain Peak stands a stiff Scarecrow, arms out, snow piling on its straw shoulders; from the valley it looks exactly like a meditating HERMIT.
reading_story: Senna roars up the hairpin road, brakes at a cave mouth, and hands his trophy to the bearded HERMIT who blesses every driver.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword HERMIT is followed by a short trailing clause ('who blesses every driver') — still reads as the end payoff, but trimming it would make the landing cleaner.

story: At the field's left edge a straw Scarecrow stands stiff, arms out; lashed to its right arm, a Protest Placard on a rough stick, ink already running in the rain — TEMPORARY.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr idles at the curb, meter ticking: "This stop is TEMPORARY, mate — five minutes, then I'm gone."
issues: (minor, non-blocking) 'ink already running in the rain' is the only detail not sourced from a component image; it is justified because it carries the semantic bridge to TEMPORARY, but a stricter length/focus pass could cut 'already'.

(minor, non-blocking) reading_story places TEMPORARY mid-sentence; gate 4 is satisfied by the meaning story's terminal keyword, but the reading line reads slightly better if the keyword closes it too.

story: Pinned at the field's left edge, the Scarecrow tips its straw head back: to its right a colossal Wax Stamp descends from the sky, red wax raining down. Nothing to do but LOOK UP.
reading_story: Gyo booms a long "Gyooo" from the pagoda's top tier, and the whole street stops to LOOK UP.
issues: Non-blocking: both stories end on the same 'figure/crowd gazes upward' beat, so the reading story adds little imagery beyond the Gyo/pagoda anchor.
Non-blocking: the Wax Stamp descends but never stamps anything - its defining action (leaving a crisp red imprint) goes unused, leaving it close to a generic falling object.
Interference note: the Wax Stamp recurs across all 卩 kanji; the distinguishing hook is the red-wax rain plus the straw scarecrow, adequate but not maximally unique.

story: UNDERTAKE: a Stepladder stands atop a giant stop sign laid flat as its launch pad — the stop holds firm underfoot while rung after rung climbs toward an unbuilt skyscraper sketched in the clouds.
reading_story: Key the locksmith rattles one clipped "kee" at the padlocked construction gate — it springs open, and he strides in, first to UNDERTAKE the giant project.
issues: Minor: 'unbuilt skyscraper sketched in the clouds' is semi-abstract; a concrete half-built structure would image more sharply.
Minor: 'rung after rung climbs' has the ladder self-extending — poetic but slightly muddies the static A-frame persona (not a cognitive-ability violation).

story: At the left edge of a boot-shaped vineyard, Scarecrow watches Rake Hand drag the soil while Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through its tines — the scorched furrows spell ITALY.
reading_story: Mr. Eaton bites into pizza in ITALY, squealing a sharp "ee!" as the molten cheese burns his tongue.

story: A FIVE-MAN SQUAD halts at the field's left edge, saluting the Scarecrow standing stiff, arms out; behind him the Horizon Line runs dead flat across the sand — the rank they must hold.
reading_story: Goh, their clipped little sergeant, barks one short syllable and the FIVE-MAN SQUAD snaps shoulder to shoulder.
issues: Non-gating (spatial fidelity): 一 is staged as 'behind him', a depth relation, but in 伍 the Horizon Line belongs to the right-hand element (五) beside the Scarecrow — 'to his right' would map the layout faithfully; the left-edge placement of ⺅ is correct.
Non-gating (coherence): setting mixes the Scarecrow's 'field' with the Horizon Line's desert 'sand' in one frame; readable as a field at the desert's edge, but it costs one inferential step.

Non-gating (imageability): the closing clause 'the rank they must hold' is the story's only abstract beat — it usefully licenses the File/Line meanings, but it is the weakest visual in an otherwise concrete scene.

Non-gating (interference watch): military register overlaps 兵 (SOLDIER) and 卒 (whose reading story already uses a 'grizzled drill sergeant'); different actors (Sotter vs Goh) and a unique Scarecrow-salute hook keep them apart, but the 'sergeant' framing for Goh is the closest collision.
Verified against corpus: no other authored story pairs Scarecrow with Horizon Line, and no prior 伍 entry exists; sibling 五 uses Sheriff Star, so the two 'five' cards do not share an image.

story: The Scarecrow looms stiffly at the field's left edge; on the right, a trembling dog flattens its belly into the mud, nose between paws, tail tucked, utterly PROSTRATED.
reading_story: Fokker the aviator buzzes low over the field; the whole crowd drops PROSTRATED in the dirt as his wheels skim their backs.
issues: GATE 1 (component coverage) PASS — both mandatory components named: '⺅' via 'The Scarecrow looms stiffly at the field's left edge' and '犬' via 'a trembling dog flattens its belly into the mud'.

GATE 2 (no phantom components) PASS — 'mud', 'paws', 'tail', 'field' are attributes of the dog/scene, not named kanji parts. NON-BLOCKING: reading_story adds 'the whole crowd', an entity absent from the record; harmless as scenery but it is extraneous detail under rubric §3 item 7.
GATE 3 (reading actor present) PASS — 'Fokker the aviator' in reading_story matches reading_actor.actor_name 'Fokker'; reading_actor_used field is consistent.
GATE 4 (meaning lands) PASS — story terminates on '...tail tucked, utterly PROSTRATED.' Keyword is the final payoff, matching meaning_placement:'end'.

GATE 5 (actor consistency) PASS — registry image 'standing stiffly at the left edge of a field' is reproduced almost verbatim as 'looms stiffly at the field's left edge'. Fokker flying low with wheels skimming is ordinary physical motion for an aviator, no invented cognitive faculty.
GATE 6 (no false etymology) PASS — no claim that 伏 historically derives from person+dog; framed purely as scene.
GATE 7 (length) PASS — story 28 words, reading_story 22 words, both well under ~40.

NON-BLOCKING (drives distinctiveness=3): the two components never interact. The Scarecrow is inert set dressing and the dog carries the entire scene; nothing binds ⺅ to the image, so recall could retrieve the dog alone. A causal link (dog cowering *because of* the Scarecrow) would tighten coherence (§3 item 12) and reduce interference with other 犬 kanji.
NON-BLOCKING (positive): spatial fidelity (§3 item 11, starred) is strong — 'left edge' for ⺅ and 'on the right' for 犬 mirror the glyph layout explicitly.
NON-BLOCKING: reading_actor.note flags the '-ku' coda, but nothing in reading_story encodes it; the actor name alone carries ふく.

story: FELL! The Barbed Pike, planted at the field's right, tips over and its hooked spur rakes through the stiff Scarecrow's straw waist — the straw figure crashes flat into the mud.
reading_story: Batcher works the orchard in tens: one heave, one crack, ten trees FELL per batch, sawdust snowing over his boots.
issues: Reading story uses "ten trees FELL per batch", which parses most naturally as the intransitive past tense of "fall" rather than the transitive keyword "fell" (to cut down); the outcome is right but the grammatical sense is the wrong one and could mis-encode the keyword. Recommend "Batcher fells ten trees per batch" or similar.
The Barbed Pike "tips over" with no cause given — an unmotivated topple slightly weakens the causal image; giving the pike a shove or a gust would tighten it.
"works the orchard in tens" is redundant with "ten trees ... per batch" in a 20-word story.

story: At the field's left edge the straw Scarecrow stands stiff, arms out, a heavy velvet coronet jammed over its straw head and ermine robes draped down its pole — the harvest's new EARL.
reading_story: A hooded Hacker crouches in the manor's wine cellar, laptop glowing, quietly draining the EARL's estate accounts one keystroke at a time.
issues: ADVISORY (non-gating): the opening clause is near-verbatim boilerplate already used across the N1 set — 俳 'At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands stiff, arms out', 佐 'At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands stiff, straw arms piled with...', plus 保/償/傍/促. 29 of 620 authored N1 stories open on this Scarecrow template, so all discriminative load falls on the coronet/ermine props; closest confusable is 催 ('banknotes pinned all over its straw, arms outstretched'), another wealth-adorned scarecrow.

ADVISORY (non-gating, spatial fidelity §3.11): 白 — the entire right half of 伯 and the source of the はく reading — is absent from both stories. The coronet and ermine robes are draped on the Scarecrow itself, so nothing occupies the right-hand position and the learner gets no cue for writing that side. Naming 白 would not be a phantom component (it is in the kanji) and the reading_story ties Hacker only to 'the EARL's estate', not to any white/白 image.

story: Strapped upright at your left side, the Scarecrow goes wherever you go — straw arms outstretched, button eyes fixed on every passerby — the one stiff companion that will always ACCOMPANY you.
reading_story: Hancock refuses to sign the Declaration alone: two escorts must ACCOMPANY him to the desk, flanking his enormous signature.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in the reading story the keyword ACCOMPANY sits mid-sentence rather than at start/end; main story placement is correct at end.

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands stiff, straw arms piled with the farmer's rake, seed bag, and hat — it can't plow, but it holds everything: the perfect ASSISTANT.
reading_story: Sah answers every order with one clipped "sa!" — the tireless ASSISTANT who has fetched the tea before you finish asking.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword ASSISTANT is followed by a trailing relative clause ('who has fetched the tea...'), slightly softening the end placement — still the payoff of the dash clause, so gate 4 passes.
Note (positive): 'field's left edge' doubles as a 左 phonetic anchor and matches the Scarecrow persona image verbatim — keep it.

story: Wind swings the stiff Scarecrow's straw arm rightward, aiming it at the Mound of Soil beside it — black, moist, flawlessly heaped, its sprout-marker gilded: the county's most EXCELLENT dirt.
reading_story: Carr the cabbie brakes at the field gate, leans out, rasps one clipped verdict at that gilded dirt — "EXCELLENT" — then guns it, meter still running.
issues: Non-blocking: keyword sits one word from the end ("the county's most EXCELLENT dirt") rather than in absolute final position; it is still unmistakably the payoff clause, so gate 4 passes.

Non-blocking: "Wind" is an ambient force, not a named actor — it is scene physics, not a phantom component, and it is what moves the straw arm, so the Scarecrow is never granted agency or cognition it lacks.

Non-blocking: the record supplies only one 土 for 佳 (the glyph's right side is 圭, i.e. stacked 土); the story is faithful to the record as given, but the component list itself may deserve review upstream.

story: The Scarecrow at the field's left edge tears free of its post, sweeps every stray wisp of straw against its chest, and stitches them all into one bulging body — JOIN.
reading_story: President Hayes clamps two rival delegates' hands inside his own and holds the handshake loooong: "You JOIN, and you stay joined!"
issues: Minor: Scarecrow tearing free of its post stretches the 'standing stiffly, a thing' registry image, but it is ordinary physical motion, which the gate explicitly permits.
Minor: the gather-into-one schema overlaps with gather/collect neighbors (e.g. 集); the bulging stitched body is the only detail preventing interference.

story: The Scarecrow stands stiff at the field's left edge, the Setting-Sun Cage hung on its outstretched arm; the trapped red sun blazes through the bars like a priceless gem — sheer VALUE.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr never haggles; he just taps his ticking meter: "This machine alone decides the VALUE of your ride."
issues: Keyword payoff relies on a simile ('like a priceless gem') rather than a physically staged stake demonstrating value — slightly weakens imageability, non-gating
'sheer VALUE' ending shape is common across the price-family neighbors (値, 評価 kanji); the visual carries the distinctiveness

story: From the field's left edge the Scarecrow watches a Rake Hand claw across the property line, dragging a Bedsheet Cover with a Rubber Glove sliding beneath — inch by inch onto the neighbor's land they ENCROACH.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender inches his cocktail tray down the counter, glass after glass, until it begins to ENCROACH on your stool.
issues: Non-blocking: the Bedsheet Cover and Rubber Glove read as checklist filler rather than motivated props; 'dragging a Bedsheet Cover with a Rubber Glove sliding beneath' is syntactically ambiguous about what drags what and clutters the central image of the rake crossing the line.
Non-blocking: 'property line' / 'neighbor's land' are setting rather than phantom actors, so the no-phantom gate holds, but the boundary-crossing image is a fairly generic realization of 'encroach'.

story: STIMULATE — the Scarecrow stands stiff at the field's left edge, straw arms thrust out; every worker who slows feels that button-eyed stare pressing between their shoulder blades and hurries, hoeing twice as fast.
reading_story: Nothing can STIMULATE a dozing crowd like Soaker: one icy blast from his water cannon and everyone leaps up sprinting.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): reading story's 'everyone leaps up sprinting' edges toward 速 (fast, also そく/Soaker); keyword anchoring mitigates but a less speed-themed reaction would reduce neighbor interference.

story: EXCELLENCE enthroned: the Scarecrow keeps stiff watch at the left while the Wishing-Well Legs hoist the Sealed Clam-Locket high like a gold medal; beneath them, the Trailing Footprint drags off, outclassed.
reading_story: Shunsuke the striker bends the ball into the top corner; the whole stadium rises, chanting his name — pure EXCELLENCE.
issues: Minor: 'like a gold medal' is a simile prop, not a component — acceptable, but generators should avoid extra objects where possible
Minor: 'enthroned' is abstract; the concrete medal-hoist image carries the scene
Minor: medal-ceremony imagery is a somewhat generic trope for excellence-type keywords, slightly capping distinctiveness

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stares as, down the Twin Ski Slopes, a snapping Wishbone and a sliding Stepladder crash into an Open Mouth gaping at the notch — VULGAR.
reading_story: Zocker rips off his headset mid-rage, screaming into the webcam — his chat floods with one verdict: VULGAR.
issues: PASS - Gate 1 (component coverage): all five supplied actors named verbatim - 'Scarecrow', 'Twin Ski Slopes', 'Wishbone', 'Stepladder', 'Open Mouth'. components_used matches the record exactly.

PASS - Gate 2 (no phantoms): every scene element traces to a supplied actor image. 'field's left edge' is verbatim from the Scarecrow image ('left edge of a field'); 'the notch' is verbatim from the Twin Ski Slopes image ('meeting at a narrow notch'). Nothing invented.
PASS - Gate 3 (reading actor): 'Zocker' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor_used. The gamer-rage framing is consistent with the Zocker persona note (voiced/heavier twin of Soaker).

PASS - Gate 5 (actor consistency / no invented cognition): 'Scarecrow stares' is licensed by its own image ('watching whoever passes') - not a new cognitive faculty. 'snapping Wishbone' matches 'caught mid-snap'. 'sliding Stepladder' and 'crash' are ordinary physical motion, explicitly allowed.
PASS - Gate 6 (no etymology): no historical or derivational claim anywhere.
PASS - Gate 7 (length): meaning story is 31 words, reading story 22 - both well under ~40.

PASS - Gate 4 (placement) but WEAK on §3 item 4 'meaning lands / keyword is the payoff': VULGAR is positionally terminal in both stories, satisfying the gate, but in the meaning story it is grammatically detached after an em dash and semantically unconnected - a wishbone and stepladder sliding into a mouth carries no vulgarity. The keyword is appended, not earned. This is the main reason imageability is capped at 3.

CONCERN - distinctiveness / neighbor interference (§3 item 10): 谷 and its three sub-parts (ハ, 人, 口) will recur in every 谷-family kanji (浴, 欲, 裕, 溶...). The Scarecrow is the ONLY discriminating element for 俗, and it is given a purely passive role ('stares') in a subordinate opening clause while the shared cluster does all the acting. Partially mitigated by first position; a causal role for the Scarecrow would raise this to 4.

CONCERN - coherence: 谷 is supplied both as the whole (Twin Ski Slopes) and as its constituents (Wishbone, Stepladder, Open Mouth), and the story depicts the constituents as loose objects tumbling *down* the whole they compose. Readable, but the image fights itself.

MINOR - spatial fidelity (§3 item 11): left placement of ⺅ is explicit and correct, and 口 correctly sits at the bottom/notch. But ハ (top) and 人 (middle) are bundled into a single simultaneous slide, losing their vertical ordering, and the 谷 cluster is never anchored as 'right'.
MINOR - syntax load: the nested 'as, down the Twin Ski Slopes, ... crash into ... gaping at the notch' requires re-reading; a flatter clause order would improve the low-load criterion (§3 item 13).

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow spreads its stiff arms; beside it a giant Open Mouth, speared atop the Tree, screams nonstop — one silent, one shrieking, together they PROTECT the field.
reading_story: Hoth plants himself in the doorway, arms crossed, and grunts one clipped syllable: "I PROTECT this house."

story: DISCIPLINE: a Lightning Bolt cracks down beside the stiff Scarecrow; on the right the Cracking Whip snaps at its back until its straw fingers rake three flawless Comb Streaks into the ground below.
reading_story: Every dawn the cobbler hammers his Shoe with monkish DISCIPLINE — same bench, same hundred strikes, never one missed.
issues: Lightning Bolt (｜) is present but causally inert — it 'cracks down beside' the scene without driving the action, slightly weakening imageability (minor, non-gating).

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands stiff, arms out; nailed to its straw chest a paper flutters — five, seven, five syllables — a HAIKU.
reading_story: Mr. Hyde slinks from the fog, snarls — then softens, whispering a delicate seventeen-syllable HAIKU before vanishing into the night.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword HAIKU is followed by a trailing clause ('before vanishing into the night') — still the payoff of the final clause, but not the literal last word.

story: Left edge of the paddy: the Scarecrow stands stiff, straw arms flung wide, straw sloughing off its ribs and heaping beside it into one fat, twine-bound rice BALE.
reading_story: In a lantern-lit barn, Hugo sprawls atop a straw BALE, scribbling Les Misérables across pages that spill down the golden heap.
issues: Non-gating: the bale is described as already 'twine-bound' with no agent tying it — the straw self-assembles. Physical rather than cognitive, so it passes the gate, but a hand-wave the editor may want to tighten.
Non-gating (distinctiveness): the Scarecrow is itself made of straw, so 'straw' is a weak discriminator against other ⮥ kanji; the memorable load rests almost entirely on 'twine-bound rice BALE'.

Non-gating: reading_story reuses BALE mid-sentence rather than as a payoff; harmless reinforcement, but the vowel-length cue for long ō is carried only implicitly by the Hugo persona, not by any stretched/full imagery in the scene.

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands stiff, arms out, a fat pay envelope skewered on each straw wrist, coins spilling into the furrows below — its weekly STIPEND.
reading_story: Ho belly-laughs down the chimney and leaves no toys — just a fat red envelope on the mantel, this year's STIPEND.
issues: Minor: 'fat ... envelope' is repeated verbatim in both story and reading_story, blurring the meaning cue and the reading cue instead of giving each its own hook.
Minor: phonetic_extra 奉 is unused (allowed, not mandatory), so the right side of the glyph has no anchor and 俸 can blur with other pay/salary kanji.

Minor: 'its weekly STIPEND' implies the Scarecrow is employed; the envelopes are physically skewered on it so this reads as framing rather than an invented cognitive ability, but it is close to the line.

story: GODOWN: a Stepladder stands astride the roof; beneath it a Falling Katana slashes one silver diagonal down the front wall, and at ground level the Open Mouth gapes as the loading door, swallowing sacks of grain.
reading_story: Sosa swings for the fences — the ball crashes through a warehouse roof and buries itself in stored rice, deep inside the GODOWN.

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow stands, straw arms stiff, watching you pass. Under that unblinking straw stare you put the stolen apple back — ETHICS.
reading_story: Lynn returns her overpaid change to the cashier, coin by coin — the whole store applauds her ETHICS.
issues: (non-blocking) Distinctiveness capped at 3: the 'scarecrow watches you do X' frame is the actor's default persona and risks blurring across other single-⺅ kanji; the stolen-apple beat is the sole unique anchor.

story: The Scarecrow leans in from the left as the Lone Barn Shutter creaks half-closed above a tome, throwing a slanted shadow across only one page — every line of the scene tilts the same way: BIASED.
reading_story: Henson auditions a hundred puppets yet always casts the frog; backstage everyone mutters the great puppeteer is hopelessly BIASED.
issues: Minor: registry image has the Scarecrow 'standing stiffly' while the story has it lean in — ordinary physical motion, not a persona contradiction, so not gating.
Minor: closing clause 'every line of the scene tilts the same way' is summarizing/abstract rather than pure image; caps imageability at 4.

story: At the left edge of the field, the Scarecrow does chin-ups on its own pole, straw arms pumping, not one rotten straw in its body — unmistakably HEALTHY.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll jogs by in tiny shorts, flexing his seamed arms: "Stay HEALTHY like me!"

story: SPY: the Scarecrow stands stiff at the field's left edge, but a thin antenna quivers on its right shoulder and a polished lens glints where a knot in the straw should be — it is watching you.
reading_story: Tay signals from the rooftop, stretching one long "Taaay" down the radio; every agent in the alley ducks. Even her code word sings — the pop-star SPY.
issues: Reworded post-generation: the original named Divining Twig and Cowrie Shell, personas of 卜/貝, which are sub-parts of the phonetic 貞 rather than direct components of 偵, so both scans flagged them. Replaced with non-persona surveillance props; the mandatory ⺅ (Scarecrow) still anchors the scene.

story: At the field's left edge, Scarecrow watches Ink Droplet plunge from above into the Coal Brazier's four coals below; the black dot hisses up as smoke, staging a harvest fire that never happened — FALSEHOOD.
reading_story: Gee inspects the smoking field, wipes a finger through cold ash-paint, and mutters, "Gee... this whole fire is a FALSEHOOD."
issues: Minor: 'staging a harvest fire that never happened' is an agentless, abstract clause — the falsehood payoff is asserted rather than shown; costs an imageability point but is not gating.
Watch for interference with other 為-family kanji that reuse Ink Droplet + Coal Brazier; the fake-fire/Scarecrow framing currently differentiates it adequately.

story: BYSTANDER: at the field's left edge a straw Scarecrow juts, arms out, watching. Beside it Twin Pillars stand up beneath a draped Bedsheet Cover, capped by a clamped Pot Lid — a silent, motionless huddle.
reading_story: Bowie, a red-and-blue flash painted across his face, leans on a lamppost as the street brawl rages — hands in pockets, singing nothing, the world's most glamorous BYSTANDER.
issues: 立 is discharged as a bare verb phrase ('Twin Pillars stand up') rather than a discrete image element — it satisfies coverage but is the weakest-encoded component and would be the first thing to fail a stricter read of gate 1
Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11): the story stacks the standing element BENEATH the Bedsheet Cover, but in 傍 the 立 sits ABOVE 冖 — the vertical order is inverted
The meaning story has no event or motion; 'a silent, motionless huddle' is thematically apt for 'bystander' but gives the learner nothing dynamic to replay, capping imageability at 3
The 立 + 冖 + 亠 'lid over draped cloth' stack is shared with other 旁-family and N1 kanji, so the meaning-story imagery carries interference risk with neighbours

The component record itself is internally redundant (并 alongside 立/亠/冖, and 亠 is the top stroke of 立) — the candidate handled it as well as could be expected, but the underlying decomposition should be reviewed upstream

story: A Stepladder stands open high above the Plus-Sign Crossroads, its splayed A-frame legs flinging rain off in sheets onto the four tarmac arms below — a giant roadside UMBRELLA.
reading_story: Santa, drenched on a rainy rooftop, pops open a red-and-white UMBRELLA over his sack before sliding down the chimney.
issues: Coherence nit: an open stepladder is a see-through A-frame, so 'flinging rain off in sheets' asks it to behave like a solid canopy. Ordinary physical behavior, not an invented cognitive ability, so it passes gating, but it slightly softens the picture.
Reading story is stock imagery (Santa + umbrella + chimney) and does little to bind さん distinctively to this glyph; Santa is present and in-persona, so gate 3 passes.
'Giant roadside umbrella' is a semantically obvious payoff for the keyword, which caps distinctiveness.

story: SPONSOR of today's stunt: the Scarecrow at the field's left edge, banknotes pinned all over its straw, arms outstretched toward Stumpy Sparrow, who staggers past balancing snow-capped Mountain Peak on its head.
reading_story: Cy fires a fastball; stitched across his jersey in huge letters is the name of his SPONSOR.
issues: Minor: keyword link relies on inferring sponsorship from banknotes pinned to the Scarecrow plus the word 'stunt' — one small inferential step, acceptable.
Minor: two simultaneous focal actions (Scarecrow's outstretched arms, Sparrow balancing the mountain) slightly split visual attention.

story: The Scarecrow guards his buried Cowrie Shell: Mound of Soil heaped over it, Pot Lid clamped on top — yet the shell's Watching Eye glares through the dirt, Wishbone legs kicking. Treasure pawned against his DEBT.
reading_story: Cy owes the ballpark: each fastball Cy hurls knocks one coin off his DEBT, so he pitches until his arm hangs limp.
issues: Minor: the payoff 'Treasure pawned against his DEBT' is conceptual rather than imaged — no lender or pawnshop appears in the scene, so the debt link rests on the word 'pawned' alone.

Minor: reading_story keyword DEBT sits mid-sentence (word 14/22) with a trailing clause; passes per corpus precedent (井, 佐) since strict start/end placement gates the meaning story, and 'Cy owes' fronts the concept at the start.
Minor: reuses the Scarecrow-guarding-the-field frame already used for 佐 (ASSISTANT); the burial-mound staging keeps the scenes separable but watch for further Scarecrow guard scenes.
Note (positive): staging Watching Eye and Wishbone as the shell's eye and legs mirrors 貝 = 目 + ハ, and the lid/soil-over-shell stack matches the vertical layout of 責.

story: The Scarecrow stands stiff at the left of a doorway hung with the Beaded Light-Fringe; the Falling Katana drops from above the strands, glances off the beads, and rips open his straw shoulder — a gaping WOUND.
reading_story: Mid-"Shoooow!" the Showman doffs his top hat, revealing a freshly stitched WOUND across his scalp — the circus crowd gasps louder than at any trick.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword WOUND is pre-final (followed by the crowd-reaction clause); it still reads as the payoff of the reveal, but moving it to the clause end would be stronger.
Minor: 'wound' on a straw scarecrow is a slight semantic stretch (rip vs flesh wound), though 'rips open his straw shoulder' keeps it concrete.

story: At the field's left edge, the Scarecrow's straw arm points across at its own double — an open Stepladder on splayed legs, a Woolly Ram draped over the top rung like a fleecy wig. That copy is ME.
reading_story: Booker the bookkeeper licks his pencil, scans the servants' wage column, and writes one name into every single row: ME.
issues: minor (non-blocking): the keyword payoff 'That copy is ME' is a conceptual identity claim rather than a picturable event — the scene is vivid but the link to 'me' rests on the abstract double/copy idea

minor (non-blocking): the 'its own double' device leans on the fact that ⺅ and 人 are the same shape, so it is reusable and could blur against other kanji pairing the person radical with a person-shaped actor

minor (non-blocking): the Scarecrow 'points across at its own double' implies recognition; acceptable since its image already grants it watching passers-by, but it is the closest thing to an added faculty in the story

story: Scarecrow stands stiff at the left of the worksite; beside him a Stepladder perches on Twin Pillars, the Sun blazes beneath them, and Sand Trickle sifts at the bottom — every object here is his COLLEAGUE.
reading_story: Detective Ryo interrogates the whole office; every suspect's alibi is the same: "Ask my COLLEAGUE." Ryo groans — colleagues covering colleagues.
issues: Evidence: all gates pass — components: 'Scarecrow' / 'Stepladder' / 'Twin Pillars' / 'Sun' / 'Sand Trickle' all named; no phantoms ('worksite' is scenery); reading actor 'Detective Ryo' present and matches hardboiled-detective persona; keyword COLLEAGUE at end of both stories; ~35 and ~22 words.
Minor: 'the Sun blazes beneath them' is spatially hard to visualize (a sun below a ladder) even if it mirrors glyph layout — costs imageability.
Minor: meaning story is a static inventory of objects; COLLEAGUE arrives as a label, not as something the scene enacts, so the keyword binding is verbal rather than visual.

Minor interference risk: 'objects gathered = colleagues' is a generic frame; the ironic twist (his colleagues are all things, echoing the ⺅-as-thing Scarecrow) is what keeps it distinct from 寮/療/瞭 — preserve that twist in any edit.

story: At the field's left edge the straw Scarecrow wears a saffron robe, its gourd head shaved smooth, a begging bowl roped to one outstretched arm — a stiff, silent, straw-stuffed MONK.
reading_story: Sammy Sosa swings for the fences; the ball sails over the wall and drops straight into the alms bowl of a startled MONK sweeping temple steps.

story: CEREMONY: at the left edge of the aisle, the Scarecrow stands stiff in a black bow tie, straw arms outstretched, while every guest files past bowing to it, rice pattering off its shoulders.
reading_story: Gee bellows one heavy note on the temple gong, and the whole CEREMONY freezes mid-bow.

story: At the field's left edge the Scarecrow tips its outstretched straw arm; the golden prize cup slides off, landing among the trampled crops it failed to guard — REPARATION.
reading_story: The Showman doffs his top hat, booms "Shoooow's over!", and hands out the ring's prize money as REPARATION for every ruined ticket.
issues: Minor: 'tips its outstretched straw arm' gives the stiff, inanimate Scarecrow slight volitional motion — physical, not cognitive, so acceptable, but a purely passive sag would fit the persona better.
Minor: 'the trampled crops it failed to guard' is narrated backstory rather than visible image; slightly dilutes the single-shot scene.
Minor: in the reading story REPARATION is followed by 'for every ruined ticket' — payoff-clause placement matches approved convention (伊, 企) but is not the literal final word.

story: A pot crammed with licenses to the brim; the Pot Lid clamps down on top, bulging as still more licenses squeeze in beneath it — FILL.
reading_story: Juno commands every temple fountain to FILL to overflowing for her festival, and none dares stop pouring.

story: An old gravestone slams down on top of the Wishing-Well Legs. The stubby stone legs buckle, tremble, then slowly straighten, hoisting the old slab skyward — the crushing weight is OVERCOME.
reading_story: Coker, bedridden for years, grips the rail and hauls himself upright, roaring — his illness is OVERCOME.
issues: Advisory (non-gating): the gravestone prop carries 古's 'old' concept; fine here since 'old' is named twice, but avoid reusing gravestone imagery in other 古-family kanji or cross-card interference will grow.

story: A Swaddling Wrap curls down over the Open Mouth, gagging it mid-shout; propped up on the Wishing-Well Legs, the mouth spits the cloth free and yells its EXCUSE.
reading_story: Pulled over, Menn hands the officer a scribbled EXCUSE instead of his license — "dog ate it."

story: A bent bronze tablet rests on the Horizon Line; beneath the sand, a Wishbone's splayed legs prop it up like altar feet. Kneeling scribes read the bend's engraved commandments — the kingdom's entire CODE.
reading_story: Detective Tennison slams the thick law CODE onto the interrogation table, quoting article after article until the suspect confesses.

story: Midway up the Twin Pillars, the Rake Hand clamps its tines across both at once — one grasp seizing two columns in the same instant: CONCURRENTLY.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll, arms molded stiff, somehow signs autographs with both hands CONCURRENTLY — two fan queues, one grinning doll.
issues: (minor, non-blocking) reading_story keyword CONCURRENTLY is followed by a short coda clause rather than sitting at the absolute end, but it is still the payoff of the main clause

story: The Sun blazes directly overhead; below, the Watching Eye stares straight up into the glare, unblinking, pupil sizzling white — one blinding stare, one reckless RISK.
reading_story: Bowie struts to the stage edge and dives into the crowd, trusting strangers' hands to catch him — every Bowie leap is pure RISK.

story: In an empty room, the Bedsheet Cover drapes over the Low Stool, edges pooling on the floor, shrouding a seat nobody has ever sat on. Completely SUPERFLUOUS.
reading_story: Joe irons his socks, alphabetizes his ice cubes, polishes rain — "Joooe," his wife groans, "all of that is SUPERFLUOUS."
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage): both mandatory actors named verbatim — "the Bedsheet Cover" (冖) and "the Low Stool" (几); components_used matches.
PASS gate 2 (no phantoms): only scenery is "empty room" / "floor"; the "seat" is licensed by the 几 registry image ("one curved crossbar for a seat"), not an invented actor.
PASS gate 3 (reading actor): "Joe" opens the reading_story and the stretched "Joooe" reproduces the registry note's long-ō cue for じょう.
PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): keyword is the terminal payoff in both stories — "Completely SUPERFLUOUS." and "all of that is SUPERFLUOUS."; matches meaning_placement="end".

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency), with one flag: 冖 tracks its registry image closely ("draped over something hidden, its edges hanging down" → "drapes over the Low Stool, edges pooling on the floor"), and 几 stays a low seat. But the reading actor drifts: the registry persona is "Average Joe", while the story portrays a compulsive perfectionist (irons socks, alphabetizes ice cubes). No invented cognitive ability and no contradiction of a defined nature, so non-blocking — but it is the weakest link and would be cleaner if the wife, not Joe, were the fussy one.
PASS gate 6 (no etymology): no historical/derivational claim; framed purely as an imaginative scene.
PASS gate 7 (length): story 27 words, reading_story 19 words — both well under ~40, no extraneous detail.
Strength — spatial fidelity (rubric item 11): 冖 sits above 几 in the glyph and the story puts the cover on top of the stool, so the picture rebuilds the writing order.
Minor imageability drag: "polishes rain" is clever but not actually picturable — it is the one clause a learner cannot render as an image, unlike the socks and ice cubes.

Distinctiveness risk: "Bedsheet Cover drapes over X in an empty room" is a template that will recur across other 冖 kanji; the differentiating hook here is only the never-sat-on seat. Acceptable, but flag for interference checks against neighboring 冖 entries.

story: A white Bedsheet Cover drapes the top; beneath it stubby Wishing-Well Legs stand at the left while a Tape Measure quivers out one inch at the right, sizing the gleaming CROWN.
reading_story: Genghis Khan reins his horse on the ridge, lifts a gold CROWN from the steppe dust, and jams it over his fur hat.
issues: Weak interaction: Wishing-Well Legs and Bedsheet Cover are inert scenery ('stand at the left', 'drapes the top') with no causal role; only the Tape Measure does anything to the keyword.

The CROWN is spatially unanchored - it appears only in the final clause as the object being sized, so the reader cannot tell whether it is under the sheet, atop the legs, or held aloft. Nothing is actually crowned.

The phrasing is a layout recitation template ('A on top; beneath it B at the left while C at the right') that will read near-identically for other 冖-topped or 儿-footed kanji (元, 兄, 光, 冗, 冥), raising neighbor interference; only the keyword differentiates it.
Minor: 'sizing' is a flat verb for the payoff - a concrete beat (the tape measure cinching the crown to fit the sheeted figure's head) would lift both imageability and distinctiveness above 3.

story: Frost Beads harden on the left edge of a winter wire; Stumpy Sparrow scoots up from the right, pressing his fat flank against them, proudly treating each frozen drop as his ASSOCIATE.
reading_story: June sweeps through the office pinning badges on desks: everyone she touches is instantly her ASSOCIATE, junior partner in everything.

story: Frost Beads harden on the windowpane's left edge; right beside them, a grey blob of doubt hangs in the air, until the bitter cold makes it CONGEAL into trembling jelly.
reading_story: Gyo hums a long, heavy note over the pond; the ripples CONGEAL mid-swell into ridged ice.
issues: Non-blocking: cold/ice framing in both stories risks interference with other 冫 kanji (凍 freeze, 冷 cool, 氷 ice); the doubt-blob-to-jelly transform is the only real differentiator.
Non-blocking: 'Frost Beads harden' is slightly redundant — the persona defines them as already hardened beads of ice.
Non-blocking: 'a grey blob of doubt' is the least imageable element; a more specific rendering of 疑 would lift the score.

story: COMMONPLACE: a glossy black Ink Droplet sits in the dust between the Low Stool's splayed legs — customers plop onto that crossbar all day, and not one has ever glanced underneath.
reading_story: In Bonn, the mayor unveils a monument to the average citizen: a grey concrete man clutching a grocery bag. The crowd shrugs. Nothing is more COMMONPLACE.
issues: Semantic link to the keyword runs through 'overlooked/unnoticed' rather than directly through 'ordinary/mediocre' — the reader must take one inferential step from 'nobody has ever glanced underneath' to COMMONPLACE. Non-gating (keyword is at position 0 and the reading_story lands the sense directly), but it is the weakest joint in the story.

Reading actor Bonn is used as a backdrop location ('In Bonn, the mayor...') rather than as an acting persona; the mayor, not Bonn, drives the scene. Gate 3 passes on presence, but the phonetic cue carries less agency than corpus norm. No prior Bonn or Hon story exists in N5-N1, so this sets the precedent for the pair — worth deciding deliberately before Hon (ほん) is authored.

The Ink Droplet is static and small while all the motion belongs to the customers and the stool; the component being cued is the least active element in its own scene. Minor imageability drag, not an actor-nature violation.

The Ink Droplet actor already carries at least eight N1 stories (丹, 偽, 凶, 博, 塾, 尽, 救, 敷) and the Low Stool two (抗, 拠). No direct pairing collision, but this scene is deliberately mundane and is the likeliest of that set to blur under interference.

story: VILLAIN mark: deep inside the Trap Pit's sheer walls, a Falling Katana carves one silver diagonal down the dirt, and a single Ink Droplet splats its black dot right across that cut.
reading_story: Kyo screams into the mic, and the crowd roars back that his stage persona is pure VILLAIN — black cape, howling feedback, spotlights blood-red.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 4, weak form): 'VILLAIN mark:' works as a label prefix rather than an earned payoff — nothing in the scene makes the cut-and-splat feel villainous or unlucky, so the keyword is attached rather than derived.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness): 'Falling Katana carves a silver diagonal' + 'Ink Droplet splats its dot' are the default generic actions for ノ and 丶; with 凵 recurring across 出/凹/凸/函, this story risks interference with other 凵-container kanji.
Non-blocking: reading_story shares no imagery with the meaning story (no pit, cut, or ink), so the きょう hook and the glyph decomposition are stored as two unlinked scenes.

story: SWORD — the Cleaver drops off its hook, broad curved edge flashing white, and splits the butcher block clean in two, standing quivering in the wood like a battlefield blade.
reading_story: Tone Loc growls into the mic; on every beat the SWORD propped behind him rings like a struck bell.
issues: Non-blocking: continuity wobble between the two stories — the story leaves the blade embedded/quivering in the butcher block, while the reading story has 'the SWORD propped behind him'. Not a gate failure (separate scenes are allowed), but a shared image would bind the meaning and reading cues more tightly.

Non-blocking: the closing simile 'like a battlefield blade' is abstract filler that spends 4 of the ~40 words without adding a picture; the concrete beats (hook, block, quivering) already carry the image.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): 'a blade splits a block' is the generic scene for the whole blade family (刃, 剣, 剣-compounds). Only the Cleaver-specific props (hook, butcher block) keep it from colliding with neighbors.

story: Ink Droplet falls from its brush and lands on the hanging Cleaver's inner curve, one glossy black dot clinging exactly where the steel is sharpest — that marked edge is the BLADE.
reading_story: Jin steps onstage gripping a mirror-polished BLADE, spotlight sliding down its edge as he sings, fans screaming at the flash.
issues: (non-blocking) reading_story is the weakest half: 'Jin onstage gripping a polished BLADE' is a generic idol-with-prop image and risks interference with other じん kanji that reuse weapons; a Jin-specific hook (mic stand, BTS staging detail) would raise distinctiveness.

story: Down the right edge of the wheatfield, the Guillotine Blade drops again and again, shearing whole rows flat in one polished sweep. Golden heads topple leftward in heaps. This is how machines REAP.
reading_story: Guy Fawkes crouches in a moonlit barley field, match in hand, muttering that tonight he will REAP the harvest of gunpowder he sowed.

story: Cupped Palms rise pleading on the left; the Falling Katana slashes down through them, and the Guillotine Blade waiting at the right edge drops with one clean thud — PUNISH.
reading_story: Kayo misses a beat mid-cancan; the cabaret owners PUNISH her — she must dance the encore wearing prisoner's chains.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in reading_story the keyword PUNISH is mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable since the placement gate targets the meaning story and PUNISH is still the capitalized payoff.
Minor: Guillotine Blade 'drops with one clean thud' has no explicit target, leaving the final image slightly underspecified.

story: Pinned high, the Wanted Poster shivers as the Guillotine Blade along its right edge drops in tiny strokes, shaving paper curls off the sketched face until only a splinter remains: WHITTLE.
reading_story: Awaiting trial, Sacco does nothing but WHITTLE — pale shavings pile around his boots as one more wooden spoon takes shape.
issues: Minor coherence seam: 'only a splinter remains' applies a wood image to a paper poster (non-gating)
Reading story keyword is clause-final (word 7 of 20) rather than literally first word; still reads as start placement, not buried

story: STURDY: at the right edge, Guillotine Blade drops onto Rampart Ridge and shatters into glinting shards — the jagged peak inside the battlements not even chipped, stone dust settling.
reading_story: General Gough hammers his boot heel against the wall, grinning: "Bring your guns — this line is STURDY."
issues: NON-BLOCKING (advisory only): 'shatters into glinting shards ... stone dust settling' spends ~6 words on aftermath; trimming to a single consequence would sharpen focus (rubric §3 item 13, conciseness), but it is still well inside the ~40-word cap.

story: Beneath a Stepladder, an Open Mouth gapes wide; the tall Guillotine Blade on the right tips over and slides down that throat, its straight edge curving into a swallowed SABRE.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll salutes with a SABRE, dead serious, but his molded plastic grip snaps and the SABRE clatters away.

story: On the left the Grain Comb rakes powder into three even rows; the Guillotine Blade at the right edge drops, slicing each row into identical piles — each pile one exact DOSE.
reading_story: Zy counts pills into paper cups, tapping each cup shut: one exact DOSE per patient, never a pill more.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in reading_story the keyword DOSE sits inside the closing clause rather than as the literal final beat — 'one exact DOSE per patient, never a pill more'; still the payoff, but trailing words slightly dilute the landing.

story: A grain heap towers past the measuring line. The Guillotine Blade, standing tall on the right edge, drops once — cleanly shearing off everything above the mark. What tumbles free is the SURPLUS.
reading_story: At harvest pay-out, Joe gets double rations; he groans a long "Joooe...!" as clerks keep piling SURPLUS into his overflowing arms.

story: A lone Guillotine Blade stands at the right edge of an empty world. It drops — the first cut ever made — and from that fresh wound, light, rivers, and life ORIGINATE.
reading_story: Sosa steps to the plate shouting "Watch where legends ORIGINATE!" — his long, slow swing cracks the very first home run into orbit.
issues: Minor: payoff imagery ('light, rivers, and life') is a diffuse burst rather than one concrete object, slightly softening imageability at the keyword moment — not blocking.

story: On the winners' podium a lone Flexing Bicep strains, veins bulging, hoisting a golden trophy overhead — raw power finally crowned as ACHIEVEMENT.
reading_story: Coe kicks down the home straight, snaps the finishing tape, and bows to the roaring stadium — the crowning ACHIEVEMENT of his career.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): trophy/podium is stock imagery for success-keywords and 効 shares both the 工+力 structure and the こう/Coe reading — distinctiveness rests mainly on the bodiless-arm oddity; consider a more 功-specific prop if 効's mnemonic also uses a victory scene.

story: INFERIORITY: only a few dry crumbs sift down from above onto the Flexing Bicep below; the arm trembles, sags, barely twitching on that pitiful scattering of fuel.
reading_story: Retzler steps into the arm-wrestling final, loses to a toddler in two seconds, and the whole crowd chants INFERIORITY.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 少 is instantiated only as the quantifier 'a few' modifying crumbs rather than as a foregrounded 'few' concept — evidence: 'only a few dry crumbs'. It satisfies the naming gate but is the weakest element of the image.
Minor (non-blocking): main story (~27 words) and reading story (~24 words) each pass the ~40-word cap individually; combined they are 51 words if the cap is ever read as applying jointly.

story: INTUITION: strapped to the right tip of a forked dowsing rod, a bodiless Flexing Bicep is hauled across dead desert — over one blank dune the muscle balloons and shudders, and water bursts up.
reading_story: Khan wakes at midnight, kicks out his fire and shifts the whole camp uphill for no reason; by dawn the flooded valley has swallowed his old ground. INTUITION.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: the sole mandatory component 力 is named verbatim as "Flexing Bicep" in `story`, and `components_used` matches.

Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS with a caveat: the "forked dowsing rod" is a prop, not a persona-styled actor, and its fork plausibly stands in for 甚 — which IS in the kanji (listed under phonetic_extra), so nothing is named that is absent from 勘. Flag for human queue only if the project reads gate 2 as banning all non-actor props.

Cognitive-ability check PASS (borderline): the bicep only "balloons and shudders" — an ordinary muscular motion fully consistent with "pure raw power". The divining/sensing role is carried by the rod, not attributed to the bicep. Note the causal chain is slightly ambiguous (does the flex cause the water, or reveal it?); a sharper draft would make the burst the bicep's doing.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: "Khan" opens `reading_story`; `reading_actor_used` = "Khan".
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: "INTUITION:" is the first token of `story`, matching meaning_placement "start"; `reading_story` also ends on "INTUITION." (redundant but not a violation).
Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: "bodiless" mirrors the registry's "no body attached"; Khan's midnight camp, fire and valley are consistent with the Genghis Khan persona (horseback not contradicted).
Gate 6 (no false etymology) PASS: no historical or radical-origin claim anywhere.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: `story` = 33 words, `reading_story` = 29 words, both under ~40.
Spatial fidelity: good — "strapped to the right tip" correctly places 力 on the right side of 勘.

Distinctiveness risk: dowsing/divining is the stock metaphor for intuition, and "leader wakes at night and moves camp before a flood" is a well-worn premonition trope; both halves also share a water payoff, so 勘 could blur with other perception/sense kanji (感, 察, 覚) if they reach for similar sensing imagery.

story: A Feathered Arrow hovers point-down over Stumpy Sparrow; at her right a Flexing Bicep pumps slow, irresistible curls. Sharp point above, raw power beside — the grumpy bird finally flaps off. That's how you PERSUADE.
reading_story: Khan reins in his horse before a walled town, smiling instead of drawing his sword — one soft word from Khan is enough to PERSUADE the gates open.
issues: Meaning-story logic is persuasion-by-intimidation (arrow threat + flexing muscle makes the bird flee), which risks being recalled as 'threaten/coerce/drive away' instead of 'persuade/recommend/encourage' — the reading story carries the true 'persuade' sense better than the meaning story does.

Feathered Arrow 'hovers point-down' is static, in mild tension with its registry image 'streaking dead straight' in mid-flight — allowed as ordinary physical positioning, but it dilutes the actor's signature motion.

story: Something impossibly heavy presses down onto the Coal Brazier's four glowing coals; at the right, the Flexing Bicep strains and hoists it clear, sparks scattering — a MERITORIOUS DEED.
reading_story: Kuhn chalks "paradigm shift" across the blackboard; the packed lecture hall roars, hailing it the century's most MERITORIOUS DEED.
issues: Non-blocking: 重 is rendered as 'Something impossibly heavy' — an unnamed mass. The component carries kanji_keyword 'heavy' with no actor/image, so coverage is satisfied, but a concrete heavy object (anvil, millstone, safe) would raise concreteness and imageability without adding words.

Non-blocking interference risk: 動 (move) is 重 + 力, and 'heavy thing + straining arm lifting it' is the natural story for that kanji too. Only the Coal Brazier's coals separate the two scenes; if 動's mnemonic reuses a lifting frame, these will compete at retrieval.

story: Early — sun barely up — a fortune-teller balances her Divining Twig upright on the breakfast surface, letting it topple to point out today's fortune: it lands flat across the TABLE.
reading_story: Tucker crawls under the dining TABLE, tugging the tablecloth until every plate slides down onto his head.
issues: Minor (non-gating): fortune-telling motif is shared with other Divining Twig kanji (e.g. 占); the table payoff mitigates but does not eliminate interference risk.
Minor (non-gating): 'breakfast surface' is a paraphrase of the table appearing before the keyword payoff — acceptable device, keyword still lands at the end.

story: The Plus-Sign Crossroads is painted across the left entrance; to its right, booths of every specialty gleam, and an Ink Droplet hangs above the top-right corner, ready to dot the ribbon of the grand EXPOSITION.
reading_story: A Hacker slips through the turnstiles and flips every screen at the EXPOSITION to his own blinking handle.
issues: Imageability drag: the three components are co-located by spatial description ('left entrance', 'to its right', 'above the top-right corner') rather than interacting causally — the scene is a static diagram, not an event. A droplet actually falling and dotting the ribbon as the Crossroads-marked gate opens would bind harder.

'booths of every specialty gleam' is the weakest beat — 'specialty' stays an abstract label attached to generic booths, with no concrete hook. This is the 専 component doing the least work in the image.

Distinctiveness risk: a grand exposition with booths is a plausible collision setting for other 専-family or exhibition-adjacent kanji; nothing in the scene is uniquely tied to 博 beyond the keyword itself.

Reading story is competent but only loosely bound to the meaning scene — the Hacker acts on generic 'screens' rather than on any of the three component actors, so meaning and reading recall stay two separate images instead of one.

story: Still Butte stands utterly motionless; at its right flank Wax Stamp slams down, and the red wax hardens into a crisp seal against the rock in an INSTANT.
reading_story: One squeeze of Soaker's trigger and you're drenched in an INSTANT — no warning, just cold water everywhere.

story: At the checkpoint you stride forward to leave; on your right a Wax Stamp thuds down, pressing red refusal across your papers — you STEP BACK.
reading_story: Kyacker screams "Kyaa!" mid-karate-chop, and the whole dojo takes one terrified STEP BACK.

story: Falling Katana slices down the warehouse's left wall, freezing at a painted stop line; on the right, Wax Stamp presses red seals onto pallet after pallet of crates — WHOLESALE.
reading_story: Shaq wheels a forklift through the WHOLESALE depot, stacking pallets higher than his own head.

story: Under the Rock Overhang's stone slab, the Village Milestone stands dwarfed, its carved arrow worn to a hairline scratch — a distance so absurdly small it measures exactly one RIN.
reading_story: Lynn squints at a copper speck on her palm: the tiniest coin ever minted, one lonely RIN.
issues: Non-blocking: the story frames 厘 as a unit of DISTANCE ('a distance so absurdly small'), while the record's meanings are fractional/monetary (1/10 sen, 1/10 bu); the reading_story correctly uses a coin, so the pair is slightly inconsistent. Swapping 'distance' for a generic 'a measure so absurdly small' would align both halves.
Non-blocking: '...it measures exactly one RIN' is the one expository clause in an otherwise concrete story; the payoff is told rather than shown.

story: Bean Sprouts stand rigidly upright atop the Rock Overhang while a daring recruit does push-ups in the hollow beneath; not one sprout bends in the gale. Everything about this cliff is STERN.
reading_story: Drill instructor Glenn inspects your bunk with a white glove; one speck of dust and his face turns STERN — he barks until the walls shake.
issues: Minor: meaning-story payoff line tells the keyword ('Everything about this cliff is STERN') rather than showing it — acceptable but slightly weaker than an enacted payoff.
Minor: reading story places STERN before a short trailing clause ('he barks until the walls shake'); still the clear payoff, not buried, so gate 4 passes.

story: In the empty sink a yellow Rubber Glove lies palm-up, fingers curled, catching a tap-drip. Plink. The tap drips into that same waiting palm again — and again — and again. OR AGAIN.
reading_story: Yuna the figure skater lands her triple, circles back, and lands it again — OR AGAIN, the crowd chants, so she throws it a third time.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 2 borderline): the story introduces 'sink' and 'tap' as scene props. Neither is presented as a kanji component, and the dripping tap is the functional engine of the repetition rather than extraneous detail, so it clears 'no phantom components' and 'length & focus' — but it is the only added machinery, so it should stay a prop, never be named as a part of 又.

Non-blocking (gate 4 partial): the keyword 'or again' is delivered at the end as required, but the story only encodes the AGAIN half (repeated drips). The 'OR' / alternation sense ('又は' = or, 'on the other hand') has no image hook at all, so the vocab 又は is unsupported by the meaning story.

Distinctiveness risk — corpus interference: 'Rubber Glove lies/rests palm-up' with 'curled fingers' is near-verbatim shared with at least three shipped stories (PELT: 'A yellow Rubber Glove lies palm-up on the butcher's block, its curled fingers...'; POLES: 'rests palm-up on the flat white Horizon Line'; LIGHTLY: 'floats palm-up atop a Mound of Soil'). The base persona posture carries almost no discriminating load here.

Distinctiveness risk — device reuse: 'again and again' appears in ~10 other authored stories (-TIMES, POLITICS, EXPENSE, REAP, APPLAUD, ABUSE, CRITICISM, AGGRESSION, REASON, TIGHTEN). It is the natural encoding for this keyword, but it means the repetition rhythm alone will not separate 又 from its neighbours — the drip-into-palm image is doing all the discriminating work.

Minor redundancy: 'catching a tap-drip' and 'The tap drips into that same waiting palm' state the same event twice; the second sentence could carry the whole beat and free words for an 'or'/alternation hook.

story: A Swaddling Wrap curls down and bundles the Open Mouth tight; through the muffling cloth the Open Mouth squeezes out just one short PHRASE.
reading_story: Ask Coo anything and the clipped pigeon-keeper answers with a single PHRASE — "coo" — never a full sentence.
issues: Non-gating distinctiveness note: third 'Swaddling Wrap muffles Open Mouth' scene in the corpus — opening clause nearly duplicates 免's accepted story ('A Swaddling Wrap curls down over the Open Mouth, gagging it mid-shout') and echoes 号; differentiators (mouth never freed, only one short phrase leaks through the cloth, no third actor) keep it passable but cap distinctiveness at 3.

story: A Meat Hook curls down the right edge; inside its frame hangs a flat Horizon Line, and beneath, an Open Mouth bellows "Action! Cut!" — that bossy mouth is the DIRECTOR.
reading_story: The Sheriff storms the film set, badge flashing: "Round here, I'm the DIRECTOR now" — one clipped "shi!" and the whole crew freezes.

story: War Helmet sits squarely on top of Open Mouth. The mouth shouts joyful congratulations up into the empty steel, which amplifies the cheer skyward — GOOD LUCK!
reading_story: Kitch scratches lottery ticket after ticket — every single one a winner. "GOOD LUCK just sticks to me," Kitch shrugs.

story: An Open Mouth gapes on the left; right beside it lands a Mound of Soil, its sprout-marker still trembling from the launch, dark grit sprayed across the pavement — one wet, gravelly SPIT.
reading_story: Toto trots over, tastes that muddy heap, and SPITS it out with a disgusted sneeze.
issues: Imageability (rubric item 9, starred): the act of spitting is inferred rather than depicted -- the Open Mouth only 'gapes' and never ejects anything; the Mound of Soil passively 'lands' and the causal link rests entirely on the phrase 'still trembling from the launch'. An active verb from the mouth would tighten the payoff.

Distinctiveness (rubric item 10): '口 + earthy object -> something expelled' is a high-collision template across the many 口 compounds, so neighbor interference risk is nontrivial; the trembling sprout-marker and 'wet, gravelly' texture are what keep it separable.

Minor redundancy: reading_story reuses the keyword ('SPITS it out') so it restates the meaning story rather than adding an independent hook for と/Toto. Not a gate violation, but the reading cue carries less unique retrieval weight than it could.

Cosmetic: the semicolon-plus-em-dash construction packs three clauses into one sentence, which is slightly higher cognitive load than rubric item 13 (conciseness / low load) ideally wants, though it stays well under the ~40-word cap at 32 words.

story: DISPLAY: the Kings Crown rises on its velvet cushion up through the Open Mouth's square hatch above, jutting out into daylight — three jeweled points blazing over the sill for the whole street to see.
reading_story: Tay hauls her prize pumpkin onto the trestle table, stretching a long "Taaay-daaa!" as the judges circle — the biggest DISPLAY at the county fair.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 口 Open Mouth is used mainly as an aperture ("square hatch") rather than as a mouth acting — it is named and its defined square-hole nature is respected, so the gate passes, but the actor is slightly demoted to scenery.

story: An Open Mouth hangs above, lets go of a Wishbone; it snaps as it falls, and both halves land in your waiting palms below. The Mouth keeps nothing back — that is GIVE.
reading_story: Goh the birthday clown empties his entire prize sack into one small kid's arms, then strolls off grinning: "GIVE till the sack is empty."
issues: PASS - Gate 1 (component coverage): both supplied actors named verbatim - 'Open Mouth' (口) and 'Wishbone' (ハ); components_used [口, ハ] matches the record exactly.

PASS - Gate 2 (no phantom components): no un-supplied kanji part is named. 'your waiting palms' is a second-person recipient/scenery, consistent with corpus precedent for non-component scenery (e.g. 'Kneeling scribes' in n1-mnemonics.json:709, 'the empty desert' in :8174).

PASS - Gate 5 (actor consistency / no invented cognition): 'a turkey wishbone caught mid-snap, its two legs splitting apart' (n5-component-actors.json:19) is honoured by 'it snaps as it falls, and both halves land'. Open Mouth holding and releasing an object is ordinary physical mouth function, and the corpus already grants it agency ('who shouts a marching beat', 沿 at n1-mnemonics.json:5465; 'swallows heap after heap', :8772). No new cognitive faculty invented.

PASS - Gate 3 (reading actor): 'Goh' appears as the agent of the reading_story and matches reading_actor_used; registry entry is name-only (n5-reading-actors.json:533-535), so the ad-hoc 'birthday clown' role is licensed by corpus practice (Goh is variously a latecomer, a star-catcher, a zazen sitter, a go player).
PASS - Gate 4 (meaning lands): keyword is the final word of the story ('that is GIVE.') and meaning_placement='end' is accurate; reading_story also lands GIVE in the closing line.
PASS - Gates 6-7: no etymology claim (the 'Kingdom of Wu' sense is untouched); story is 32 words, reading_story 24 - both under ~40.
PASS - spatial fidelity: 呉 stacks 口 over ハ and the story stages Open Mouth 'above' with the Wishbone falling to the palms 'below'.

CONCERN (distinctiveness, non-blocking watch-item): 誤 (n3-mnemonics.json:4867) already stages this exact actor pair plus a snap - 'The Speech Bubble jams a turkey Wishbone into a wide Open Mouth, yanks its two legs apart - SNAP'. Since 呉 is the 呉 inside 誤, imagery overlap is high; the discriminators are only direction (mouth releases vs mouth receives) and payoff. Direction reversals are a classic confusion source.

CONCERN (distinctiveness): 沿 (n1-mnemonics.json:5465) uses the same two actors in the mirrored vertical arrangement ('Wishbone jogs ... atop Open Mouth'), so the 口/ハ pair now carries three cards distinguished mainly by stacking order.

MINOR (reading): the registry note stresses Goh is the CLIPPED short-vowel twin of Gough (ごう); nothing in 'empties his entire prize sack ... strolls off grinning' encodes shortness - the same non-blocking gap already logged on 碁 (n1-mnemonics.json:6812).
MINOR (coherence): how a disembodied Open Mouth was holding the Wishbone before it 'lets go' is left to inference (lips? teeth?), the weakest visual beat in an otherwise clean image.

story: SORROW: an Open Mouth hangs in the chest of the Hanger Kimono, wailing up from beneath the folded collar, while the wide empty sleeves sway on either side, soaked dark with tears.
reading_story: Ira arrives too late to the funeral, kneels in the doorway, and lets one long cry carry her whole village's SORROW.
issues: Non-gating: reading_story is generic sorrow scenery ('too late to the funeral', 'one long cry') and risks interference with other N1 grief kanji (悲, 嘆, 慟); only the actor name 'Ira' distinguishes it.
Non-gating: 'soaked dark with tears' is stock grief imagery rather than a distinctive hook; a more specific consequence of the wailing on the garment would raise distinctiveness.
Non-gating: the reading_story does not encode the short vowel length of あい in any way, so the 'short' cue rests entirely on the actor persona.

story: TEMPT — the Open Mouth croons at the Sealed Clam-Locket perched on the Wishing-Well Legs: "open up, come away." The stone legs totter toward the voice, stamping a muddy Trailing Footprint below.
reading_story: Sah leans through the door and breathes one bare syllable — "sa" — nothing more; that clipped little sound is somehow enough to TEMPT everyone out of their seats.

story: The Open Mouth gapes on the left; on its right perches the fat Stumpy Sparrow. Of every bird alive, the Open Mouth shouts for this one dumpy bird SOLELY.
reading_story: Yui plays her encore to one lone fan in an empty hall — tonight her guitar sings SOLELY for him.

story: Left, an Open Mouth gapes wide; right, two Suns stack one on the other. Every syllable the Open Mouth booms pushes the stacked Suns blazing higher — a thunderous dawn CHANT.
reading_story: The Showman raises his top hat and the whole circus answers in one CHANT — "Shoooow!" — held long as his sweeping bow.

story: From the right, Cracking Whip snaps the Lone Barn Shutter open; beneath, the Open Mouth bellows every hidden secret into daylight — DISCLOSE.
reading_story: Mid-cabaret, Kayo freezes the spotlight, leans over the footlights, and purrs one scandalous secret she is dying to DISCLOSE — the audience gasps.
issues: Minor (non-gating): reading_story appends a short reaction coda after the keyword ("DISCLOSE — the audience gasps"); keyword still lands as the payoff of the final clause.

story: Perched atop a giant Open Mouth, the Woolly Ram sheds warm fleece straight down into that square hole; the mouth below hums thanks through the wool. Sheer fluffy generosity — utterly VIRTUOUS.
reading_story: Zen sits cross-legged beneath a waterfall, waving away every gift offered him, smiling: "The empty hand is the only VIRTUOUS hand."
issues: Minor (non-blocking, §3.12 coherence): meaning story is about generous giving while reading story is about refusing gifts ('the empty hand') - the two halves pull thematically against each other and could cross-blend at recall.
Minor (§3.9 imageability): closing clause 'Sheer fluffy generosity' is abstract commentary rather than image, and 'hums thanks through the wool' is the least picturable beat.
Minor (§3.10 distinctiveness): 羊 recurs in many kanji (美, 洋, 群, 養, 鮮, 詳), so Woolly-Ram scenes carry interference risk; 'virtuous = generosity' is also a predictable framing.

story: On the left edge of the street stands Open Mouth, a perfect square hole stretching wider and wider until every window shatters from its deafening YELL.
reading_story: Khan rears his horse on the steppe and unleashes a YELL so fierce the grass flattens for miles.
