issues: Advisory (non-blocking): distinctiveness pressure from 口-noise neighbors — 叫 'terrified SHOUT' (n2), 呼 CALL (n3), 鳴 CRY (n3) all use Open Mouth producing loud sound; the solo-mouth staging, window-shatter payoff, and Khan/steppe reading scene are the only separators between YELL and SHOUT.

Minor: in the reading story the keyword YELL is mid-sentence rather than at start/end; it is still the payoff of the sentence, and start/end gating is enforced on the meaning story (meaning_placement=end), so not gated.

story: SCOLD erupts from the square Open Mouth on the left, blasting the stack to its right: Sun blazing overhead, a Swaddling Wrap curling down to bundle a clattering Soup Ladle.
reading_story: The Cutler drops a blade mid-polish; his master's SCOLD cracks across the workshop, and every knife on the rack trembles.
issues: Non-gating (imageability): 'blasting the stack to its right' is layout meta-language, not an image — the reader pictures a kanji slot rather than a scene. Replacing 'the stack' with the actual pile of things would lift the score.
Non-gating (imageability): Sun is inert scenery ('blazing overhead') and never acts on anything; it is the weakest-anchored of the four components.

Non-gating (distinctiveness): Open Mouth + SCOLD is the highest-interference pairing available (competes with 叱/吼/号/呼), and Sun+Wrap+Ladle recurs across the whole 曷 family (渇/掲/褐/謁), so the discriminating element is the generic one.

Non-gating (reading story): the Cutler's clipped/short-vowel かつ quality (per reading_actor note, '-tsu coda', short) is not signalled in the story — a clipped, abrupt beat would reinforce the vowel-length cue the registry encodes.

story: A Lightning Bolt cracks down through the Horizon Line; beneath it an Open Mouth wails, and lowest of all a Hanger Kimono hangs draped in funeral black — MOURNING.
reading_story: Sosa steps up in a black armband, swings for the fences, then rounds the bases in silence — the whole stadium is in MOURNING.
issues: Meaning story is three vertically stacked vignettes linked by theme rather than a single fused action — acceptable, but slightly listy.
Silent-stadium reading story relies on mood (silence) as the mourning cue; the black armband carries it, so it passes.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the sand; beneath it an Open Mouth gapes wide over the flat Horizon Line, and a Falling Katana slices down through the empty air — leaving one long, silver SIGH.
reading_story: Tanner the leatherworker stretches a hide too thin, watches it split open, and lets out one long SIGH.
issues: NON-GATING (imageability drag): the payoff 'leaving one long, silver SIGH' is a metaphor, not a picture — a katana slash cannot literally leave a sigh, so the keyword lands as a word rather than an image. Evidence: story text '...slices down through the empty air — leaving one long, silver SIGH.'

NON-GATING (coherence): the Open Mouth is the natural source of a sigh but is left inert ('gapes wide over the flat Horizon Line') while the sigh is instead attributed to the Falling Katana. The one actor whose nature matches the keyword does no work.

NON-GATING (distinctiveness risk): the ⺾ / 口 / 一 stack recurs across 漢・難・勤・謹, and the scene's first two-thirds ('Grass Tuft crowns the sand; beneath it an Open Mouth ... over the flat Horizon Line') is a generic vertical stack that will read the same in those neighbours; only the katana+sigh close differentiates it.
NON-GATING (spatial fidelity): the story renders a purely top-to-bottom stack, but 嘆 is left/right (口 radical left, 𦰩 right) — the left-hand mouth's position is not staged.

NON-GATING (semantic thinness): meanings include lament/grieve, but the story carries no grief affect; 'silver SIGH' reads aesthetic rather than sorrowful. The reading_story ('stretches a hide too thin, watches it split open') carries the disappointment better than the meaning story does.

story: APPLAUD — the Fortune Slip whips high on its shrine branch, lucky brushstroke flashing, its stiff paper cracking again and again in the gale: a one-slip ovation that will not quiet.
reading_story: Carr the cabbie brakes at the shrine gate, slaps his taxi roof — "ka!" — one short, clipped APPLAUD, then speeds off.
issues: Minor: the 'gale' is unmotivated scenery introduced solely to make the slip snap — not a phantom component (it is not a kanji element), but the scene would be tighter if the wind were tied to the shrine setting rather than appearing mid-clause.
Minor: 'lucky brushstroke flashing' compresses the actor image's 'GOOD' brushwork to the point of near-abstraction; naming the brushed 'GOOD' would anchor the 吉 actor more firmly.
Minor: APPLAUD appears in caps in both the story (start) and the reading story; harmless reinforcement, but slightly dilutes the keyword-as-payoff placement signal.
Note: phonetic_extra 加 is unused. Not a gate failure (it carries no actor and the authored corpus does not require it), but the story offers no hook explaining the か reading beyond Carr himself.

story: Four Open Mouths gape at the corners of the table; the Starfish sprawled in the middle stretches one arm into each, scooping and scrubbing them clean — a living UTENSIL.
reading_story: Key jimmies open the locked kitchen drawer — inside, every UTENSIL is chained down, each spoon and fork wearing its own tiny padlock.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in reading_story the keyword UTENSIL sits mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable because the closing image (padlocked spoons and forks) is itself the utensil payoff, but an end-positioned keyword would be cleaner.
Minor: meaning story stacks two actions ('scooping and scrubbing') — one verb would sharpen the single snapshot rubric item 7/9 favors.

story: At the Plus-Sign Crossroads a Grass Tuft splits the tarmac; beneath it a buried Cowrie Shell rattles with rising pressure. Beside them, the Open Mouth blasts everything — shell, grass, asphalt — skyward: ERUPT.
reading_story: Fonda, deadpan on set, lights his cigarette on a geyser just as it ERUPTS — hat gone, face soaked, expression unchanged.
issues: Minor: in the reading story the keyword ERUPTS is mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable because the trailing clause (hat gone, face soaked) is the eruption's direct aftermath, keeping it the payoff.
Minor: causal geometry is slightly fuzzy — the Open Mouth is 'beside them' yet blasts the buried shell skyward; consider making the mouth the vent the debris erupts through.
Interference watch: buried Cowrie Shell under the crossroads may echo future 賁-family stories (e.g. 墳 tomb mound); the 口 mouth-blast differentiator should be kept central in those siblings too.

story: The Walled Box seals a scroll inside its gateless walls; the trapped paper unrolls, coiling round and round until it packs the whole enclosure into one enormous paper SPHERE.
reading_story: Ken pounds his little plastic fists on the glass of a snow globe, sealed inside his glittering SPHERE.
issues: Minor coherence wobble in main story: the scroll 'unrolls' then 'coils round and round' — the two motions slightly contradict, costing a point of imageability (not gate-failing).

story: A Mound of Soil sits stacked squarely atop a second Mound of Soil, their sprout-markers aligned; pressed into the upper heap's peak, catching the sun, gleams one perfect SQUARE JEWEL.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer spins under the spotlight, a SQUARE JEWEL blazing on her headdress, throwing sharp green flashes across every table.
issues: Static scene: the only verbs are 'sits', 'gleams', 'catching' — no action drives the image, which caps memorability. A single motion (the jewel being pressed in, or light sweeping) would lift imageability.

Minor cross-story inconsistency: the main story has the jewel 'catching the sun' with no colour, while the reading_story has it throwing 'sharp green flashes'. Colour should be fixed in the meaning story or dropped from the reading story.

Distinctiveness risk: 'gem resting on soil' is a generic frame that could interfere with other 土-only N1 glyphs; the stacking is the sole differentiator and is stated fairly quietly ('stacked squarely atop').

story: TWO-MAT AREA: two tatami mats lie edge-to-edge on ground so flat a dropped marble won't roll, while a Mound of Soil squats just off their left edge, sprout-marker leaning over the straw.
reading_story: President Hayes chalks a TWO-MAT AREA on the White House ballroom floor, then reclines inside it for a long, leisurely nap, top hat tipped over his eyes.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the Mound of Soil is inert -- it 'squats just off their left edge' and never acts on the mats. Only the sprout-marker leaning over the straw links the two components; a mound actively spilling onto or crumbling at the mat edge would bind 土 to the scene more tightly.

Non-blocking (interference risk): 'so flat a dropped marble won't roll' is a portable 平 device that will likely be reused verbatim on other 平-containing kanji, which is exactly the neighbor-interference rubric item 10 warns about. Worth tracking for uniqueness across the 平 family.

Minor: the two tatami mats carry the keyword rather than any component, so the keyword and the 平 concept both occupy the same flat-ground region of the image; the mats are doing the semantic work while 'flat' is only an adjective on the surface beneath them.

story: DROOP — the Drooping Willow lets its fronds fall in matched pairs, straight as plumb-lines, curtaining the low earthen mound at its foot; not one strand lifts, even in wind.
reading_story: Swee ducks beneath the fronds and whistles one short, clipped note; the heavy strands slide off his shoulders and hang lower still — DROOP.
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage): components[] is empty and phonetic_extra is 垂 itself; the story runs on 垂's own registered persona, so nothing mandatory is left unnamed.

PASS gate 2 (no phantom components): 'Drooping Willow', the 'fronds' and the 'low earthen mound' are not invented — data/authored/n2-component-actors.json:123-125 registers component 垂 as actor 'Drooping Willow' with image 'A weeping willow whose long fronds hang straight down in drooping symmetrical pairs over a low earthen mound'. 'plumb-lines' is a simile for how the strands hang, not a claimed sub-part.

PASS gate 3 (reading actor): 'Swee' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor_used; 'one short, clipped note' correctly encodes the short/clipped vowel per data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json:837-841 and docs/07 §1.2. Male pronoun ('his shoulders') matches the corpus majority for Swee (n1-mnemonics.json:3557, 6329, 7756).
PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): keyword 'DROOP —' opens the story and closes the reading_story; meaning_placement 'start' matches. docs/07 §2 permits start or end.

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): candidate phrasing tracks the registry image nearly clause-for-clause (fronds hanging in matched pairs, over the low earthen mound) and is consistent with the same actor's use in 郵 at data/authored/n2-mnemonics.json:5559.
PASS gate 6 (no etymology): purely imaginative scene; no historical/derivational claim.
PASS gate 7 (length & focus): story 29 words, reading_story 24 words — both well under ~40, single sustained image.

NON-GATING DISTINCTIVENESS RISK: 柳 (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:4405) already runs on 'trailing long drooping branches… the strands sag lower… a weeping WILLOW'. A drooping willow with sagging strands is therefore the core image of two different N1 cards (垂 = droop, 柳 = willow), a genuine neighbour-interference channel. Inherited from the registry choice rather than invented here; the differentiators offered ('straight as plumb-lines', 'not one strand lifts, even in wind') are the only things separating them.

NON-GATING TAUTOLOGY: the actor name literally contains the keyword ('Drooping Willow' → DROOP), so the story is close to circular — it tells the learner droop means droop. Registry-imposed, not a candidate defect, but it caps how much retrieval work the scene actually does.

NON-GATING DATA NOTE: dominant_reading is kun た.れる, yet the supplied reading_actor is on'yomi すい. Per docs/07 §1.3 kun'yomi get no reading actor, so this reading_story teaches すい and leaves た.れる untaught. Input-record mismatch, not a candidate defect — same pattern flagged at data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:6342.

Scale collision: 一's registry image is a miles-away desert horizon and 旦 is a sun on that horizon, yet both are compressed into a 'waist-high HEDGE' with the sun 'beneath' the twigs. Surreal is tolerable but it blurs the scene.

Actor-name interference: 'Horizon Line' and 'Horizon Sunrise' share a root token in the same sentence, so the two right-side components are easy to confuse on recall (and 旦's own image already contains a horizon line).

story: At the palace gate, an elegant Hourglass drains her sand while the Stop Barrier lies lowered flat to her right, halting every carriage until the last grain falls — such waiting is owed only a QUEEN.
reading_story: Hee, the clipped giggler, snorts behind a velvet curtain every time the QUEEN's crown slips — "hee!" — and the whole throne room pretends not to hear.
issues: Non-blocking (imageability): the keyword payoff is an abstract proposition rather than an image -- 'such waiting is owed only a QUEEN' asserts royalty instead of showing it. No queen figure appears in the scene, so the retrieval cue for the meaning is verbal inference rather than something visible. Placing an actual crowned figure stepping past the barrier would strengthen the payoff.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the palace/royalty setting is the default frame for every royalty kanji, creating interference risk with the near-neighbor 姫 (princess, also 女 on the left) and 后 -- especially since this kanji's own meanings list already includes 'Princess'. The Hourglass + level-crossing-barrier pairing is what keeps it above threshold.

Minor (conciseness, §3.13): 'palace gate', 'carriage', 'velvet curtain' and 'throne room' are scenery that adds load without carrying a component; harmless for the phantom-component gate but not free.

story: Left, the Hourglass's bottom bulb bulges round as a belly. Right, the Falling Katana slashes down through the Kings Crown perched on the War Helmet — golden sparks shower the swollen glass: PREGNANCY.
reading_story: Ninn cradles her diary against her rounded belly, writing one glowing page about her PREGNANCY.

story: The Hourglass has almost run out: only a few grains spill rightward from its pinched waist, and each lands as a perfect cut diamond — so rare, so EXQUISITE.
reading_story: Myo lifts one paper-thin porcelain cup to the light, breathing a long "myooo..." of awe — it is simply EXQUISITE.

story: A Hawk Talon plunges from above onto the fragile Hourglass — yet its three hooked claws close around the pinched glass waist feather-soft, not one grain of sand disturbed. GENTLE.
reading_story: Heavy-handed Dah practices being GENTLE: he lowers one thick finger onto a soap bubble — "dah..." he breathes — and it doesn't pop.

story: Jammed sideways into the fire exit's left doorframe, the Hourglass spills sand across the threshold until the packed grey drift wedges the door shut — glass and grit OBSTRUCT every escape.
reading_story: Bowie, mid-song, plants his glittered boot against the stage door to OBSTRUCT the roadies hauling his piano away.
issues: Minor persona friction: the registry Hourglass is a sealed 'elegant glass hourglass', but the story has it spilling sand onto the threshold, which implies it cracked. Ordinary physical consequence of being jammed sideways, so it does not fail gate 5, but 'glass and grit' is doing quiet work to license it.

Distinctiveness risk: 'something blocks a door' is the default image for the whole N1 obstruct cluster (阻, 遮, 塞, 邪). Only the sand-drift mechanism separates this one; if sibling kanji reuse door-blocking, interference is likely.

Scenery density borders on gate 7's 'no extraneous detail': 'fire exit', 'left doorframe', 'threshold', 'door' are four near-synonymous props in one 30-word story. Learners may mis-encode 'door' as a component even though it is not claimed as one.

reading_story is competent but low-yield for the ぼう hook: it repeats the same door-blocking beat as the meaning story rather than giving ぼう an independent scene, so the two stories cue each other instead of cueing reading vs meaning separately.

story: PRINCESS — the Hourglass stands on the left, sand streaming through its pinched waist, while on its right a retainer kneels low, forehead to the floor, bowing to the glass as royalty.
reading_story: A brass Key turns once in the tower lock, one clipped click, and the PRINCESS steps out into the light.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): 臣 has no assigned actor, so it is carried only by the generic noun 'retainer'. 臣 recurs in 臨/蔵/監/臥 etc., and 女→Hourglass is one of the highest-frequency actors in the set; the entire discriminating load therefore rests on the single pose ('kneels low, forehead to the floor'). If later 臣 cards also use a generic kneeling/bowing retainer, interference is likely. Consider a dedicated 臣 actor.

Non-blocking (persona thinness, not a gate failure): reading_actor 'Key' is defined in the registry as 'the clipped locksmith' (a person), but the reading_story uses it as a literal brass key in a lock. The short-vowel cue is encoded well ('turns once', 'one clipped click'), and Key/locksmith are not contradictory, so gate 5 passes — but the locksmith persona itself does not appear.
Minor: the combined story + reading_story runs 55 words (31 + 24). Each field is individually under the ~40-word cap, so gate 7 passes on the per-field reading, but the pair is not short.

story: The Hourglass stands alone on a low pedestal, sand streaming from top bulb to bottom, cinching its pinched glass waist — every falling grain sculpting that perfect FIGURE.
reading_story: At dusk the Sheriff freezes: a lone FIGURE stands silhouetted at the far end of the dusty street.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword FIGURE sits mid-clause ("a lone FIGURE stands silhouetted at the far end of the dusty street") rather than as the terminal payoff word; still reads as the payoff, so not a gate failure.
Minor: the main story is static — the only motion is falling sand — which slightly caps imageability.

story: Under the Rock Overhang, a Falling Katana slashes down on the left and the Barbed Pike looms in from the right; between them the Hourglass rattles, sand streaming double-speed — this is how you INTIMIDATE.
reading_story: Eaton barks one clipped "ee!" and the whole boardroom freezes — nobody can INTIMIDATE like Eaton.

story: On the left shelf the elegant Hourglass tilts, its lower bulb swollen round as sand streams in, the glass belly bulging heavier every second — unmistakably WITH CHILD.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender slides a mocktail across the bar, winking: no gin tonight, this customer is WITH CHILD.
issues: Minor: 'the glass belly bulging heavier every second' is physically impossible for rigid glass — read as perceptual exaggeration of the filling lower bulb, so it passes the actor-nature gate, but a phrasing like 'looking swollen' would be cleaner.

Interference risk: 妊 (the other half of 妊женство/妊娠) is also 女-left with pregnancy semantics; a Hourglass + swollen-belly scene is the obvious route for both. Recommend the registry keep 妊's story on a distinctly different prop so the two do not blur.
The phonetic 辰 is unused (it is not mandatory), so しん is carried solely by Shinn — acceptable, but no redundant phonetic anchor.
Combined word count across both fields is 46; each field is individually within the ~40 limit, which is how the §3 length gate reads.

story: Left of the shoreline the giant Hourglass topples over, its pinched waist jetting glittering sand out into a slide, a sandcastle, a volleyball pit — instant RECREATION.
reading_story: Goh cannonballs off the pier, shouting that RECREATION beats work, soaking everyone on the sand.
issues: Minor (non-blocking, spatial fidelity): "Left of the shoreline" anchors the left-position cue to scenery rather than to the glyph's other half (呉 has no actor supplied), so the positional hint reads as filler rather than as structure. Dropping it or rewording to "On the left of the beach" would be cleaner.
Minor (distinctiveness risk): sand is the Hourglass actor's most predictable emission, so sand-based scenes will recur across other 女 kanji; the beach-play payoff is what keeps this one separable.

story: On the left a mirror-polished Hourglass blazes under the stage lights. Right: a Hawk Talon hooks the velvet curtain, a Falling Katana slices its last cord, and a Rubber Glove below catches the dropping cloth — unveiling a BEAUTIFUL WOMAN.
reading_story: At Maranello, Enzo drapes a red racing jacket over the shoulders of the BEAUTIFUL WOMAN who just lapped his test track faster than any driver.
issues: Imageability drag: the Hourglass (女, the meaning-bearing component) has no action — it only 'blazes under the stage lights', a static, near-abstract verb for a glass object, and it is spatially detached from the curtain business happening on the right. The weakest-depicted actor is the most important one.

Persona drift on 女: 'mirror-polished' is the sole descriptor and it fights the registry image ('elegant glass hourglass with a pinched waist, sand streaming'). A mirror is silvered/opaque, glass is transparent. Not a gate failure (ordinary physical description, no invented ability) but the pinched-waist/streaming-sand signature that makes this actor recognizable is absent.

Doubled woman-image: the Hourglass IS the woman radical, yet a separate BEAUTIFUL WOMAN is unveiled behind the curtain. Two female-coded entities in one scene risks the learner re-deriving a second 女 at recall.

Distinctiveness ceiling (rubric item 10, interference): 'curtain drops to reveal a beautiful woman' is the stock showbiz trope for exactly this keyword and will collide with other 女-family kanji (姫, 娘, 婦) if they draw similar reveal scenes. The distinctiveness that exists comes from the component actors, which are fixed anyway, not from the scene concept.

Conciseness: three simultaneous curtain actions (hook, slice, catch) plus a reveal plus the detached left-hand tableau at exactly the 40-word ceiling. 'velvet', 'last', 'stage lights' are the trimmable filler if a retry is wanted.

Phantom-adjacent props: the velvet curtain and its cord carry real structural work in the scene and are named alongside the actors. Passes rubric line 91 as scenery rather than a component-persona, but the curtain is memorable enough that a learner could mis-file it as a fifth component.

story: An Hourglass stands at the left, sand streaming down like a veil; to its right a Thatched House caps a Muddy Boar wallowing beneath the eaves, his snorting welcome to the BRIDE.
reading_story: Carr the cabbie idles at the curb, meter ticking, while the BRIDE bundles her enormous veil into his back seat.
issues: Spatial staging is glyph-position narration ('stands at the left', 'to its right') rather than physical interaction; the Hourglass never engages the rest of the scene, weakening spatial fidelity.
The BRIDE is addressed off-stage rather than depicted, so the keyword payoff is thin; the sand-as-veil simile is the only element binding the Hourglass to 'bride'.
'Thatched House caps a Muddy Boar beneath the eaves' is the generic 家 unit and will recur across 家/稼/嫁, leaving the Hourglass/veil as the sole discriminator against neighbours.

story: Left of the Twin Pillars, the Hourglass recoils: Rake Hand claws across their shared ledge, a Lightning Bolt cracks straight down between them, and the Wishbone snaps at their base — every grain of sand freezes in DISLIKE.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll poses on the toy-shop shelf, flashing his molded smile; every child wrinkles their nose and turns away — pure DISLIKE.
issues: Minor (non-gating): four simultaneous actions (clawing, lightning, snapping, freezing) make the tableau dense; still resolves to one freeze-frame, but a single dominant action would lower cognitive load.

story: ORPHAN: a Swaddle Basket left alone on the orphanage doorstep at midnight, rocking itself, its swaddled bundle wailing — and no one comes to the door.
reading_story: Coco kneels beside the ORPHAN, ties a tiny black bow on its swaddling, and whispers: "Elegance, darling — even when no one comes for you."
issues: Minor (non-gating): aloneness conveyed partly by negation ('no one comes to the door'), less imageable than a positive cue — same weakness accepted on shipped 独.
Minor (non-gating): reading_story places ORPHAN mid-clause ('kneels beside the ORPHAN, ties...') rather than as the final payoff; meaning story carries correct start placement.
Note: phonetic_extra 瓜 unused — permissible, reading is carried by Coco; no phantom introduced in its place.

story: Under one Thatched House roof, the Falling Katana slashes down across the Horizon Line, and the Sealed Clam-Locket still huddles beneath with room to spare — that roof is impossibly WIDE.
reading_story: Coe rounds the final bend and the track fans WIDE — eight lanes become eighty — Coe sprinting alone across the vast openness.
issues: Non-gating: interference risk with 広 (wide, also 厶 + roof-shape, also read こう) and 弘 (こう, contains 厶) — the katana-slashing-across-the-horizon beat is the load-bearing differentiator and should be preserved in any edit.

Non-gating: in the reading_story the keyword WIDE lands mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable since the meaning story carries the placement gate and the reading story still closes on 'vast openness'.

story: Under the Thatched House's peaked roof, robed villagers show a sacred relic, lifting it high in candle-glow while everyone kneels — this solemn show sheltered by the Thatched House is RELIGION.
reading_story: A cobbler nails a giant Shoe above the chapel door; pilgrims kiss its leather toe each dawn — worship of the Shoe became their RELIGION.
issues: Non-blocking: meaning story leans on stock worship imagery (robed villagers, candles, kneeling); distinctiveness is carried by the 'show sheltered by the Thatched House' anchor rather than the props.

story: A tornado wrenches the Thatched House off its foundations; it hangs frozen high above the empty field, straw trailing from its eaves, shadow circling far below — the whole cottage stuck in MID-AIR.
reading_story: Chewbacca leaps for his ship's ramp, misses, and hangs howling in MID-AIR, furry legs pedaling over empty sky.

story: Under the Thatched House's sloping eaves sits a Stacked Shelf Crate, its three shelves crammed with wrapped farewell gifts for the departing neighbours — a whole crate of BEST REGARDS.
reading_story: Gee doffs his cap at the gate, grinning, and calls BEST REGARDS after the loaded cart rolling away.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): the reading story reuses a farewell-to-a-departing-vehicle beat already carried by Gee in 欺 — data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json: 'Gee shakes your hand warmly, palms your wallet, then waves cheerfully from the departing train — pure DECEIT.' Here it is 'calls BEST REGARDS after the loaded cart rolling away.' Same actor, same departure-wave frame; mild interference between the two Gee cards.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): the opening formula is near-identical to several shipped 宀 cards — 宮 'Beneath the Thatched House's sloping eaves', 官 'Under the Thatched House's sloping eaves', 宿 'Under the Thatched House's sloping roof'. Only the 且 crate and the gift payoff differentiate it.

Checked and NOT a violation — phantom components: 'wrapped farewell gifts', 'departing neighbours', 'the gate', 'the loaded cart' are narrative props, not named component actors. Precedent for props is well established in shipped content (宗 'robed villagers', 審 'farmers', 査 'The detective', 宝 'a velvet cushion').

Checked and NOT a violation — actor consistency: 'sloping eaves' matches the 宀 image ('two eaves sloping down'); 'its three shelves' matches the 且 image ('three horizontal shelves'). Spatial layout (宀 above, 且 beneath) is honored by 'Under ... sits'.

Checked and NOT a violation — length: story 29 words, reading story 17 words, both under the ~40-word cap (§3 item 7). Keyword lands at the end of the story as declared by meaning_placement. Reading actor 'Gee' is present, with no persona conflict — the registry entry (data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json) defines only the name and 'voiced/heavier twin of Key (き). Short.', and shipped Gee cards vary freely (inspects, bangs a gavel, squints). No etymology claim; no invented cognitive ability (the crate only 'sits' and holds).

story: Beneath the Thatched House's peaked roof, a Horizon Line hangs like a banner rail; under it the Horizon Sunrise bursts through the doorway, gilding every wall — dawn itself rising to PROCLAIM.
reading_story: On the podium, Senna seizes the microphone from the announcer to PROCLAIM his own victory, champagne spraying over the crowd.
issues: Minor: 'dawn itself rising to PROCLAIM' is a slightly abstract payoff — no audience or spoken act; a concrete proclamation beat would image harder.
Minor: the Horizon Sunrise 'bursts through the doorway' while the scene is staged beneath the roof — slight inside/outside tension, though it reads as ordinary light-motion, not a persona violation.

story: Beneath the Thatched House's sloping eaves, a giant spine stands bolted upright, vertebra stacked on vertebra as the sacred pillar; pilgrims clap twice and bow to the bones — the SHINTO SHRINE.
reading_story: Governor Cuomo bows stiffly at the SHINTO SHRINE, tossing a coin and clapping twice, praying for one more term.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in the reading_story the keyword SHINTO SHRINE sits mid-clause rather than at the very start or end, though it directly follows the reading actor.

story: The MANAGER inspects the Thatched House kitchen beneath its low thatch, jabbing the Chili Needle into every bowl before it leaves — no stinging, eye-watering jolt, and the whole batch goes back.
reading_story: Cy Young stalls on the mound at ninety pitches; the MANAGER climbs the dugout steps, palm out, and takes the ball from Cy without a word.
issues: Minor (non-blocking) coherence: the final clause of the meaning story drops its conditional — 'no stinging, eye-watering jolt, and the whole batch goes back' should read 'if there's no stinging, eye-watering jolt, the whole batch goes back' to parse on first read.

story: Beneath the Thatched House's peaked thatch, a blazing Sun hangs low, roasting the whole table; at floor level an Hourglass streams golden sand over the platters — a glittering, gritty BANQUET.
reading_story: Enzo parks his red convertible right in the hall, engine revving while waiters set trays along its hood — the loudest BANQUET Modena ever hosted.
issues: Minor spatial nit: an Hourglass 'at floor level' streaming sand 'over the platters' on a table implies an oversized hourglass; the reader must infer scale. Non-blocking.
Reading story's keyword placement is mid-clause ('the loudest BANQUET Modena ever hosted') rather than terminal; gate 4 is satisfied by the meaning story, so this is cosmetic only.

story: Rain drums the Thatched House. Inside, one uncle eats alone at a table laid for twelve, his spoon scraping the only sound in the world. LONELINESS.
reading_story: Jacker breaks into the cottage expecting treasure, finds one uncle and twelve cold plates, and slips away carrying only LONELINESS.
issues: Distinctiveness risk: 'one person eating alone at a table laid for many' is the single most stock image for loneliness, so it could interfere with neighbouring lonely/quiet kanji (孤, 独, 淋, 静) if any of them later draw a similar scene. The 'table laid for twelve' count is the main thing keeping it separable — worth reserving that specific hook for 寂.

The 叔 slot is carried by the bare keyword 'uncle', a faceless generic figure next to corpus-standard vivid actors (Muddy Boar, Chili Needle, Stacked Shelf Crate). It is compliant since 'uncle' is the supplied kanji_keyword, but the imagery load falls almost entirely on the props rather than on the component itself.

Combined length across both fields is 46 words. Read per-field (the corpus convention, where story and reading_story are counted separately) this passes gate 7 comfortably; flagged only in case the ~40-word cap is ever applied to the pair.

story: A Thatched House drops like a lid over the Mountain Peak; the one certain thing hidden between roof and summit is buried in SECRECY.
reading_story: Mitter seals his lips with wax; interrogators pry for hours, but Mitter's SECRECY never cracks.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'the one certain thing' is abstract and unpicturable — unavoidable since 必 has no actor persona, but it weakens the central hidden object of the scene.
Minor (non-blocking): 'house conceals X' is a frequent 宀 pattern; the mountain-capping scale inversion mitigates but does not eliminate neighbor-interference risk with other 宀 kanji.

story: A Thatched House lets a Grass Tuft sprout beneath its roof and a Periscope shove up from below, lens swiveling among the blades — it shelters both intruders without complaint, endlessly TOLERANT.
reading_story: Genghis Khan storms the surrendered village, raises his sword — then sheathes it and pardons everyone. The dreaded Khan, unexpectedly TOLERANT.

story: TRANQUILITY: inside the Thatched House, a warm heart drifts down onto the Fishing Net, which settles flat along the Horizon Line, where a lone Meat Hook hangs beneath, barb pointing up, swaying to stillness.
reading_story: Nay whispers "nay" to every clanging alarm bell in the village, and the whole valley sinks into TRANQUILITY.
issues: PASS coverage: all five mandatory components named — 宀 'Thatched House', 心 'heart', 罒 'Fishing Net', 一 'Horizon Line', 亅 'Meat Hook'.
PASS no phantoms: only 'warm' and 'lone' are added, both plain adjectives, no extra objects introduced in the story.

PASS actor consistency: 'barb pointing up' matches the Meat Hook image verbatim; the net 'settles flat' matches 'stretched flat… cast down'; 'inside the Thatched House' matches 'shelter everything beneath it'; no invented cognitive ability.
PASS reading actor: 'Nay' present in reading_story and its pun ('whispers "nay"') carries ねい.
PASS meaning placement: TRANQUILITY at position 1, matching meaning_placement='start'.
PASS length: story is 34 words, under the ~40 cap; no etymology framing.
STRENGTH spatial fidelity: story order House → heart → Net → Horizon Line → Hook mirrors the actual top-to-bottom stacking of 寧.

WEAK imageability (3): verbs are all soft and passive — 'drifts', 'settles', 'sways to stillness' — nothing collides, nothing is absurd, so there is no hook to snag recall. A desert Horizon Line sitting inside a cottage interior is also hard to picture as one coherent scene.

WEAK distinctiveness (3): 'calm/quiet/stillness inside a house with a heart' is the generic frame every 宀+心 card will reach for; only the Meat Hook keeps this from blurring with neighbors. The reading_story is the stronger half.
MINOR: reading_story ends on TRANQUILITY too, so the keyword fires twice — acceptable, but the meaning payoff is slightly diluted by repetition.

story: Under the peaked roof of the Thatched House, farmers shuffle forward one turn at a time, each kneeling on the packed earth to plead their case before the JUDGE.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender raps his cocktail shaker on the bar like a gavel: in every last-call dispute, Shinn is the JUDGE.

story: Under the Thatched House's peak, Sand Trickle pours across a blazing Sun; beneath them Twin Pillars balance on a Stepladder — the whole cramped stack is a student DORMITORY.
reading_story: Ryo the hardboiled detective kicks open every door in the DORMITORY, trench coat dripping, hunting the roommate who never signed the register.
issues: Non-blocking (imageability): the keyword is asserted, not depicted — 'the whole cramped stack is a student DORMITORY' labels the scene instead of showing anything dormitory-like (bunks, roommates, a corridor of doors). The reading story does this better than the meaning story.
Non-blocking (distinctiveness): 'Under the Thatched House's peak…' is the generic 宀 opener and will be shared with many other N1 宀 kanji; interference risk sits in the framing, not the interior.

Non-blocking (focus): the story is a static top-to-bottom inventory joined by 'beneath them' rather than a single striking event — borderline against §2's 'one vivid image' guidance, though under the ~40-word cap at 28 words.
Minor (actor plausibility): heavy stone Twin Pillars 'balance on a Stepladder' is physically odd — striking, but a reader may stall on it. Ordinary placement, so not a persona violation.

story: The Tape Measure snaps out one quivering inch above the workbench, its metal tongue trembling like a struck tuning fork — the smallest possible MEASUREMENT.
reading_story: Sunn squints at the sundial's shadow, marking one thin inch of dark across the stone — his daily MEASUREMENT of how far summer has slipped.
issues: Reading story buries the keyword: 'his daily MEASUREMENT of how far summer has slipped' leaves six words trailing after the payoff. Gate 4 is satisfied by the main story (meaning_placement 'end' is accurate), but the reading story would read stronger ending on the keyword.

Near-tautological premise: the component actor ('Tape Measure') and the keyword ('measurement') are the same concept, so the story restates the definition rather than supplying an independent retrieval hook. Largely inherited from the registry actor choice for 寸, and partly offset by the 'one quivering inch / smallest possible' specificity.

Mild redundancy against gate 7's 'no extraneous detail': 'one quivering inch' and 'its metal tongue trembling' encode the same motion twice, and the 'struck tuning fork' simile spends four words on a second object.
Story drops the registry image's most distinctive visual attribute, 'A yellow retractable tape measure' — the colour cue is free imageability that went unused.

story: Profile-left, the Expectant Torso's bulging belly bends back like a drawn bowstring; at its right the yellow Tape Measure's tongue snaps out one quivering inch and whips forward — belly bow, tape arrow: SHOOT.
reading_story: Shaq rears back at the free-throw line, elbow cocked like a bow, and lets the ball SHOOT off his fingertips straight through the net.
issues: Gate 2 (no phantom components, §3.2) — borderline pass, flag: the story names a 'bowstring' and an 'arrow'. These survive only because they are appositive re-castings of the supplied actors ('belly bow, tape arrow'), not added entities. Risk is real though: 射 contains neither 弓 nor 矢, and a learner who retains only the punchline 'belly bow, tape arrow' could back-map to the wrong graphemes. Recommend the punchline restate the actors instead (e.g. 'torso bow, tape bolt' -> 'Torso draws, Measure flies').

Imageability (§3.9) — physical mismatch in the central image. The component image defines 身 as 'the belly bowed OUT in one heavy pregnant curve ... the whole body reduced to that outward-bulging line', but the story says the belly 'bends BACK like a drawn bowstring'. A drawn bowstring is pulled toward the archer and is straight-then-V; an outward convex curve maps to the bow's limb/stave, not its string. Reader must reconcile 'bulging' with 'bends back'. Fix: 'the Expectant Torso's belly curves like a bent bow-stave'.

Imageability — competing verbs on 寸: the tongue both 'snaps out one quivering inch' (extension, matches the registry image) and 'whips forward' (flight). Two motions in one clause blur the single frame. One verb would land harder.

Distinctiveness (§3.10) — both halves are the default association for their cue. Bow+arrow is the single most predictable image for 'shoot', and Shaq shooting a basketball is the single most predictable image for Shaq. Interference risk against other archery/projectile kanji in the N1 set (e.g. 撃, 弾) is non-trivial; only the odd pregnant-belly/tape-measure pairing keeps it above threshold.

Reading story (§3.3) passes on actor presence but is generic: 'Shaq shoots a free throw' carries no hook tying it back to 射 specifically, and shares nothing with the meaning story's imagery. Cocking the elbow 'like a bow' already echoes the meaning story — leaning into that link (or into an injection/注射 beat) would raise retrieval value at no word cost.

story: To INQUIRE how deep the chasm goes, Rake Hand claws the left cliff while Open Mouth bellows from the right; the I-Beam Girder spans between them, and a Tape Measure unspools from its center into the fog.
reading_story: Jin leans over that same chasm, microphone in hand, calling down to INQUIRE whether anyone below can still hear the chorus.
issues: Spatial fidelity (graded, non-blocking): 尋 stacks ヨ over 工 with 口 tucked at right and 寸 at the bottom; the story arranges them left/right/between/center, which does not mirror the glyph's top-to-bottom stack. Not a gating failure per docs/07 §3, but it costs a point on item 11.

Distinctiveness risk (graded): Tape Measure (寸) recurs across many N1 kanji (尊, 導, 対...), so the 'measuring instrument at a chasm' frame could interfere with neighbors; the fog/echo-sounding detail is what keeps this one separable.

story: Three Bean Sprouts crown the Goalpost Frame like a laurel; beneath the crossbar an Open Mouth roars up at them, spraying spit across the grass — raw, deafening ESTEEM.
reading_story: The Showman doffs his top hat, bellowing "Shoooow!" as the whole tent bows — nothing earns ESTEEM like a ringmaster's flourish.
issues: Non-blocking: 'roars' is a default/generic action for the Open Mouth actor and likely recurs across other 口 mnemonics, creating mild interference risk.
Non-blocking: the keyword is asserted ('raw, deafening ESTEEM') rather than depicted — the laurel-crown image carries the esteem sense, but the roar itself does not obviously mean esteem.
Non-blocking: 'spraying spit across the grass' is extraneous scenery under gate 7 (focus); it adds sensory salience but no component work.

story: TAKE POSITION! At the capital's right flank, the Lunging Fencer freezes mid-lunge, back leg sweeping wide, mole gleaming on his raised shoulder — the city's champion claims his post.
reading_story: The cobbler nails his Shoe to the palace floor, marking the exact spot where the new minister must TAKE POSITION — step in, and the job is yours.

story: Wind pins a Draped Cloak flat against the convent belfry rail; wedged low inside its folds a Soup Ladle slips loose, clanging down the stairs and waking every sleeping NUN.
reading_story: Knee, the clipped little man, skids across the frozen courtyard, barks one short "ni!" up at the NUN, and is gone before the echo returns.
issues: Minor: 'convent' pre-signals the keyword mid-story, weakening the end-placed NUN payoff as a retrieval target — a neutral tower/stair setting would keep the punch at the end.
Minor spatial tension: the cloak is 'pinned flat' against the rail yet the ladle is 'wedged low inside its folds' — flat and folded are slightly at odds; 'billowing against' would reconcile the two.
Minor interference risk: a wind-blown Draped Cloak is a generic frame likely to repeat across other 尸 kanji in the N1 batch; the clanging ladle is doing most of the distinctiveness work.

story: The Folding Ruler dips its sharp angle to measure the ink one last time: a single Ink Droplet clings beneath its leg, falls, dries — the supply is completely EXHAUSTED.
reading_story: Jin holds his final high note until nothing is left — voice EXHAUSTED, he bows to the silent, stunned crowd.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in the reading_story the keyword 'EXHAUSTED' lands in the closing clause ('voice EXHAUSTED, he bows...') but is not the literal final beat; the meaning story ends cleanly on it, so placement gate passes.

Minor: the Folding Ruler measuring liquid ink (dipstick-style) slightly stretches a length-measuring tool, but it is ordinary physical motion consistent with the actor's measuring nature — not an invented cognitive ability.

Gates 6/7 PASS: no etymology claim; 27 words (story) and 21 words (reading_story), both under the ~40 cap in docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §3.7.

issues: Distinctiveness risk with shipped 弱 (data/authored/n2-mnemonics.json): 'The taut LONGBOW's string has snapped, its arc sagging limp' vs this candidate's 'string slips off... the yew stave eases out of its arc'. Both open on the same event (bow loses its string, arc relaxes). The payoffs diverge (lies flat and two paces longer on grass vs. frost-brittle and WEAK), so it clears the gate, but a learner cueing on 'unstrung bow' could retrieve either.

Reading-story physics is backwards: stamping a boot down on a folding brass telescope would collapse the segments, not make them 'shoot out'. Not a gate failure (ordinary physical action, no invented cognitive ability) but it weakens coherence — a pull or a flick of the wrist would drive the LENGTHEN payoff more cleanly.
'at the left of the lawn' is low-value spatial filler: with only one component there is nothing to position 弓 against, so the left-hand cue costs words without earning imagery.

Minor plausibility stretch: an unstrung longbow retains some curve and gains inches, not 'two full paces'. Acceptable as mnemonic exaggeration, and it is the main thing separating this card from 弱, so it should stay.

story: The Longbow stands at left, string still humming; at right its shot is simple — no shaft, no feathers, just one plain lead ball drilling through the barn door. A BULLET.
reading_story: Dan digs a flattened BULLET out of the target board with his thumbnail and drops it, still hot, into his pocket.
issues: NON-BLOCKING: 単 is carried only as the adjective 'simple' modifying 'shot' rather than as a concrete object or scene element, making it the weakest retrieval hook in the story.
NON-BLOCKING: 'no shaft, no feathers' describes absent objects, which spend ~4 words on low-imageability negative space.
NON-BLOCKING: reading_story shifts venue (target board) from the main story (barn door), a small coherence drift between the two scenes.

story: Under a Pot Lid cap, Twin Pillars stand up straight; beneath them, sheltered by the Rock Overhang, he rakes Comb Streaks through his wet hair — the preening LAD.
reading_story: Heavyweight Glenn hoists the LAD onto his shoulders and parades him around the ring like a trophy.
issues: Minor (non-gating): meaning story splits into two stacked sub-scenes — the Pot-Lid-capped Twin Pillars are stage-setting the lad never interacts with, so it is not one fused image (cost to imageability, not a gate).
Minor (non-gating): hair-combing is the most obvious use of Comb Streaks (彡); watch for interference if a future 彡 kanji also uses a hair-combing scene.
Note: keyword in the reading story appears near the start (word 5), not terminal — acceptable under start-or-end rule.

story: Hawk Talon perches atop the Tree, dipping each claw in pigment; to the right, Comb Streaks rake three wet rainbow stripes down the bark — brilliant COLORING.
reading_story: Cy winds up and hurls a paint-filled baseball; it bursts on the catcher's mitt, splattering the whole stadium with COLORING.

story: CARVE: Comb Streaks rake three biting furrows down the right face of an upright jade seal, white stone-dust spitting from each groove as a family name surfaces in the green.
reading_story: Cho drags her wand across a frozen lake, holding the long "chooo" until the ice splits into her initials — only a witch can CARVE with sound.
issues: Distinctiveness risk — template collision inside the 彡 family: 杉 already reads "Comb Streaks score three diagonal slashes down its right flank; fragrant red sap streams from every cut", and the candidate is the same frame ("rake three biting furrows down the right face … white stone-dust spitting from each groove"), with 彰 ("down the certificate's right margin, Comb Streaks rake three gleaming diagonal lines") and 影 as further neighbours. The jade seal / surfacing family name is what keeps it recoverable; the cut-and-emit template itself is now on its fourth reuse.

Prop collides with unrelated registry actors: n4-component-actors.json defines 卩 as "Wax Stamp — A carved seal-stamp pressed down into a blob of red wax" and 官 as "Wax Seal Press", and n3 defines 黄 as "Jade Pendant Bearer". A "jade seal" therefore echoes three actors for components not in 彫. Not a phantom-component gate failure (no registry actor NAME is used, and the corpus precedent 彰/影 introduces non-actor meaning props like a "certificate" and "scenery"), but it is the weakest choice of prop available.

Reading-story device already spent: 聴 uses "Cho the witch presses her wand-tip to her lips — 'Chooo…' she breathes, long and low". The candidate reuses the literal spelled-out "chooo" + "long" cue. The scene (frozen lake, ice splitting into initials) is genuinely different, so this is duplication of the vowel-length device rather than of the image.

Minor: 彡's registry image is a comb raked through wet hair or paint; here it bites furrows into stone hard enough to spit dust. Allowed under the gate (ordinary physical exaggeration, not an invented cognitive ability) and consistent with 杉/彰 precedent, but the actor is being used as a chisel rather than a comb.

Minor abstraction at the payoff: "a family name surfaces in the green" is passive and slightly under-specified compared with the very concrete dust-and-groove clause preceding it; "CARVE with sound" in the reading story is likewise the one abstract beat, rescued by the concrete ice-splitting image.

story: PATENT granted: down the certificate's right margin, Comb Streaks rake three gleaming diagonal lines, each a touch shorter than the one above, making the invention's design perfectly clear.
reading_story: Under the big top, the Showman flourishes his top hat and unrolls a glittering PATENT for his one-of-a-kind circus trick.

story: A postcard-perfect scenery glows in full sun; along its right edge, Comb Streaks rakes three slanting lines, and every raked groove kills the light, smearing a long dark SHADOW.
reading_story: At sunset Abe cannot outrun his own SHADOW — it stretches long and dark ahead of his every stride.

story: The Forked Footpath branches before the lord standing at its right; he plants one boot on the worn left trail, then the other, and walks until dusk — his JOURNEY begins.
reading_story: Keeper Owen holds the only key; no JOURNEY starts until Owen slides back the bolt, groaning a long "oooh" as the gate swings wide.
issues: Minor ambiguity: 'plants one boot on the worn left trail, then the other' can read as the other boot or the other trail
'walks until dusk' is harmless scenery but consumes word budget without encoding anything
Distinctiveness capped at 3: 'figure walking the footpath' is a common template across 彳-radical stories; the lord actor and JOURNEY payoff carry the differentiation

story: The Forked Footpath swells into a paved war-road, both branches slamming down across hills and villages, flattening everything beneath — the land itself pressed into surrender: SUBJUGATE.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage taps his staff once on that war-road, and two kingdoms kneel — he needs no army to SUBJUGATE.
issues: Minor: the phonetic component 正 is unused, so nothing in the story hooks the せい reading beyond the Sage actor itself.
Minor: 'flattening everything beneath' reads closer to 'flatten/pave' than 'subjugate'; the meaning rests on the 'pressed into surrender' clause, the most abstract phrase in the story.

story: Left of a round garden plot the Forked Footpath splits; right, a Mound of Soil sits crowned by a yellow Rubber Glove whose stretched fingertips reach rim to rim — the plot's DIAMETER.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer snaps her feather fan open across the stage circle, its ribs stretching exactly the spotlight's DIAMETER.
issues: Spatial incoherence: the Rubber Glove sits atop the Mound of Soil which is placed to the RIGHT of the plot, yet 'stretched fingertips reach rim to rim' requires it to be centered inside the plot. The reader has to mentally relocate the glove to see the payoff.

The 'round garden plot' is a non-component prop inserted into the positional description ('Left of a round garden plot the Forked Footpath splits'), which muddles the 彳 | 圣 left-right staging into a three-object chain. Not a phantom-component gate failure (it is the measured object, not a named actor), but it dilutes spatial fidelity (rubric item 11).
The 又-over-土 stack is rendered correctly ('crowned by'), but nothing in the story marks WHY the glove is up there, so the vertical relation is decorative rather than load-bearing.
'Forked Footpath splits' is near-tautological filler; the footpath contributes nothing to the diameter payoff and could interfere with other 彳 kanji stories.
Reading story is clean and gate-passing (Kayo, cabaret persona, fan ribs spanning the spotlight, DIAMETER terminal) and is the stronger of the two images.

story: Beside the Forked Footpath, a Stepladder stands over a Rice Stalk; the stalk's ripe golden head sinks one rung at a time down the ladder — GRADUALLY.
reading_story: GRADUALLY, Jo lets her cropped hair grow back — a fraction of an inch each morning, measured against a ruler.
issues: Non-blocking spatial-fidelity wobble (rubric §11): 'a Stepladder stands over a Rice Stalk' places the ladder above the stalk, but the head then 'sinks one rung at a time down the ladder' — the reader must silently move the head to the ladder's top for the descent to parse. Rewording to 'a Stepladder leans against a Rice Stalk' or having the head start at the top rung would fix it.

Non-blocking distinctiveness risk: 'descends slowly' is the default generic encoding for 'gradually' and may interfere with neighboring slow/descend kanji; the memorable load is carried almost entirely by the reading story, not the meaning story.
Minor: the mechanism of gradualness (rung-by-rung) is bound to 人 only; 彳 is inert scenery contributing nothing to the payoff.

story: Beside the Forked Footpath stand the Twin Pillars; wedged beneath their shared ledge, the Fabric Roll unspools its strip along whichever way the trail bends, hugging every turn — cloth made to OBEY.
reading_story: Juno strides ahead, and her fan-tailed peacocks fall into single file behind her — everything must OBEY the queen.
issues: Minor: cloth 'hugging every turn' while the roll stays wedged under the ledge requires a beat to visualize (non-blocking)
Minor: peacocks in reading_story are an embellishment beyond the registry note, though consistent with the Juno persona (non-blocking)

story: The Forked Footpath skirts a tiny Mountain Peak; from the right a Cracking Whip snaps, and the miniature summit's snowcap shivers off in single flakes — so DELICATE.
reading_story: A Bee alights on the tiny summit's snow without denting a single flake, humming: even my wings are not this DELICATE.
issues: Advisory (non-gating): 徴 (N1) shares 彳+山+攵 — ensure its mnemonic scene diverges clearly from this whip-snaps-snowflakes image to avoid neighbor interference.

story: Along the Forked Footpath at the Plus-Sign Crossroads, the Fishing Net hangs slung as a hammock, gently rocking a sleeping heart; every passerby lowers their voice, hushed by cradled VIRTUE.
reading_story: Toker stubs out his joint to help an old woman across the street; she pats his cheek, beaming — even Toker glows with VIRTUE.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): keyword payoff 'hushed by cradled VIRTUE' is an ambient mood rather than a pictured action, slightly softening the meaning landing
Minor (non-blocking): Fishing Net is repurposed as a hammock rather than its registry image of a flat cast net — physically plausible, so not an actor-consistency violation

story: On the Forked Footpath you halt: a Mountain Peak balances atop a Kings Crown, and from the right a Cracking Whip raps the summit — crack, crack — drumming out an unmistakable SIGN.
reading_story: Cho hovers on her broom, wand streaming long trails of sparks; they hang in the night sky as a glowing SIGN for the whole school.

story: PENETRATE — beside the Forked Footpath stands the son you bring up; from the right the Cracking Whip snaps, and he bores headfirst through both branching trails, penetrating clean out the far end.
reading_story: Tetsuo raises one glowing hand and lets his psychic blast PENETRATE Neo-Tokyo's stadium wall, boring a tunnel straight through.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'bores headfirst through both branching trails' is spatially fuzzy — trails are surfaces you travel along, so penetrating 'clean out the far end' of them is harder to picture than boring through a solid obstacle; the reading story's stadium-wall tunnel carries the crisp image.

story: Lowered flat across the road, the Stop Barrier pins a raw red heart to the gravel beneath it. The trapped heart thuds against the striped bar, blackening with ABHOR.
reading_story: Key, the clipped locksmith, turns his single "kee" in the lock and shudders — he has come to ABHOR the door he must seal every year.
issues: Non-gating: in reading_story the keyword ABHOR is buried mid-clause (word 18 of 25) rather than at start/end; rubric item 4 is satisfied via `story` (meaning_placement: end), but the reading story would land harder if it closed on ABHOR.
Non-gating: 'blackening with ABHOR' is the one abstract beat in an otherwise concrete scene — a physical consequence (heart going black-veined, splitting, curdling) would raise concreteness slightly.
Note only, not a violation: 'the door he must seal every year' leans on the Death Anniversary sense; this is a listed meaning, not an etymology claim, so gate 6 passes.

story: A blade hangs point-down above your bare heart, tip grazing the skin. The heart keeps thudding steadily against the cold steel, beat after beat, never breaking rhythm. ENDURE.
reading_story: Ninn writes all night by guttering candlelight, ink freezing, fingers numb — she will ENDURE until the final page is filled.
issues: Non-blocking coherence slip: the blade only 'grazes the skin' yet the heart thuds 'against the cold steel' — anatomically the heart is inside the chest, so the contact is implied rather than staged. A learner may briefly stumble on the geometry.

story: Down at the bottom of your chest, your heart strains upward against your ribs, pounding in one fixed direction like a compass needle — that single unwavering pull is INTENTION.
reading_story: The Sheriff rides into town at dawn, hand hovering over his holster, with one clipped INTENTION: clean this place up.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in the reading story the keyword is followed by a trailing clause ("INTENTION: clean this place up"), slightly softening the payoff, though it is still not buried.
Minor (non-blocking): main-story imagery is partly kinesthetic (internal chest sensation); the compass-needle simile is what carries the visual — keep it if the story is ever edited.

story: Beneath the Cliff Awning a huge heart hangs from the slanted roof. Press it like a doorbell — it thuds back one warm answering beat. That's how you APPLY here.
reading_story: Keeper Owen never opens his gate unless you APPLY: ring his bell and his long "Ooooh!" booms back in answer.
issues: Non-gating: keyword payoff is asserted ('That's how you APPLY here') rather than dramatized as an act of applying
Non-gating: in reading_story the keyword appears mid-sentence, though the placement gate is satisfied by the meaning story's end placement

story: LOYALTY: you kneel and lay your beating heart on the ground beneath you; wherever your master walks, the heart drags itself after him, faithful to its last beat.
reading_story: Chewbacca stands over his wounded friend, roaring, refusing every order to retreat — a Wookiee's LOYALTY is a life-debt he never abandons.

story: NEGLECT: a heart slumped at the very bottom of the frame, grey with dust, cobwebs stringing between its lobes, beating slower and slower because nobody ever came back to tend it.
reading_story: Ty leaves his bat rotting in the rain, glove mildewed in the dugout — a hall-of-famer's total NEGLECT of the gear that made him.
issues: Partial spatial staging: the top element 台 (phonetic_extra) is never staged, so the scene only accounts for the bottom half of the glyph — not a gate failure (phonetic extras are non-mandatory), but the frame reads as heart-only.

Semantic direction is inverted: 怠ける is agentive ('to be lazy / neglect one's duties'), while the story casts the heart as the *object* of neglect ('nobody ever came back to tend it'). The keyword still lands, but the story does not cue the 'shirking' sense carried by the second meaning, Laziness.

Distinctiveness risk against a not-yet-authored neighbour: 惰 (indolence/laziness) is also a 忄/心 kanji in the same semantic field; a generic 'sad neglected heart' image is a prime interference candidate. The cobwebs-between-the-lobes detail is what keeps it separable — that detail is load-bearing and should not be edited out.
Minor anatomical looseness: hearts have chambers/ventricles, not 'lobes' (lungs/liver do). Harmless as an image, slightly off as a description.

story: SUSPICIOUS: at the scene's left edge Twin Candle Wicks flicker; to their right a yellow Rubber Glove lies palm-up atop a fresh Mound of Soil, fingers curled as if something just crawled out.
reading_story: Kai the surfer paddles back early, board unscratched but wetsuit dripping black ooze — the lifeguards trade SUSPICIOUS glances.
issues: Minor: 'something just crawled out' is an unnamed off-screen entity — not a phantom component actor (no persona/image asserted), but it leaves the story's payoff slightly under-imaged.
Minor: the tableau is largely static (flicker + a past-tense crawl); the three actors are arranged rather than interacting, which weakens encoding a little.

story: On their left ledge the Twin Candle Wicks burn unwavering while, across the sand, the Horizon Sunrise lifts each morning toward the Horizon Line ruled above it — CONSTANCY.
reading_story: Coe runs the same dawn lap every day of his life, stride never varying — timekeepers set their watches by his CONSTANCY.
issues: Non-gating: story says the Twin Candle Wicks 'burn unwavering' while the registry image has their flames 'trembling as if the heart beneath them is beating' — a physical-detail drift, not a cognitive contradiction, so it passes the persona gate, but the trembling-heart flavor is lost.

Non-gating: two actors sharing the word 'Horizon' (Horizon Line, Horizon Sunrise) in one scene slightly blurs the single-image ideal; the reader must hold the line ruled ABOVE the sunrise, which is spatially correct for 亘 (一 over 旦) but momentarily counterintuitive since horizons sit below the sun.

Non-gating watch item: the 'Coe runs the same dawn lap' motif is generic for a runner persona — with こう being the most common on-yomi, near-identical Coe-runs-daily stories on other こう kanji could cause reading-story interference.

story: On the narrow ledge at the room's left edge, Twin Candle Wicks gutter black, dripping wax down the wall that hardens into one scorched, unforgiving word: GRUDGE.
reading_story: Conn lifts his glass, smiles at the man who betrayed him thirty years ago, and drinks nothing — still nursing the GRUDGE.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the keyword is delivered as text materializing in wax ('hardens into one scorched, unforgiving word: GRUDGE'). This is a reusable template that would read identically for any other 忄 kanji (悔/憎/悩/慎), so interference risk with heart-radical neighbours is elevated. A grudge-specific physical payoff (wax hardening into a clenched fist, a stain that will not scrub off) would separate 恨 from its neighbours.

Non-blocking (shown vs told): the 'grudge' semantics are carried by the abstract adjective 'unforgiving' rather than by anything visible in the scene. The image itself is a static still-life with no consequential action.
Non-blocking: the phonetic 艮 does no mnemonic work. Correctly omitted per the gates (it is phonetic_extra, not a mandatory component), but nothing in the story anchors こん beyond the reading actor.

Note (not a violation): 'dripping wax' introduces wax, which is not in the actor image (wicks and flames only). Judged as ordinary physical behaviour consistent with a candle wick's nature, not an invented capability.

story: The cause of everything you are presses down from above; the heart beneath cushions it, glowing warmer with every beat, and sends that warmth back up as GRACE.
reading_story: Onslow, crumbs still on his vest, bows his head and rasps out a surprisingly tender GRACE before supper.
issues: Non-blocking: '因' slot is filled by the abstraction 'the cause of everything you are' — no picturable object presses down, so imageability leans entirely on the surrounding physics (pressing, cushioning, glowing); caps imageability at 3.

Non-blocking: 'X presses on the heart beneath' is the stock staging for all top-bottom 心 kanji (思, 念, 忠...); only the cushion-returns-warmth-as-grace mechanism differentiates it; caps distinctiveness at 3.
Minor: reading story keyword GRACE is followed by the two-word tail 'before supper' — still terminal payoff, judged not buried.

story: A Wishbone snaps beneath the Wellhead Grid, its two legs splaying over the dark shaft; far below, a single heart floats on the black water, motionless and REVERENT.
reading_story: Kyo kills the amp mid-howl, drops to one knee at the stage edge, head bowed — the whole pit goes silent and REVERENT.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11) is muddled: 'snaps beneath the Wellhead Grid, its two legs splaying over the dark shaft' places the Wishbone under the crib and simultaneously over the shaft it caps — the two prepositions fight. 'Snaps across the Wellhead Grid' would fix the geometry without cost.

Keyword bond in the meaning story is asserted rather than earned: a heart 'motionless and REVERENT' floating on black water reads as stillness or death, not reverence. The reading story dramatizes REVERENT far better (bowed head, silenced pit); the meaning story leans on the adjective as a label.

Distinctiveness risk: 'a single heart floating in dark water' is a generic 心 treatment likely to recur across other heart-radical N1 kanji (慕, 憂, 慎) and interfere. The Wishbone-over-wellhead pairing is what carries the uniqueness, not the heart.

story: Dangling from the flat Horizon Line, a giant wherefore blazes: WHY such kindness? Below it a warm heart pulses in the sand, no answer required — pure FAVOR.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer stops mid-show, drapes her feather boa around a shivering fan — a FAVOR she stretches out as long as her final note.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 由's concept is rendered as a floating word ('a giant wherefore blazes') rather than a concrete object, slightly reducing concreteness, though the blazing-sign treatment keeps it picturable.

story: Twin Candle Wicks tremble on their narrow left-edge ledge, burning through a night they can never take back; by dawn they are drowned in their own hardened wax tears — pure REGRET.
reading_story: Kai the surfer lets the perfect wave roll past, hesitating one heartbeat too long; he slaps the water, choking on REGRET.

story: On their narrow left ledge the Twin Candle Wicks tremble; from the lower right an Open Mouth gasps, and that rush of breath makes both flames blaze blinding white — ENLIGHTENMENT.
reading_story: Goh sits zazen until dawn; at the first temple-bell toll, Goh's eyes snap open — ENLIGHTENMENT at last.
issues: Minor: reading story trails 'at last' after the keyword — 'ENLIGHTENMENT' is still the payoff at clause end, but exact-end placement would be cleaner.
Minor: a 'gasp' is an inhale, so the 'rush of breath' fanning the flames is slightly physics-muddled; 'exhales'/'shouts' would sharpen the image.
Watch-item: light-burst-as-enlightenment metaphor may mildly interfere with other awakening/light kanji (e.g. 覚); the candle-and-breath mechanic keeps it distinct for now.

story: ECSTASY: Twin Candle Wicks flare along the left edge, while beside them Twin Pillars perch atop an Open Mouth roaring skyward, the whole shrine balanced on Wishing-Well Legs that rock and hop across the floor.
reading_story: Etzler wins the village lottery, flings his hat over the tavern roof, and spins barefoot in the fountain — ECSTASY.
issues: Keyword functions as a header label rather than a payoff: nothing in the meaning story actually enacts ecstasy — 'roaring skyward' and 'rock and hop' are the only weak gestures toward it, so the ECSTASY: prefix is detachable from the image.

'the whole shrine' introduces a collective object not in the component list; it reads as anaphoric shorthand for the pillars/mouth/legs stack so it does not trip the phantom gate, but a stricter phrasing ('the whole stack') would remove the ambiguity.
The reading story (lottery, hat, fountain) shares no imagery with the meaning story, so the two halves do not reinforce each other — Etzler never touches the wicks, pillars, mouth, or legs.
Composition is mostly static stacking ('perch atop', 'balanced on') with little causal interaction between actors, which lowers durability against neighbouring 忄+口 kanji.

story: LAMENT: Twin Candle Wicks gutter at the room's left edge, their wax weeping in long streaks across the table beside them, each drip cooling into a pale, sobbing shape.
reading_story: Tone drops a gravel-voiced elegy over a slow beat; lighters rise, the crowd stops dancing, and the whole smoky club begins to LAMENT.
issues: Non-blocking: 卓 is weakly integrated — 'the table beside them' is passive furniture; the wax pools on it but the table does nothing, so the main discriminator against other 忄 grief kanji (悲/哀/嘆) is thin. Stronger would be the wax weeping *onto* the table so the tabletop itself becomes the mourning surface.
Non-blocking: 'each drip cooling into a pale, sobbing shape' borders on abstraction — 'sobbing shape' is less imageable than the concrete 'wax weeping in long streaks' that precedes it.

story: Under the Barbed Pike's hooked blade, the Open Mouth croons honeyed promises; the heart lying below floats up entranced, straight onto the hidden spur — BEGUILE.
reading_story: Walker treks a thousand miles because one roadside smile managed to BEGUILE him; he circles the same tent all night, boots worn through.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword BEGUILE is mid-story with a trailing clause ('he circles the same tent all night...'); corpus convention applies the start/end gate to the main story only, so gate 4 passes, but a tighter end placement would be stronger.
Minor: 'honeyed promises' is auditory/semi-abstract; a visible lure (e.g. dripping honey) would image more sharply.
Note (positive): spatial staging is faithful — Mouth under the Pike's blade, heart below floating up matches the 或-over-心 layout of 惑.

story: PITY the Twin Candle Wicks: two blue pinpricks of flame on their narrow left ledge, each pinched to the stingiest thread, hoarding the wax below unmelted so the hall stays pitch dark.
reading_story: PITY the diners: Sekka the chef flips one ladle and lets a single stingy drop of gold broth fall into each vast empty bowl, then locks the stockpot away.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 'PITY' is used as a vocative interjection ('PITY the Twin Candle Wicks' / 'PITY the diners') rather than as the semantic payoff. Rubric gate 4 (docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md:93) only requires the keyword at start or end, which is satisfied, but the concept actually carried by both stories is the secondary meaning 'stingy / be sparing of' (pinched flames hoarding wax; one drop of broth). Passes, but the keyword-to-scene link is weaker than the stingy-to-scene link.

Minor (non-gating): both stories open with the identical frame 'PITY the <noun>:', so meaning story and reading story are near-parallel in structure; slight interference risk with other 'PITY the ...' N1 entries if that template recurs.

Checked and clear: 忄 / Twin Candle Wicks named with correct left-edge placement (gate 1, 5, spatial fidelity); no phantom actors (wax, ledge, hall are scene props of a candle, not invented components); phonetic_extra 昔 correctly omitted from the story rather than smuggled in as a component; reading actor Sekka present with her registry persona verbatim ('chef, one ladle flip') (gate 3, 5); no etymology (gate 6); 32 words / 29 words, both under ~40 (gate 7). Personification of the wicks as 'hoarding' is ordinary in-character behaviour for a named actor persona, not an invented cognitive faculty.

story: Twin Candle Wicks stand on their narrow left-edge ledge, flames guttering as freezing rain drowns them one drip at a time; hissing, blackened, half-dead, they flicker on — utterly WRETCHED.
reading_story: Santa slides down the chimney into a flooded, freezing hovel; soot streaks his beard as he mutters that no home this WRETCHED deserves coal, let alone gifts.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 'WRETCHED' also appears buried mid-clause in reading_story; gate 4 (§3 line 93) scores the meaning story, where placement is correctly terminal, so this is cosmetic only.

Minor (non-gating): 'freezing rain' on a 'ledge' leaves the indoor/outdoor staging slightly ambiguous against the component image's unlocated 'narrow ledge at the left edge of a scene' — coherence (§3 line 101) dips a fraction but spatial fidelity is otherwise explicit.

story: Strings crossed above, the Masked Marionette dangles stiff over a bare red heart, sawdust sifting from its painted mouth onto the beating muscle below, burying it: FOOLISH.
reading_story: Goo, thick and gray, seeps across the puppet stage and swallows the show; the audience keeps applauding the empty puddle — utterly FOOLISH.
issues: Non-blocking: reading_story adds scene-dressing not tied to any component ('puppet stage', 'the audience'); harmless under gate 2 but slightly pads a 23-word story.
Non-blocking: reading_story repeats the keyword FOOLISH, which the meaning story already delivers as its payoff; redundant emphasis, no gate violation.
Non-blocking: the 禺 image's 'wooden altar-stand' is unused; omission only, not a phantom-component failure.

story: A flat Horizon Line caps Twin Pillars; between the two, a Silk Cocoon slips down and lands on a huge warm heart pulsing beneath — MERCY.
reading_story: Jee grabs the mic, clipped and quick, and shouts one word — "MERCY!" — and the roaring arena instantly falls silent.
issues: Non-blocking, spatial fidelity: 'between the two' is ambiguous — reads as either between the two pillars or between the Horizon Line and the pillars; naming the pillars explicitly would fix it.
Non-blocking, actor scale: the registry image for 一 is a vast desert horizon, which sits oddly as a lintel on two *short* stone pillars.
Non-blocking, imageability: 'slips down and lands' is a flat verb pair; only the 'huge warm heart' carries MERCY, leaving the horizon/pillars as inert scaffolding.
Non-blocking, distinctiveness risk: 'small object lands on a big warm heart' is a template likely to interfere with other N1 心 kanji (愛/恵/慕).

story: Glowing ability balances on top of a huge beating heart; every heartbeat jolts it into chin-up swagger or sulky slump. The angle the heart leaves it at is ATTITUDE.
reading_story: Ty spikes into second base and glares down the umpire — nobody recalls the stats, everyone recalls Ty's ATTITUDE.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'glowing ability' is an abstract protagonist — 能 has no actor/image, so learners must visualize an amorphous glow; the physical staging (balancing on the beating heart, swagger/slump postures) compensates.
Minor (non-blocking): Ty Cobb's spiking scene is mildly violent but within ordinary baseball-history bounds; no safety concern.

story: Twin Candle Wicks glow at the left as a Watching Eye beneath the Plus-Sign Crossroads studies the Horizon Line below, testing the Wishbone underfoot before taking a single step — PRUDENT.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender is PRUDENT: he sniffs every bottle, counts the till twice, and cuts everyone off after two drinks.
issues: Minor: Twin Candle Wicks are decorative scenery ("glow at the left") rather than participants in the prudent action — acceptable but weakens integration.
Minor: the Watching Eye is implied to have feet ("underfoot", "taking a single step") — ordinary physical motion, allowed by the gate, but slightly strains the actor's image.

story: Twin Candle Wicks tremble at the left edge; to their right the Sun spotlights a Fishing Net hauled up holding one limp Rubber Glove — a catch so pathetically lazy it earns pure RIDICULE.
reading_story: Thomas Mann trips onstage mid-lecture, notes scattering across the boards; laughter erupts, and he endures the RIDICULE with one stiff bow.
issues: minor (non-blocking): the 慢/漫/蔓 (曼) family will reuse 日+罒+又, so the net-hauls-a-catch frame risks interference with future siblings; the limp glove + candle wicks keep this one separable for now.

story: Twin Candle Wicks tremble on the left ledge; Still Butte stands unmoved; at its right flank the Boar's Tusk scrapes its empty notch where a twin fang will never regrow. That endless scraping is the sound of RUE.
reading_story: Guy Fawkes, hauled up from the cellar, stares at his damp powder barrels and lets out one clipped gasp of RUE.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS — all three mandatory actors named verbatim: 'Twin Candle Wicks' (忄), 'Still Butte' (艮), 'Boar's Tusk' (牙); components_used matches.

Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS — 'left ledge' comes from the 忄 image, 'empty notch'/'twin fang' from the 牙 image ('a deep interlocking notch cut where it once ground against its opposite fang'); 'cellar'/'powder barrels' belong to the Guy Fawkes persona, not to an invented component. Nothing outside the record is introduced.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Guy Fawkes' opens reading_story; reading_actor_used='Guy' matches reading_actor.actor_name.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS — 'RUE' is the final word and the payoff clause ('That endless scraping is the sound of RUE'); meaning_placement='end' is accurate.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS — 'tremble' echoes the wicks' 'flames trembling'; 'stands unmoved' echoes the butte 'utterly still... refusing to budge'; the tusk scraping is ordinary physical motion, not an invented cognitive faculty; damp powder in a cellar is on-persona for Guy Fawkes.

Gate 6 (no false etymology) PASS — no claim about historical derivation; 'a twin fang will never regrow' is story fiction extrapolated from the supplied image, not an etymological assertion. Note 既 (phonetic_extra) is unmentioned, which is allowed since it is not a mandatory component.
Gate 7 (length) PASS — story 38 words, reading_story 21 words; each under ~40.

Imageability weakness (3, not 4): the central beat is mechanically muddy — a lone tusk 'scrapes its empty notch' with no stated surface or agent doing the scraping, so the motion is hard to picture; and the payoff converts the image into an abstraction ('is the sound of RUE') rather than showing it. 'Still Butte stands unmoved' is concrete but actionless, so the middle of the scene has no motion.
