Distinctiveness weakness (3, not 4): 'Still Butte stands unmoved' is a near-default rendering of that actor and will read identically across other 艮 kanji, risking interference. The distinctive hook (lost twin fang, endless scraping) carries the whole card; the 忄 and 艮 beats are placeholders.

Minor: RUE appears in both story and reading_story, which is not a gate violation but slightly dilutes the reading story's own hook — 'one clipped gasp' would carry the がい sound better if the keyword were not repeated verbatim there.

story: The Tiger-Hide Cowl hangs its striped canopy low over your head; crouched beneath it, you think twice before every single step — that hooded, careful thinking is PRUDENCE.
reading_story: Ryo-short reaches for the last cake, stops his hand mid-air, and withdraws it — clipped, careful PRUDENCE, always cutting his desires short.
issues: Keyword payoff ('hooded, careful thinking is PRUDENCE') rests on an invisible mental act; the concrete imagery (canopy, crouch, steps) carries it but the keyword itself is not directly depicted.
Reading story places a short trailing clause ('always cutting his desires short') after the keyword — still an end placement, but slightly dilutes the landing.
Cautious-person theme has mild interference risk with other N1 care/discretion kanji (e.g. 慎-type keywords); the tiger-cowl staging mitigates it.

story: CONSOLATION: an officer stoops from above and pins a tin second-place medal onto a small heart lying in the mud below. The heart wears the medal like armour, ribbon stiff with battlefield dirt.
reading_story: Mr. Eaton, his name an "ee" clipped short, hangs the losers' ribbon round the last runner's neck at the finish line — Eaton's specialty is CONSOLATION.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the meaning story and the reading story share nearly identical imagery (tin second-place medal / losers' ribbon), so the two scenes risk blurring into one memory rather than cueing meaning vs. reading separately.

story: Under the Cliff Awning, the Bedsheet Cover is whipped off a huge glowing heart; below, a Trailing Footprint stamps the dust in a happy dance of JUBILATION.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer high-kicks off the stage, feathers flying, and the whole hall erupts in JUBILATION, chanting her name.
issues: Minor: reading_story keyword is followed by a trailing clause ("chanting her name") — still end placement, but the payoff would land harder as the final beat.
Watch interference with 憂 (shares 冖+心+夂); the 广 Cliff Awning and jubilant unveiling carry the contrast, keep them prominent in any edit.

story: The Horizon Line lies flat over oneself — your own bowed head; a Bedsheet Cover is drawn down across it like a mourning veil, your heart hangs heavy beneath, and one Trailing Footprint drags away from the grave — MELANCHOLY.
reading_story: Yuna skates her farewell program alone in an empty rink, holding the final long ūūū of the music, MELANCHOLY.
issues: Hand-authored replacement: the generated candidate was judge-rejected for inverted affect (it staged a birthday party — 'grinning', 'cake', 'frosting' — for the keyword MELANCHOLY, with the keyword orphaned as a front label). Rewritten as a funeral scene keeping the same five components in their correct vertical stack order (一 over 自 over 冖 over 心 over 夂) with the keyword as the terminal payoff.

story: INDIGNANT, the Twin Candle Wicks on their narrow left ledge flare white-hot: fresh tarmac has sealed a Cowrie Shell underground, and a Grass Tuft bursting from its slit cracks the Plus-Sign Crossroads' paint.
reading_story: Fonda slams his fist on the town-hall table, demanding to know who paved over the meadow — INDIGNANT, unshaven, refusing to sit back down.

story: Top-left, Lolling Tongue droops from a gasping Open Mouth; top-right, oneself slumps flat against the wall; below both, the heart's hammering sinks to one slow, blissful thud — RECESS.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer freezes mid-kick, drops onto the stage steps and gulps cold water — the band grants her one glorious RECESS.
issues: Distinctiveness risk (main deduction): the 自+心 half is nearly the same scene as neighbor 息 (BREATH, data/authored/n3-mnemonics.json) — 'oneself above, the pounding heart below' vs 'oneself slumps... the heart's hammering sinks'. 憩 literally contains 息 and both map to 'rest' vocab (休息 / 休憩), and 息's own record already flags that it 'risks interference with other calm/rest-themed kanji'. Separation rests entirely on the Lolling Tongue + Open Mouth.

'a gasping Open Mouth' pushes the scene toward breathing, which amplifies the 息 collision above; a non-respiratory use of the Mouth (yawning wide, or the Tongue flopping out slack) would keep the differentiator without borrowing 息's semantics.
Minor (non-gating): 'the wall' is unsupplied scenery not among the components — same class as the 'open hands below' noted on 与, not a phantom component actor.

Minor (non-gating): 'the heart's hammering sinks to one slow, blissful thud' is interoceptive/auditory rather than visual; 'blissful' is an emotion label, not an image. It is the keyword payoff, so it passes the same way 憶's 'the forgotten moment floods back' did.

Minor (non-gating): the reading_story opener recycles the standing Kayo template — 契 'halts mid-kick', 恵 'stops mid-show', 啓 'freezes the spotlight', 景 'stops mid-step'. The rest-and-water payoff is apt and keyword-specific, but the setup adds no separation from the other けい cards.

Minor (non-gating): vowel length is not signalled in the reading_story (cf. 恵 'as long as her final note', 計 'a long kayyy'). The Kayo persona itself encodes long ē, and several shipped entries omit it, so this is stylistic only.

story: Inside the Thatched House, a Pot Lid clamps down on a Mound of Soil; beneath them a Fishing Net stretches flat, pinning a beating heart — carved into that trapped heart is the CONSTITUTION.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll stands stiff on a podium, one rigid arm raised, squeakily swearing to defend the CONSTITUTION.
issues: Minor: five stacked elements form two loosely coupled sub-scenes (Pot Lid on Soil vs. Net pinning heart), slightly raising visualization load — not gating.
Minor: 心-bottom 'trapped/pressed heart' imagery recurs across the corpus; the 'constitution carved into the heart' detail mitigates interference risk.

story: Twin Candle Wicks tremble at your left; you stand up above the Sun, a sound ringing down into your heart until the forgotten moment floods back — RECOLLECTION.
reading_story: Occam slices away every false memory with his razor until only one true RECOLLECTION remains.
issues: Minor (non-gating): final clause 'the forgotten moment floods back' is slightly abstract, but it serves as the keyword payoff rather than a depicted image.

story: Twin Candle Wicks gutter on the left ledge. Above, a Falling Katana slashes past the Barbed Pike's shaft; below it an Open Mouth wails down at the heart lying on the floor, flooding it with REMORSE.
reading_story: Khan reins his horse at the village he burned, head bowed in the ash — a conqueror's first taste of REMORSE.
issues: Gating passes: all five components named — 忄 'Twin Candle Wicks', ノ 'Falling Katana', 戈 'Barbed Pike', 口 'Open Mouth', 心 'the heart' — no phantoms, Khan present in reading_story, REMORSE terminal in both stories, no etymology, 36 words (story) / 20 words (reading).

Weak link, not a gate failure: 忄 is inert. 'Twin Candle Wicks gutter on the left ledge' is a standalone scene-setting clause that never touches the katana, pike, mouth, or heart — it could be deleted without changing the story. Since 憾 differs from its nearest neighbour 感 (and the phonetic 感 is listed in phonetic_extra) precisely by 忄, the one component that must carry discriminative load is the one doing no work. Suggest the guttering wicks reacting to the wail or the heart's remorse.

Both 忄 and 心 appear in the same story as separate objects (trembling wicks vs. a heart on the floor) with no relationship. Learners will plausibly forget which of the two heart-forms is the radical and which is the base, or double-write one.

'flooding it with REMORSE' is the only abstract move in an otherwise concrete scene — remorse is not a visible substance and the verb 'flooding' has no source (tears? sound? light?). A physical payoff (the wail pouring down as something the heart visibly absorbs) would raise imageability without adding words.
Spatial fidelity is good: 忄 left, ノ/戈 above, 口 tucked under the pike, 心 at the floor — matches 憾's layout. Conciseness fine, safety fine.

reading_story is the stronger half: Khan reining up in the ash of a village he burned is concrete, matches the registered persona (Genghis Khan on horseback), and makes 'a conqueror's first taste of REMORSE' land as an earned payoff rather than a tacked-on keyword.

story: Hawk Talon presses down from above, Prowling Jackal creeps in at the left, Slinking Marten arches between them — three lone hunters settling onto one huge warm heart, nuzzling instead of fighting: perfectly SOCIABLE.
reading_story: Conn raises a martini and charms every guest at the embassy party — no spy was ever so SOCIABLE.
issues: Minor: Hawk Talon is a disembodied talon, so 'nuzzling' is slightly awkward to visualize for that actor (non-blocking; motion itself is ordinary/physical)
Minor: 'three lone hunters' loosely metonymizes the talon as a hunter; acceptable but a touch abstract

story: Twin Candle Wicks flutter on the left ledge. Beside them a Hanger Kimono hangs beneath a Plus-Sign Crossroads, its sleeves folding a Fishing Net into its silk belly — one deep, secret POCKET.
reading_story: Kai the surfer carves inside the wave's barrel, tugging a wax stub from the POCKET of his boardshorts.
issues: Minor: the reading_story repeats POCKET, so the keyword payoff is spent twice — the meaning cue and the sound cue blur slightly (not a gate failure, keyword is correctly final in the main story).

Minor: 'sleeves folding a Fishing Net into its silk belly' is self-motion by a hanging garment. Allowed as ordinary physical motion (no invented cognitive faculty), but it is the least concrete beat in the scene.
Distinctiveness risk: kimono + net is a combination that will recur across other 衣/罒 kanji (e.g. 壊/懐 family, 買, 罪). The 'one deep, secret POCKET' payoff is what saves it — keep that phrasing unique.

story: Beside the Forked Footpath, the Mountain Peak slams down onto the Kings Crown, and the Cracking Whip flogs the crushed heart pinned beneath — everything on this hillside is PENAL.
reading_story: Cho raps her wand on the bench, sentencing cauldron-cheats to PENAL servitude in the dungeons.

story: High above a chasm, the Dangling Tassel Knot suspends a beating heart in its loose silk strands; the heart sways, helpless — on that one knot it must DEPEND.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll dangles from a thread by one hand over the toy box, his molded grin insisting he is happy to DEPEND on it.

story: A hand clenches the Meat Hook dangling at its wrist and swings the Barbed Pike on its right, slashing at anyone who reaches for what is "mine" — pure EGO.
reading_story: Garr guns her growling engine outside the theater, drowning out every other star — her EGO demands the loudest entrance.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'clenches the Meat Hook dangling at its wrist' is slightly ambiguous to visualize — is the hook gripped in the hand or hanging from the wrist? Consider 'grips the Meat Hook hanging at its wrist' for a cleaner image.

story: Cupped Palms rise from below, hoisting the Barbed Pike overhead; sunlight blazes off its hooked spur, spelling one burning word across the sky — COMMANDMENT.
reading_story: Kai wipes out, gets dragged ashore, and kneels: the sea's first COMMANDMENT is etched on his surfboard — "Thou shalt respect the wave."
issues: Minor: 'spelling one burning word across the sky' (glint-as-skywriting) is the least concrete beat in an otherwise vivid scene.
Minor: in reading_story the keyword COMMANDMENT is followed by a trailing quote ('Thou shalt respect the wave') rather than being the final word — still in the payoff clause, so gate 4 passes.

story: FROLIC! On the left a bottomless void yawns open; right at its lip the Barbed Pike rocks and tips on its planted shaft, hooked spur swishing playfully through the emptiness.
reading_story: Gee cannonballs into the pool, splashing every deckchair in one short, giddy burst of FROLIC.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11) is muddled: the story tries to encode 虚-left / 戈-right, but 'right at its lip' reads far more naturally as an intensifier ('immediately at its edge') than as a position. The left side is explicitly marked ('On the left'), the right side effectively is not — the reader gets no reliable right-hand anchor for the Barbed Pike.

Imageability (item 9): the payoff action — 'hooked spur swishing playfully through the emptiness' — happens in empty space and therefore produces no visible consequence: nothing is struck, displaced, or splashed. The one motion that is supposed to carry FROLIC is the least picturable thing in the scene.

Meaning-lands is satisfied only by placement, not by depiction. 'FROLIC!' is a bare interjection bolted to the front, and the scene justifies it via the adverb 'playfully' — telling rather than showing. A pike that merely 'rocks and tips' is closer to precarious than to frolicking; the keyword is asserted, not earned.

Concreteness (item 8): 虚 is supplied with no actor and no image, only kanji_keyword 'void', and the story renders it as a bare abstract noun, then restates it as 'the emptiness'. The component is named twice yet never made concrete — 'bottomless void yawns open' is the generic default image, not a distinctive one.

Distinctiveness (item 10): 'object teetering at the lip of a chasm' is a reusable trope. 戈 recurs in many neighbors (戦, 我, 成, 戒...), so the Barbed Pike carries little separating power on its own; the void-plus-pike pairing is what saves this, and the scene around it is generic.

story: The Lone Barn Shutter creaks on its single hinge; knotted to its bottom corner, sweeping arcs in the doorway dust with every gust, swings a fat crimson TASSEL.
reading_story: Bowie struts onstage twirling a glittering TASSEL on his microphone stand, flinging sparkles over the front row.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword TASSEL is mid-sentence with a trailing clause ('flinging sparkles over the front row') rather than the final payoff — consistent with Minor-only precedent (佐), meaning story placement is clean.

story: A FAN takes shape: the Lone Barn Shutter hangs crooked overhead, while directly below it the Feather Pair spreads into a wide white arc, sweeping hot air across the barn floor.
reading_story: Senna, helmet off in the pit lane, cools his scorched face with a paper FAN, snapping it open and shut between laps.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): registry image for 羽 shows the Feather Pair as shed feathers lying on the ground, while the story has them airborne and actively fanning — permissible ordinary physical motion, but a slight energy shift from the defined persona.

story: A billionaire's marble mansion entrance holds no oak grandeur — just the Lone Barn Shutter, creaking crooked on its single hinge, wind swinging it open across the gilded threshold. That warped panel is the whole FRONT DOOR.
reading_story: Hee, the clipped giggler, crouches behind that mansion's FRONT DOOR, letting out one sharp "hee!" every time the crooked panel creaks open.
issues: Non-blocking: near-tautological framing (a shutter used as a door) means the main distinctiveness load is carried only by the mansion setting; verify the 戸 mnemonic does not also make the Lone Barn Shutter the payoff, or the two will interfere.
Non-blocking: 'holds no oak grandeur' encodes by negation, asking the learner to picture an absence; a positive contrast image would encode better.

story: On the right a husband buckles mid-stride, one leg folding under him. From the left the Grabber Claw glides in, wedges three steel fingers beneath his sagging shoulder, and props him upright, matching him step for step — AID.
reading_story: Foo lopes up the pavement, slides under the husband's free side, and matches the claw stride for stride — two of them, one steady AID.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 10, distinctiveness): the reading story is redundant with the meaning story — Foo simply duplicates the Claw's action ('matches the claw stride for stride'), so 'ふ' gets no independent hook of its own beyond the name. A distinct Foo action (e.g. Foo doing something only a rock guitarist would do) would separate 扶 from its aid/help neighbours (助/援/佑/補) more sharply.

Non-blocking (gate 11, spatial/coherence): 'matching him step for step' is slightly off-model for an arcade grabber-claw, which travels on a gantry rather than walking. The motion is still ordinary physical translation, not an invented cognitive faculty, so it passes gate 5 — but 'gliding alongside him rail by rail' would be truer to the actor's image.

story: CRITICISM: at the left edge, the Grabber Claw lowers onto a fresh manuscript, snatches it up, and slaps it down again and again, striking red gouges through every line.
reading_story: Every time the CRITICISM lands, Hee lets out one clipped "hee!" — a giggle per insult.
issues: Minor (non-gating): slap/strike action overlaps conceptually with other 扌 kanji such as 打 'strike'; the gouged-manuscript prop carries the distinctiveness, so keep it prominent in any edit.

story: The Grabber Claw reaches in from the left and clamps the kneeling Wax Stamp, grinding it down into its own red wax until nothing can rise — REPRESS.
reading_story: A Yorker on a packed subway must REPRESS the urge to scream — jaw clenched, knuckles white on the pole.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword REPRESS sits mid-sentence ("must REPRESS the urge to scream") rather than at start/end; acceptable because it is capitalized and is the clear payoff, and meaning_placement 'end' correctly describes the main story.
Minor: "until nothing can rise" is slightly abstract next to an otherwise fully concrete scene.
Watch-item (not a defect): crush/press imagery is a crowded motif among 扌 neighbors (押, 圧, 抵); the Wax Stamp victim keeps this one distinct.

story: The Grabber Claw dives from the left at the Pot Lid perched on the Low Stool; the lid clamps down tight, the stool trips its fingers — every snatch fails: DEFY.
reading_story: Officials rope off the track, but Coe vaults the rope mid-stride and keeps running — born to DEFY.
issues: Minor: 'the stool trips its fingers' is physically slightly awkward (a stool tripping a claw's fingers), though consistent with the Low Stool's trip-over persona and still imageable — not gating.

story: The Grabber Claw dangles at the left of the glass case; inside, the only prize is the Draped Cloak slumped over a chair. Steel fingers dip, clamp a drooping fold, lift — one snatch to CHOOSE.
reading_story: Tucker stands before two vending buttons, coin trembling in his hand — press one, lose the other. Tucker must CHOOSE.
issues: Coherence wobble: 'the only prize' removes any alternative, so 'one snatch to CHOOSE' is choosing among one option — the keyword link is asserted rather than dramatized in the meaning story (the reading story's two-buttons dilemma does it better).

Interference risk: scene hews close to the Grabber Claw's stock image (claw snatches prize), and semantic neighbors 採/拾/摘 (pick/pick up/pluck) also use 扌 — the imagery cues grab/pick as readily as CHOOSE. Distinctiveness capped at 3.

story: At the left edge the Grabber Claw lowers, three fingers hooking the velvet curtain and dragging it wide, leaving the whole lit stage naked and EXPOSED.
reading_story: Hee crouches behind the dragged-back drape, but one clipped giggle rings out and the spotlight swings to EXPOSE her.
issues: (non-blocking) Distinctiveness risk: 'curtain pulled back to reveal' is the most predictable image for EXPOSE and could interfere with neighbouring N1 reveal/open kanji (露, 暴, 啓, 開) if the same trope recurs there; the arcade-claw + velvet-drape pairing is what currently keeps it separable.
(non-blocking) Keyword appears as inflected 'EXPOSED' rather than the bare keyword 'expose'; still the final payoff word, so gate 4 passes.

story: From the left the Grabber Claw descends on the Family Crest Banner; the cloth snaps taut around its three fingers, binding them so the claw can't rip it from the pole — RESIST.
reading_story: Tay hugs the gatepost, belting one long endless note — "RESIST!" — and no amount of tugging can peel her off.

story: From the left the Grabber Claw plunges elbow-deep into a packed junk bin, fingers burrowing to the very bottom, and wrenches one buried boot up through the heap — PLUCK.
reading_story: Deep in the Falcon's smoking engine pit, Chewbacca reaches shoulder-deep and PLUCKs out the one blown coupling, roaring in triumph.
issues: Non-blocking: verb 'pluck(s)' already appears uncapitalized in the shipped stories for 技 and 挑 (n2/n1-mnemonics.json), slight keyword-interference risk with PLUCK as 抽's payoff.
Non-blocking: reading_story keyword lands mid-sentence rather than start/end; consistent with shipped reading-story precedent (注, 宙), so treated as meaning-story-only gate.
Non-blocking: 'elbow-deep' is figurative for an arcade claw; acceptable as ordinary physical motion but could be tightened.

story: The Grabber Claw hangs at the left edge, lowers, and slaps its three steel fingers flat against a gleaming white drumhead — smack, smack, smack in steady rhythm — CLAP!
reading_story: The Hacker cracks a stadium jumbotron; each time his code executes, ten thousand robot hands CLAP in perfect sync, applauding the hack.
issues: Non-blocking: the claw's action reads more as drumming a drumhead than clapping; acceptable since 'Beat (music)' is a listed meaning and the CLAP! payoff still lands at the end.

story: The Grabber Claw swings in from the left and snatches a screaming Open Mouth off the shelf; below it the Cleaver hangs on its hook, blade glinting. Textbook KIDNAP.
reading_story: Kai the surfer paddles out past the break, then vanishes — a rogue wave curls over him and completes a clean KIDNAP, board bobbing empty.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 12 coherence / graded): the Cleaver (刀) is named but wholly inert — it 'hangs on its hook, blade glinting' and plays no role in the kidnap. Coverage passes, but a passive prop is weakly encoded and is the likeliest component to be forgotten at recall.

Non-blocking (gate 4, reading story only): 'completes a clean KIDNAP, board bobbing empty' places the keyword one clause before the end rather than as the final payoff. The meaning story ('Textbook KIDNAP.') satisfies the gate cleanly, so this does not fail.
Note, not a defect: 'shelf' and 'hook' are scenery, not phantom components — 'hangs from a hook' is verbatim from the Cleaver's registry image, so gate 2 and gate 5 pass.

story: From the left the Grabber Claw dips to snatch tools, but the Toolbox Tray's open maw faces away to the right; steel fingers clang off three blank walls that flatly REFUSE.
reading_story: Cole answers every invitation the same way: a clipped, one-syllable shake of the head — REFUSE.

story: The Grabber Claw lowers from the left, clamps the mossy Boulder squatting on the right, and hauls it skyward off the stubbled acre — rock by rock, CLEAR LAND.
reading_story: Tucker sweats at dawn, dragging stones out of his pasture one by one until he has enough CLEAR LAND for a first furrow.
issues: Minor coherence: story stages a single Boulder but the payoff says 'rock by rock', implying plural rocks.
Minor: in reading_story the keyword is in the final clause but not final ('CLEAR LAND for a first furrow'); the main story satisfies the placement gate, so non-blocking.

Minor: Boulder is relocated from its registry setting (wedged under a cliff-overhang) to an open field; persona traits (squat, mossy) are preserved, so treated as scene-setting rather than an actor-consistency violation.

story: From the left, the Grabber Claw swings in and clamps its three fingers around the Quote Hook mid-snatch — hook, mouth, and half-spoken phrase locked in one steel grip. ARREST.
reading_story: Coe breaks the finish tape at record pace — cuffs snap over his wrists before the medal ceremony: an ARREST mid-victory-lap.

story: At the left the Grabber Claw grips the Low Stool steady in the mud; the muddy Trailing Footprint stamps down onto the stool's seat — a FOOTHOLD.
reading_story: Cole wedges his boot into a cliff crack, bouncing twice to test the FOOTHOLD before hauling himself up.
issues: Non-blocking: reading_story keyword is near-final but trailed by 'before hauling himself up' — meaning gate is satisfied by the main story's terminal FOOTHOLD, so this is stylistic only.
Non-blocking: shares 夂+几 cast with 処 — curation should verify the 処 story stages a clearly different scene to avoid neighbor interference.

story: EXPAND: the Grabber Claw hooks the Cliff Awning's edge and hauls it wider and wider, stretching the slanted roof until the tiny Sealed Clam-Locket huddled beneath sits inside a vast, echoing shelter.
reading_story: Knuckles winds up one punch; on impact his boxing glove balloons, forced to EXPAND until it fills the whole ring.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): closing image (vast shelter over the Clam-Locket) is near-identical to the likely end-state of 広 'wide' (广+厶); the Grabber Claw actively hauling is the sole discriminator — keep that action foregrounded in any edit.

story: FASTEN: the Grabber Claw swings in from the left edge and clamps the Open Mouth shut, while above those squeezed lips a Falling Katana slices down across the Plus-Sign Crossroads.
reading_story: The Cutler snaps his knife-roll shut, straps drawn tight, and tugs the buckle twice to FASTEN every blade in place.
issues: Non-blocking: the upper half of the story (Falling Katana slicing across the Plus-Sign Crossroads) is decorative co-occurrence — those two actors do not participate in the FASTEN action carried by the Grabber Claw clamping the Open Mouth shut, so recall pressure on ノ and 十 is weaker than on 扌/口.

Non-blocking: 'Grabber Claw clamps X shut' is a high-frequency motif for 扌 kanji in the grip/seize/hold family (捕/執/把 neighbours), a mild interference risk; the katana-over-crossroads pairing is what keeps this one separable.

story: A CHALLENGE: the Grabber Claw swings in from the left, snatching at the Frost Beads frozen onto the Wishing-Well Legs — pluck both icy beads without toppling the stone legs, and win.
reading_story: Cho flings down her glove and shouts her CHALLENGE — a wizard's duel at dawn, her wand already sparking.

story: RAISE! A hand punches up from the dirt, hoisting a Wishbone whose legs spring apart; atop it, Bean Sprouts stretch taller and taller as the hand lifts them all skyward.
reading_story: At the auction, Cole is fastest to RAISE his paddle — the auctioneer only ever hears Cole's bid.

story: From the left, the Grabber Claw reaches under the Rock Overhang, clamps the Hanger Kimono dangling in that stone hollow, and rattles it until dust bursts from both spread sleeves — SHAKE.
reading_story: Behind his bar, Shinn grips the frosted cocktail tin in both fists and gives it one violent SHAKE; the ice cracks like gunfire.

story: At the left, the Grabber Claw grips an entire residence — where you reside — and lowers it dead-level onto wet foundation concrete; the bolts thunk home: INSTALL.
reading_story: Before moving in, Cole must INSTALL his arcade cabinet dead-center; he bolts it down, pats it, and declares the place home.
issues: Non-blocking, cross-story repetition: 'bolts' + 'home' + 'dead-level'/'dead-center' appear in BOTH story and reading_story, so the two scenes blur into one another and the reading card loses independent retrieval value. Vary the reading story's verbs/props.

Non-blocking, rubric §1.2 (vowel length encoding): reading_actor is the SHORT twin (きょ, note: 'clipped twin of Kyo. Short.'), but the reading_story carries no clipped/shrunken cue -- Cole is written like any full-length persona, so the story does not reinforce きょ vs きょう.

Non-blocking, §3.4: the keyword INSTALL sits mid-sentence in reading_story ('Cole must INSTALL his arcade cabinet dead-center'). The gate governs the meaning story (where placement is correctly terminal), but the buried mid-clause keyword is slightly off-pattern.

Minor, §3.10 distinctiveness: 'bolts it down onto concrete' is generic install imagery shared with other set/establish kanji; the only load-bearing distinguisher is the claw lifting an entire residence.

story: The Grabber Claw swings down the left wall, clamps a glowing textbook out of the prize pit, and lowers it gently into your cupped hands: IMPART.
reading_story: Juju presses her lucky charm into your palm at the school gate, the one bit of magic she can IMPART.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness, prop collision): 'the prize pit' is already the signature setting of 握/GRIP in the same corpus — n1-mnemonics.json: 'At the left edge, the Grabber Claw lowers over the prize pit, three half-clenched fingers closing on a plush toy... GRIP' — and of another 扌 story ('the arcade Grabber Claw plunges into the prize pit, clamps a mold-furred plush'). Both are 扌 kanji, so the shared locus is the worst possible place for overlap. The motions do diverge (gentle release vs. squealing clamp) and the glowing textbook is unique in the corpus, so it clears the bar, but swapping 'prize pit' for a classroom-specific source (a lectern, a shelf of texts) would lift distinctiveness from 3 to 4 at zero cost.

NON-BLOCKING (neighbor interference with 受): 授 = 扌 + 受, and 受 already ships as n3-mnemonics.json 'Hawk Talon reaches down through the Bedsheet Cover... dropping a parcel straight into the waiting Rubber Glove below — the glove closes: ACCEPT.' Both stories are 'overhead agent lowers an object into a waiting receiver', and both use the same reading actor Juju (じゅ). Saved by opposite payoffs (IMPART vs ACCEPT), different actors (Grabber Claw vs Hawk Talon/Rubber Glove), and the fact that the claw is absent from 受 — so the claw is a reliable disambiguator — but the frame is close enough to note.

NON-BLOCKING (near-miss on gate 2): 'your cupped hands' sits one word from the registry actor 廾 = 'Cupped Palms' (n4-component-actors.json), which is not a component of 授. Precedent exists for the casual usage (n3-mnemonics.json: 'pours into the cupped, waiting hands of my kneeling DAUGHTER'; 'shouts through cupped hands'), so this is not a phantom component, but 'your open palms' would remove the ambiguity entirely.

NON-BLOCKING (reading story): the reading_story places Juju but does nothing with her defined note ('clipped twin of Juno (じゅう)... voiced/heavier twin of Shu (しゅ). Short.') — no cue reinforces the short vowel. Gate 3 only requires presence, so this passes, but the corpus does better elsewhere (e.g. 'clipped little Juju can't keep up with the DEMAND').

story: A colossal hand rises from below, fingers peeling back like petals until the ridged, sweat-slick, city-sized plain at its centre stands revealed: the PALM OF HAND.
reading_story: The Showman whips off his top hat, slaps it down, and a tiny circus tent pops open on his outstretched PALM OF HAND.
issues: Non-gating: the meaning story is close to tautological — 手 'hand' revealing its own palm restates the keyword rather than encoding a distinct scene, so the retrieval cue leans on the sensory adjectives ('ridged, sweat-slick, city-sized plain') to do all the work of separating 掌 from other 手-radical neighbours.
Non-gating: 'stands revealed' is the one abstract beat in an otherwise concrete image; a physical verb would sharpen it.

Verified passing (no action needed): 手 named as 'colossal hand'; no phantom components ('like petals' is a simile, top hat / circus tent are Showman props); Showman present in reading_story and consistent with the top-hatted ringmaster persona; PALM OF HAND is the terminal payoff in both stories, matching meaning_placement 'end'; no etymology; 26 and 23 words. Spatial fidelity is a bonus — the hand rising 'from below' and the hat/tent sitting above the palm mirror 尚-over-手.

story: EXPEL: at the left edge, the arcade Grabber Claw plunges into the prize pit, clamps a mold-furred plush by the scruff, swings right, and hurls it out through the reject chute onto the pavement.
reading_story: Mid-lecture, Dr. Jekyll turns into Mr. Hyde; the headmaster points a trembling finger at the snarling monster and roars "EXPEL him!" — guards drag him out.

story: Grabber Claw hangs at the left, lowering toward the Burrow Hole on the right — Thatched House capping the Wishing-Well Legs that frame its dark mouth — then stops, fingers curling shut on nothing: HOLD BACK.
reading_story: Coaches scream "HOLD BACK, Coe!" — Coe eases his stride, letting the pack pass, saving his kick for the final lap.
issues: Minor: mid-story appositive stacks 宀/儿/穴 in one static structural clause, slightly dense but within length and coherent
Note: 工 (phonetic_extra) is unmentioned in the meaning story but covered by reading actor Coe (こう) — not a coverage failure

story: The Grabber Claw descends from the left toward Stumpy Sparrow, perched fat and motionless on her wire. Will those three fingers close on feathers or on empty air? Pure CONJECTURE.
reading_story: Swee feeds the machine another coin, pointing: "It grabs dead center this time!" Every CONJECTURE costs him a quarter, and the prize never drops.
issues: Minor: reading-story keyword is at the start of the final sentence but followed by a trailing clause ('...costs him a quarter, and the prize never drops') — payoff still lands, not gating.

story: Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through the Horizon Line and both Railway Tracks, stopping just above the Sun. From the left, Grabber Claw plucks that Sun free and swings it away — SET ASIDE for later.
reading_story: Saul Goodman slides your case file to the desk's far corner: "SET ASIDE for now — I'll call you."
issues: Non-blocking: Grabber Claw removes the Sun from the scene, but 日 stays inside the glyph — slight spatial-fidelity softness (rubric item 11), acceptable because the removal IS the keyword payoff.
Non-blocking: the bolt/horizon/tracks-over-sun tableau will repeat across 昔-family kanji (借, 錯, 惜); distinctiveness rests on the claw-sets-sun-aside action, which carries it here.

story: At the town notice board, the Grabber Claw hoists its exhibit: the Sun pinned up top, the Swaddling Wrap curled below it hugging the Soup Ladle tight — one last shove and everything is PUT UP.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer refuses to go on stage until her glittering poster is PUT UP over the theater door.

story: Grabber Claw hangs at the left, dragging one muddy fingertip across the Rice-Paddy Grid while the Grass Tuft crowns it from above — line by line, a perfect mud SKETCH.
reading_story: Beau strikes a movie-star pose and holds it for hours, demanding a flawless SKETCH of his famous face.

story: The Grabber Claw dips from the left, pinches the blazing Sun like a giant engagement ring, and holds it high while the Fabric Roll unspools a white aisle below — lowering it to PROPOSE.
reading_story: Tay rehearses all week; at last she kneels, holds out the ring, and finally dares to PROPOSE.
issues: Minor coherence wobble: claw 'holds it high' then is 'lowering it' in the same beat — non-blocking, but the final frame's motion is slightly contradictory.

story: From the left edge of the arcade machine, Grabber Claw clamps the fattest prize and, cables shrieking, cranks it up and up, through the ceiling hatch, into the sky — HOIST!
reading_story: Riggers HOIST Yoyo's cello on ropes toward the rafters; Yoyo saws his bow below, holding one long rising ōōō as the case climbs.
issues: Minor coherence wobble (non-gating): reading story has Yoyo bowing below while his cello is the object being hoisted, so he plays without an instrument

story: At the left edge, the Grabber Claw lowers over the prize pit, three half-clenched fingers closing on a plush toy until the metal squeals — a perfect, unbreakable GRIP.
reading_story: Acker greets you with a handshake so fierce your knuckles pop — nobody ever escapes Acker's GRIP.
issues: Non-blocking: story closely tracks the actor's canonical image ('lowering to snatch a prize' -> 'lowers over the prize pit... closing on a plush toy'), so only the 'unbreakable, metal-squealing grip' beat differentiates 握 from other 扌 kanji using Grabber Claw — distinctiveness capped at 3.
Non-blocking: right-side 屋 is unrepresented in the scene; acceptable since it is phonetic_extra (no supplied actor), but the story anchors nothing kanji-specific spatially on the right.

story: At the arcade's left edge the Grabber Claw snatches a glowing toy sword — but instead of dropping it down the chute, it swings the blade in wild flashing circles overhead: pure BRANDISH.
reading_story: Key the clipped locksmith whips out one giant skeleton key and gives it a full BRANDISH, slashing the air until the stuck lock surrenders.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in reading_story the keyword BRANDISH appears mid-sentence rather than at the very end, though the trailing clause depicts the brandishing action itself

story: From the left edge a Grabber Claw lowers into the vault; top-right a Hawk Talon grips the ledge, a Falling Katana slashes down past the flat Horizon Line, and a Rubber Glove lies palm-up below, catching loot — rigged to ABET.
reading_story: Enzo skids his red racer beside a stalled truck and bumper-pushes it uphill to the garage, gladly stopping his own race to ABET a stranded driver.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS — all five supplied actors named verbatim: 'a Grabber Claw lowers', 'a Hawk Talon grips', 'a Falling Katana slashes', 'the flat Horizon Line', 'a Rubber Glove lies palm-up'.
Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS — 'the vault', 'the ledge', 'loot' are scene staging, not actors or glyphs presented as parts of 援; no sixth component is introduced.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Enzo skids his red racer' opens the reading story; matches the えん persona (Enzo Ferrari) and the red-racer detail is consistent with it.

Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS but weak — ABET is terminal in both stories ('rigged to ABET' / 'to ABET a stranded driver'). The kanji story's payoff is vague: 'rigged to ABET' has no object, so the reader must infer 'abet the heist'. The reading story's payoff is the stronger of the two.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS — no invented cognitive faculty. Grabber Claw 'lowering to snatch a prize' -> lowers into the vault; Hawk Talon 'pressing into a branch from above' -> grips the ledge; Falling Katana 'slicing down on a diagonal' -> slashes down; Rubber Glove 'palm-up, fingers loosely curled' passively catching falling loot is ordinary physics for a curled glove, not an invented ability.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS — nothing framed as historical derivation; the phonetic 爰 is not mentioned.
Gate 7 (length) PASS at the ceiling — kanji story is exactly 40 words; reading story ~26. No slack left for further detail.
Spatial fidelity GOOD — 'from the left edge' for 扌 and 'top-right' for 爪 match 援's left-radical / right-top layout, and ノ一 mid, 又 below tracks the right-hand stack top-to-bottom.

Imageability weakness (drives the 3): §2 asks for 'one vivid/striking image', but this is five adjacent props each doing one small thing rather than a single interaction. 一 is inert — the katana merely slashes 'past' the Horizon Line, which does nothing.
Coherence weakness: a 'flat desert Horizon Line' inside a bank vault is a setting clash. The registry image is explicitly an open desert horizon, so it reads as pasted into a scene it cannot occupy.

Distinctiveness weakness (drives the 3): heist-vault-with-grabber-claw is a high-collision frame likely to recur across other 扌 kanji, and 'rigged to ABET' is a generic tag. The reading story (bumper-pushing a stalled truck uphill, sacrificing his own race) is the distinctive half and maps well onto 援助 = assistance.

story: A Hawk Talon clamps the tip of an Antenna Mast planted inside a Trap Pit; from the left a Grabber Claw yanks it side to side until the whole mast starts to SWING.
reading_story: Yoyo rides a playground SWING, cello between his knees, bowing one long note that wobbles with every sway.

story: Grabber Claw dangles at the left edge, fingers half-clenched, plucking prize after prize off the rubber belt rolling endlessly rightward beneath it: CONVEYOR.
reading_story: Hancock leans over the CONVEYOR, signing his huge looping signature on every crate that glides past before it vanishes through the flaps.
issues: Non-gating: phonetic_extra 般 has no supplied actor, so it is carried only phonetically by Hancock in the reading story and is absent from the meaning story's visual scene — acceptable under the rubric (no actor supplied = no coverage obligation), but the meaning story leans entirely on the single 扌 actor.

Non-gating: 'rubber belt / prizes' is keyword scenery rather than a component, so it clears the phantom gate, but the generic conveyor-belt image risks interference with other N1 transport kanji (輸/運/送) — hence distinctiveness capped at 3.

story: At the bus steps, the Grabber Claw hoists a Snap-Lid Bento — a Grass Tuft sprouting from its snapped-shut lid — and sets it on a seat: even the lunchbox gets to BOARD.
reading_story: Tone drawls the final boarding call — "Wiiild thing, time to BOARD" — stretching the long ō all the way down the jet bridge.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (coherence, rubric item 12): the meaning story is set at a bus ('At the bus steps... sets it on a seat') while the reading story is set at an airport ('all the way down the jet bridge'). Two different vehicles for the same kanji weakens the single unified image; aligning both on one boarding scene would help.

NON-BLOCKING (imageability, rubric item 9): the Grass Tuft is delivered inside an em-dash appositive ('— a Grass Tuft sprouting from its snapped-shut lid —') so it is a static decoration rather than a participant. Coverage gate 1 passes (actor is named), but the weakest-imaged element is the one most likely to be dropped on recall.

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness, rubric item 10): ⺾+合 is shared with 塔 (tower) and 合 recurs in 答/拾; the only differentiator here is the Grabber Claw + bus frame. Watch that the 塔 story does not also lead with a grass-topped Snap-Lid Bento or the pair will interfere.

story: Grabber Claw dangles at the left, clamping a giant Listening Ear; beneath it two Frost Beads melt, and the cupped lobe soaks the icy trickle straight in — ABSORB.
reading_story: The Settler kneels on frozen prairie, pressing a dry cloth to the thaw, watching it ABSORB every drop before winter returns.
issues: Non-blocking: in reading_story the keyword is buried mid-clause ('watching it ABSORB every drop'); §3 gate 4 is scored on `story` (where ABSORB is the end payoff, matching meaning_placement='end'), so this passes, but a start/end placement in the reading line would be cleaner.

Non-blocking: the reading actor's phonetic hook is weak — 'Settler' appears but nothing in the scene reinforces the -tsu coda noted in reading_actor.note; the frozen-prairie setting also duplicates the Frost Beads' winter imagery rather than adding a distinct sound cue.
Non-blocking: 'clamping a giant Listening Ear' leaves the Grabber Claw causally inert — it holds the ear but contributes nothing to the ABSORB payoff, which is carried entirely by lobe + melt.

story: At the arcade's left edge, the Grabber Claw descends over a tray of ripe strawberries, ignores the plush prizes, and closes just two metal fingertips on one tiny stem — a perfect PINCH.
reading_story: Tekker taps the joystick once — "Don't grab, PINCH!" — and the claw lifts the prize by a single thread.

story: At the very bottom, a hand grinds furious circles against the rough surface pressing down on it, rubbing until the palm glows raw and hot — CHAFE.
reading_story: Mah breaks in stiff new boots; by noon her heels CHAFE, rubbed so raw she walks home barefoot.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): scene is a literal keyword illustration; mild interference risk with 擦 (the other 手-based rub/scrape kanji) — the 'very bottom' spatial anchor and canopy 'surface pressing down' are what differentiate 摩, so preserve them in any edit.

story: Top-left, a heavy Cartwheel crashes down; top-right, the Lance-Butt Grip jabs forward; beneath both, a bare hand hammers the packed earth in relentless rhythm — BEAT.
reading_story: Gecker stomps into the ring, cracks his knuckles, and lays a thunderous BEAT on every challenger who dares step forward.
issues: GATES PASS. All three mandatory components named: 車 as "Cartwheel" (actor), 殳 as "the Lance-Butt Grip" (actor), 手 as "a bare hand" (actor is null, so kanji_keyword "hand" is the correct handle).

No invented cognitive faculties: the Cartwheel "crashes down" (ordinary motion for a rolling wheel), and "the Lance-Butt Grip jabs forward" is verbatim consistent with its image ("as if about to jab it forward").
Reading gate OK: reading_actor "Gecker" appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor_used; nothing contradicts the げき/short-vowel note.
Keyword gate OK: meaning_placement="end" and the story terminates on "— BEAT", matching keyword "beat".
Length OK: story 25 words, reading_story 20 words, both under ~40. No etymology language (spatial layout "top-left/top-right/beneath" is scene staging, not historical derivation).

MINOR: "the packed earth" is scenery, not a claimed component, but "earth" is close enough to the common radical 土 to risk being re-read as a fourth component on later reviews; "the packed ground/dirt floor" would be safer.

MINOR (imageability): the story is three parallel impacts rather than one interacting scene — the Cartwheel, the Grip and the hand never touch the same target, so the image fragments into three unlinked panels. "Relentless rhythm" is the only binding element and it is abstract.

MINOR (distinctiveness): a generic striking/pounding scene is the most predictable framing for keyword "beat", giving weak interference resistance against neighbouring strike kanji; the only real differentiators are the two named actors. The reading_story's ring-and-knuckle-cracking brawler is likewise stock imagery.
NOTE: "BEAT" is repeated in reading_story; harmless and mildly reinforcing, not a gate violation.

story: WITHDRAW! On the left the Grabber Claw drops and plucks up the recruit the army hoped to bring up, while on the right the Cracking Whip snaps, lashing every straggler into retreat.
reading_story: Tetsuo mutates, flesh engulfing the stadium; the army screams WITHDRAW and every tank rolls back out of Neo-Tokyo.

story: Grabber Claw drops from the left edge and clamps onto the utmost prize on the right — the tallest, shiniest one — and that frozen instant of clenching is your perfect SNAPSHOT.
reading_story: Satcher lunges across the arcade floor, snatching the falling plush inches from the tile — the ceiling camera catches his dive as the week's most-shared SNAPSHOT.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the meaning story's keyword link is metaphorical — 'that frozen instant of clenching is your perfect SNAPSHOT' — with no camera, shutter, or flash imagery; a visible photographic beat would make the payoff seen rather than asserted.
Minor (non-gating): 'frozen instant = SNAPSHOT' is a portable formula that would fit any grasping/clamping kanji, which caps distinctiveness against neighbours like 掴 or 握.
Minor (non-gating): the reading_story reuses the same arcade backdrop as the meaning story (arcade floor, falling plush), so the two stories blur together instead of occupying separate scenes.

story: From the left edge, the Grabber Claw swings across at the Woolly Ram balanced atop the Stepladder — fleece rippling, horns rattling from one echoing SLAP.
reading_story: Booker slams his ledger shut with a SLAP that echoes across the empty gym.

story: Grabber Claw swings in from the left, scoops up the grumpy Stumpy Sparrow, and clamps the Pot Lid down over her from above, squeezing bird and lid together in one crushing HUG.
reading_story: Yoyo finishes his cello suite, lays down the bow, and spreads both arms wide as the whole audience rushes the stage for a HUG.
issues: Minor: 'squeezing bird and lid together' slightly blurs the single freeze-frame (imageability capped at 4)
Minor: reading story (audience rushes stage for a hug) is generic compared to the meaning story; adjacent 扌+隹 kanji like 推 could interfere, mitigated by the Pot Lid clamp

story: At the left edge the Grabber Claw lowers, half-clenched, toward a Tree whose top branches balance three stacked goods. One deft swivel, one snatch — a flawless MANEUVER.
reading_story: Sosa checks his swing mid-pitch, bat corkscrewing around his shoulders — the umpire gapes at the MANEUVER.

story: The Grabber Claw misses its prize and grinds its half-clenched steel fingers down the arcade cabinet's left glass wall — three screeching tracks, paint curling off in ribbons. SCRAPE.
reading_story: Satcher skids into the rink boards, boot blades dragging along the ice and spraying white shavings — one long, ringing SCRAPE.
issues: Minor coherence (non-blocking, §3 item 12): the claw drags down a 'glass wall' yet 'paint curl[s] off in ribbons' — glass is not painted. Suggest 'the cabinet's painted left side panel' to keep the ribbon detail physically consistent.

Minor watch-item (§3 item 10): 擦 shares the 扌 actor and a near-identical semantic field with 摩/磨 (rub/chafe/polish); the arcade-cabinet + paint-ribbon staging currently carries the whole distinctiveness load, so any future 扌 'rub' story must avoid reusing an abrasion-on-a-flat-surface image.

story: AGGRESSION incarnate: from the right, the Cracking Whip snaps down again and again, its lash raking red stripes across a cowering target, driving it forward under relentless attack.
reading_story: Final lap: Coe surges past with sheer AGGRESSION, elbows out, spikes flashing, attacking every rival on the bend.
issues: Distinctiveness is only adequate: the story is essentially the Cracking Whip's default persona behavior (rap and drive into action) aimed at a generic unnamed 'cowering target', which may interfere with other 攵-family kanji stories; a more specific target/anchor would sharpen it.

story: From the right, the Cracking Whip snaps down again and again, each stinging lash rapping out the same demand from the empty air: no excuses — give me the REASON.
reading_story: In her atelier, Coco snips away every ribbon that cannot justify itself: "Elegance demands a REASON for everything."
issues: Whip 'rapping out a demand' voices speech — borderline anthropomorphism, though within its rap-and-drive persona (non-blocking)
Lash strikes 'empty air': no concrete target in the scene, which caps imageability
Verbal/auditory hook ('no excuses — give me the REASON') rather than a distinct visual scene; moderate interference risk with other 攵 (Cracking Whip) stories

story: Every dancer lined up on the left leaps the instant the Cracking Whip snaps in from the right — every lash whistles under their heels, never landing once. AGILE.
reading_story: Binny vaults the closing turnstile, AGILE as a cat, landing on the platform without a sound.
issues: Minor: 'every' is used as a modifier of 'dancer' rather than a standalone concept, though naming it twice mitigates this
Minor: keyword also appears mid-sentence in the reading story ('AGILE as a cat') rather than as a terminal payoff — acceptable since placement gating applies to the meaning story

story: The Tsunami Wave curls over, about to swallow the tiny Ink Droplet clinging to its crest. From the right the Cracking Whip snaps out, coils around the droplet, and yanks it clear — a RESCUE.
reading_story: Cuomo wades before the cameras, hauls a stranded family into his boat, and grins: every channel replays the Cuomo RESCUE on loop.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): rescuing a water droplet from a wave is conceptually water-from-water; the ink-black droplet color is what keeps the image legible — preserve that detail in any edit.
Minor (non-blocking): the wave+droplet pair is shared with other 求-family kanji, so distinctiveness rests entirely on the whip-rescue action.

story: On the left, a Listening Ear leans into the roaring furnace mouth; on the right, a Cracking Whip snaps, driving it nearer until the lobe blisters. That is DARING.
reading_story: Khan spurs his horse straight into the wall of spears, laughing as the shafts splinter — the steppe still sings of such DARING.
issues: Non-blocking: the 'roaring furnace mouth' is unattested scenery; it reads as setting rather than a claimed component, but a learner could back-form a fire element not present in 敢. Consider making the whip itself the hazard.

Non-blocking: reading story ('charges the wall of spears') is stock bravery imagery and may interfere with neighbouring valor kanji (勇/猛/豪); a Khan-specific detail (steppe, horsehair standard) would sharpen it.

story: KINDLINESS: a Pot Lid presses down over a shrieking Open Mouth, hushing it above the Swaddle Basket rocking below; on the right a Cracking Whip snaps only at empty air, never at the basket.
reading_story: Tony the soup-cart cook ladles free bowls to everyone shivering on the curb; the whole street calls it pure KINDLINESS.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the Pot Lid 'pressing down over' a shrieking mouth reads faintly as smothering rather than kind; the KINDLINESS payoff rests almost entirely on the whip's restraint. 'Hushing it so the baby sleeps' would align the lid beat with the keyword.

story: On the left a sloppy bundle of sticks sprawls loose; from the right the Cracking Whip lashes down, and every stick leaps into neat, straight ranks — ORGANIZE.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage strokes his beard, and cluttered scrolls glide onto their shelves — to ORGANIZE anything, summon the Sage.
issues: Minor: reading story's gliding-scroll image is softer than the main story; sage-consistent, not gating
Minor: whip-imposes-order motif is shared across 攵 kanji (e.g. 政); stick-bundle anchor mitigates collision risk

story: A drip pings the Pot Lid, Twin Pillars stand up beneath it, and the Goalpost Frame arches over Plus-Sign Crossroads and a screaming Open Mouth — then the Cracking Whip lashes in from the right, driving them at you: ENEMY.
reading_story: Tekker storms the ring, ripping his own poster in half — the fighter printed on it is tonight's ENEMY.
issues: Minor: 8 components make the scene crowded; the single composite image (drip/lid/pillars over goalpost/crossroads/mouth, whip at right) takes effort to assemble, capping imageability at 3.
Minor: reading_story links Tekker to ENEMY only via a poster-ripping scene with no component tie-in — acceptable per rubric, but the semantic bridge is thin.

story: The Ink Droplet falls at the Plus-Sign Crossroads, seeps down across the Rice-Paddy Grid, and the Cracking Whip on the right flogs it along the direction arrow below — one dot whipped into a vast black SPREAD.
reading_story: Foo the glowing orb skims the banquet table, one shining pass smearing melted butter edge to edge — a perfect SPREAD across every slice of bread.
issues: Minor: 方 has no registry actor/image; story renders it as a 'direction arrow' — the added 'arrow' visual is an acceptable gloss, not a phantom, but is generator-invented detail.
Minor: in the reading story SPREAD sits in the final payoff clause but is not the literal last word ('...a perfect SPREAD across every slice of bread').
Minor: butter-spread-on-bread is a cliché image for 'spread'; acceptable because it binds Foo (ふ) to this keyword, but it is the least original element.

story: Under a chiseled sentence, Falling Katana and Lightning Bolt drop side by side into Cupped Palms, which lay them along the Grain Comb's evenly trimmed teeth — blade, bolt, teeth all one height, perfectly ALIKE.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage trims every disciple's beard against his own; by evening all the beards in the temple hang exactly ALIKE.

story: Beneath a sacred sentence, Falling Katana slashes down the left, Lightning Bolt cracks down the right; between them Cupped Palms lift Railway Tracks while a Sand Trickle sifts down to show the shrine scrubbed clean — PURIFICATION.
reading_story: Before pitching, Cy ladles icy water over both hands at the shrine trough — one clipped splash of PURIFICATION, then he grips the ball.
issues: Reading story keyword is near-end but not final: 'then he grips the ball' trails after PURIFICATION
'A sacred sentence' (文) is a weak visual anchor — abstract object, hard to picture; consider a calligraphy banner or inscribed plaque
Scene is crowded (7 components in one tableau); 'shrine' scenery is fine but adds a non-component object to an already busy frame

story: Stage-left, the whole scene leans one direction; a Falling Katana drops, clanging onto the taut Horizon Line, while beneath it a River Eel writhes in glistening S-curves — PERFORM.
reading_story: The Sheriff kicks open the barroom doors, slaps his badge onto the piano lid, and growls at the frozen players: PERFORM.
issues: Gate 5 (actor consistency) is borderline: the Horizon Line registry persona is 'a perfectly flat desert horizon — one unbroken line where sky meets sand', but the story makes it 'taut' and has the katana 'clang' onto it, recasting it as a stretched metal wire. Not a cognitive-ability violation so it passes the stated gate, but it drifts from the persona and muddies the picture.

Concreteness weak spot: 'Stage-left, the whole scene leans one direction' is an abstract stage direction rather than an image. 方 is only carried by the bare word 'direction' embedded in a non-visual clause — the weakest link in the story for retrieval.

Possible double-encoding of 一: 'leans ONE direction' plus the separate 'Horizon Line' gives the learner two cues for the same component, risking an extra 一 on reconstruction. 'a single direction' would remove the ambiguity.

No blocking failures: all four components named (ノ=Falling Katana, 方='direction', 一=Horizon Line, 也=River Eel), no phantom actors (stage/scene is setting, not a component), Sheriff present in reading_story, PERFORM at end in both, no etymology, 28 words. Spatial fidelity is decent — stage-left for 方, katana over line, eel beneath.

story: ROTATION: a signpost on the left points its direction arrow; beside it on the right, the Fabric Roll tips over and spins, flinging its cloth strip in whirling circles around the post.
reading_story: Senna grips the wheel at Monaco, hands blurring in one continuous ROTATION as the car sweeps the hairpin.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (gate 2, phantom components): the story introduces a 'signpost' that is not a supplied component. It survives the gate only because it is the concretization vehicle for 方 and the supplied keyword word 'direction' is explicitly bound to it ('points its direction arrow'), not presented as a separate part. Flagging because 方/㫃-left neighbours (旅, 族, 施, 旗) risk reusing the same prop; if the registry later gives 方 a real actor, this story should be rewritten to use it.

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness): 'spins / whirling circles' is the most obvious possible image for 'rotation', so the scene leans on a generic motion verb; only the cloth-streamer-around-a-post (maypole) detail keeps it from being interchangeable with any other spin-themed kanji.

NON-BLOCKING (reading story): 'ROTATION' is repeated mid-sentence in reading_story. Not a rubric violation (gate 4 governs the meaning story) but it duplicates the payoff word and slightly dilutes the せん/Senna sound hook, which carries no other cue than the name itself.

story: Direction stands at the left like a flagpole; lashed to it flies a flat Candy Tin, striped candy glinting, with a Wishbone dangling beneath, legs snapping in the wind — the NATIONAL FLAG.
reading_story: At dawn Key the clipped locksmith unlocks the palace flag chest — one crisp "kee!" — and hoists the NATIONAL FLAG up the pole.
issues: Minor: 方 has no registry actor, so 'Direction' is used as an abstract concept-figure ('stands at the left like a flagpole') — acceptable per rules but slightly less imageable than an actor would be.
Minor: shared 其-family pair (Candy Tin + Wishbone) recurs across 期/基/棋/欺 mnemonics; the flagpole-lashing configuration differentiates this one adequately.

story: A Boar's Tusk juts from Still Butte's right flank, ivory weathered gray, the gouge long healed into solid rock — whatever struck here struck PREVIOUSLY.
reading_story: Key slides into a rusted lock and meets no resistance — the door swings open, oiled smooth: someone turned this lock PREVIOUSLY.
issues: Minor: 'gouge long healed into solid rock' — rock healing is a slightly abstract time cue; a more picturable trace of age (moss, sand drifts burying the scar) would push imageability to 5.

story: Balanced atop the blazing Sun, the Soup Ladle simmers golden broth in its deep bowl over that fiery burner — the rising steam smells impossibly DELICIOUS.
reading_story: The Sheriff kicks open the saloon door, tastes the stew, and barks one clipped verdict — "DELICIOUS" — before holstering his spoon.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword DELICIOUS is followed by a trailing clause ('before holstering his spoon') — still the payoff, but ending on the keyword would be cleaner
Minor: 'impossibly DELICIOUS' leans on an abstract intensifier instead of a sensory detail (smell/taste), slightly capping imageability

story: A Swaddling Wrap curls down from above and bundles the blazing Sun like a newborn; the Sun dozes tucked inside the cloth and won't shine again for one full TEN-DAY PERIOD.
reading_story: June slices her calendar page into three strips — early, mid, late — declaring each TEN-DAY PERIOD its own little month.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): reading_story keyword lands in the final clause but is trailed by 'its own little month' — payoff still reads clearly.

story: At dawn the Curled Cat uncoils on the left horizon, stretching tall as the Sun heaves itself up beside her — cat silhouette black against the blazing disk: the RISING SUN.
reading_story: RISING SUN duty: Kyoker cranks a giant winch at dawn, hauling the sun up on a rope, grunting "kyo-ku, kyo-ku" with every turn.

story: Sun blazes directly overhead while, beneath it, Twin Spoon Silhouettes stand shoulder to shoulder — identical as parent and child, every curve matching — the sunlit proof that a bloodline copies itself perfectly into its DESCENDANTS.
reading_story: Conn straightens his tuxedo at the family reunion, scanning a hall of identical chins and eyebrows: every one of them his DESCENDANTS.
issues: Story's second half is propositional rather than pictorial: 'the sunlit proof that a bloodline copies itself perfectly into its DESCENDANTS' asserts a claim instead of showing an image — the concrete scene ends at 'every curve matching'.
The parent/child resemblance link to DESCENDANTS is stated abstractly rather than staged (no visible generations, no small copies of the spoons), which weakens the meaning hook.
'compare' framing (sun overhead + two identical silhouettes side by side) is close to the generic 比 setup and risks blurring with other 比-based cards; the only differentiator is the bloodline gloss.

Minor: no gate failures — both mandatory actors named verbatim (Sun, Twin Spoon Silhouettes), no phantom components, no invented cognitive abilities, keyword at end in both stories, reading actor Conn present, 34 words.

story: One Sun settles directly atop a second Sun; stacked, they blaze with doubled daylight, and everything beneath their double brightness ripens and glitters — PROSPEROUS.
reading_story: The Showman sweeps off his top hat — "Shoooow!" — and coins cascade endlessly into it; every performance sells out, leaving him PROSPEROUS.

story: The Sun blazes on the left. Right of it the Cleaver hangs blade-down, bouncing that glare straight into the Open Mouth gaping below — throat and tongue lit up SHINING.
reading_story: The Showman tips his top hat, spotlight striking the silk, and the whole big top goes SHINING as he bellows "Shoooow!"
issues: Distinctiveness risk: 'sun makes it shine' is the default framing for this keyword and 昭 neighbours 照 (illuminate), which literally contains it, plus 明/昌/晶 in the same 日-brightness cluster; only the cleaver-reflector hook separates them.
Keyword 'SHINING' is reused in the reading story, weakening its role as the exclusive payoff of the meaning story.
Both stories run the same 'light bounces off a shiny surface' beat (blade glare / spotlight on silk), so meaning and reading lines are less mutually distinctive than ideal.

story: The midday Sun blazes directly overhead; below it, the Fabric Roll unspools its cloth in one dead-straight, wrinkle-free line aligned with the light — everything JUST SO.
reading_story: Zeh straightens the picture frame one millimeter, steps back, and grunts in his deep voice: "JUST SO."
issues: Non-gating: reading story uses a picture frame rather than reusing the sun/fabric scene — slight cohesion loss between meaning and reading stories.

story: High above, the Sun blazes; below it three Bean Sprouts perch on the Horizon Line, itself balanced on stubby Wishing-Well Legs — desert air so sharp you count every sprout hair. CLEAR.
reading_story: Coe sprints the final lap; the stadium haze lifts and the finish tape stands CLEAR ahead of him.
issues: (non-blocking) Slight setting friction: Bean Sprouts are defined as pushing up through soil, but the scene is set in the Horizon Line's desert — sand vs soil is a small coherence wobble, not a phantom element.
(non-blocking) The main story is a static vertical stack (sun above, sprouts on line on legs) with no action or causal hook; the only dynamic beat is the 'count every sprout hair' sensory line.

story: ADVANCE: the Sun rolls flat-out across the dunes, white-hot dot at its center, plowing a smoking furrow of sand forward, while the Horizon Line stays ruled taut and unbroken above the whole charge.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender kicks the stools aside and shoves his entire counter three feet toward the door, forcing the packed crowd to ADVANCE with him.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk, docs/07 §3 item 10): the 日 + horizontal-line pairing is shared with many neighbors (旦, 早, 亘, 昌, 百); recall leans entirely on the desert/furrow setting to disambiguate. If a nearby N1 card reuses a desert or rolling-sun image, re-check for interference.

story: One Sun balanced atop two more Suns, all three blazing at once — the tripled midday light stacks up and detonates into a single blinding SPARKLE.
reading_story: The top-hatted Showman flings his arms wide, roaring "Shoooow!" — and the whole big top erupts in one dazzling SPARKLE.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS — the sole mandatory actor 日/Sun is named and used three times, matching the glyph's three 日: 'One Sun balanced atop two more Suns'. Registry image ('bright round midday sun blazing') is honored via 'blazing at once' / 'tripled midday light'.

Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS — meaning story names only Suns. Reading story's 'top hat' and 'big top' come from the Showman persona note ('top-hatted circus ringmaster'), not invented components.
Gate 3 (reading actor present) PASS — 'the top-hatted Showman ... roaring "Shoooow!"' matches reading_actor Showman and encodes the long ō per docs/07 §1.2 (vowel length in persona).
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS — keyword is the terminal payoff in both stories ('...into a single blinding SPARKLE'), consistent with meaning_placement 'end'.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS — no persona drift; Sun behaves as a blazing light source, Showman as a ringmaster. Only ordinary physical behavior (stacking, blazing, arms flung wide); no invented cognitive faculty.
Gate 6 (no false etymology) PASS — no origin claim is made; the three-suns arrangement is presented as an imaginative visual, not a historical derivation.
Gate 7 (length) PASS — story 25 words, reading story 22 words, both well under ~40.
Spatial fidelity is a strength: 'One Sun balanced atop two more Suns' correctly renders 晶's one-over-two layout rather than a vague pile.

Weakness (non-gating, docs/07 §3 item 10): the reading story is formulaic — 'Showman roars Shoooow! and the tent erupts in KEYWORD' is a template that will recur across every しょう kanji, contributing nothing 晶-specific. It hooks the keyword but not the glyph.

Weakness (non-gating): interference risk with the listed phonetic neighbor 昌 (two stacked 日). The only discriminator is the count 'all three'; if 昌's story also leans on stacked Suns, the pair may blur. The explicit 'all three' plus the detonation payoff mitigates but does not eliminate this.

story: A Feathered Arrow flies straight into the Open Mouth beside it; below them, the Sun rises to floodlight the pair — swallowing a straight answer under full daylight is WISDOM.
reading_story: Chee snaps one clipped cheer — "Chee!" — then falls silent; the sage bows: knowing when to stop is WISDOM.
issues: Non-blocking: distinctiveness risk with phonetic sibling 知, which shares the arrow-into-mouth core image; only the Sun/'full daylight' element differentiates 智 — monitor for interference in review data.
Non-blocking: 'the sage' in the reading story is an unregistered bystander (generic scenery, not a component actor) — acceptable per gating rules but keep an eye on scenery creep.

story: SPARE TIME: the Sun blazes over the left half of the sky while a yellow Rubber Glove lies palm-up on the right windowsill, fingers curled around nothing.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr parks his taxi, tips his cap over his eyes — no fares all afternoon, nothing but SPARE TIME.
issues: Imageability (graded, non-gating): the two actors share a frame but never interact — the Sun 'blazes' and the Rubber Glove 'lies', with no causal link between them. Per docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §2 Stage 2 the target is 'one vivid/striking image'; this reads as a spatial inventory (same failure mode logged for 之 in data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json, which also scored imageability 3).
Mundanity: a glove on a sunlit windowsill is an entirely ordinary scene with no bizarre, emotional or surprising hook. Concrete and picturable, but low arousal means weaker encoding.

Meaning payoff is a label, not an event: 'SPARE TIME:' is asserted up front as a heading and the scene never earns it — only 'fingers curled around nothing' gestures at idleness. Gate 4 passes (start placement, matches meaning_placement 'start'), but the keyword is stapled on rather than delivered.

Distinctiveness risk: 日 and 又 are among the highest-frequency components in the corpus, so 'the Sun blazes on the left / [object] on the right' is a template that will recur across many neighbours. Only the windowsill + empty-glove detail discriminates.

Phantom-component check passes but note the added props ('sky', 'windowsill', and in the reading story 'taxi', 'cap'): these are scene staging, not registry actors, consistent with accepted entries (e.g. 'desert'/'sand' in 丁, 'subway platform' in 乏). No component outside 日/又 is personified.

Data-level observation (not the candidate's fault, not gating): dominant_reading is kun ひま, yet reading_actor is か (Carr). The reading story therefore drills か while the headword vocab 暇 is read ひま; か is only justified via 休暇. Worth a pipeline check on reading-actor selection for kun-dominant kanji.

Unused phonetic_extra 叚 — not required by the gates, but the 又 in this kanji is actually nested inside 叚, so the flat left/right staging is a simplification of the real geometry (spatial fidelity is otherwise correct: 日 left, 又-bearing element right).

story: The Sun hangs dead overhead, roasting the Greybeard Mask below it; the carved wooden face sweats resin, its long grey beard dripping and steaming in air so thick it feels SULTRY.
reading_story: Shaw fans himself with his own manuscript in a packed theatre, collar soaked through — even his wit wilts in the SULTRY heat.
issues: Minor: reading story keyword is penultimate word ("SULTRY heat") rather than final word — still end-placed, non-blocking
Minor: "even his wit wilts" is a slightly abstract flourish in the reading story
Watch-item: Greybeard Mask + heat imagery has mild interference potential with 煮 (boil) in the 者 phonetic family

story: Left, the Sun blazes; right, a Hawk Talon clamps down onto the flat Horizon Line, and beneath that line your friend curls up, cheeks reddening in the stacked glow — WARMTH.
reading_story: Dan cranks the radiator dial, then presses both palms flat against its ribs, grinning as WARMTH floods the frozen room.
issues: Non-gating: distinctiveness is the weak axis - Sun + WARMTH is the most predictable pairing available and is likely to interfere with neighbours 温, 暑, 熱 that will recruit the same Sun actor and the same payoff keyword. Consider leaning harder on the Talon/Horizon oddity as the retrieval hook.

Non-gating (coherence): the story is a stacked tableau rather than a causal chain - the Hawk Talon clamping the Horizon Line does not act on the friend or produce the glow, so the middle component is spatially placed but narratively inert.
Non-gating (imageability): 'stacked glow' is the one abstract phrase in an otherwise fully concrete scene; a physical heat source would image better.
Non-gating: WARMTH terminates both the meaning story and the reading story, which slightly flattens the contrast between the two cards.

story: Under the Rock Overhang, a grove stands in tidy rows; low beneath the trunks the Sun blazes, scorching one fresh black char-mark into the cliff floor each dawn — a burning CALENDAR.
reading_story: Recker rips last month off the wall CALENDAR, wrecking the page into confetti, then hammers the next month up with one nail.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'one ... each dawn' turns the scene into a time-lapse rather than a single frozen image, slightly weakening snapshot recall; 'a fresh mark each morning' inside one dawn scene would be tighter.
Minor (non-blocking): 'low beneath the trunks the Sun blazes' is momentarily ambiguous spatially (sun under the grove yet under the overhang) though it does mirror the glyph stacking correctly.

story: DAWN: Sun hauls his blazing round face over the left horizon, his tiny center dot glaring straight into the police station on his right, flooding its barred cells with first pink light.
reading_story: Shaw, silver beard aflame, stands on the police station steps declaring that DAWN has arrived precisely on cue.
issues: Non-gating (distinctiveness): the story is close to a literal restatement of the keyword (sun rising = dawn), so it risks interference with dawn/morning neighbours 暁, 旭, 朝, 晨; only the police-station cells differentiate it.

Non-gating (actor consistency, minor): 日's registry image specifies a *midday* sun in a clear sky, while the story stages it low on the horizon in pink first light — staging/motion rather than a persona contradiction, so it passes gate 5.

Non-gating (redundancy): 'DAWN' is repeated in the reading_story, which spends words on the meaning instead of anchoring the しょ reading; Shaw is present so gate 3 passes, but the reading link (Shaw = しょ) carries little distinctive hook of its own.

story: Beside the Still Butte, the Full Moon rises at its right shoulder, silver light washing the flat stone; nothing moves, nothing sounds — the desert night is utterly SERENE.
reading_story: After the filthiest job of his life, Rowe rinses off, exhales one long slow breath, and lies back completely SERENE.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): 'still moonlit night = peaceful' is a stock trope; scene could mildly interfere with other calm/quiet-register keywords if those also use nocturnal stillness — the unique Still Butte + Full Moon pairing and the right-shoulder spatial anchor mitigate this.

story: The Falling Katana slices down from above, splitting the Unripe Peach below; out of the hard green flesh gushes thick molten pigment that drenches the blade — VERMILION.
reading_story: Master Shu dips his brush in the lacquer pot and signs his name across the temple gate in dripping VERMILION.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): combined story + reading_story is ~47 words; each individually is within budget (27 / 20).

Minor (non-blocking): 'thick molten pigment' gushing from hard green flesh is a property surprise rather than a natural consequence — it works as a hook but leans on the reader accepting the peach as a pigment source.

story: Tinsel, gold paint and glass baubles rain onto Tree; each one slides straight down the slick trunk and piles into a bright tangle at its roots, leaving every branch above stubbornly PLAIN.
reading_story: Booker strips the gaudy jackets off every book on his shelf and rebinds them in coarse grey cloth — a whole wall of identical, unlabelled, PLAIN spines.
issues: Non-blocking: reading_story leans on the default Booker-to-books association, which is likely to recur across other ぼく entries (木, 目, 牧, 僕, 撲, 睦, 墨) and risks interference; only the coarse grey rebinding distinguishes it.
Non-blocking: the meaning payoff is an absence (bare branches) rather than a positive image, which slightly weakens imageability.
Non-blocking: phonetic_extra 卜 is unused — permitted, but a hook there could have raised distinctiveness.

story: In a shrine courtyard, Tree stands tall while Comb Streaks score three diagonal slashes down its right flank; fragrant red sap streams from every cut — the unmistakable perfume of CEDAR.
reading_story: Santa sniffs the winter air, follows the scent through deep snow, and stacks every present beneath one enormous CEDAR.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): Santa stacking presents beneath a tree evokes a Christmas pine/fir, a slight interference risk with 松 (pine); mitigated by CEDAR being the explicit end payoff in both stories.
Minor (non-blocking): 'fragrant'/'perfume'/'scent' lean olfactory rather than visual in both stories, slightly diluting imageability.

story: Beneath the Tree a Swaddle Basket rocks; peel back the swaddling and there is no baby inside — just one huge, dew-wet purple PLUM.
reading_story: Lee coils, snaps his famous one-inch punch — the PLUM explodes into purple mist across the dojo.

story: Above the bare Tree, the Cracking Whip snaps down, driving the muddy Trailing Footprint across a parchment nailed to the topmost branch — each lash underlining one numbered clause of the ARTICLE.
reading_story: Average Joe refuses to sign: every ARTICLE hides one more condition, and he groans a long "Joooooe..." at each new clause.
issues: Minor: the footprint being 'driven across' the parchment is slightly surreal — picturable as a muddy smear, but costs a half-second of assembly (imageability docked to 4).
Minor: three actors plus a parchment prop make the scene a touch busy, though it stays one coherent frame and within length.

story: A Wishbone snaps in half above a Sealed Clam-Locket dangling from the Tree's branch; the secret wish locked inside seeps into the trunk, sprouting evergreen needles — a PINE TREE.
reading_story: The Showman sweeps off his top hat — "Shoooow!" — and a full-grown PINE TREE springs from it, showering needles over the circus ring.
issues: Minor: 'secret wish seeps into the trunk' is a slightly abstract, invisible action — the weakest visual beat in an otherwise concrete scene.
