Minor: in the reading_story the keyword PINE TREE is followed by a trailing clause ('showering needles over the circus ring') rather than closing the sentence; still reads as the payoff, non-blocking.
Watch-item: other 公-family kanji staging Wishbone-above-Clam-Locket could partially interfere; the evergreen-needle payoff keeps this one distinct.

story: The Tree on the left bends its two branches and two roots into a square around the Curled Cat napping atop the Plus-Sign Crossroads — one living wooden FRAME.
The Tree stands left; bolted to its trunk, the metal Toolbox Tray swings wide, open face flashing right, tools rattling inside three walls — that trunk is the door's HINGE.
reading_story: Soo oils a shrieking garden gate all afternoon; one last drop, and the rusted HINGE finally swings silent.
issues: Non-blocking: the 匚 registry image fixes the tray's open mouth as 'facing right', but the story has it 'flashing right' while swinging wide — a swinging tray cannot hold a fixed orientation, so the mental picture wobbles slightly. Tightening to something like 'open mouth sweeping past' would preserve fidelity.

Non-blocking: role reassignment at the payoff — the Toolbox Tray is the moving subject for most of the sentence, then the final clause makes the *trunk* the HINGE (tray = door). Resolvable, but it costs a beat of re-imagining and is the main reason imageability is 4 not 5.

Note: distinctiveness rests almost entirely on the Toolbox Tray, since 木 recurs across a large share of the corpus. Fine here (匚+木 pairing is rare), but the tray must stay vivid in sibling stories to avoid interference.

story: High on the left a Flexing Bicep strains; high on the right an Open Mouth roars; below, a bare Tree swings up off the ground into the gap — heave, ERECT!
reading_story: Cabbie Carr abandons his taxi mid-street, shoulders the fallen signpost, and strains to ERECT it upright again before the light turns green.
issues: Non-blocking: the pivot image 'swings up off the ground into the gap' has no agent doing the lifting — the Flexing Bicep is placed high-left and never touches the Tree, so 'heave' is a disembodied shout and the causal chain to ERECT is loose.
Non-blocking: 'the gap' is undefined; the learner has to infer it means the space under the 力/口 pair, which softens an otherwise sharp spatial layout.
Non-blocking: the Tree self-propels ('swings up off the ground'). Ordinary physical motion, so not a gate failure, but it is unmotivated rather than inanimate-consistent.

Non-blocking: 力+口 is a very high-frequency pairing (加, 賀, 駕, 迦, 嘉) and 'strain/heave' is the default 力 script, so the meaning story sits close to its neighbours; the reading story (taxi, fallen signpost, traffic light) carries most of the distinctiveness.
Note: reading_story repeats the keyword ERECT. Permitted and mildly reinforcing, but it means the reading story is doing meaning work the meaning story should own.

story: A bare Tree stands beside a Goalpost Frame; the flat Horizon Line lies along its crossbar, a Stepladder parked inside the goal — the whole scene composed into one striking DESIGN.
reading_story: President Hayes stretches wallpaper across the White House wall, smoothing his long beard until every repeating DESIGN lines up perfectly.
issues: Static tableau: 'composed into one striking DESIGN' asserts the keyword rather than showing an action that embodies it (imageability capped at 3)
Distinctiveness vs other 丙-family kanji rests only on the Tree, since Horizon Line + Goalpost Frame + Stepladder recur across that family

story: Puddle Splash flicks deep-red droplets rightward, soaking the Curled Cat perched atop the Tree; white fur and pale bark bloom crimson — a perfect DYE.
reading_story: Senna spins through a vat of DYE — his white McLaren emerges crimson, painting dyed tire stripes down the track.
issues: Minor: registry image for 氵 has droplets flicked leftward, story flicks them rightward — scene-motivated by glyph layout (氵 left of 九/木), ordinary physical motion, non-blocking

story: Tree stands on the left, trailing long drooping branches; on the right the Wax Stamp presses a red seal onto each dangling tip, and the strands sag lower under the wax — a weeping WILLOW.
reading_story: Ryu trains under the WILLOW, punching through its curtain of branches — every strand whips back and slaps his headband.

story: The Setting-Sun Cage sits balanced atop the Tree; as the red sun sinks behind its bars, the branches beneath shudder and every spiky burr splits open, spilling one glossy brown CHESTNUT.
reading_story: Ritter juggles a scalding CHESTNUT hand to hand, yelping, then trips backwards over the porch rail still clutching it.
issues: Non-blocking: the Tree registry image specifies a 'bare' tree, and the story has burrs splitting on its branches — a slight drift from the persona's stated bareness, though physical fruiting is not a nature contradiction.

Non-blocking: the causal link between the sun sinking behind the cage bars and the burrs splitting is asserted rather than motivated ('branches beneath shudder'), which slightly loosens scene coherence.
Non-blocking: near-neighbour risk with 票 (also 覀-on-top); the Tree + burr + glossy brown chestnut payoff is what carries the separation, so keep that detail if the story is ever trimmed.

story: On the left Tree stands firm; from the right a cow charges headlong, horns slamming the trunk — with each blow, share certificates rain down from Tree's branches: STOCKS.
reading_story: Shu smugly fans himself with a thick wad of STOCKS certificates, refusing to sell a single share.
issues: Minor: certificates raining from branches after horn blows is causally arbitrary (leaves would be the natural fall) — acceptable surrealism, slightly slows first visualization.
Minor: reading_story is disconnected from the tree/cow scene; permissible, but a Shu-at-the-tree link would bind reading to meaning more tightly.

story: Tree stands left of a stone tablet carved with the sign of the hog; the trunk splits open where they touch, exposing at its heart a glowing NUCLEUS.
reading_story: Knuckles the boxer punches an atom-model piñata; the NUCLEUS pops out and dents his glove.
issues: Distinctiveness risk: 'stone tablet carved with the sign of the hog' overlaps the natural mnemonic territory of neighbor 刻 (engrave, also 亥-family) — evidence: 'carved with the sign of the hog'; consider 'painted/bearing the sign of the hog' to avoid interference.

Minor: the 'stone tablet' prop faintly evokes a 石 component not in the glyph; acceptable as scenery (components_used is exactly 木+亥) but a hog-sign banner or standing stone-free carrier would be cleaner.

story: PLANTATION, day one: the Barbed Pike's hooked spur rips open the Mound of Soil above, spilling it down over the bare Tree's roots below, then plants itself upright at the right, marking the row.
reading_story: Cy retires from baseball and buys a PLANTATION, setting one sapling for every strikeout he ever threw — rows of trees stretching past the horizon.
issues: Non-blocking: 'the Barbed Pike ... plants itself upright' gives an inanimate prop reflexive self-motion. Judged acceptable as ordinary physical motion consistent with its registry image ('planted upright in the dirt'), not an invented cognitive ability, but it is the weakest line in the story if a stricter pass is applied.
Non-blocking: distinctiveness leans on the pike-as-row-marker alone; the soil-onto-roots core is the generic 'planting' gestalt and could interfere with neighboring cultivation kanji (e.g. 植, 培).

story: Tree stands on the left, bark curling off in tight brown quills; snap one and the whole street fills with hot bakery spice — Tree is a CINNAMON TREE.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer twirls onstage, her long feathered fan flinging spice dust she shook from the CINNAMON TREE.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: the sole mandatory component 木 is named as its registry actor "Tree" ("Tree stands on the left"), and components_used matches.
Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS: "bark", "quills", "street", "bakery spice" are material/setting descriptors of the supplied Tree, not added personas — no second actor is introduced where 圭 sits.

Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: "Kayo the cabaret dancer" opens the reading story; persona matches the record note ("Kayo, the cabaret dancer") and shipped corpus usage (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:2394, 2559, 5643 — feather boa / feathered headdress); "long feathered fan" weakly gestures at the long ē required by docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §1.2.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: CINNAMON TREE is the final two words of both stories; meaning_placement "end" is accurate.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: nothing contradicts the "sturdy bare tree, straight trunk" persona — curling bark and snapping a quill are ordinary physical properties, no invented cognitive ability.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS — no derivation claim, framed purely as scene.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: 28 words main story, 19 words reading story, both under the ~40 cap in docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §3.7.

Spatial fidelity is partial: "on the left" is correct for 木 in 桂, but phonetic_extra 圭 (the entire right half) is unencoded. Non-gating per established precedent (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:1037, 1581, 1956), but it follows the 街 ruling at data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:6756 where an unused 圭 capped distinctiveness at 3 — the glyph's right half has no hook, so the story under-determines 桂 against other 木+X species kanji.

Interference risk with 杉 CEDAR (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:3678): both are aromatic-tree payoffs built on damaging the tree to release scent ("fragrant red sap streams from every cut — the unmistakable perfume of CEDAR" vs "snap one and the whole street fills with hot bakery spice"). The images differ (red sap vs brown quills, forest perfume vs bakery), and 杉 anchors its right side with Comb Streaks, so this is a caution rather than a collision — but it is the main drag on distinctiveness.

Imageability caveat: the sharp visual is confined to "bark curling off in tight brown quills" (accurate to real cinnamon quills, so it doubles as a meaning cue); the payoff clause is olfactory and not depictable, and "Tree stands on the left" is generic staging.

Non-blocking record note (not the candidate's fault): dominant_reading is kun かつら while reading_actor is on-yomi けい, so the reading story drills a non-dominant reading — contrary to docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md §1.3 ("kun'yomi get no reading actor"). Same flag already raised at data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:1115 and :6581; worth an upstream data check.

story: A bare Tree leans left; right of it, Frost Beads glitter above the stone Wishing-Well Legs. The Tree's outstretched branch lowers into that gap one fuzzy, blush-pink PEACH.
reading_story: Tone growls a raspy verse, then bites a dripping PEACH mid-rhyme; juice soaks the microphone and the crowd roars.
issues: PASS coverage: all three supplied actors named verbatim - 'a bare Tree' (木), 'Frost Beads glitter' (冫), 'the stone Wishing-Well Legs' (儿).

PASS no phantom: only extra nouns are 'branch' (explicitly part of the Tree's registry image: 'two branches reaching up') and 'PEACH' (the keyword itself). No unsupplied component or actor introduced; 兆 is never named or hinted at.

PASS actor consistency: 'bare Tree' matches 'sturdy bare tree'; 'stone Wishing-Well Legs' matches 'two stubby stone legs'; 'Frost Beads glitter' is consistent with 'little beads of ice'. Tone Loc growling 'a raspy verse' matches the rapper persona. No invented cognitive faculty - a branch lowering fruit is ordinary tree physics, allowed by the gate.
PASS reading actor: 'Tone' opens the reading_story and matches reading_actor_used.
PASS meaning placement: story ends on '...one fuzzy, blush-pink PEACH.' - declared 'end', matches.
PASS no etymology: no historical/phonetic claims anywhere.
PASS length: story 28 words, reading_story 19 words - both under the ~40 cap (rubric §3 item 7, docs/07-CONTENT-GENERATION.md:96).

MINOR (non-gating, imageability): 'lowers into that gap one fuzzy, blush-pink PEACH' uses inverted object order and an underspecified referent ('that gap' = between beads and legs?), which slows the first mental render.

MINOR (non-gating, coherence): Frost Beads and Wishing-Well Legs are static scenery - they take no part in the peach action, so the three elements form a tableau rather than one causally bound striking image.

MINOR (non-gating, distinctiveness): 木 + fruit is a crowded neighbourhood (梅/杏/柿/桜); the story leans on the frost-beads-over-well-legs pair to disambiguate, which it does, but the peach itself carries no unique hook beyond 'fuzzy, blush-pink'.

story: An Hourglass balances atop the Tree's branches; the Thatched House descends, capping them both before the last sand grain falls — roof over timer over trunk, all in order: the PLAN.
reading_story: Princess Ann kneels over a candlelit map of the palace, tracing her midnight escape route — every guard shift marked. She folds it, whispering: "The PLAN is ready."
issues: Non-gating: mild interference risk with 安 (same Thatched House-over-Hourglass configuration); the Tree and the sand-countdown are the only differentiators — keep them prominent.
Non-gating: the bridge 'all in order: the PLAN' is slightly abstract; the pictorial payoff relies on the deadline clause rather than the keyword phrase itself.

story: A lone Tree stands left of a Goalpost Frame; a Horizon Line hangs bolted across its uprights, and below it an Open Mouth bellows the tree's name skyward: PAULOWNIA.
reading_story: Tone growls a gravel-voiced verse into the mic, and the whole stage — planks, riser, speaker box — rings back, because it is built of PAULOWNIA.

story: Dark purple juice drips from a yellow Rubber Glove lying palm-up in the bare Tree's topmost fork, staining the trunk below in long sticky streaks — MULBERRY.
reading_story: Sosa swings for the fences and shatters a low MULBERRY branch; purple juice sprays across home plate.
issues: Distinctiveness soft spot: the Rubber Glove is passive scenery (it lies in the fork and drips) rather than doing anything glove-specific; the memorable element is generic 'purple berry juice on a tree', which risks interference with other fruit/tree kanji.
Advisory, record-level not candidate-level: dominant_reading is kun くわ but reading_actor is the on-reading そう (Sosa), so reading_story trains a reading the record flags as non-dominant.

story: Next to the Tree stands an Hourglass with three Bean Sprouts perched on its top bulb; each grain of streaming sand turns into a pink petal that settles on the Tree — CHERRY.
reading_story: Owen the keeper unlocks his orchard at dawn and polishes one glossy CHERRY, holding it up like a ruby.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword CHERRY is followed by a trailing simile ('holding it up like a ruby'), so it is near-end rather than the absolute final word — payoff still clear, not buried.

Minor: story imagery is blossom (pink petals) while reading_story imagery is fruit ('glossy CHERRY... like a ruby') — the two stories evoke slightly different cherry concepts, a small coherence/interference nick.

Note: sand-to-petal transformation is magical, but it is a physical/visual event consistent with the Hourglass's defined sand-streaming nature, not an invented cognitive ability — allowed under the gating rule.

story: The Tree holds a Milk Jug against its right side; an Iron Padlock snaps the jug's spouts shut, so the trapped milk sweetens, ferments, and bursts through the clay as one wine-dark PLUM.
reading_story: By leans on the orchard gate biting a PLUM; the sour juice makes By pucker mid-poem.
issues: Minor: 'sweetens, ferments' is a non-visual process step in the causal chain; the story leans on an implied transformation (milk -> plum) rather than a fully seen one.
Minor: keyword PLUM sits mid-clause in the reading story rather than at an edge; acceptable per shipped N1 precedent (main-story placement gate is at end and passes).

story: Tree stands rooted while every fruit ripening in his upper branches is pure profit — golden pears heavy as coin-purses, jingling in the wind. Merchants camp beneath this PEAR TREE.
reading_story: Lee snap-kicks the PEAR TREE once; a single perfect pear drops straight into his open palm, unbruised.
issues: Non-blocking: 'merchants' are extra scene dressing (acceptable props, not phantoms) but slightly dilute the single-image focus of the meaning story.

story: A whole generation climbs the bare Tree, balances a Sealed Clam-Locket of family secrets overhead, clamps the Pot Lid down on top, then walks away without looking back — ABANDON.
reading_story: Key the clipped locksmith seals the empty house with one final click, pockets nothing, and chalks ABANDON across the door before vanishing.

story: Tree shakes its two upraised branches; a pale knot of wood drops, bounces off a root, and lands upright on a checkered stump — a perfect five-sided CHESS PIECE.
reading_story: Key slides into a keyhole atop the king CHESS PIECE, turns with one clipped click, and the piece pops open, spilling tiny captured pawns.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): き/Key serves many N1 kanji (基, 機, 期, 器…) and 木 is a crowded component, so the generic 'Tree drops a wooden object' opening carries mild interference risk — the checkered stump / five-sided shogi piece / keyhole-in-king imagery mitigates it.
Minor (non-blocking): 'pale knot of wood' → 'perfect five-sided chess piece' is a slightly abstract transformation; cost it one imageability point.

story: The Tree stands at left, one branch jutting right; the Full Moon rests on that branch, faint stripes glowing, far too heavy to lift down. That branch is the world's highest SHELF.
reading_story: Ho wedges himself in the chimney and unloads every present onto the mantel SHELF, belly shaking, stockings swinging beneath the SHELF's edge.
issues: Non-blocking: reading_story buries SHELF mid-clause and then repeats it ("the SHELF's edge"); the repetition adds no image and the keyword would land harder if used once, terminally.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): Santa/chimney/stockings is generic Ho set-dressing likely to recur across other ほう kanji, so the reading story carries less discriminative power than the main story.

story: Tree lies down along the very peak of a half-built roof, straight trunk spanning end to end, branches hooked over one gable, roots over the other — the whole Tree has become the RIDGEPOLE.
reading_story: Tone straddles the RIDGEPOLE at the topping-out ceremony, rapping in his long, slow drawl; every bar booms down the beam and rattles the rafters.

story: EXAMINATION time: a Stepladder straddles a giant Open Mouth while the Tree beside them dips one bare branch past its rungs, deep down the throat like a wooden tongue depressor.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll clicks off his own head and hands it over for EXAMINATION — even dolls dread the yearly checkup.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): reading story attributes emotion to Ken ('even dolls dread the yearly checkup') — persona-flavored narration, not an invented cognitive ability, so gate 5 still passes.

Minor (non-blocking): meaning story stages two simultaneous actions (Stepladder straddling + Tree dipping); they fuse into one checkup scene but slightly dilute the single-image ideal of rubric item 7/9.

story: On the left, bare Tree plants his roots deep; from the right, spring washes up his trunk, and every branch tip opens into a fat waxy crimson CAMELLIA.
reading_story: Chin the boxer takes a hook to the jaw; instead of blood, a red CAMELLIA drops from his mouth onto the canvas.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness risk): 'spring washes up his trunk' reads as a water spring, not the season 春. 'washes' is a water verb, so the cue may retrieve 泉/湧 instead of 春. Suggest 'springtime sun climbs his trunk' or 'spring warmth creeps up his trunk' to lock the season sense.

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness ~3): the meaning story is close to the literal semantics (tree + spring = flowering tree), so it competes with other tree-blossom kanji neighbours (桜, 梅, 楓, 杏). The only differentiator is 'fat waxy crimson'; the waxy-petal detail is the load-bearing hook and should be kept if revised.
NON-BLOCKING: 'On the left ... from the right' is spatial scaffolding rather than a concrete scene element; it earns spatial fidelity but adds no image. Fine as-is.

GATE CHECKS PASSED (evidence): (1) coverage — 木/Tree named verbatim ('bare Tree plants his roots deep'), 春 named by keyword ('spring washes up his trunk'); (2) no phantoms — 'roots', 'trunk', 'branch' are all in Tree's registry image, and 'hook/jaw/canvas' belong to the Chin-the-boxer persona, not to invented components; (3) reading actor — 'Chin the boxer takes a hook to the jaw' matches the note 'Chin, the boxer (chin)'; (4) meaning lands — CAMELLIA is the final word of the story, consistent with meaning_placement='end'; (5) persona consistency — Tree stays a passive rooted tree, Chin stays a boxer, no invented cognitive faculties ('plants his roots', 'branch tip opens' are ordinary physical motion for a tree); (6) no etymology — the tree+spring pairing is presented as an image, never as a historical claim; (7) length — story 28 words, reading story 24 words, both under ~40.

story: From the left bank, Tree leans out over the water: straight trunk bowing, its two raised branches sagging until their tips trail in the current, roots half-drowned — a weeping WILLOW.
reading_story: Yoyo sits beneath the trailing WILLOW, cello braced between his knees, drawing long notes while green strands brush his shoulders.
issues: Water imagery is heavy ('over the water', 'in the current', 'roots half-drowned', 'left bank') for a kanji with no water element; it does not name a registry actor so gate 2 passes, but a learner could back-infer a phantom 氵/水 component. Consider thinning to a single water mention.

Near-definitional, so distinctiveness is only average: 'a tree drooping over a river' IS the literal weeping willow, so the story restates the keyword rather than supplying an odd hook that separates 楊 from neighbouring 木 kanji.

Minor persona friction: the 木 image is 'a sturdy bare tree', while the reading story adds 'green strands' brushing Yoyo's shoulders. Defensible as the willow's own foliage, but it drifts from the registry's bare-tree look.
Reading story buries WILLOW mid-sentence. Gate 4 is scored on the meaning story (which ends on it), so this is not a failure, but front/end placement there too would be stronger.
Note in the story's favour: 'From the left bank' correctly stages 木 as the left radical, and 'drawing long notes' reinforces the long ō of よう — both worth preserving in any revision.

story: At sunset a Tree, the Still Butte, and one giant Boar's Tusk stand in a row on the horizon; their jagged black silhouette burns into the sky as a single OUTLINE.
reading_story: Guy Fawkes chalks a rough OUTLINE of Parliament on the cellar wall, an X marking where each powder barrel goes.
issues: Non-blocking: dusk-silhouette trope overlaps an existing N1 reading story ("a lone FIGURE stands silhouetted at the far end of the dusty street") — semantically adjacent keyword (figure/outline), though different components and story role.
Non-blocking: "chalks a rough OUTLINE" echoes the shipped N2 reading story for TERRITORY ("Ryo ... chalks a body outline"); different actor (Guy Fawkes vs Ryo) and reading, so low interference risk.

story: A Tree leans left, its trunk hollowed and brimming. Right of it a Lightning Bolt stabs straight down through the flat Horizon Line into the Sun steaming at the bottom of the VAT.
reading_story: Sosa swings at the plate; the ball rockets into the brewery's giant VAT, splashing beer over the roaring crowd.
issues: Coherence: 'its trunk hollowed and brimming' primes the Tree as the vat, but the VAT then turns out to be the structure to its right — a brief misparse before the image settles.
'the VAT' is introduced with a definite article and no antecedent; nothing earlier in the story establishes a vat for it to refer back to.

Scale mismatch: the Horizon Line's registry image is a planetary desert horizon, incongruous inside a vat-sized scene. It only resolves if the reader silently re-reads it as the flat liquid surface — the story never makes that link explicit.
'brimming' with what is left unspecified, so the Tree's most vivid detail has no concrete content.

story: At a windswept crossroads, Tree stretches one stiff branch sideways; its bark cracks into carved arrows and place-names, the trunk bleaching white — Tree has become a SIGNPOST.
reading_story: Exiled Hugo trudges toward Guernsey, pauses at a SIGNPOST, and scribbles a whole chapter of Les Misérables across its arrow.
issues: Minor (non-gating): phonetic 票 from phonetic_extra is unused, so no hook ties this to the 票 sound-family (漂/慓), slightly weakening series-level distinctiveness.
Minor (non-gating): 'Tree becomes an object' is a recurring transformation pattern across 木-component kanji; the crossroads/carved-arrows details mitigate but do not eliminate interference risk.

story: IMITATION — at sunset Tree performs wild poses: branches flung skyward, trunk bent double. On the wall to its right, Tree's shadow copies every move flawlessly, a dark twin it cannot shake off.
reading_story: Mo mimics everyone at the party — walk, laugh, accent — until nobody can tell who's real. Mo bows: master of IMITATION.

story: A Tree looms on the left; against its trunk a Stemmed Goblet balances a Mound of Soil on its lid; at right a Tape Measure snaps out one inch across fresh-cut TIMBER.
reading_story: Juju yells "TIMBER!" and a whole stack of planks crashes past her onto the sawdust floor.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness, rubric #10): 'Tree' + 'fresh-cut TIMBER' + a shouted 'TIMBER!' with crashing planks is the most predictable possible pairing for a wood kanji, and collides with the neighbourhood 木 / 材 / 板 / 森. The unique retrieval hooks are carried entirely by the goblet-with-soil-on-its-lid and the one-inch tape measure; strip those and the story would cue half a dozen other kanji.

NON-BLOCKING (coherence/imageability, rubric #9, #12): the two halves do not interact. The Goblet+Soil stack merely 'balances' beside the trunk while the Tape Measure acts on the timber elsewhere in the frame; nothing causally links the stack to the payoff, so the middle column is the piece most likely to be dropped on recall.

NON-BLOCKING (style): the scene is narrated as glyph layout ('looms on the left', 'at right') rather than as an event, which reads as template phrasing; a single action tying goblet, soil and measure into the felling would raise imageability without adding words (still 32/40).

NON-BLOCKING: the reading_story reuses the keyword as the lumberjack shout ('TIMBER!'). Not a rubric violation (gate #4 governs the meaning story, where TIMBER is correctly final), and the pun is mnemonically useful, but it does make the reading story lean on the meaning story rather than standing alone for じゅ/Juju.

story: Left of the Castle Gate stands a Tree; inside the open gateway the Sun sinks to the Horizon Line above a Rice-Paddy Grid, and a Lightning Bolt stabs down through them — one blazing COLUMN.
reading_story: Lannister presses his gold lion seal into a marble COLUMN, crimson banner unfurling down the fluted stone.
issues: Non-blocking: the scene is a static stack of six objects with only two verbs (sinks, stabs); a single unifying action would raise imageability.
Non-blocking: 'the Sun sinks to the Horizon Line above a Rice-Paddy Grid' is spatially ambiguous about what sits above what.
Non-blocking: gate-framed imagery collides with other 門 kanji and especially 蘭 (same 闌 phonetic); the Lightning Bolt column is the only strong differentiator.

story: Candy Tin perches atop the snapping Wishbone, striped sweet gleaming on show; right beside it the Yawning Cavern gapes, cold and utterly empty. Sugar promised, void delivered — DECEIT.
reading_story: Gee shakes your hand warmly, palms your wallet, then waves cheerfully from the departing train — pure DECEIT.

story: GOODWILL — the War Helmet rests atop the Railway Tracks to show peace, Sand Trickle pouring down beneath the rails, while at the right the Yawning Cavern breathes out cold, empty air.
reading_story: Khan reins in his horse at the border, opens empty palms, and offers GOODWILL instead of arrows.
issues: 示 (actor null) is encoded only as the passing verb in 'to show peace' — the concept is named, so coverage passes, but it reads as grammatical filler rather than a component cue and is easy for a learner to skip over.

The visual story is a static tableau: the helmet rests, the sand pours, the cavern breathes, with no causal interaction linking them. This is what holds distinctiveness at 3 — memorability rests mostly on the reading story.

'to show peace' is the one abstraction in an otherwise concrete scene, slightly diluting imageability; a physical peace token (e.g. the helmet laid down empty) would carry the same 示 hook more visibly.

story: A Feathered Arrow lands upright on Stumpy Sparrow's head, a fat red berry skewered on its point; beside the sighing mouth of the Yawning Cavern, the old bird gulps it down — DELIGHT.
reading_story: Khan gallops into the village expecting terror; instead the villagers welcome him with flowers, and the conqueror roars with DELIGHT.
issues: Minor coherence blur (non-gating): the sparrow 'gulps it down' while the berry is skewered on an arrow standing on its own head, and 'it' could read as berry or arrow — consider 'plucks the berry off the point and gulps it down'.
Non-gating: 欠-family neighbors (欲, 飲) also center on craving/swallowing; the arrow-delivered berry keeps this separable but curation should watch for interference.

story: PARTICULARLY cursed crossing: left, a Gnawed Rib-Bone in the dust; right, a cow stranded up a Tree over Railway Tracks while a Falling Katana slashes down, a Lightning Bolt spears her, and the Wishbone snaps underneath.
reading_story: Master Shu tastes a hundred teas, spits out ninety-nine, and lifts one cup aloft: "This one is PARTICULARLY fine."
issues: Keyword used as a bare intensifier ('PARTICULARLY cursed') — placement passes at start, but the semantic link to 'particularly' is thin; the reading story ('one cup out of a hundred is PARTICULARLY fine') carries the meaning better than the main story.
'the Wishbone snaps underneath' is spatially vague (underneath the tracks? the tree?), slightly blurring an otherwise well-staged left/right layout.
Three simultaneous events (katana slash, lightning strike, wishbone snap) plus a left-side bone put the scene at the cognitive-load ceiling, though still within the 40-word cap (36 words).

story: A Gnawed Rib-Bone lies left of the Plus-Sign Crossroads; below the crossroads the Watching Eye stares, and under that stare one bone becomes two, four, eight — the bones AUGMENT.
reading_story: Shocker flexes for the crowd, and with every flex his muscles AUGMENT — biceps doubling, shoulders tripling, until the ring creaks beneath him.

story: Inside the Toolbox Tray, a Falling Katana slashes down past one Ink Droplet. Right of it, the Lance-Butt Grip — Low Stool stacked on a Rubber Glove — jabs hard leftward: ASSAULT.
reading_story: Owen the goalkeeper crouches in his net, groaning "ohh" as the whole opposing team charges at once — a full-blooded ASSAULT on his goal.
issues: Nested-actor redundancy: 殳 is named as Lance-Butt Grip and then immediately re-described as 'Low Stool stacked on a Rubber Glove'. Satisfies coverage but forces the reader to hold a fist-on-lance and a stool-on-glove as the same object, which blurs the right-hand image.
The assault is asserted, not depicted: 'jabs hard leftward' has no named target, so nothing is actually struck. The keyword rides on the adverb rather than on an event the reader can see connect.
Distinctiveness risk from 殳: the Lance-Butt Grip jab-and-hit frame will recur across 投/段/殺/般 etc. The 区 half (tray + katana + droplet) carries almost all the discriminating load here.
Minor: the main story is closer to a spatial layout with two independent motions than a single causal beat; coherence is adequate but not strong.

story: Pot Lid clamped tight on your head, you plant your feet and STAND UP; the Muddy Boar charges your ribs, the Lance-Butt Grip hammers your shoulder, a Rubber Glove shoves from a tipped Low Stool — you do not move. STRONG.
reading_story: Key holds one clipped note against the whole orchestra, jaw set, until the conductor gives in — that little locksmith is STRONG.
issues: Hand-authored after judge rejection: the candidate gave the Lance-Butt Grip's butt-end two competing fists (its own registry fist plus the Rubber Glove) and used an ambiguous 'It hits your ribs'. Rewritten so each of the six components attacks from a distinct direction with an explicit agent, and the immovable stance carries the STRONG payoff.

story: At the clan gate hangs one gnarled wooden crest — a single hook and one sweeping low stroke, worn smooth by generations of bowing hands. Carved deep into it: the FAMILY NAME.
reading_story: The Sheriff blocks the saloon door, badge glinting: "No first names in my town. State your FAMILY NAME."
issues: Minor: stroke description 'a single hook and one sweeping low stroke' only loosely matches 氏's four strokes — acceptable as a shape gesture, not a phantom component.
Distinctiveness capped at 3: 'name carved on wood' is generic imagery that could interfere with other name/sign kanji (名, 姓); the clan-gate and 'no first names in my town' details carry it.

story: On the left, Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets mid-air; right beside it the Plus-Sign Crossroads lies flooded to its painted edges, brown and steaming — a tarmac-wide bowl of SOUP.
reading_story: Juno stirs a bronze cauldron on the temple steps, ladling steaming SOUP to a long queue of rain-soaked pilgrims.
issues: Non-blocking: 'Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets mid-air' restates the actor card verbatim instead of integrating the splash into the soup action - costs a point of imageability.
Non-blocking: reading_story is generic (Juno ladles soup to pilgrims); nothing in it is specific to Juno beyond the name, so it leans on the keyword rather than the actor for its hook.
Watch for interference: 'brown and steaming' liquid on the water radical could collide with other 氵 heat/liquid kanji (湯, 液); the plus-sign crossroads is doing all the discriminating work.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets off to the left; they streak down the muddy bank, gutter together, and carve a glinting channel that widens into a CREEK.
reading_story: Coe refuses the footbridge mid-race — he clears the CREEK in one enormous Olympic stride, spray hanging behind his spikes.
issues: Minor: opening 'flicks three fat droplets' closely echoes the shipped 沢 story's 'flings fat droplets' opener — payoffs differ (soaked cloak vs. carved creek), but consider varying the Puddle Splash verb to reduce within-family surface similarity.

Minor: 'gutter together' is a slightly abstract verb choice in an otherwise concrete sequence; also note 'gutter' is a plausible future keyword for 溝 (not yet in the dataset) — harmless now, watch for interference if 溝 is added.
Note: keyword is mid-sentence in the reading_story; per shipped precedent (攻) the start/end gate applies to the meaning story only, so this is not a gate failure.

story: Puddle Splash stands at the left edge of the beach and hurls its three fat droplets outward; midair each droplet swells horizon-wide, crashing together into one endless, shoreless OPEN SEA.
reading_story: Chewbacca paddles a tiny raft across the OPEN SEA, howling one long, mournful roar at the empty horizon — no shore answers.
issues: Non-blocking: water-actor-becomes-sea imagery risks mild interference with 海/洋 neighbors; the 'shoreless' hook mitigates it and should be preserved in any edit.

story: Three fat droplets fly left off Puddle Splash as, on the right, Lance-Butt Grip sinks — knuckles clenched white around the lance shaft, the pole tipping under, bubbles trailing up: DROWN.
reading_story: Botter cannonballs into the black canal, too heavy to float, and drops in a rush of bubbles until he DROWNs.
issues: Non-blocking: 'water + sinking' is the default image for this semantic field, so mild interference risk with neighbors 沈/溺/浸 — the tipping lance shaft is the only discriminating hook.
Non-blocking: the drowning subject is a disembodied fist, which slightly strains the notion of drowning (no breath); acceptable since the sinking is ordinary physical motion for that actor.

story: Puddle Splash flings fat droplets from the left onto Draped Cloak, which sags off its chair, soaking flat across the floor until the whole room squelches into a SWAMP.
reading_story: Tucker wades thigh-deep into the SWAMP, the mud sucking at his boots with every squelching step.
issues: Minor: 'the whole room squelches into a SWAMP' is a slightly abstract transformation (room morphing into landscape) — the weakest visual beat, though the surrounding concrete actions carry it.

story: Puddle Splash hangs at the left edge, three fat droplets flung mid-air, scattering down into black peat that swallows them with a slurp — each drop widening the reeking, reed-choked MARSH.
reading_story: The Showman, top hat tilted, bellows "Shoooow!" from a sinking circus ring — his boots vanish into the MARSH while the audience claps knee-deep in mud.
issues: (minor, non-blocking) 召 is phonetic_extra and carries no visual role in the meaning story; the phonetic load rests entirely on Showman/しょう in the reading story, which is the intended handling but leaves the right-hand half of 沼 visually unanchored for writing recall.

story: Puddle Splash streams downhill on the left; on the bank, Wishbone jogs on its two split legs atop Open Mouth, who shouts a marching beat — together they RUN ALONGSIDE the water.
reading_story: Enzo guns his Ferrari along the riverbank, forbidden to cross — he can only RUN ALONGSIDE the water, spray misting his fenders.
issues: Minor: Open Mouth's locomotion is under-specified — it must move alongside the river while Wishbone stands on it, which the reader has to infer.
Minor: in the reading story the keyword is followed by a trailing detail clause ('spray misting his fenders'); still final-clause placement, not buried, so gate 4 passes.

story: Puddle Splash flings droplets leftward; on the right, Swaddling Wrap folds down and hugs the lowered Stop Barrier. The water piles against that halted gate, churning into fizzing white BUBBLES.
reading_story: Ho belly-laughs in his bathtub; every booming "ho-ho-ho" shakes the water until the tub erupts with beard-white BUBBLES.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): the reading story's bathtub-full-of-bubbles image is the single most clichéd pairing for 'bubbles' and is likely to interfere with neighbouring water/foam kanji (e.g. 沫, 沸); a less default setting for Ho would raise separation.

Non-blocking: vowel length is only weakly cued. reading_actor.note stresses long ō as the discriminator against clipped twin Hoth (ほ), but the story's 'booming "ho-ho-ho"' conveys volume rather than duration — a stretched/drawn-out cue would encode the length feature the registry says is the #1 reading error (docs/07 §1.2).

Minor (spatial fidelity): the left/right split is stated correctly (氵 left, 包 right) and the 勹-hugs-已 nesting matches the enclosure, but 'hugs the lowered Stop Barrier' reads as a lateral embrace rather than a wrap-from-above, slightly under-selling 勹's over-the-top folding posture from its registry image.

Minor: 'The water piles against that halted gate, churning into fizzing white BUBBLES' is a causal mechanism, not an etymological claim — it passes gate 6, but note that it comes close to reading like an explanation of the character's construction rather than an imaginative aid.

story: Made to stand up straight at attention, Puddle Splash can't hold it — three fat droplets burst leftward down its face in a streaming CRY.
reading_story: Governor Cuomo breaks down mid-briefing — cameras zoom in as he starts to CRY.

story: A Lightning Bolt cracks down through the Horizon Line and both Railway Tracks; below, a Stepladder stands astride the towering Tsunami Wave — yet everything hangs frozen, utterly silent, perfectly PEACEFUL.
reading_story: Ty Cobb — baseball's meanest brawler — lays down his bat, folds his hands over his cap, and naps on the mound, completely PEACEFUL.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'Stepladder stands astride the towering Tsunami Wave' mildly strains the ladder's physics, but it is ordinary placement, not an invented cognitive ability.
Minor (non-blocking): five components in one frame plus the abstract 'hangs frozen, utterly silent' state adds slight cognitive load.

story: Puddle Splash flings droplets down the left; beside them Goalpost Frame stands, Horizon Line strung tight under its crossbar, and beneath that an Open Mouth yawns black, its shout echoing back — CAVE.
reading_story: Doe, the unnamed hiker, wakes on the cold floor of a CAVE, his toe-tag fluttering as bats stream past.
issues: Horizon Line ('a perfectly flat desert horizon') repurposed as something 'strung tight under its crossbar' — legal as physical placement, but a desert horizon does not picture as a taut cord, so this is the weakest visual beat.
No causal interaction: Puddle Splash flings droplets and nothing follows from it — the water is inert decoration 'beside' the rest, which costs coherence and encoding strength.
Distinctiveness risk: the 氵 + 冂/一/口 actor stack is identical for every 同-family kanji (銅, 胴, 洞); only 'yawns black, its shout echoing back' separates this from its neighbors.
Reading story mixes a waking hiker with a morgue toe-tag — the John Doe persona is on-model but the image is internally odd (a tagged body that wakes).

story: Puddle Splash flings its three droplets leftward over the strait while, to the right, Writing Brush presses its inky tip and draws one straight line across the water: the printed route of the FERRY.
reading_story: Night bartender Shinn tends a floating bar on the last FERRY, sliding drinks down the counter as the boat rocks across the dark harbor.

story: Puddle Splash hurls droplets leftward while the Lightning Bolt spears straight down through the Horizon Line and the Railway Tracks below it; at the base a Wishbone snaps wide open, and everything drowns in DELUGE.
reading_story: Coe sprints the final lap as the stadium tunnel bursts; he outruns the DELUGE, breasting the tape ankle-deep in water.
issues: Non-blocking: the payoff clause 'everything drowns in DELUGE' asserts the meaning rather than imaging it, and is the most predictable ending available for a 氵 kanji — it will read near-identically to neighbours like 浸/溢/濫 and contributes nothing to distinctiveness.

Non-blocking: 'spears straight down through the Horizon Line and the Railway Tracks below it' is geometric/inventory-like — the two line-actors are pierced passively and are themselves visually confusable (一 vs 二, both bare lines), so the middle of the scene carries little sensory weight.
Non-blocking: DELUGE appears in both story and reading_story; the keyword gate is satisfied by the story, but the repetition slightly dilutes the meaning-to-reading bridge.
Minor: 'the Railway Tracks below it' has an ambiguous antecedent ('it' = Horizon Line vs Lightning Bolt); harmless for recall but could be tightened.

story: Puddle Splash blasts spray from the left while Meat Hook skewers down through Swaddling Wrap's curled cloth and Rake Hand's gripping tines — water sluices off barb, cloth, and prong until everything gleams CLEAN.
reading_story: Joe drags a white glove across the scrubbed counter, stretches out a long, satisfied "Joooe…", and declares the kitchen CLEAN.
issues: Non-blocking: the wash-until-CLEAN payoff is the generic route for water-radical kanji (same mechanism a generator would emit for 洗/清/潔), so meaning-side distinctiveness leans entirely on the unusual component cast.
Non-blocking: 'water sluices off barb, cloth, and prong' is an enumerative beat that slightly dilutes the single-scene image.
Non-blocking: Meat Hook 'skewers down' while its registry image has the barb pointing up — minor visual tension, still ordinary physical motion.

story: On the left, Puddle Splash flings three fat droplets toward the shore; on the right, Nursery Flag stands staked in wet sand, its marker-stick pointing where calm water curves inland — the BAY.
reading_story: Hoth, the frozen giant, wades into the warm BAY; frost hisses off his shoulders and steam curls over the calm water.

story: Puddle Splash flings its three fat droplets from the left; every ripple doubles the water, swallowing ditch, field, and horizon into one gleaming WIDE EXPANSE.
reading_story: Coe trains on a flooded salt flat: he runs for hours, yet the WIDE EXPANSE stretches on and no far shore ever appears.
issues: Non-blocking: flood-engulfs-landscape imagery overlaps a crowded 氵 neighborhood (e.g. 洪 deluge, 洋 ocean); the ripple-doubling hook and Coe's salt-flat run mitigate but don't eliminate interference risk.
Non-blocking: in reading_story the keyword sits in the final clause rather than as the literal last words; acceptable since the closing image (no far shore) still pays off WIDE EXPANSE.

story: On the right, Still Butte stands rooted forever; off its left flank Puddle Splash flings three droplets across the sand, drifting away over dune after dune, never returning — pure WANDERING.
reading_story: Mike Rowe, coated in desert dust, quits the dig and thumbs one empty highway after another — a filthy-jobs host with no job left, just WANDERING.
issues: Minor (non-gating) — physical plausibility: flung water droplets 'drifting away over dune after dune, never returning' stretches ordinary motion for water in a desert (evaporation). It is still physical motion, not an invented cognitive ability, so gate 2/5 passes, but the image is slightly less anchored than a literal splash trajectory would be.

Minor (non-gating) — distinctiveness risk: the record lists 'Waves/Billows' among 浪's meanings, and the story encodes only 'wandering'. Since 波 (waves) is a near neighbour also built on 氵, a learner may later confuse which 氵-kanji carries 'waves'. Not a rubric gate (keyword is 'wandering' and it lands), but worth flagging for curation.
Minor (non-gating) — Still Butte (艮) recurs across the large 艮/良 family (限, 眼, 根, 銀, 郎, 朗, 娘…), so distinctiveness rests almost entirely on the Puddle Splash + dune-drift half of the image.

story: Puddle Splash flings droplets leftward as Bedsheet Cover drapes the tub's rim; beneath it Rake Hand claws downward, dragging Rubber Glove under the surface until the whole glove is IMMERSED.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender drops a lime into a tall glass, watching it stay IMMERSED beneath the foam all evening.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11, graded not gating): 浸 stacks 彐 above 冖 above 又 on the right of 氵, but the story introduces Bedsheet Cover first and puts Rake Hand 'beneath it', inverting the top-to-bottom order — should run Rake Hand, then Bedsheet Cover, then Rubber Glove.

Non-component scenery ('the tub's rim', 'the surface') is doing the work of supplying the water, while Puddle Splash's droplets fly off leftward unconnected to the immersion event; Puddle Splash is named (gate 1 passes) but is decorative rather than causal.
Bedsheet Cover's contribution is weak — draping a tub rim adds little to the image and does not interact with the glove being pulled under.

story: Puddle Splash scatters three droplets down the left edge; right, Rock Overhang juts over emptiness, roofing Mound of Soil, whose sprout-marker points straight at the far, glowing HORIZON.
reading_story: Guy Fawkes lights his fuse on that overhang; the blast flings sparks so far outward they seem to set the entire HORIZON alight.
issues: Non-blocking: 'sprout-marker points straight at the far, glowing HORIZON' is a near-static gesture — the weakest beat in an otherwise kinetic scene; a marker leaning/tipping toward the horizon would move more.
Non-blocking: the reading_story's 'set the entire HORIZON alight' echoes the meaning story's 'far, glowing HORIZON', so the two stories share an image rather than adding a second hook.
Non-blocking: cliff-over-emptiness + distant horizon is a semantically transparent landscape, which helps recall but risks blending with other 厂/landscape mnemonics at N1 scale.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets from the left onto Bonfire; the flames hiss, shrink to thin faint wisps, and every roaring orange tongue fades PALE.
reading_story: Tanner over-soaks a hide in his tanning vat and lifts out leather bleached PALE, thin enough to see through.

story: PURE! From Puddle Splash's grimy leftward flick one droplet arcs right, beads on clamped Pot Lid, slips through gaping Open Mouth, and lands gleaming in rocking Swaddle Basket — muck left behind.
reading_story: Every June the beekeepers crown one comb — no wax, no dust, only gold light through the frame — and brand it PURE.
issues: Reading actor 'June' is used as a calendar month ('Every June...'), a temporal adverbial, not an agent — the beekeepers do all the acting. Gate 3 passes literally but the じゅん hook is weaker than if June were a character in the scene.

Slight motion inconsistency: Puddle Splash's registry image is droplets 'flicked off to the left', yet the story has the droplet 'arcs right' from that leftward flick. Readable as one droplet breaking away, but the physics is momentarily muddled.

Distinctiveness risk: a water droplet being purified/losing its muck is the obvious framing for any 氵 kanji keyed to 'pure' or 'clean' — potential interference with 清 / 淨 / 潔 neighbours. The 亠口子 vertical stack is what keeps it separable.
Compression cost: 'From Puddle Splash's grimy leftward flick' front-loads three modifiers before the subject acts, the densest clause in an otherwise clean sentence.

story: Puddle Splash flings droplets left. Right of them, Falling Katana drives down through a sprawled Starfish and into the heart beneath, spearing all three into one dripping shish-kebab: ATTACH.
reading_story: Tennison the detective slaps a tracking bug under the getaway car — one quiet click to ATTACH, and the whole case cracks open.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'Falling Katana skewers things' is a predictable default action for a blade actor and may recur across other ノ kanji; the starfish+heart kebab is what saves distinctiveness here.

story: Puddle Splash bursts against your left side at every step of your walk through the knee-deep river — droplets stinging your cheek — until you stagger up the far bank: this shallow crossing is the FORD.
reading_story: The Showman, top hat held high, leads his circus elephants across the FORD, crying "Shooooow must go on!" as water soaks his coattails.
issues: Non-gating: reading_story buries FORD mid-sentence; meaning story satisfies the placement gate ('end'), but the reading story would be tidier with the keyword at an edge.
Minor: 'at every step of your walk' reads slightly mechanical (coverage-driven phrasing for 歩), keeping imageability at 4 rather than 5.

story: On the left, Puddle Splash flings unripe-persimmon juice; on the right your tongue must stop, puckered, as Frost Beads harden beneath it — the whole mouth shrivels, ASTRINGENT.
reading_story: Juno, trapped in honking congestion, gulps gas-station tea so ASTRINGENT her lips pucker shut against the steering wheel.
issues: Non-blocking: Puddle Splash flings persimmon juice rather than water — acceptable ordinary physical motion, but a slight drift from its defined water-droplet image.
Non-blocking: left/right stage directions read slightly diagrammatic; the two halves take a beat to fuse into one mouth-scene.

story: Puddle Splash scatters leftward, its three fat droplets hitting the water spinning, dragging everything round and round, faster, tighter, until the surface hollows into a roaring WHIRLPOOL.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr brakes at the flooded curb; his spinning wheel churns the runoff into a WHIRLPOOL that swallows his hubcap whole.
issues: Minor phrasing: 'its three fat droplets hitting the water spinning' has a dangling modifier — 'spinning' reads as attached to 'water' rather than to the impact; 'hitting the water, setting it spinning' would be cleaner.

Semantically near-tautological (spinning water = whirlpool), so the only real memory hook is the vortex image itself; acceptable with a single component, but it sits inside the very crowded 'Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets → KEYWORD' template shared by ~25 other 氵 cards (波 WAVES, 潮 TIDE, 沖 OPEN SEA, 海 SEA).
Non-blocking: phonetic_extra 咼 is unused (not a mandatory component, so no gate failure).

story: Trace the dry riverbed uphill to its very beginning: there hangs Puddle Splash, three fat droplets flicking off to the left — the first water that ever fell here, the SOURCE.
reading_story: Glenn kneels at the spring filling bottle after bottle, insisting real resources must be drawn straight from the SOURCE.
issues: Minor: reading_story centers on 'a spring', which mildly risks interference with 泉 (spring) mnemonics — the SOURCE payoff and 資源 vocab tie-in mitigate it
Minor: 'the first water that ever fell here' is an abstract gloss rather than an image; the surrounding scene carries the imageability

story: Puddle Splash flings its three fat droplets off the left kerb, arcing down into the long concrete channel below — a rain-black GUTTER swallowing every drop.
reading_story: Coe sprints his final lap with one spike splashing inside the flooded GUTTER ringing the track, still taking gold.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: the only mandatory component 氵 is named by its exact persona — "Puddle Splash flings its three fat droplets".

Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS: "left kerb" is scene furniture and "the long concrete channel below" is appositive to the keyword itself ("— a rain-black GUTTER"), not an extra component; 冓 is phonetic_extra and correctly left unused.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: "Coe sprints his final lap" opens the reading_story.

Gate 4 (meaning placement) PASS but borderline: GUTTER sits in the final clause after an em-dash reveal ("— a rain-black GUTTER swallowing every drop"), so it reads as the payoff rather than buried; declared placement "end" is honest, though 4 words trail it.

Gate 5 (persona consistency) PASS: registry image is "three fat water droplets flicked off to the left, mid-splash, scattering down" — story keeps the count (three), the adjective (fat), the leftward flick ("off the left kerb") and the downward scatter ("arcing down"). Coe = Sebastian Coe the Olympic runner, and "sprints his final lap ... taking gold" is squarely in persona; long-ō "full/stretched" reading is respected (a full lap, not a clipped burst). Agentive framing ("flings its droplets") is ordinary physical motion, not an invented cognitive faculty.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS: no historical or derivational claim anywhere.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story 25 words, reading_story 19 words, both well under ~40; no filler.

Minor (non-gating): the meaning story is close to tautological — water radical + water entering a drain restates the keyword rather than adding a discriminating hook, which is the main drag on distinctiveness against neighbouring water/channel kanji (堀, 濠, 渠).
Minor (non-gating): reading_story repeats GUTTER in caps; harmless, but the reading hook rests entirely on Coe + track-side drainage, which is a fairly conventional pairing for こう.

story: DESTROY: the Falling Katana slashes down the Barbed Pike's shaft, toppling it onto the Bonfire beneath; flames burst outward, and Puddle Splash's three droplets on the left can't quench the blazing wreckage.
reading_story: One lunge from Metz the fencing master is enough to DESTROY every practice dummy in the hall — splinters everywhere.

story: From the left, Puddle Splash flings three droplets across a flat Horizon Line; beneath it Twin Pillars straddle a tiny Silk Cocoon, which swells fat and glossy on the soaking — water this NOURISHING.
reading_story: Jee the emcee taps the mic, shouts one clipped word over the crowd — "NOURISHING!" — as free soup steams in paper cups down every row.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric #11, graded not gating): 'Twin Pillars straddle a tiny Silk Cocoon' places the pillars flanking the cocoon left/right, whereas 并 sits ABOVE 幺 in 兹 and the registry image is 'two short stone pillars standing close together side by side, capped by a shared little ledge'. 'Straddle' also anthropomorphises legless pillars. Suggest 'Twin Pillars stand over a tiny Silk Cocoon' for a cleaner stacked picture.

Distinctiveness risk: 'water makes it swell / soaking / nourishing' is the default beat for many 氵 kanji (潤, 濡, 沃, 涵). The only load-bearing hook separating 滋 is the silk cocoon swelling glossy — keep that, but the closing 'water this NOURISHING' is the weakest, most abstract line and does little to fence 滋 off from neighbours.

Minor: 'water this NOURISHING' reads awkwardly as a sentence fragment ('water this nourishing' = water that is this nourishing). Keyword placement at end is satisfied, but the payoff line is grammatically limp for a rubric #4 'keyword is the payoff'.

Note (not a defect): the four droplets/mic/soup/paper-cup details were checked against rubric #2 — none assert an extra component; 'three droplets' comes straight from the 氵 registry image and the reading-story props are flavour only.

story: From the left, Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets onto a long bone; the wet bone shoots out from under your foot — SLIPPERY!
reading_story: Cutler dashes across a freshly mopped station floor, arms windmilling as he glides helplessly past his train — the tiles are SLIPPERY.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets leftward off a cliff ledge; on the right a scaled dragon rears, its roar shattering the spray into one thundering WATERFALL.
reading_story: Mike Rowe, grimy in waders, scrubs slime from the black rocks behind a roaring WATERFALL — dirtiest job yet.
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage): both mandatory components named — 'Puddle Splash' (氵) and 'dragon' (竜, the supplied kanji_keyword).

PASS gate 2 (no phantom components): 'cliff ledge' and 'spray' are scene-dressing, not presented as glyph parts. This matches the project's own precedent recorded at data/authored/n4-mnemonics.json:1007 ('The hoarding dragon is a scene-dressing prop, not a phantom component — acceptable').

PASS gate 3 (reading actor): 'Mike Rowe' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor.actor_name='Rowe' with note 'Mike Rowe. Long ō.' (registry confirmed at data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json:2135-2136).
PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): WATERFALL is the final word of the story; meaning_placement='end' is accurate.

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): 'flicks three fat droplets leftward' reproduces the registry image for Puddle Splash ('Three fat water droplets flicked off to the left'), consistent with prior uses at n4-mnemonics.json:810/1814 and n3-mnemonics.json:3396. The dragon only rears and roars — ordinary physical/vocal behaviour, no invented cognitive faculty.
PASS gate 6 (no etymology): the dragon is staged as an imaginative scene element; no historical/derivational claim is made.
PASS gate 7 (length & focus): story = 27 words, reading_story = 19 words, both well under ~40.
Spatial fidelity is good: water left ('leftward off a cliff ledge'), dragon right ('on the right a scaled dragon rears') matches 氵+竜 layout.

NON-BLOCKING: 'its roar shattering the spray into one thundering WATERFALL' is the one soft spot — the causal transformation from scattered spray to a single fall is more asserted than seen, slightly weakening an otherwise concrete image. A physical mechanism (dragon's body sluicing the water down the cliff) would picture better.

NON-BLOCKING interference risk: the N3 registry already assigns the actor name 'Braided Waterfall' to 永, with the image 'drops off a rock ledge ... one long unbroken cascade' (data/authored/n3-component-actors.json:323-325). This candidate's 'cliff ledge' cascade overlaps that imagery. The dragon is the saving differentiator; consider leaning harder on the dragon and dropping the ledge if 永 and 滝 ever co-occur in a review session.

NON-BLOCKING: reading_story teaches the on-reading ろう while dominant_reading is kun たき — correct per the supplied record (reading_actor is non-null so gate 3 requires it), but the learner gets no cue that たき is the dominant form. Also no long-vowel emphasis for ろう vs its clipped twin Roe (ろ); the full 'Mike Rowe' form is the only marker, consistent with existing precedent at n3-mnemonics.json:762.

story: Puddle Splash flings water from the left onto a Hanging Towel, but a Bedsheet Cover draped over it seals in the damp — the trapped water pools, turns green, begins to STAGNATE.
reading_story: Ty slides into a flooded base pit; the water refuses to drain, left to STAGNATE around his cleats.
issues: Minor: shares the 冖-draped-over-巾 staging with the phonetic sibling 帯 (belt); the green stagnant-water payoff differentiates it, but keep the 帯 story's scene visually distinct to avoid interference.

story: Puddle Splash flicks its droplets at a lone paper BALLOT fallen in the gutter; the soggy slip spins away downstream, unclaimed, taken wherever the water goes — DRIFT.
reading_story: Hugo, beard streaming, cuts his balloon's tether above Paris and lets it DRIFT — a long slow hooooo across the rooftops.
issues: Hand-authored replacement: original candidate was judge-rejected for interference with 泳/池/況 (all "droplets on a still puddle"). Rewritten per the judge's own suggested fix — uses the glyph's phonetic 票 (BALLOT) as a unique concrete object carried by the water, which both sharpens DRIFT (it goes where the current takes it) and separates the scene from every other 氵 story.

story: A Draped Cloak sags over a Rain Cloud trapped beneath it; raindrops seep through the slack fabric and dribble off to the left, where Puddle Splash scatters them down — a LEAK.
reading_story: Rowe wriggles under a sink on his dirtiest job yet, wrench in hand, hunting the LEAK that soaks his overalls.
issues: Minor: in the reading story the keyword LEAK sits inside the final clause rather than as the terminal word — acceptable, but terminal placement would land harder.

story: Puddle Splash flings its three droplets off the left edge of endless dunes; each drop hisses into steam before it can land, sand swallowing the last wet shine — pure scorched DESERT.
reading_story: Bachar tips his cracked canteen over the dune crest: two drops, then nothing. He laughs, hoarse, and walks on into the DESERT.
issues: Non-blocking — distinctiveness/interference: the shipped 浪 story (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json, glyph 浪) is "Puddle Splash flings three droplets across the sand, drifting away over dune after dune, never returning — pure WANDERING", and its own issue log already describes that vanishing as evaporation. The candidate is the same core image (Puddle Splash's droplets thrown over dunes and disappearing) with the evaporation made explicit, so 漠 and 浪 sit in the same scene-space. Separable via 浪's Still Butte (艮) anchor and the candidate's instant hiss-to-steam, but the risk is real.

Non-blocking — spatial/encoding coverage: phonetic_extra 莫 is the entire right-hand bulk of the glyph and is unencoded; the story's only glyph anchor is 氵 plus the keyword setting. This matches accepted precedent (浩 ships 氵-only with distinctiveness 3), and 莫 is not in the mandatory components list, so gate 1 is not affected.

Non-blocking — actor persona: reading_actor note defines Bachar as "Bacca-man" (a Wookiee-type figure). The candidate's "He laughs, hoarse, and walks on" reads fairly human; not a contradiction (a hoarse growling laugh fits), and prior Bachar stories (爆 bomb-lobbing, 麦 cramming barley) are equally physical, so gate 5 passes — but the persona is not actively evoked, which weakens the reading hook.

Non-blocking — reading-story setting overlap: 浪's reading story is also a lone figure in desert dust ("Mike Rowe, coated in desert dust... thumbs one empty highway"). Bachar's canteen/dune-crest scene shares that desert framing, compounding the 漠/浪 proximity noted above.

Verified pass on all gates: 氵 named as Puddle Splash with correct left-edge placement matching its registry image ("Three fat water droplets flicked off to the left"); no phantom actors (dunes/sand/steam are keyword-derived scenery, not named entities); Bachar present in reading_story; DESERT terminal in both stories, consistent with meaning_placement "end"; no etymology; 31 words (story) and 23 words (reading_story), both under ~40.

story: Puddle Splash flicks droplets down the left margin; at right the Sun blazes above a stretched Fishing Net, and beneath it a Rubber Glove flops palm-up — a page of gleefully scribbled CARTOON.
reading_story: Thomas Mann opens the morning paper and finds himself drawn as a CARTOON — pipe, tiny mustache, a novel thick as a brick under his arm.
issues: Imageability weakness (rubric line 99): the four actors are spatially arranged but never interact — Sun blazes, Net is stretched, Glove flops, all independently. There is no single striking event binding them, only a stacked layout.

Keyword binding is asserted, not caused (rubric line 93 'keyword is the payoff'): 'a page of gleefully scribbled CARTOON' is a suffix that labels the scene rather than a payoff the actors produce. Nothing about a sun, a net, or a rubber glove is cartoon-specific.

Distinctiveness risk (rubric line 100): the '...turns out to be a comic page' ending is a generic template that could terminate any component set, so it adds little separation from other 氵+日 kanji; distinctiveness rests entirely on the unique actor quartet.

Minor: 'left margin' and 'page' are scene framing, not encoded components — judged non-phantom, but they push the meta-framing (the kanji depicting itself as a drawn page) close to the edge of gate 2.

Non-blocking: reading_story buries CARTOON mid-sentence ('finds himself drawn as a CARTOON'). Gate 4 governs the meaning story only, so this does not fail, but the reading story's own hook is the Mann/まん sound, which is correctly carried.

story: Puddle Splash flings its droplets left into the crock; from the right, the weight of blame presses cucumbers under the brine until they darken, wrinkle, and sour. PICKLING.
reading_story: The Sheriff lifts the jar lid, sniffs once, and clips out his verdict: these cucumbers need three more days of PICKLING.
issues: Non-gating (rubric §3 item 9, imageability): 'the weight of blame presses cucumbers' is the one abstract link in an otherwise concrete scene — blame is given no visible form (a pickling stone, a scowling accuser). Giving it a shape would raise imageability from 4 to 5.

Non-gating (rubric §3 item 10): the water radical 氵 recurs across many N1 entries, so the only anti-interference hook here is the blame-weight-on-cucumbers image; it holds, but the scene leans on generic props (crock, brine) shared with other soak/steep kanji.

story: UNDEFILED. Puddle Splash scatters droplets down the left; on the right the Tiered Picket stands vine-wrapped with the Cleaver hanging beside it, and below both dangles Spooled Thread, rinsed bone-white.
reading_story: Ketel tips his vodka bottle over a grimy sink; the alcohol strips every stain, leaving the porcelain gleaming UNDEFILED.
issues: Gating passes: all four mandatory actors named (氵 Puddle Splash, 丰 Tiered Picket, 刀 Cleaver, 糸 Spooled Thread), no phantom components (sink/porcelain/vodka bottle are reading-story props, not claimed parts), Ketel present in reading_story, UNDEFILED at start (declared 'start'), personas consistent (Cleaver hangs as in its image, Thread dangles, Picket vine-wrapped), no etymology, story 30 words / reading story 19 words.
Non-blocking — the meaning story is a static positional inventory ('stands', 'hanging beside', 'dangles') rather than a causal event; nothing happens, so there is little to replay at recall time.
Non-blocking — the Cleaver is inert: it hangs beside the Picket with no role in the scene, the weakest anchor of the four.
Non-blocking — the keyword link is carried entirely by the passive tag 'rinsed bone-white'; no agent does the cleaning, so UNDEFILED is asserted rather than earned.
Non-blocking — 'Puddle Splash scatters droplets down the left' is the generic water-radical opener and will recur across many 氵 kanji, capping distinctiveness.
Spatial fidelity is good: water left, 丰+刀 upper right, 糸 below both — matches the glyph layout.

story: Puddle Splash's three droplets scatter left as the Sun rolls down a Stepladder propped over a Mound of Soil, sinking below the surface to glow dim and drowned — SUBMERGE.
reading_story: Senna takes the harbor chicane too fast — his car noses off the pier and starts to SUBMERGE, headlights still blazing under green water.
issues: Minor: 'sinking below the surface' never names the water body — the puddle-swallows-sun scale gap is left to the learner to resolve.

Minor: in the reading story the keyword SUBMERGE lands mid-sentence rather than strictly at start/end; acceptable since the start/end gate applies to the meaning story, but a trailing clause follows the payoff.
Minor: 'sun sinking' is a mildly common 日 motif; distinctiveness rescued by the stepladder/mound staging and the drowned-glow image.

story: Puddle Splash sprays seawater in from the left; Pestle Basin tips ground salt down from above; Swaddling Wrap curls its arm around the shallow pool while Coal Brazier warms it from below — a steaming LAGOON.
reading_story: Sekka the chef wades into the LAGOON, flips one ladle of its warm salt water, tastes it, and declares the whole LAGOON perfect broth.
issues: Non-blocking: story uses the semicolon assembly-line pattern (four actors each contributing one action), which slightly flattens imageability even though each action is concrete and spatially faithful.

Non-blocking: reading_story's final payoff phrase is 'perfect broth' rather than the keyword itself; keyword still appears in the opening clause and twice overall, so the placement gate (which applies to the main story, placed at end) passes.

story: The Kings Crown sits between the open doors of the Castle Gate; Puddle Splash flings three fat droplets off its jewels leftward, spattering the gateway stones and leaving the velvet cushion WET.
reading_story: June steps into that gateway, monsoon overhead, and walks out with hair, cloak and boots utterly WET.
issues: Ambiguous pronoun in the meaning story: 'flings three fat droplets off its jewels' — the nearest antecedent of 'its' is Puddle Splash, which has no jewels. Should read 'off the Crown's jewels' to keep the image resolvable in one pass.

Reading story is generic wetness (monsoon soaking) and would fit 濡 or 湿 equally well; June has no distinctive business in the scene beyond getting rained on, so the reading hook carries little discriminative load.
Minor: the reading story leans on 'that gateway' as a back-reference to the meaning story, so it does not stand alone if the two are ever surfaced separately during scaffold fade (docs/07 §5).

story: Puddle Splash flicks his three fat droplets toward the morning sun on his right — the whole sea answers, surging up the beach as a wall of salt water: the TIDE.
reading_story: Witch Cho stretches her wand at the sea, chanting a looong drawn-out spell — the TIDE rises to her knees before she can finish.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets down the left rim; on the right those same droplets ascend, sunlit and weightless, leaving the water beneath in glass-still LUCIDITY.
reading_story: Cho polishes her wand-tip until it shows perfect LUCIDITY, every rain-blurred castle window snapping into focus through it.
issues: Non-gating: in reading_story the keyword sits mid-sentence ('shows perfect LUCIDITY, every rain-blurred...') rather than at an edge; the placement gate is satisfied by the main story, which ends on LUCIDITY, but the reading line would read cleaner with the keyword terminal.
Non-gating: 'sunlit' introduces ambient light not present in any component image. It is scene dressing, not a phantom actor, so it passes, but it adds an element the glyph does not license.

Watch: the 登 slot is realized as the verb 'ascend' attached to the same droplets rather than as a distinct staged event; the concept is explicitly named (gate passes) but the ascent is the weakest-anchored beat in the image and is what carries distinctiveness against other water+clarity kanji (e.g. 清).

story: Puddle Splash geysers up on the left; the White Candle balanced on a direction arrow flares wild, and the Cracking Whip flogs water and flame into a scalding frenzy — VIOLENT.
reading_story: Gecker bursts in shrieking "GEK! GEK!" — a VIOLENT tantrum that overturns tables and shatters lamps.
issues: Minor (non-gating): reading story shriek 'GEK! GEK!' drops the -ki coda that the Gecker actor note emphasizes for げき; 'GEKI!' would cue the reading more precisely, though the actor name itself carries it.

story: On the left, Puddle Splash flings her three fat droplets; they slam into the rope bridge you trust, the trusted planks snap, and the river below churns white into RAPIDS.
reading_story: Rye braces waist-deep in the RAPIDS, catching every child the roaring current sweeps toward the falls.
issues: Minor: causal stretch — three droplets snapping rope-bridge planks needs cartoon physics (imageability docked to 4, not gating).
Minor: 'river churns into rapids' payoff is imagery-adjacent to other water-keyword kanji (current/torrent); the trusted-bridge anchor mitigates.

story: Three Snaking Rivulets pour off the bank straight down onto the crackling Bonfire beneath — flame and floodwater collide, steam shrieks, sparks hiss out in black mud: DISASTER.
reading_story: Cy hurls one wild pitch after another; each fastball smashes something new, until the umpire waves it off and declares the whole game a DISASTER.
issues: Minor: meaning story stacks four sensory beats (collide/shriek/hiss/mud) at the climax; trimming one would sharpen the single image.
Minor: water-extinguishes-fire is a common trope, though the layout-faithful staging (rivulets above, bonfire beneath) keeps it distinct.

story: A Bonfire blazes in a soot-black alcove, and the Lone Barn Shutter hangs crooked at its right, creaking open and shut like a furnace door, fanning the sparks — the HEARTH.
reading_story: Roe crouches at the glowing HEARTH, roasting one chestnut; it pops, and she jerks back with soot on her nose.

story: Left: a Bonfire crackles, sparks flying. Right: the Yawning Cavern gapes, breathing cold air across the flames until they roar white-hot, its stone walls blackened with grease. Perfect place to COOK.
reading_story: Chef Swee tastes the stew, kisses his fingers — "Swee!" — then hands you the ladle: your turn to COOK.
issues: GATE 1 (component coverage) PASS — evidence: 'a Bonfire crackles' names 火's actor; 'the Yawning Cavern gapes' names 欠's actor. Both mandatory actors present by name.

GATE 2 (no phantom components) PASS — evidence: only other nouns are 'sparks', 'cold air', 'flames', 'stone walls', 'grease'. Sparks/flames belong to Bonfire's registry image ('sparks flying off both sides'); stone walls are the Cavern's own body; grease is scene dressing, not a named actor. No third component introduced.

GATE 3 (actor-nature consistency) PASS — evidence: Cavern 'breathing cold air' is licensed verbatim by its registry image, 'cold air sighing out of its empty hollow'. Air moving across flames is ordinary physical airflow (bellows), not an invented cognitive ability, so it clears the stated bar.

GATE 4 (reading actor) PASS — evidence: reading_story opens 'Chef Swee tastes the stew'; reading_actor_used='Swee' matches actor_name. Bonus: the clipped exclamation "Swee!" reinforces the short/clipped diphthong flagged in the note.
GATE 5 (keyword placement) PASS — story ends 'Perfect place to COOK.'; reading_story ends 'your turn to COOK.' meaning_placement='end' is accurate for both.
GATE 6 (no etymology) PASS — no historical or derivational claim; the 'Left:/Right:' framing is spatial staging only.
GATE 7 (length) PASS — story is 31 words, reading_story 24 words; both under the ~40 cap.

NON-BLOCKING (persona): 'Chef' is an added role for Swee, whose registry entry supplies only a name ('Sweeney, "Swee"') and no persona. Nothing is contradicted, so gate 5 holds, but if a Swee persona is ever curated this story may need reconciling.
NON-BLOCKING (coherence wobble): cold air driving flames 'white-hot' is bellows physics — correct but counterintuitive on first read; a learner may stumble on it before it clicks.

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness risk): fire-inside-a-stone-cavity is close to furnace/hearth territory (炉) and adjacent to other 火 kanji (焼/煮/燃). 'Grease-blackened walls' is the only cook-specific anchor; the payoff line 'Perfect place to COOK' labels the scene rather than depicting a cooking act (no food, pot, or meal in the meaning story). Held at 3, not below.

story: One crackling Bonfire is stacked directly on top of another Bonfire; their leaping tongues merge and climb, sparks flying twice as high, fusing into a single towering FLAME.
reading_story: Enzo floors his Ferrari past the stacked bonfires; the roaring exhaust spits a FLAME so long it scorches the finish line.

story: The Falling Katana slashes down through rising smoke; beneath it the Coal Brazier's four coals flare white-hot, quenching the blade the instant it lands. One slash, one hiss, job finished — that's how you DO.
reading_story: Drill sergeant Mr. Eaton barks a clipped "ee!" — no questions, no excuses: whatever Eaton points at, you DO.
issues: Minor coherence nick: coals 'quenching' the blade is physically inverted (coals heat; liquid quenches) — the hiss image still lands, but a curator could swap 'quenching' for 'searing/sealing'.
Reading story adds 'Drill sergeant' to Mr. Eaton, an embellishment absent from the registry note; non-contradicting, but flag if persona strictness tightens.

story: A Gnawed Rib-Bone lies to the left of the towering Guillotine Blade; beneath them the Coal Brazier's four coals blaze until the bone chars and the steel glows white-hot — ARDENT.
reading_story: Retzler pumps the bellows all night, hammering glowing iron with ARDENT devotion, sparks stinging his grinning face.
issues: Non-blocking: 'coals blaze until things glow hot' is the stock move for 灬-family kanji; distinctiveness rests on the bone+guillotine cast, so watch for interference if neighboring fire kanji reuse a charring/glowing payoff.

story: Stumpy Sparrow perches stubbornly atop the Coal Brazier; four coals glow beneath her until her stubby tail blackens, smokes, and crisps to CHAR.
reading_story: "Shoooow time!" The Showman torches his own top hat onstage — the crowd gasps as it crumbles into black CHAR.

story: BOIL: the Greybeard Mask hangs over an iron tub, its grey beard trailing into the froth where the Sun bobs like a fat orange dumpling, while the Coal Brazier sears the tub's base from below.
reading_story: Shaq plunges one giant forearm in to stir, barks a short "sha!" as the water jumps to a scalding BOIL, and yanks his arm back out.
