issues: Reading-story phrasing collides with the direct neighbor 者 (n4-mnemonics.json), whose reading story is "Shaq lifts the Greybeard Mask off the Sun, barks a short 'sha', and asks who SOMEONE hiding there could be." The candidate reuses the near-verbatim beat "barks a short \"sha!\"" with the same actor and two of the same components — since 煮 = 者 + 灬, this is the highest-interference pair in the set. Recommend a different Shaq beat (e.g. the sound of the splash, not a bark).

Meaning-story overlap with 暑 (n1-mnemonics.json): "The Sun hangs dead overhead, roasting the Greybeard Mask below it; the carved wooden face sweats resin, its long grey beard dripping..." Same two actors plus heat. The candidate does invert the vertical arrangement (mask above, Sun submerged below) and adds the Coal Brazier, which is what keeps it separable — but the 'beard + heat + moisture' motif is shared.

Minor: the Sun's registry image is "a bright round midday sun blazing in a clear sky, a small dot at its blazing center"; recasting it as "a fat orange dumpling" bobbing in water is a defensible simile (round, buoyant, orange) and only ordinary physical motion, but it softens the persona and drops the defining central dot. Not a gate failure under Actor consistency.
Minor: "iron tub" is a prop, not a phantom component — consistent with existing shipped stories that use unnamed scenery ("vat" in 沸, "winter den" in 熊, "desert/sand" in 丁). Gate 2 passes.

Minor: the Greybeard Mask merely "hangs over" the tub — the least active of the three actors. Spatial fidelity is otherwise correct (⺹ top, 日 middle inside the water, 灬 bottom), so this is a vividness nit rather than a placement error.
Tub-and-steam staging has mild thematic company in 湯 HOT WATER and 浴 BATHE (both n2), though those use Puddle Splash and different keywords, so cross-talk is low.

story: Deep in a winter den: the Sealed Clam-Locket dangles over the sunken Full Moon, a Soup Ladle stirs on the right, and the Coal Brazier smolders under everything — cozy heat for one hibernating BEAR.
reading_story: Mid-routine, Yuna spins into a lift — her surprise skating partner is a huge BEAR, hoisting her aloft on its skates.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'a Soup Ladle stirs on the right' has no object being stirred — giving it a pot of honeyed stew (or similar) would sharpen the visual beat.
Minor (non-blocking): 'sunken Full Moon' inside a den is slightly hard to place; 'half-buried in the den floor' would be more literal.

story: Pot Lid clamps shut the Open Mouth perched on the Swaddle Basket; beside them the Curled Cat, dotted by one Ink Droplet, dozes as the Coal Brazier's low coals beneath make everything RIPEN.
reading_story: Juker guards his crates of green bananas, slapping away every grabbing hand: "Nobody buys until they RIPEN!"
issues: Payoff is slightly abstract: 'make everything RIPEN' has no concrete ripening object in the meaning story (the bananas only appear in the reading story)
Residual interference risk with 熱, which shares Curled Cat + Ink Droplet + Coal Brazier (丸 + 灬); mitigated by the 'low coals / slow' framing but worth watching

story: A stubborn cow refuses to move until, from the right, the Cracking Whip snaps down across its rump, driving it out onto the wide green PASTURE.
reading_story: Heavyset Booker leans on the PASTURE fence, thumping his big ledger as he books every cow in and out.

story: A garlanded cow trembles on the stone altar; drums pound, torches flare, the blade descends — the ANIMAL SACRIFICE.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage strokes his long beard, then solemnly chants the blessing over the ANIMAL SACRIFICE.
issues: Distinctiveness risk: scene is the near-default image for 'sacrifice' and may interfere with 犠 (partner kanji in 犠牲, also built on 牛) — consider a detail unique to the animal-as-victim (e.g. the garland as the pivot image) when 犠 is generated.
Props 'stone altar' and 'blade' echo common component keywords (石, 刀) but are clearly staged as scenery, not glyph parts — acceptable, worth keeping an eye on across the batch.

story: On the altar stone's left edge a garlanded cow stands rigid, steam curling from its nostrils, horns tipped skyward, hooves painted red — the year's SACRIFICE.
reading_story: Gee tugs off his cap at the smoking altar, eyes wet: his own prize heifer is this year's SACRIFICE.
issues: Gate 2 (no phantom components) — borderline pass: the altar stone, garland, steam and red paint are staging/scene props, not presented as component actors. 犠 = 牛 + 義, and 義 is listed under phonetic_extra (carried by reading actor Gee), so nothing in the story is claimed as an unsupplied component. Accepted as staging, but the altar is doing a lot of load-bearing work for a prop.

Distinctiveness (3, not higher) — 'cow on an altar = sacrifice' is the near-tautological image for this kanji and will collide with 牲, the other half of 犠牲, which also carries the 牛 radical and the same offering semantics. Whoever generates 牲 must be handed a deliberately different scene (no altar, no garlanded ox) or the two cards will interfere.

Reading story leans on the same altar scene as the meaning story ('smoking altar' / 'altar stone'), so the two stories are one image rather than two hooks. Not a gate failure (Gee is present and the keyword lands at the end), but it halves the redundancy the two-story design is meant to buy.

Evidence for the passing gates: coverage — 'a garlanded cow' names 牛/cow (§3.1); reading actor — 'Gee tugs off his cap' (§3.3); meaning placement — both stories end on SACRIFICE, matching meaning_placement 'end' (§3.4); actor consistency — Gee only removes a cap and weeps, no invented cognitive ability contradicting the short voiced-twin persona (§3.5); no etymology — no historical or phonetic claim anywhere (§3.6); length — 25 words and 20 words, both well under ~40 (§3.7); spatial fidelity — 'the altar stone's left edge' correctly seats 牛 as the left radical (§3.11).

story: The Prowling Jackal snatches the Kings Crown from the cushion at its right, jams it crooked over one ear, and howls at nothing — a crowned LUNATIC.
reading_story: Kyo howls one endless note into the mic, eyes rolling, until the whole arena chants LUNATIC, LUNATIC.

story: HUNT: the Prowling Jackal pins itself to the clearing's left edge, ribs heaving, frost cracking under one lifted paw, amber eyes locked on the scent-trail cutting rightward through the grass.
reading_story: Master Shu clamps a whistle in his teeth; one short, clipped blast and the HUNT explodes across the frozen field.
issues: GATES ALL PASS. (1) Component coverage: the single mandatory component 犭 is named verbatim as 'the Prowling Jackal'. (2) No phantom components: frost, grass and the scent-trail are un-capitalised scenery/staging, no registry actor is introduced that isn't supplied. (3) Reading actor: 'Master Shu' opens the reading_story. (4) Meaning: 'HUNT:' at position 1, matching meaning_placement='start'. (5) Persona fidelity: image says 'lean jackal crouched low at the LEFT edge of a clearing... frozen mid-prowl' -> story says 'pins itself to the clearing's left edge, ribs heaving... frozen'/lifted paw; registry note says 'Master Shu - clipped twin of Shoe. Short.' -> story says 'one short, clipped blast'. Corpus-consistent with 取/守/首/珠 which all use 'Master Shu' + clipped/precise. (6) No etymology claim. (7) Length: story = 30 words, reading_story = 20 words, both under the ~40 cap.

NON-BLOCKING - tautology weakens the retrieval hook: the actor's defining nature ('Prowling Jackal', 'frozen mid-prowl') IS the keyword 'hunt', so the story is near-circular. It adds no contrastive element the learner can use to distinguish 狩 from the other jackal cards; only 'frost' and the whistle do any disambiguating work.

NON-BLOCKING - the visually dominant right half (守, listed in phonetic_extra) is unrepresented. The story fills that space with an invented 'scent-trail cutting rightward through the grass' rather than anything mapping to the real right-hand shape. Not a phantom-component failure (no actor is named), but it costs spatial fidelity.

NON-BLOCKING - boilerplate collision: 'the clearing's left edge' is near-verbatim shared with 犯, 猫, 独, 猪 and 獄 (all 犭 cards in data/authored/n3-mnemonics.json and n1-mnemonics.json). It reads as template filler, not as a discriminating cue.

NON-BLOCKING - dominant_reading is kun か.る, but the reading_story teaches only the on'yomi しゅ. Per docs/07 §1.3 kun'yomi get no reading actor and are consolidated via vocab, yet vocab[] is empty for this entry, so か.る is currently taught nowhere.
MINOR - 'clamps a whistle in his teeth' echoes the existing 珠 story ('bites the PEARL between his teeth'), a mild Shu-motif repeat.
MINOR - 'pins itself to' is a slightly strained verb for a crouching animal, and a scent-trail is inherently non-visual; both nudge concreteness down a notch.

story: Prowling Jackal crouches at the left edge of the clearing, no pack anywhere — only Fat Grub curling and uncurling in the soil to his right. One jackal, one bug: ALONE.
reading_story: Docker seals himself inside one shipping container, ALONE, stamping "single occupant" on the door — no crew allowed in his box.
issues: Minor (non-gating): reading_story places the keyword mid-sentence ("ALONE, stamping...") rather than as the final payoff; meaning story carries correct end placement.
Minor (non-gating): aloneness is partly conveyed by negation ("no pack anywhere"), which is less imageable than a positive cue.

story: The Prowling Jackal, crouched at the left of a canyon crack, wedges in — ribs scraping both walls, fur tearing off in tufts. The passage is brutally NARROW.
reading_story: Kyo howls his encore jammed in a NARROW backstage corridor, shoulders wedged between the walls, his long ō echoing down the squeeze.

story: The Prowling Jackal plants itself at the left, guarding the Swaddle Basket rocking atop the Serving Platter — hackles up, fangs bared at anyone who steps closer. FIERCE.
reading_story: Moe whirls around, slapping and eye-poking with such FIERCE fury that everyone flees the stage.

story: GAME-HUNTING: a Prowling Jackal, crouched at the left edge, utilizes a Low Stool as its hide, three Bean Sprouts poking up over the stool's seat to screen its pointed snout.
reading_story: Ryo, the hardboiled detective, lowers his hat brim: in this city, tailing a suspect through neon alleys is just GAME-HUNTING by another name.
issues: minor (non-blocking): 用 'utilizes' carries no spatial anchor — it is a verb linking jackal to stool rather than a placed element, so spatial fidelity is only partial (sprouts-above-stool is right, but the middle slot is unrepresented)

minor (non-blocking): the generic 'predator concealed in a hunting blind' frame risks interference with other 犭 hunting kanji (e.g. 狩); the stool + sprouts specifics are what carry the discrimination load, so keep them if this is ever revised

story: A bristling BOAR charges across the clearing — the Prowling Jackal freezes low at the left edge, while high on the right a Greybeard Mask dangles, its long beard brushing the blazing Sun below.
reading_story: Choe kicks open the barn door and a mud-caked BOAR shoots past his knees, squealing into the night.
issues: Minor (non-gating): two animals share one scene — a charging BOAR and the Prowling Jackal in the same clearing. Risk of the learner blending them; the jackal is spatially anchored ('left edge'), which mitigates but does not eliminate it.

Minor (non-gating): the BOAR is a spectator, not a participant — it 'charges across the clearing' without touching or affecting any component actor. A boar colliding with the jackal or knocking the mask loose would bind the keyword to the components rather than leaving a static tableau.

Minor (non-gating): scale incoherence in 'its long beard brushing the blazing Sun below' — the Sun is simultaneously a sky object ('blazing') and a low-hanging prop within beard's reach. Imageable but physically muddled.

Minor (non-gating): the ⺹+日 (Greybeard Mask over Sun) block is the 者 phonetic and will recur across 著/諸/都/暑 etc.; distinctiveness rests almost entirely on the jackal. Worth checking for interference when sibling 者-kanji are generated.

story: At the shrine's south gate, a dog rears up and lays a steaming bone on the altar, tail wagging solemnly — its humble OFFERING.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll lies stiff-armed on the altar tray — the strangest OFFERING the shrine has ever received.
issues: Minor, non-blocking: 'south gate' pairs the 南 component with 'gate', the keyword/actor of 門 (Castle Gate, N5 registry) which is not in 献 — reads as scenery per project precedent (cf. 導, 監 judge notes), but risks cueing a false 南+門 reconstruction; consider 'south entrance' or 'southern steps'.
Minor, spatial fidelity: 献 stages 南 on the left and 犬 on the right; the story colocates dog and south gate without staging the left-right arrangement — acceptable but loose.
Advisory: reading_story restates no glyph components (only Ken + keyword) — acceptable per precedent since full component coverage lives in the main story.

story: At the clearing's left edge the Prowling Jackal freezes. Stacked before it: a Mound of Soil crowning an Open Mouth, both draped in a Hanger Kimono — and swinging from its sleeve, a screeching MONKEY.
reading_story: Enzo Ferrari lifts the hood at the pit stop and a MONKEY in tiny racing goggles is perched on the engine, clutching his stopwatch.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: all four mandatory actors named verbatim — 'Prowling Jackal' (犭), 'Mound of Soil' (土), 'Open Mouth' (口), 'Hanger Kimono' (衣).

Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS: 'clearing' comes from the jackal's registry image, 'sleeve' from the kimono's ('wide sleeves spread open'); no unlisted actor is introduced. 袁 (phonetic_extra) is correctly left implicit rather than invented as an actor.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: 'Enzo Ferrari lifts the hood at the pit stop' — matches note 'Enzo Ferrari', persona intact.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: story terminates on '...a screeching MONKEY.', matching meaning_placement 'end'; reading_story also re-lands the monkey.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: jackal 'freezes' at 'the clearing's left edge' mirrors 'crouched low at the left edge of a clearing... frozen mid-prowl'; draping/stacking/heaping are ordinary physical placements, no invented cognitive ability.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS: nothing is framed as historical derivation.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story = 34 words (≤~40); reading_story = 24 words.
Spatial fidelity is a strength: jackal pinned to the left, then soil-over-mouth-under-kimono stacked vertically to its right, which tracks 犭 + 袁 (土/口/衣 top-to-bottom).

Non-blocking, imageability: the central three actors form a static heap ('Stacked before it: ...') with no action or causality — it reads slightly as an inventory list rather than an event; only the jackal and the monkey actually do anything. This is what caps imageability at 3.
Non-blocking, wording: 'swinging from its sleeve' — the antecedent of 'its' is ambiguous (kimono vs. mouth vs. jackal). 'from the kimono's sleeve' would be tighter at no word cost.

Non-blocking, distinctiveness: 袁 is shared with 遠 and 園, so the kimono/mouth/soil stack alone will not disambiguate; the whole load is carried by the jackal, and jackal-vs-monkey is a mild animal-on-animal interference risk. Adequate but not strong — hence 3.

story: PRISON: the Prowling Jackal crouches against the left wall, a solid Speech Bubble of stacked words wedged between the middle bars, and a chained guard dog snarls at the right-hand gate.
reading_story: Gocker, the night warden, drags his keyring down the PRISON bars until every cell rattles awake.
issues: Two canines in one scene (Prowling Jackal for 犭 + guard dog for 犬) risks internal confusion about which animal encodes which component; the dog is only distinguished by position and the 'chained/guard' qualifier.
'Chained guard dog at a prison gate' is stock imagery and may interfere with neighbouring 犭 kanji that also use the Prowling Jackal.
Story is a static three-item tableau with no causal action linking the elements; only the Speech Bubble 'wedged between the middle bars' creates a genuine binding hook.

Non-blocking: 'night warden' is a scene role invented for Gocker, whose registry entry supplies only a name and the Coker-twin note — acceptable since no fixed persona is defined, but worth confirming reading actors are meant to be role-flexible.

story: BEAST: Bean Sprouts crown a stacked totem — Rice-Paddy Grid below them, Open Mouth gaping at the base — while a snarling dog stands guard on the right, hackles up.
reading_story: Juno hurls a flaming torch into the cave; the shaggy BEAST inside roars back, shaking the walls.
issues: Main story is a static spatial inventory rather than a scene: the Bean Sprouts 'crown', the Rice-Paddy Grid 'is below', the Open Mouth 'gapes' — no component acts on another, so the image has no motion to bind it in memory (docs/07 §3 item 9, flagged as the LLM weak spot).
'stacked totem' is a generic assembly scaffold that will likely recur across other kanji with ⺌/田/口 vertical stacks, creating interference risk (§3 item 10).
The dog reads as semantically on-the-nose for 'beast' — it explains the keyword instead of surprising it, which weakens the retrieval hook even though it is the correct component.
The dog is spatially placed ('on the right') but narratively detached from the totem; it guards nothing in particular, so the 犬 element is the easiest one to drop on recall.

story: SEIZE! The Prowling Jackal springs from the left, jaws snatching the Stumpy Sparrow that sits under a Grass Tuft, and drops the grumpy bird into a palm-up Rubber Glove waiting below.
reading_story: Knuckles the boxer lunges across the ring to SEIZE his opponent's belt, fists locked, refusing to let go.
issues: Minor: components_used array order (犭, ⺾, 隹, 又) does not match narrative order in the story (jackal, sparrow, grass tuft, glove) — cosmetic, no rubric impact.
Minor: reading_story repeats the keyword SEIZE, which is redundant since the meaning story already carries it; harmless but adds a word of load.
Distinctiveness watch: 'predator catches bird' is a generic trope that could interfere with other 隹 kanji; the 犭 jackal and the rubber-glove drop are what keep it separable from 穫/護.

story: Pry up the Pot Lid: beneath it, no dinner — only a pale Silk Cocoon glowing in pitch-black depths, thread slowly unwinding. What's inside? MYSTERIOUS.
reading_story: At midnight Glenn knocks, steps inside without a word, and vanishes down the hallway. Nobody knows what Glenn wants — he's utterly MYSTERIOUS.

story: The Dark Silk Coil dangles above the Plus-Sign Crossroads, Frost Beads clinging to either side of its thread — exactly two icy beads per ten black loops, a perfect RATIO.
reading_story: Ritter tallies laughs per pratfall on his clipboard, obsessed with keeping his sitcom's RATIO perfect.

story: Tipped on the left edge of its velvet cushion, the Kings Crown spills — from its three jeweled points one milk-white sphere rolls out, wet and glowing, settling dead centre: a flawless PEARL.
reading_story: Master Shu snaps a quick bow, bites the PEARL between his teeth to test it, and grins at the sharp little click.
issues: (non-blocking) Distinctiveness is the weak axis: a milk-white sphere rolling off the Kings Crown risks interference with other 王-radical neighbors, especially 球 (sphere/globe) and 玉 (jewel). The pearl-specific texture ('milk-white', 'wet and glowing', 'flawless') and the tipped-cushion action are what keep it separable — if 球 later gets a rolling-ball story with the same actor, one of the two should be re-cut.

story: A heavy Kings Crown rests on its velvet cushion; the Guillotine Blade slams down on its right, cleaving crown and cushion into two equal halves — one for each SQUAD.
reading_story: Hancock signs the muster roll with a flourish, one enormous signature per SQUAD, ink still dripping.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11, graded not gating): in 班 the 刂 sits BETWEEN the two 王 halves, not at the right edge. The story says 'slams down on its right', which faithfully follows the supplied component image ('standing on the right edge') but does not match the actual glyph layout. Non-blocking — the candidate is consistent with its input data; the fix belongs in the 刂 component image, not this story.

Meaning link is slightly arbitrary: cleaving one crown into 'two equal halves — one for each SQUAD' gets to 'divide into groups' only by inference. It works (squad/unit/group = a divided portion) but a learner could equally retrieve 'half', 'split', or 'divide' from this image. This is the main reason distinctiveness is capped at 3.

Interference risk: 'Guillotine Blade slams down and cleaves X in two' is the default action for every 刂 kanji in the deck. The crown-on-cushion object keeps it separable, but the verb phrase carries no distinguishing load.

Reading story is clean and passes all gates (Hancock present, SQUAD present, ~19 words), though it does not exploit the actor note's '-n ending' / short-vowel cue at all — the persona is used as a generic signer. Not a gate failure, just a missed reinforcement of the はん vs はん-long distinction.

story: Kings Crown balances atop a Stepladder, its three jeweled points snagging taut strings stretched between the splayed legs. The whole rickety tower twangs and hums — a golden, teetering HARP.
reading_story: On the marble steps, King raises one hand and a golden HARP swells behind every word of the dream.
issues: Spatial fidelity is slightly loose: the Kings Crown sits 'atop' the Stepladder, yet its points 'snag taut strings stretched between the splayed legs' — the reader must infer the strings run from the crown down to the legs to resolve the harp shape.

Label proximity risk: component actor 'Kings Crown' (meaning story) and reading actor 'King' (reading story) are near-identical strings on the same card; inherent to the record, but a mild interference hazard when both are recalled together.
The strings are an added prop not present in the component registry — justified as the keyword payoff, not a phantom component, but it is the only unsourced object in the scene.

story: Dawn: a rainbow arcs off the Mountain Peak's snowcap and pours into the Kings Crown on the left, brimming it with gold; beneath the peak, Chin Whiskers' four rigid strands chime like tuning forks — the omen spells CONGRATULATIONS.
reading_story: Zwee hauls the temple's bronze bell rope down with both fists — a deep "ZWEEEE" booms across the valley, the toll that means CONGRATULATIONS.
issues: Non-blocking (§3.10 interference risk): rainbow + gold + auspicious-omen framing is generic celebration imagery that may collide with neighbouring 'congratulate/celebrate' kanji (祝, 賀, 慶). The whiskers-as-tuning-forks beat is what keeps it separable — it is carrying most of the distinctiveness load.

Non-blocking (cross-story bleed): the meaning story ends on whiskers that 'chime like tuning forks' and the reading story on a bronze bell toll — two metallic ringing payoffs on the same card, which blurs which cue retrieves which half.
Minor (§3.9): 'the omen spells CONGRATULATIONS' is the one abstract link in an otherwise concrete scene; a physical payoff (e.g. the crown overflowing) would image slightly better.

Minor (§3.11): the registry image specifies a triple-peaked mountain with the middle summit tallest; the story reduces it to 'the peak' / 'snowcap', leaving the distinctive three-point silhouette of 山 unused.

story: A Fishing Net drops over an Open Mouth peeking from the Hanger Kimono's collar; the trapped mouth blows one glowing hoop of smoke that settles around the Kings Crown's points — a perfect RING.
reading_story: Khan, galloping at full speed, spears the golden RING with his lance and wears it as a bracelet.
issues: Minor: Kings Crown's location is not spatially anchored relative to the net/kimono scene — the smoke hoop 'settles around' it but where the crown sits must be inferred (does not block; imageability docked to 4).

story: ARMOR: pried whole from the flooded paddy, the Rice-Paddy Grid bakes into a four-plated breastplate, mud dikes for ridges; the Lightning Bolt fused through its center dangles below the plates as a blinding tasset.
reading_story: On the podium, Coe raises his gold medal wearing full ARMOR, holding the pose so looong that the plates creak.
issues: Minor: 'tasset' is obscure armor jargon; a plainer phrase like 'hangs below the plates as a blinding blade' would picture faster for most learners (non-blocking).

story: The Rice-Paddy Grid's mud dikes squeeze together beneath it, twisting into one tall pedestal that hoists the flooded four-square field skyward — a paddy on a stem, utterly DIFFERENT.
reading_story: Eaton squints at the paddy balanced on its stem, gasps a clipped "Ee!", and stamps the deed: certified DIFFERENT.
issues: Minor: 共 (together, null actor) is realized only adverbially in 'squeeze together' rather than as a distinct visual entity; concept is named and spatially correct (beneath 田), so it passes coverage, but could be sharpened.

story: Left of the counter, Fabric Roll unspools gauze so wide-gapped that the tight bundle stacked at its right shows straight through the holes — threads stretched thin, SPARSE.
reading_story: Saul spreads his court files across a huge empty table: three pages, acres of bare varnish — evidence SPARSE.
issues: Non-blocking (imageability): 'threads stretched thin' is an abstract tag-on after an otherwise concrete image; the scene would be crisper ending directly on the see-through gauze.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness): 'loosely woven fabric + stacked bundle' is the most predictable framing for this component pair, so mild interference risk with other 束-containing kanji that also use a stacked/tight bundle; the see-through hook is the only differentiator.
Non-blocking (concreteness): 'wide-gapped' takes a beat to resolve visually compared with a plainer 'so full of holes'.

story: The Leaning Sickbed tips forward while the Lance-Butt Grip, wedged under its lower right, jabs the shaft up — launching the fever-cloth off the rail to sail steaming down the whole street. EPIDEMIC.
reading_story: Ecker sprints the quarantined street, stamping EPIDEMIC in wet red paint across every shuttered door before the sirens reach him.
issues: Minor (non-blocking, rubric §3 item 12 coherence): 'tips forward while ... jabs the shaft up' uses 'while', leaving it ambiguous whether the jab causes the tip; 'as' or 'when' would tighten the causal chain.
Minor (non-blocking, §3 item 9 imageability): 'sail steaming down the whole street' jumps scale abruptly from a hand-sized fever-cloth to a street-length trajectory, slightly straining the visual.

story: The Leaning Sickbed tilts over the top-left corner; from beneath its rumpled blanket a Feathered Arrow bursts, streaking dead straight across the ward and quivering in the far wall — RAPIDLY.
reading_story: Schitt bolts from the motel office so RAPIDLY his coat is still floating in the doorway behind him.

story: On the Leaning Sickbed, the patient's fever chart shows one flat Horizon Line, and beneath it the pulse trace comes to a dead stop — unmistakable SYMPTOMS.
reading_story: The Showman staggers mid-act, sweating under the spotlight, listing his SYMPTOMS to the gasping crowd — "the shoooow must go on!"

story: Under the Leaning Sickbed's tilted frame, a Feathered Arrow streaks left-to-right and lodges in an Open Mouth gaping mid-shout on the pillow. Swallowing an arrow while yelling: STUPID.
reading_story: Chee, the clipped cheerleader, bounces once and yells "chee!" at an empty stadium — nobody came, the game was yesterday. Cheering alone: STUPID.
issues: Minor (non-gating, coherence): the story says the arrow 'lodges in' the mouth, then the payoff line calls it 'Swallowing an arrow' — 'lodges' and 'swallowing' are slightly inconsistent actions for the same beat; 'Swallowing' could be tightened to 'Catching an arrow mid-yell' for a cleaner single image.
Minor (non-gating): 'streaks left-to-right' is slightly mechanical phrasing for a learner-facing story, though it does correctly encode the 矢-left / 口-right layout inside 疒.

story: HEALING: propped inside the Leaning Sickbed, a Stepladder holds the Full Moon high; the Guillotine Blade drops along the right edge, slicing the fever-cloth free, and moonlight spills down onto the bare heart beneath.
reading_story: Hugh, clipped and small, hiccups one short syllable — "yu!" — over every scraped knee on the playground, and each sting vanishes instantly: pure HEALING.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11): the glyph has 人 above 月 inside 俞, but 'a Stepladder holds the Full Moon high' places the moon on top of the ladder, inverting the vertical order. 心 ('beneath') and 刂 ('right edge') are placed correctly.
reading_story spells out the romanized reading ('yu!') rather than letting the Hugh persona carry it — a mild crutch, not a gate failure.

Distinctiveness risk: moonlight-on-a-heart is a common healing trope and both 月 and 疒 are high-frequency components, so the only strong anti-interference hook is the Guillotine Blade slicing the fever-cloth free.

story: Atop the Kings Crown on its velvet cushion stands a White Candle, wax dripping down over the three jeweled points — a crown too sacred to wear, lit only for the EMPEROR.
reading_story: Coe sprints his final lap into the palace, kneeling breathless at the throne so the EMPEROR can crown him with laurel.

story: High overhead a Wishbone snaps, its legs flying apart; beneath it a Cleaver plunges down and thuds into the Serving Platter below, water sloshing over the rim — a butcher's rinsing BASIN.
reading_story: In Bonn's market square, fishmongers scrub eels in a cold stone BASIN, Rhine mist curling off the water.
issues: Non-blocking interference: n1-mnemonics.json:6601 (益 BENEFIT) already uses 'a Wishbone snaps and both lucky halves clatter onto the Serving Platter' — same two actors in the same above/below relation, and 益/盆 are visually confusable. Only the Cleaver and the water/basin payoff separate them.
Non-blocking overlap: n2-mnemonics.json:4078 (粉 FLOUR) already uses 'a Cleaver slams down, snapping a Wishbone apart', so the Cleaver-snaps-Wishbone beat is reused rather than fresh.

Non-blocking persona drift: n5-reading-actors.json:1785-1789 defines 'Bonn' with no persona body, and this is the corpus's first ぼん story. The candidate uses Bonn as a German city ('In Bonn's market square') rather than as a character agent, which sits against docs/07 §1.2 ('named people... persona can recur as a story agent'). Since this sets the precedent for all later ぼん kanji, consider fixing Bonn as a person now.

story: Twin Pillars stand atop the Horizon Line; just below, a Wishbone snaps and both lucky halves clatter onto the Serving Platter — double the BENEFIT.
reading_story: Accountant Ecker rings his cash register all night, cackling — every chime another BENEFIT in the ledger.
issues: minor: reading story styles the actor as 'Accountant Ecker' — occupation epithet not in the registry note, though nothing in the note is contradicted

story: PROSPER — planted upright on the wide Serving Platter, the Barbed Pike stands guard while the Falling Katana slashes down its diagonal; with every slash the platter grows wider, heavier, gleaming richer, its stubby feet sinking under sheer abundance.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage raises his staff over the village square, chants one long "sēēē", and every stall, field, and family begins to PROSPER.
issues: Non-gating: causal link between katana slashes and the platter growing is arbitrary, though it serves the PROSPER payoff
Non-gating: 'gleaming richer' is slightly abstract garnish; 'stands guard' is a stock beat for the Barbed Pike

story: The Sun sinks in from the left, the Full Moon glides in from the right; edge to edge they settle atop the Serving Platter, fire fusing with silver in one blinding ring — an ALLIANCE.
reading_story: Prime Minister May holds the handshake endlessly — "Mēēēy!" chants the crowd — as she signs the ALLIANCE treaty.
issues: Minor interference risk: 'fire fusing with silver in one blinding ring' evokes brightness, which overlaps conceptually with 明 (bright) — a 日+月 neighbor also listed in phonetic_extra; consider a payoff image keyed to joining/pact rather than light.
Reading story keyword is followed by 'treaty' ('signs the ALLIANCE treaty') — still in the terminal clause and acceptable, but a strict end-position check could flag it.

story: A retainer kneels beside the Railway Tracks, peering into a huge water-filled Serving Platter sunk beneath the rails: its still mirror-surface shows the whole railyard and every worker he must OVERSEE.
reading_story: Khan reins in his horse atop a ridge, rising in the stirrups to OVERSEE ten thousand riders wheeling across the steppe below.
issues: Minor: 'water-filled' introduces water, a common kanji element (氵) not present in 監 — reads as scenery, not a phantom component, but could be trimmed
Minor: the 'mirror-surface' motif slightly overlaps the semantic territory of 鑑 (metal+監, 'mirror'); acceptable since it is a prop, not the keyword

story: TRAY: a wide Serving Platter carries a Dugout Canoe on its left; on its right a Low Stool, a Rubber Glove flopped beneath it, steadies a Lance-Butt Grip jabbing skyward. Nothing spills.
reading_story: Bann the sumo waiter thunders through the banquet hall, one enormous lacquer TRAY balanced flat on his palm, gongs booming with every step.
issues: Non-blocking: the meaning story is a static positional inventory rather than an event; the appositive interruption ('a Low Stool, a Rubber Glove flopped beneath it, steadies a Lance-Butt Grip') crowds the right-hand cluster and is the least picturable part. A single causal beat would lift imageability and reduce interference with other 皿 kanji.

story: The Watching Eye stares upward from below; a Pot Lid clangs down flat across it, knob trembling, metal sealing out every ray. Beneath, the huge pupil rolls in total darkness, seeing nothing — BLIND.
reading_story: Moe gropes across the stage, palms flailing, eyes clamped shut after the pie hit, roaring that his brothers have left him BLIND.

story: A hand presses flat above the Watching Eye like a sailor's visor; shaded from the glare, the huge pupil sweeps the horizon, never blinking — this is how you WATCH OVER.
reading_story: Khan reins in his horse on a ridge, hand shading his brow, to WATCH OVER the endless camp below.
issues: Minor: reading story keyword sits in the final clause ("to WATCH OVER the endless camp below") rather than the very last words — still terminal-payoff, passes gate 4.
Minor: "sweeps the horizon" varies from the registry image's "staring straight at you", but is ordinary eye motion consistent with the Watching Eye persona — not a violation.
Note: "Khan surveying from a ridge" is a slightly generic Khan pose; the repeated hand-shading gesture ties it to this glyph and mitigates interference with other かん kanji (監/観).

story: Perched on the cliff's left edge, the Watching Eye locks onto the far horizon, pupil widening, unblinking through sunset and moonrise — one endless, unbroken STARE.
reading_story: Cho hovers motionless on her broomstick above the empty Quidditch pitch, holding a silent STARE at the spot where the snitch vanished.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: the only mandatory component 目 / "Watching Eye" is named verbatim ("the Watching Eye locks onto the far horizon"). 兆 is phonetic_extra, not mandatory, and is correctly not forced in.

Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS, with a note: "cliff's left edge", "far horizon", "sunset and moonrise" are scenery, not named component actors — no registry persona or radical is smuggled in. "cliff's left edge" additionally does spatial work for 目 as the left radical (rubric item 11, spatial fidelity).
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: "Cho hovers motionless on her broomstick" — actor_name "Cho" present in reading_story, reading_actor_used matches.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: "one endless, unbroken STARE" is the final payoff, matching meaning_placement="end".

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS on both registries: the eye image says "A big unblinking eye ... staring straight at you" and the story keeps it "unblinking"; Cho's note says "Cho Chang, the witch" and the broomstick/Quidditch pitch/snitch framing is consistent with that persona. No invented cognitive faculty — an eye locking onto a point and widening its pupil is ordinary physical behavior for an eye.
Gate 6 (no false etymology) PASS: no claim about 眺's real derivation; purely imaginative.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story 25 words, reading_story 22 words, both well under ~40.

Distinctiveness weakness (graded, non-gating): the component persona "Watching Eye" and the keyword "stare" are near-tautological, so the core image is close to "an eye stares" — a frame that could equally serve 看/眼/睨/覧 and risks interference among 目-family kanji. What rescues it is the far-horizon/vista detail, which does map to the vocab (眺め = scene, 眺める = to look out over); hence 3 rather than 2.
Minor: STARE appears in the reading_story too. Not a gate breach, but it slightly blurs the meaning-story vs reading-story division of labour.

story: Left: Watching Eye stares, never blinking. Right: Still Butte squats, rooted against the howling wind. Wedged glistening in the narrow crack between them, squeezed and quivering, sits one enormous EYEBALL.
reading_story: Sergeant Gunner squints down his scope; the lens pops loose and a huge wet EYEBALL rolls out across the sand, still aiming at him.

story: The Watching Eye stares from the left; from the right the Drooping Willow trails frond after frond across its wide dark pupil, until everything behind that green curtain swims out of focus — DROWSY.
reading_story: Swee stands guard at midnight, spear upright, hiding one short clipped "swee" of a yawn behind his hand — a sentry too DROWSY to notice the gate swing open.
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage): the only mandatory component 目 is named as 'The Watching Eye' and components_used lists 目; registry image (big unblinking eye, dark pupil) is honored by 'stares' and 'its wide dark pupil'.

PASS gate 2 (no phantom components): 'Drooping Willow' is not invented — data/authored/decomposition-overrides.json gives 睡 = [目, 垂], and data/authored/n2-component-actors.json defines 垂 as actor_name 'Drooping Willow' (image: weeping willow whose long fronds hang straight down over a low earthen mound). 垂 is also the supplied phonetic_extra, so naming it is legitimate, not a phantom.

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): fronds trailing across the pupil and forming a 'green curtain' is ordinary physical motion for a willow and matches the registry image; no cognitive ability is invented for either actor. Swee is male ('his hand'), matching the corpus majority for this reading actor (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:3557, 6329, 7756).

PASS gate 3 (reading actor): 'Swee' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor_used; 'one short clipped "swee"' correctly encodes vowel_length=short per data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json:837-841.

PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): DROWSY is the final word of story and meaning_placement='end' is accurate; in reading_story it lands as the late payoff ('a sentry too DROWSY to notice the gate swing open').

PASS gate 6 (no etymology) and gate 11 (spatial fidelity): 'stares from the left' / 'from the right the Drooping Willow' matches the 目-left, 垂-right order in decomposition-overrides.json; no historical/etymological claim is made.
PASS gate 7 (length): story 33 words, reading_story 28 words, both under ~40. Minor non-gating clutter: 'spear upright' in reading_story is decorative and carries no encoding load.

NON-GATING (distinctiveness, why 3 not 4): near-neighbor 眠 SLEEP (data/authored/n3-mnemonics.json) already builds on the same Watching Eye with a covering coming down ('the heavy lid slams down like a shop shutter'). This card's 'green curtain' of willow fronds over the pupil is the same schema with a different prop, and DROWSY vs SLEEP are semantically adjacent — real interference risk at review time, mitigated only by the willow's colour/texture.

NON-GATING (imageability, why 4 not 5): slight POV shift — the eye is first seen from outside ('across its wide dark pupil') then from inside ('everything behind that green curtain swims out of focus'). The image survives it, but the camera moves mid-sentence.
components_used corrected to include the phonetic 垂 (Drooping Willow), genuinely present in the glyph and legitimately staged by the story (same class as 鳩/九).

story: Your uncle sits high on the dugout roof; below him a giant Watching Eye presses to the fence, pupil locked on every sloppy pass. Uncle above, Eye below — the league's most relentless COACH.
reading_story: Toker strolls onto the track still puffing; the COACH plucks the joint away, blows the whistle, and sends him running laps until sundown.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: both mandatory components are named verbatim — 叔 via its kanji_keyword ("Your uncle sits high on the dugout roof") and 目 via its registry actor ("a giant Watching Eye presses to the fence").
Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS: dugout roof, fence, league and the whistle/track/laps are scenery and props, not named component actors; nothing outside 叔+目 is presented as a piece of the glyph.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: reading_actor "Toker" opens the reading_story ("Toker strolls onto the track still puffing"), and the とく sound is carried by the name itself.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: keyword is the terminal payoff — "the league's most relentless COACH." meaning_placement="end" is accurate.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: Watching Eye stays within its registry image ("big unblinking eye… dark pupil, staring straight at you") — "pupil locked on every sloppy pass" is its defined function, and "presses to the fence" is ordinary physical motion, not an invented cognitive ability. Toker matches the established corpus persona (cf. n1-mnemonics 徳: "Toker stubs out his joint…"; n3 惑/得-line: "short, clipped puffs — 'toku, toku'").
Gate 6 (no false etymology) PASS: nothing is framed as historical origin.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story is 33 words, reading_story 23 — both under ~40.
Spatial fidelity is a strength: 督 is 叔 over 目 and the story states the stack twice ("sits high on the dugout roof; below him…", then "Uncle above, Eye below").
Minor coherence wobble (non-gating): "dugout" is baseball but "sloppy pass" is a soccer/basketball action — the sport slips mid-sentence. "sloppy throw" would tighten the image.

Distinctiveness risk (non-gating, drives the 3): "Watching Eye" appears 24 times in n1-mnemonics.json, and eye-based supervision already carries 監 ("a hand presses flat above the Watching Eye like a sailor's visor… this is how you WATCH OVER") and 眺 ("one endless, unbroken STARE"). The uncle-on-the-dugout-roof anchor is what separates 督 from that family; without it the frame would be generic.

Secondary interference (non-gating): 宰 already uses a baseball-dugout authority figure in its reading_story ("the MANAGER climbs the dugout steps… takes the ball from Cy"). MANAGER vs COACH in the same dugout setting is a mild confusion pair worth watching during curation.

Content safety (non-gating): explicit cannabis reference ("still puffing", "plucks the joint away"). It is inherent to the registry actor name and matches existing precedent in the corpus, and the framing is corrective rather than glamorizing, so no change required.

story: Watching Eye stares from the left: Hawk Talon pins a Bedsheet Cover over the Bickering Twins, whose kicking legs hook a Crescent Moon and trip a cow. It's over so fast even the unblinking eye must BLINK.
reading_story: Shunsuke the striker fires his shot — BLINK and you miss it; the net is already rippling.
issues: Minor: 'kicking legs hook a Crescent Moon and trip a cow' packs two component payoffs into one clause, slightly crowding an otherwise clean tableau (evidence: rubric §3 item 13 conciseness/low load — non-gating).

Note: Watching Eye's registry image says 'unblinking' and the story makes it blink; allowed as ordinary physical action (not a cognitive-ability contradiction) and it is the keyword payoff, but flagging for the human queue's awareness.

story: A stubby Wall Peg juts from the castle stone, and slung over its blunt arm — blade up top, long shaft dangling to the floor — hangs one dusty, cobwebbed HALBERD.
reading_story: Moo the cow chews the HALBERD's tassel until the guard yanks the weapon back, and she lets out one short, flat "moo."
issues: Non-gating (distinctiveness risk): 'hang an object on the peg' is the single most predictable use of the Wall Peg persona ('to hold up whatever is slung over it'). Any other マ-kanji story built on this actor will likely reuse the same frame, so interference risk across the マ family is real. Only the 'dusty, cobwebbed' + 'blade up top, shaft dangling to the floor' specifics keep it above threshold.

story: A Falling Katana slashes a notch at the top, the Horizon Line lies ruler-straight beneath it, and a Starfish sprawls wide below — the three lock together as one Feathered Arrow streaking skyward: ARROW.
reading_story: The Sheriff draws no gun — he snatches an ARROW out of midair, snaps it over his badge, and the outlaws surrender on the spot.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 'the three lock together as one Feathered Arrow' is slightly diagrammatic — an assembly assertion rather than one continuous scene, though each element is concretely imaged.
Minor (non-gating): assembly-into-whole-glyph framing is a reusable pattern; keep an eye on interference with visually adjacent kanji such as 失.

story: On the left, the Boulder rolls free from its overhang; right, the Curled Cat springs off the Plus-Sign Crossroads as the grey rock hits tarmac and SMASHES into gravel.
reading_story: Cy winds up on the mound and hurls a fastball straight through the dugout window — glass SMASHES across the bench.
issues: Non-blocking: 'the grey rock hits tarmac' re-labels the Boulder mid-sentence, which can read as a second object; naming it 'the Boulder' again would tighten coherence.
Non-blocking: the core scene (stone smashing on pavement) is the expected image for 'smash', so distinctiveness against 壊/破/割 rests entirely on the leaping cat.

story: The rough grey Boulder is prised from under its cliff-overhang, mossy flank and all, and rammed down a huge bronze barrel; the fuse hisses, the hillside jumps, and the immovable stone thunders skyward — fired from a CANNON.
reading_story: Ho stuffs himself down the CANNON instead of the chimney this year — "Ho-ho-hooo!" booms the blast, launching Santa from rooftop to rooftop.

story: Acid-yellow SULPHUR crusts the scene: the grey Boulder squats left while a Pot Lid clangs down onto a Sealed Clam-Locket, both perched above River Rapids boiling milky-white below.
reading_story: Ryu hurls a Hadouken into a volcanic vent; the blast belches choking yellow smoke that dusts his white gi with SULPHUR.
issues: Non-gating nit: 'SULPHUR crusts the scene' leaves the keyword attached to no specific object; crusting it onto the Boulder itself would sharpen the payoff.

Non-gating nit: 'boiling' lends the River Rapids a heat property absent from its registry image ('fast parallel channels of white-water rapids rushing straight downhill') — reads as churn here, but watch for drift if reused.

story: Beneath the cliff-overhang, the mossy grey Boulder settles onto one square of a giant grid scratched into the rock floor — the heaviest black playing stone ever set down in a game of GO.
reading_story: Goh cracks his knuckles, drops a stone with a thunderclap, and sweeps the board clean — nobody in the valley beats Goh at GO.
issues: Non-blocking: component actor 石/Boulder is defined as 'squat and immovable' yet the story has it 'settles onto one square' — ordinary physical placement, so it passes the actor-consistency gate (only invented cognitive abilities are rejected), but the wording brushes against the persona's stated immobility.

Non-blocking: the reading actor note stresses that Goh is the CLIPPED short-vowel twin (vs ごう Gough); the reading_story conveys weight/voicing ('thunderclap') but nothing signals shortness, so the vowel-length cue is under-encoded.

Non-blocking: phonetic_extra 其 is unused. Not a gating failure (only supplied mandatory components must appear, and naming an unsupplied actor would risk a phantom), just noted for coverage bookkeeping.
Non-blocking: 'grid scratched into the rock floor' / 'black playing stone' / 'board' are scene props denoting the keyword GO, not actors from another kanji — no phantom-component violation.

story: Boulder squats at the left edge of the grave plot, mossy flank chiselled flat and lettered deep. Rain pools in the cut names. The immovable grey slab now stands as a TOMBSTONE.
reading_story: Hee hides behind the TOMBSTONE, clipped little giggles — "hee, hee" — ricocheting off the wet granite until the whole graveyard snickers back.
issues: Gate 1 component coverage PASS: the sole mandatory component 石 is named as its registry actor in the opening word ('Boulder squats at the left edge'); components_used ['石'] matches.

Gate 2 no phantom components PASS: only scenery is added ('grave plot', 'rain', 'granite', 'graveyard') — no unsupplied actor persona is introduced. Correctly does NOT personify 卑 (phonetic_extra, no actor supplied, so naming it would have been a phantom).
Gate 3 reading actor PASS: 'Hee hides behind the TOMBSTONE ... "hee, hee"' — reading_actor_used 'Hee' matches reading_actor.actor_name for ひ.
Gate 4 meaning lands PASS: keyword is the final payoff word — 'now stands as a TOMBSTONE.' — matching meaning_placement 'end'.

Gate 5 actor consistency PASS: Boulder registry image is 'rough grey boulder ... squat and immovable, moss creeping across its cold flank'; story reuses squat/immovable/grey/mossy flank verbatim in spirit. Hee's note 'clipped giggler — "hee". Short.' matches 'clipped little giggles'. Chiselling is an ordinary external physical action on a stone, not an invented cognitive ability.
Gate 6 no etymology PASS: no historical or origin claim; framed purely as an imagined scene.
Gate 7 length PASS: story is 32 words, reading_story 23 words, both under ~40 with no filler.
Spatial fidelity: 'left edge' correctly stages 石 as the left-hand radical of 碑.

Non-blocking weakness (drives the distinctiveness 3): the story is semantically near-transparent — a stone chiselled into a grave marker IS a tombstone — so the scene carries little cue value beyond the meaning itself. Retrieval depends on remembering the keyword rather than the image. A more arbitrary hook would score higher.

Non-blocking: 卑 contributes nothing to the story; the ひ reading rests entirely on Hee. Acceptable since 卑 is phonetic_extra with no supplied actor, but the card has no visual handle for that half of the glyph.

story: MAGNET: the Boulder (Horizon Line capping an Open Mouth) drags the Twin Pillars — and the Silk Cocoon beneath them — skidding leftward across sand until they slam against its mossy flank.
reading_story: Jee grabs the mic, and every steel folding chair in the club slides toward him mid-verse — the clipped emcee is a human MAGNET.
issues: Imageability drag: '(Horizon Line capping an Open Mouth)' is a static parenthetical gloss, not an action — 一 and 口 are named but inert, which is the weakest form of coverage and interrupts the single-frame scene.

Physical incongruity softens the payoff: a magnet dragging STONE pillars is off-key (magnets take iron, not rock). The reading story's 'steel folding chairs' does the job correctly; the meaning story does not.

Distinctiveness risk: 'across sand' inside a 石-family scene invites interference with 砂 (sand = 石 + 少). The sand comes from the Horizon Line image, so this collision will recur on every Boulder + Horizon Line kanji.
Minor: the Silk Cocoon is purely passive ('beneath them') — named but doing nothing, so it carries little retrieval weight.

story: Boulder squats where cliff meets surf, immovable, moss steaming as each green wave shatters white against his cold flank — he is the first stone the tide slaps at the SEASHORE.
reading_story: Key the locksmith wades the SEASHORE at low tide, jiggling his single "kee" into barnacled crevices — every tide pool, he insists, is a lock to pick.

reading_story: Saul chisels "Better Call Saul" into the courthouse CORNERSTONE — every case, he brags, is built on him.

story: You stop dead on the path; on your left, the Roadside Shrine's hovering spirit presses the steaming offering bowl into your hands — free hot food for all: WELFARE.
reading_story: The Sheriff empties his saddlebags in the town square, dealing out WELFARE checks with one clipped "shi!" to the whole dusty town.

story: HELP arrives on the left of the frozen mountain path: the Roadside Shrine's offering bowl gushes incense, its hovering spirit thawing my numb right hand until I can stand and walk again.
reading_story: Yuna the figure skater lands her triple axel, then glides straight over to HELP a wobbling toddler peel himself off the rink wall.

story: A white ram trots up to the Roadside Shrine on the left, dipping its nose into the smoking offering bowl; the hovering spirit flares gold over the path — AUSPICIOUS.

(non-blocking) 羊 is handled as phonetic_extra only ('a white ram'), which is legal, but the ram does nothing that ties to しょう — it is decorative rather than load-bearing in either story.

story: Atop a pedestal built to show results, the Setting-Sun Cage creaks open, and a single folded BALLOT flutters down between its red-lit bars.
reading_story: Hugo, exiled and dramatic, casts his BALLOT with a flourish as long as one of his novels.

story: Behind the Rice Stalk, the Falling Katana slashes a heart open; the Ink Droplet drips in and blots the wound shut, sealing inside it one SECRET.
reading_story: Hee cups the SECRET behind her hand, leaking clipped giggles — "hee! hee!" — every time someone begs her to tell.

story: On the left of the paddy, the Rice Stalk sways like a metronome, and every grain it loses drops to its right, landing in one flawless, evenly spaced line — REGULARITY.

story: Left stands the Rice Stalk. A Falling Katana slashes its name down to the Horizon Line, and a Sand Trickle pours from the cut, spelling out the stalk's proud APPELLATION.

Interference risk: the 禾+小+ノ cast (rice stalk, sand, blade) overlaps with 秒-series neighbors; only the sand-spelling-letters image differentiates the scene

story: The golden Rice Stalk leans in from the left as a Stepladder straddles a huge beating heart on the right, splayed legs planted either side — every drooping grain shakes loose. HARVEST.

story: On the left a golden Rice Stalk bows its ripe head; perched right on that head, Stumpy Sparrow flaps stubby wings, squeaking for chewed grain like a nestling — old yet utterly IMMATURE.
reading_story: Chee, the clipped cheerleader, barks one sharp "chee!" — her squad dissolves into giggles, pom-poms flying, the routine collapsing into an IMMATURE mess.

Reading story's payoff phrase 'collapsing into an IMMATURE mess' is the generic half of the pair — abstract 'mess' rather than a concrete image; it leans on the story for distinctiveness.

story: Beside the golden Rice Stalk, a Hawk Talon plunges from above, nailing a Lightning Bolt upright next to the setting Sun — from that seared mud springs one perfect RICE PLANT.

issues: Minor persona drift: story says 'the setting Sun' but the registry image defines Sun as 'a bright round midday sun blazing in a clear sky' — a visual-state deviation, not an invented cognitive ability, so not gate-failing.
Slight busyness: four actors in one causal chain ('talon nails bolt next to sun') keeps coverage but the bolt-as-nail plus sun-on-horizon juxtaposition takes a beat to picture.

story: The Rice Stalk stands ripe beside the Thatched House; under its roof the Muddy Boar hauls sheaves in all day, snout caked, bristles dusted with grain — sweating for its EARNINGS.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr idles at the farm gate, meter ticking; every sack of rice he ferries to market clinks another coin onto his EARNINGS.
issues: Minor style: 'hauls sheaves in all day' is slightly awkward phrasing, marginally softens the single-frame image
Payoff word 'sweating for its EARNINGS' ends on an abstraction, though anchored by concrete labor imagery

story: A Rice Stalk droops in at the left; beside it the Pot Lid presses down on the Open Mouth, squeezing its chewed straw through the Goalpost Frame below into flat pages — a MANUSCRIPT.
reading_story: Coe sprints the final lap clutching his MANUSCRIPT overhead, pages streaming behind him; he refuses to drop a single sheet before the finish line.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the open Goalpost Frame has no flat surface, so the squeeze-into-flat-pages step is slightly hand-wavy as an image.
Minor (non-gating): Rice Stalk is a passive scene-setter ('droops in at the left') rather than a participant in the action.
Minor (non-gating): 'Coe sprints the final lap' is Coe's generic default action and may recur across other kou-reading kanji; distinctiveness rests on the manuscript-pages detail.

story: Braced on the Low Stool, the Lance-Butt Grip thrashes the Rice Stalk; grain sprays over the Bedsheet Cover, fills the upturned War Helmet, and buries the Rubber Glove below in a golden drift of CEREALS.
reading_story: Coker cannonballs into the grain silo; CEREALS erupt over the rim in a golden wave, and only his hat still shows.
issues: PASS component coverage: all 6 mandatory actors named verbatim — 'Low Stool' (几), 'Lance-Butt Grip' (殳), 'Rice Stalk' (禾), 'Bedsheet Cover' (冖), 'War Helmet' (士), 'Rubber Glove' (又).
PASS no phantom components: the only non-actor nouns are 'grain' and 'golden drift', both licensed by the 禾 image ('heavy with grain', 'golden rice stalk').

PASS actor consistency: thrashing with a gripped lance-butt, being braced on a stool, an upturned helmet catching grain, and a glove being buried are all ordinary physical motions — no invented cognitive faculty contradicts any persona.
PASS meaning placement: story ends on '...golden drift of CEREALS', matching meaning_placement='end'.
PASS reading gate: reading_actor_used='Coker' appears as the first word of reading_story, and CEREALS is the payoff of the silo image.
PASS no etymology: purely imaginative scene, no historical/derivational claim.
PASS length: story is 35 words (≤ ~40); reading_story 21 words.

NON-BLOCKING — spatial fidelity (rubric §11, graded not gating) is loose: 穀 is 士 over 冖 with 禾 lower-left and 殳 right, but the story opens on 几/殳 (right side) and reaches 士 (top) third-to-last. Only 'buries the Rubber Glove below' carries positional information.

NON-BLOCKING — 'golden' is reused in the story, the reading_story ('golden wave') and the 禾 source image; one of the three could be swapped for a fresher sensory detail (dust, husks, rattle) to sharpen distinctiveness.

NON-BLOCKING — distinctiveness risk: threshing/harvest is the default scene for the 禾 family (穂 / 稲 / 穫 / 積), so this story could interfere with neighbours unless those use clearly different action verbs.

story: EAR of ripe grain droops from the Rice Stalk standing left; to its right a Plus-Sign Crossroads sits atop the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid, a red heart pounding in the mud beneath.
reading_story: EAR clenched in his teeth, Swee sprints along the paddy dike at sunset, loose seeds spraying behind him.
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage, docs/07 §3.1): all four supplied components are named — 禾 'the Rice Stalk standing left', 十 'a Plus-Sign Crossroads', 田 'the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid', 心 'a red heart pounding in the mud' (心 has actor=null, so kanji_keyword 'heart' is the correct surface form).

PASS gate 3 (reading actor): 'Swee' appears in reading_story and reading_actor_used matches. NON-GATING DATA NOTE: dominant_reading is kun ほ, yet the supplied reading_actor is on'yomi すい — per docs/07 §1.3 kun'yomi get no reading actor, so this reading_story teaches すい, not the dominant ほ. That is an input-record mismatch, not a candidate defect, but the ほ reading is left untaught.
PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): keyword 'EAR' is the first word of the story and meaning_placement='start' matches. Same in reading_story.

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): no invented cognitive ability. 'Crossroads sits atop the Rice-Paddy Grid' is ordinary physical placement (explicitly permitted); 'heart pounding' is a heart's defined nature; the drooping ear is verbatim 禾's registry behaviour.
PASS gate 6 (no etymology): purely imaginative staging, no historical claim.
PASS gate 7 (length): story 31 words, reading_story 18 words — both under ~40.
STRONG on spatial fidelity (rubric item 11): 穂 = 禾 left + 恵 right with 十 over 田 over 心, and the story stages exactly that — 'standing left' → 'to its right' → 'atop' → 'beneath'.

DISTINCTIVENESS WEAKNESS (rubric item 10, scored 3): the scene is built almost entirely from rice-field furniture (rice stalk, grain, flooded paddy, mud, dike, seeds), which is the shared vocabulary of the whole 禾/田 neighbourhood (稲, 種, 穫, 秋…). Only the crossroads-over-paddy-with-heart-beneath is interference-resistant, and it is static.

KEYWORD DOES LITTLE WORK: 禾's registry image already reads 'its ripe head drooping over gracefully at the top', so 'EAR of ripe grain droops from the Rice Stalk' restates the component rather than earning the keyword. Any 禾 kanji could open with this line, which is what caps distinctiveness at 3.

MINOR IMAGEABILITY BLUR: 'a red heart pounding in the mud beneath' leaves the referent of 'beneath' ambiguous (beneath the crossroads or beneath the grid), and a tarmac-painted crossroads resting on flooded water is spatially unanchored — vivid, but the picture wobbles.

story: Left, the Rice Stalk sways. Right, a Hawk Talon grips from above, the Rake Hand curled beneath it, prongs combing a trembling heart at the bottom until every beat slows into CALM.
reading_story: Onslow wades into the flooded paddy at dusk, breathing slowly; the ripples flatten around his knees and the whole valley goes CALM.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): 穏 shares its entire right side (爪+ヨ+心) with 急 and 隠, so 禾 is the sole discriminator — yet 'Left, the Rice Stalk sways' is decorative and never joins the calming action. The payoff ('every beat slows into CALM') would read identically for a story built only on 爪ヨ心. Recommend making the rice stalk causal (e.g. the stalk's swaying is what settles the heart) rather than a scene-setting clause.

Non-blocking (imageability): the 'Left, ... Right, ...' opening reads as a positional diagram rather than a scene; spatial fidelity is excellent but the first sentence spends 5 words on stage directions with no action.

Non-blocking: the reading story's payoff (ripples flattening into CALM) is thematically near-identical to the meaning story's payoff (beats slowing into CALM), so the two lines carry one image instead of two distinct retrieval hooks.

story: HARVEST: a lone chopstick — one of a pair — stands stabbed upright in a heaped mound of grain, a Grass Tuft knotted at its tip; the Rice Stalk, lashed on from the left, shakes its grain loose over the mound.
reading_story: Knuckles the boxer is paid in sacks of grain, hauling his purse out of the ring one sack at a time — an entire fight-night HARVEST.
issues: Non-gating: 隻 is concretized as an unnamed prop ('a lone chopstick') rather than a registry actor; coverage still passes because the kanji_keyword 'one of a pair' is stated verbatim, but the chopstick is invented dressing that will not recur across other 隻 kanji.

Non-gating coherence wobble: the mound of grain already exists before the Rice Stalk 'shakes its grain loose over the mound', so the harvesting action reads as redundant to the scene it is supposed to produce.
Distinctiveness risk: the grain-mound harvest framing overlaps the semantic field of 穂/稲/収穫-adjacent kanji; the chopstick+grass-knot hook is the only thing separating it from neighbours.

story: Beneath the Thatched House's peaked roof, the Wishbone snaps apart, its two legs punching down through the grassy bank — splitting open the Burrow Hole, a dark den yawning underneath: a HOLE.
reading_story: Ketel the vodka man tips his bottle and pours every last clear drop down a HOLE, then peers in after it, moaning "ketsu..."
issues: Non-blocking: the keyword 'HOLE' is pre-echoed mid-story inside the mandated actor name 'Burrow Hole' before the final payoff -- unavoidable for a self-component kanji whose actor name contains the keyword; the true payoff still lands at the end.

Non-blocking: in the reading_story the keyword HOLE sits mid-sentence ('...down a HOLE, then peers in...'); allowed per approved precedent (丸, 久), but an end placement would bind reading-to-keyword slightly tighter.
Non-blocking: the spatial mash of a grassy bank directly beneath a cottage roof is mildly contrived, costing one imageability point.

story: A masked burglar crouches above the Burrow Hole, tipping a sack of gold candlesticks in past its low roofed lip; they slide down into the dark without one clink — pure STEALTH.
reading_story: Settler Seth siphons his neighbour's seed corn at moonrise, wagon wheels bound in sheepskin, rolling away over soft pasture in perfect STEALTH.
issues: GATE 1 (component coverage) PASS - the sole mandatory component 穴 is named verbatim as 'the Burrow Hole'.

GATE 2 (no phantom components) PASS - 'masked burglar', 'sack of gold candlesticks', 'dark' are lowercase generic scene participants, not Title-Case registry actors. House precedent explicitly licenses this: data/authored/n3-mnemonics.json 盗 opens 'A thief eyes the buffet', 米 'A farmer's hand flings...', 客 'shelter a stranger'; and a prior judge note on 伏 in data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json reasons that scene attributes 'are not named kanji parts' and pass this gate.

ADVISORY on gate 2 (non-blocking): 窃 = 穴 over 切, and 切 appears only in phonetic_extra with no supplied actor, so the bottom slot of the glyph is un-actored. The burglar is the story's agent and physically occupies that vacancy, creating some risk a learner binds 'burglar' -> 切. Not a failure (he is generic, not a persona), but the Burrow Hole is demoted to a passive receptacle rather than acting.
GATE 3 (reading actor) PASS - 'Settler Seth' opens the reading_story; reading_actor_used 'Settler' matches actor_name in data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json:905.
GATE 4 (meaning lands) PASS - STEALTH is the final word of both stories, matching meaning_placement 'end'.

GATE 5 (actor consistency) PASS - the component image ('a little roofed opening leading down into a hidden underground den') is reproduced faithfully as 'past its low roofed lip; they slide down into the dark'. Tipping a sack and objects sliding are ordinary physical motion, no invented cognitive faculty.

ADVISORY on gate 5 (non-blocking): the Settler registry entry supplies only a name and coda note, but every prior corpus use paints an upstanding homesteader (n2 'plants his flag on the frontier', n2 'plants the final fencepost... ESTABLISHMENT', n3 'declares his own bold OPINION to the whole town'). Casting him as a moonlight corn thief is a tonal inversion of that established persona. Physically ordinary and keyword-appropriate, so it does not fail gating, but it is drift.
GATE 6 (no false etymology) PASS - nothing framed as historical derivation.
GATE 7 (length) PASS - 31 words (story) and 22 words (reading_story), both well under ~40.

SPATIAL (graded, non-gating): good - 穴 is the crown of 窃, and staging the loot as passing down THROUGH the roofed lip into the space beneath correctly maps the top-over-bottom layout. Minor nit: the burglar himself crouches above the crown, a position no element of the glyph occupies.

DISTINCTIVENESS (scored 3): the criminal-with-loot frame directly echoes its nearest neighbour 盗 in data/authored/n3-mnemonics.json ('A thief... slips it under his coat to STEAL the feast') and, more loosely, 奪's 'Datcher the pickpocket'. The Burrow Hole and the silent no-clink drop are genuine differentiators and carry the card, but the protagonist type is near-identical to 盗's. Both stories in this candidate are also theft-under-cover-of-night scenes, so meaning and reading stories cross-cue rather than diversify.

story: Burrow Hole gapes in the grassy bank; the Landed Meteor drops straight down into its throat and jams there, smoking, sealing the den's mouth so nothing passes — PLUG UP.
reading_story: Chitter squeaks in the dark, clawing at the smoking rock overhead — one crash was enough to PLUG UP her only door forever.
issues: Minor (non-blocking, rubric item 4 'meaning lands'): in reading_story the keyword is followed by a trailing tail — 'enough to PLUG UP her only door forever' — so PLUG UP is near-final rather than final. The main story's placement is clean ('— PLUG UP.'), which is what meaning_placement='end' governs, so this does not fail the gate.

Minor (rubric item 10 'distinctiveness'): 穴 is a high-frequency component (空/究/突/窓/窮/窃) and 至 also feeds 室/到/致; 'something blocks the hole' is a generic trope for this radical family. The meteor-jammed-in-the-burrow-throat specifics carry the load and keep interference low, but the cue is not maximally unique.

story: DESTITUTE — the Expectant Torso huddles under the Burrow Hole's dark opening, heavy belly pressed to bare earth, the taut Longbow propped to her right, string humming over an empty den.
reading_story: Governor Cuomo stands at the podium announcing budget cuts, pockets turned inside out, declaring the whole state officially DESTITUTE.
issues: Static tableau: the three actors are positioned relative to each other but never interact causally, which weakens distinctiveness against other 穴-crown kanji (窟, 窯, 窒).
'string humming over an empty den' implies a shot was just fired, but nothing in the scene fires the bow — mildly incoherent carryover from the Longbow's registry image.
'huddled in a dark hole, empty den' is fairly generic destitution imagery; the component actors, not the scene, are doing the disambiguating work.
Reading story is competent but formulaic (politician + empty pockets); it does not encode the long-ū vowel length beyond relying on the persona itself.

story: The flooded Rice-Paddy Grid rears upright like a scaly chest, mud dikes flexing as ribs; below it a barbed Fishhook curls and twitches as the lashing tail. The whole paddy uncoils, roaring — a DRAGON.
reading_story: Ryu throws a Hadouken; the blue fireball spirals mid-air into a roaring DRAGON that coils around the dojo rafters.
issues: GATE 1 (component coverage) PASS — both actor-bearing components named verbatim: 'Rice-Paddy Grid' (田) and 'Fishhook' (乙). 竜 itself carries actor:null, so nothing owed for it.
GATE 2 (no phantoms) PASS — 'scaly chest', 'ribs', 'tail' are similes describing the two supplied actors, not new components; the phonetic_extra 立 is correctly left unused (extra, not mandatory).
GATE 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Ryu' opens the reading_story and matches reading_actor_used.
GATE 4 (meaning lands) PASS — story terminates on '— a DRAGON.'; meaning_placement:'end' is accurate. Keyword also lands in the reading_story.

GATE 5 (actor consistency) PASS, and unusually tight: the story reuses the registry image's own nouns ('flooded', 'mud dikes' for 田; 'barbed', 'twitches' for 乙). Motion only — rearing, curling, uncoiling — no invented cognitive faculty. Ryu/Hadouken is in-persona for Street Fighter.
GATE 6 (no etymology) PASS — no historical claim; 竜 is in fact a dragon pictograph, and the candidate wisely never says so.
GATE 7 (length) PASS — story 34 words, reading_story 20 words, both under ~40.

MINOR (non-gating, coherence): the transformation mixes metaphors — the paddy first 'rears upright like a scaly chest' (a torso), then 'uncoils' (a serpent body that was never staged). Picking one shape would sharpen the image.
MINOR (non-gating, distinctiveness): 'roaring' appears in both the meaning story and the reading story, blurring the two retrieval cues. Varying the verb in one would separate them.

MINOR (non-gating): Ryu's dragon-named move is the Shoryuken ('rising dragon fist'), not the Hadouken — using it would make the reading cue less generic and tie the persona to DRAGON more tightly. Not a persona violation, just a missed hook.
SPATIAL FIDELITY (graded, strong): 'below it' places Fishhook under Rice-Paddy Grid, matching 竜's actual top-to-bottom stacking with the hook stroke at the bottom right.

story: You stand up on a clifftop; at your right, Mountain Peak balances atop Chin Whiskers' rigid grey beard, snowy summit swaying, stiff strands dangling over empty air — one gust from tipping off the EDGE.
reading_story: Tanner trims a fresh hide, blade gliding along the very EDGE of the leather — one slip past that line ruins the whole skin.
issues: Minor: 'Mountain Peak balances atop X, about to fall' repeats the schema of shipped 崩 (Mountain Peak balanced on Full Moons, then CRUMBLES); bases and payoffs differ but the precarious-balance trope is shared within N1.
Minor: Tanner blade-on-leather scene is adjacent to 短's reading story (Tanner snips strap SHORT); edge-line-of-hide vs stubby-belt payoffs keep them separable.

story: Under the towering Bamboo Grove, a Longbow bends low, bowstring scratching 1, 2, 3 into wet clay beneath each stalk — the grove ranked, every stalk wearing its own NO.
reading_story: Dyer stencils indigo digits onto dripping sheets, snapping each onto the line in order — every sheet hung under its own bold white NO.

Non-blocking: numbering/ranking imagery is a common hook for ordinal kanji (番, 号, 序, 次), so distinctiveness caps at 3 — the Longbow-scratching-clay detail is what keeps it separable.

Non-blocking: registry image for 竹 describes exactly two stalks; story implies several ('each stalk', 'every stalk'). Consistent with the actor name 'Bamboo Grove', so not an actor-consistency failure, but slightly loose against the registry image.

story: BAMBOO GRASS: beneath the creaking Bamboo Grove's towering stalks, a whole generation kneels in the dust, dwarfed to ankle height, their bowed backs bristling into narrow striped blades that carpet the grove floor.

story: Beneath the Bamboo Grove, the Tree wears the Goalpost Frame; a Hanging Towel drapes its crossbar, a Meat Hook waits below, Wishbone legs splay, and one Lightning Bolt pins it all — a perfect trap SCHEME.

Reading story keyword slightly trailed: 'escape SCHEME into the wall, step by step, arrow by arrow' softens the payoff, though the main story's terminal 'trap SCHEME' satisfies the placement gate (and 'step by step' echoes the secondary meaning 'Step').

story: Beneath the creaking Bamboo Grove, a green stalk splits downward — but in an instant the crack stops dead, jammed against a thick, knuckle-ringed NODE.

story: Beneath the Bamboo Grove's creaking stalks, a Cartwheel rolls through wet clay; a dangling Fishhook scratches loops in each rut, and the Wax Stamp presses red seals between them — one endlessly repeating PATTERN.

Non-blocking: the Fishhook 'dangles' from an unspecified support; naming what it hangs from would sharpen the image.

Non-blocking: the payoff phrase 'one endlessly repeating PATTERN' is generic and risks interference with other repetition/model-themed kanji (e.g. 模, 型); a more idiosyncratic closing image would raise distinctiveness.
Non-blocking: 卩's position (right side) is only implied by 'between them'; spatial fidelity is carried mainly by the correct 竹-on-top placement.

story: Beneath creaking Bamboo Grove stalks, Puddle Splash flings three droplets leftward, away from the right-hand ledger of my specialty, where one Ink Droplet falls from the brush tip and dots the last name in the REGISTER.
