issues: GATE 1 (component coverage) PASS — all four supplied components named: 竹 'Bamboo Grove' ('Beneath creaking Bamboo Grove stalks'), 氵 'Puddle Splash' ('Puddle Splash flings three droplets leftward'), 専 concept 'specialty' ('the right-hand ledger of my specialty' — correct handling since actor/image are null and only kanji_keyword is supplied), 丶 'Ink Droplet' ('one Ink Droplet falls from the brush tip').

GATE 2 (no phantom components) PASS — non-actor nouns are all scenery or drawn from the supplied images: 'stalks' and 'creaking' are verbatim from the 竹 image, 'three droplets' + 'leftward' from the 氵 image ('Three fat water droplets flicked off to the left'), 'brush tip' and 'dots' from the 丶 image. No extra kanji part is asserted.

MINOR (gate 2 adjacent, non-blocking): 'ledger' is a near-synonym of the listed meaning 'Record Book' used as a prop. It reinforces rather than leaks a distinct answer, but it slightly dilutes the REGISTER payoff by pre-announcing the concept mid-story.
GATE 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Bo' opens reading_story; reading_actor_used='Bo' matches reading_actor.actor_name for ぼ.
GATE 4 (meaning lands) PASS — 'REGISTER' is the final word of the story; meaning_placement='end' is accurate, not buried.

GATE 5 (actor consistency) PASS — no invented cognitive faculty. Puddle Splash 'flings' and Ink Droplet 'falls ... and dots' are ordinary physical motion consistent with their defined natures; Bo Derek's beach/wet-braids framing matches the Bo persona note.
GATE 6 (no etymology) PASS — no historical or derivational claim; purely imaginative staging.
GATE 7 (length) PASS — 36 words, under the ~40 cap.

IMAGEABILITY DRAG (score 3): the middle clause 'away from the right-hand ledger of my specialty' stacks two prepositional phrases around an abstract possessive. 'My specialty' has no picturable referent, and the relation is a negative one (motion *away from* a thing), which is a weak encoding compared to contact or causation. A concrete specialist prop (e.g. an expert's stamped ledger) would fix it without adding words.

SPATIAL FIDELITY (strength): layout is staged correctly — 竹 on top ('Beneath...'), 氵 on the left ('leftward'), 専 on the right ('right-hand'). Slight cost is that 'right-hand' reads as meta glyph-description rather than in-scene geography.

DISTINCTIVENESS (score 3): 'ink dots a name in a register' is a generic scribe scene and the main interference risk with other writing/record kanji; the bamboo canopy and the left-flung splash are what lift it above a 2. The reading_story is well differentiated by the Bo Derek beach imagery.

COHERENCE (minor): the connective 'where' after 'specialty' makes the ledger the location of the ink drop while the droplets are simultaneously moving away — two competing motion vectors in one sentence make the scene slightly harder to hold as a single image.

story: CHIC: Scattered Rice Grains burst like confetti on the left while, to the right, Curled Cat perches atop Plus-Sign Crossroads, tail tucked, holding a flawless pose under fashion-week floodlights.
reading_story: Swee sweeps down the runway in a rice-paper trench coat, collar popped, utterly CHIC.
issues: Non-blocking: 'fashion-week runway' is the default frame for 'chic' and will likely recur on neighbouring N1 style kanji (e.g. 洒, 雅), creating interference risk — a more idiosyncratic setting would raise distinctiveness.
Non-blocking: reading_story reuses the same runway set and the rice motif ('rice-paper trench coat') as the meaning story, so the two cues are less separable than they should be.
Non-blocking: 'holding a flawless pose' is a light abstraction; a concrete posture (arched back, one paw raised) would picture harder.

story: Scattered Rice Grains fling leftward; you rub a handful between your palms and they grind like gravel, rasping your skin raw. Not one grain is smooth — pure gritty COARSE.
reading_story: Saul's cheap suit is woven from burlap; he struts into court scratching furiously, lapels COARSE as sackcloth.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 2 checked, passes): 'gravel', 'palms', 'burlap', 'sackcloth', 'court' are scene props/similes, not named kanji components — no phantom component actor is introduced.

Non-blocking (gate 5): Saul Goodman is canonically loud/flashy rather than literally burlap-clad, but 'cheap suit' + courtroom strut is a costume detail consistent with the persona, not a contradiction of his nature.

Distinctiveness risk (graded, not gating): 'rice that is gritty/not smooth' is the single most obvious association for 米 + a roughness keyword, so this story could interfere with other 米-family or roughness kanji (e.g. 荒/礪-type neighbours). The palm-grinding/rasping-skin execution is what saves it from a 2.
Right-side 且 is left unused, but it is listed under phonetic_extra rather than components, so coverage (gate 1) is satisfied by 米 alone.

Word counts well inside limits: story ~29 words, reading_story ~20 (gate 7 pass). Keyword COARSE is the final word of the story, matching meaning_placement 'end' (gate 4 pass). Reading actor Saul named in reading_story (gate 3 pass). No etymology framing (gate 6 pass).
Spatial fidelity is a plus: 'fling leftward' correctly places 米 as the left radical of 粗.

story: Scattered Rice Grains spray from the left onto the Fortune Booth — none bounce off; every grain glues fast to the divining rod and counter window. The whole booth is STICKY.
reading_story: Nenn claps once and cannot pull his hands apart — everything Nenn touches today is STICKY.

story: A Rake Hand claws overhead; a Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through its center; a Falling Katana slashes the left edge; Scattered Rice Grains burst below; a Fistful of Tail dangles beneath — the hall goes SOLEMN.
reading_story: The Shucker pries open a single oyster in total silence; the whole feast hall stops chewing and bows its head, SOLEMN.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric #11): 隶 'Fistful of Tail dangles beneath' is placed as a sixth region under the rice, but 隶 is not a lower sub-part of 粛 — and it already contains ヨ and 米, which the story has just placed separately overhead and below. The learner is asked to render the same two shapes twice in contradictory locations.

Coherence (#12): the story is a positional inventory, not an event — five actors occupy five slots (overhead / center / left edge / below / beneath) and none of them touch or affect one another. No causal chain to hang recall on.

Imageability (#9): 'the hall goes SOLEMN' is an unearned payoff. The hall is introduced in the final three words with nothing established before it, so the keyword is attached to a setting rather than to any actor's action.

Distinctiveness (#10): the assembly template ('A does X; B does Y; C does Z — KEYWORD') is a generic slot-filler likely to interfere with sibling N1 stories built the same way. The reading story is the stronger half — silent oyster shucking stopping a feast hall is a genuinely distinctive fit for 'solemn'.

Minor persona strain: 隶's registry image is a violent seizure of a bolting animal ('caught just before it can escape'); 'dangles beneath' drains that energy to a static hang. Passes the actor-consistency gate but wastes the most memorable component.

story: Scattered Rice Grains fly in from the left toward a Cliff Awning; sheltered beneath it, an Open Mouth catches every grain, each dissolving on the tongue into pure SUGAR.
reading_story: Tone struts onstage, rips open a sack, and rains SUGAR over the crowd, rapping low and slow: "S-U-G-A-R."
issues: minor (non-gating, distinctiveness): 'Open Mouth catches food' is a high-frequency trope for 口 stories; interference risk with other 米/口 kanji (e.g. 粉, 精, 糧) unless the Cliff Awning stays the memorable anchor.
minor (non-gating, imageability): the payoff 'pure SUGAR' is a substance-noun rather than a percept — a crystalline/white-grit image would land harder than the abstract word.

minor (non-gating, reading story): vowel length for とう (long ō) is only implied by 'low and slow'; the registry note says Tone is the full/stretched parent of clipped Toto, and that stretch is not explicitly staged.

story: Scattered Rice Grains lie flung along the left edge of the road; the Sun sinks toward the flat Horizon Line above the Village Milestone, where you shovel every grain into your sack — PROVISIONS for the journey.
reading_story: Ryo the hardboiled detective cracks open a suspect's trunk — no loot, just canned bread and rice sacks. "PROVISIONS," he growls, pocketing a loaf as evidence.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): registry image for Sun is a blazing midday sun, story has it sinking at dusk — ordinary physical motion, allowed under gating, but a blazing-noon staging would match the actor image more tightly.
Minor (non-blocking): shared sunset/milestone staging with phonetic sibling 量 aids the りょう series but slightly raises meaning-interference risk; the sack-of-provisions payoff mitigates it.

story: The Falling Katana slashes down and snags the Spooled Thread's loose strand; from its blade dangle the Silk Cocoon and, below it, the Sand Trickle — generations strung on one unbroken strand: LINEAGE.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer high-kicks beneath framed portraits of her dancing mother and grandmother — the audience applauds three generations, one glittering LINEAGE.
issues: Minor: 'Sand Trickle' dangling from the blade is physically strained (sand falls rather than hangs) — non-blocking, actor's nature not contradicted
Minor: Spooled Thread (糸) and its subcomponents (幺, 小) all depicted as separate objects per the record's component list, adding slight visual clutter, though vertical order matches the glyph

story: Spooled Thread hangs left, Silk Cocoon knotted above a Sand Trickle of grains. Right, a Lightning Bolt cracks straight down into the Plus-Sign Crossroads, wrenching the trailing silk into one scorched TWIST.
reading_story: Cuomo grips the podium's microphone cord mid-speech and gives it a furious TWIST, the cable coiling tight around his white-knuckled fist.
issues: GATE 1 component coverage — PASS. All five supplied actors named verbatim: 'Spooled Thread', 'Silk Cocoon', 'Sand Trickle', 'Lightning Bolt', 'Plus-Sign Crossroads'.

GATE 2 no phantoms — PASS. 'grains' is licensed by Sand Trickle's image ('three small grains scattering downward'); 'trailing silk' is licensed by Spooled Thread's image ('one loose strand trailing off'). Nothing else introduced.
GATE 3 reading actor — PASS. 'Cuomo grips the podium's microphone cord' places the きゅう actor in reading_story; reading_actor_used matches.
GATE 4 meaning lands — PASS. Keyword closes the story: '...into one scorched TWIST.' meaning_placement 'end' is accurate.

GATE 5 actor consistency — PASS. Lightning Bolt 'cracks straight down' matches 'cracking straight down from sky to ground'; Silk Cocoon 'knotted' matches 'wound into a small soft knot'; Crossroads stays a painted tarmac junction. All motion is ordinary physical motion; no invented cognitive faculty.
GATE 6 no etymology — PASS. No historical/derivational claim anywhere.
GATE 7 length — PASS. Story is 32 words (limit ~40); reading_story 24 words.

NON-BLOCKING (coherence, rubric §3 item 12): the causal chain is loose — the bolt strikes the Plus-Sign Crossroads on the right, yet 'wrenching the trailing silk' acts on the left-side spool. The strike and the twist are asserted as one motion but are not physically joined.

NON-BLOCKING (imageability, rubric §3 item 9): the first clause 'Spooled Thread hangs left, Silk Cocoon knotted above a Sand Trickle of grains' is a static arrangement inventory rather than an event — the LLM inventory-listing failure mode. Only the second clause carries action.

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness, rubric §3 item 10): the payoff image (silk being twisted) is semantically near-identical to what any 糸-family kanji story would produce, so interference risk with neighbours like 紐/絡/縄 is real. The Lightning-Bolt-scorches-the-crossroads element is what keeps it above threshold.

NOTE ON INPUT (not the candidate's fault): the component list is redundant — 幺 and 小 are the constituent halves of 糸, so the story must stage three objects that are really one. Spatial fidelity (§3 item 11) is nonetheless honoured: 糸 left, 幺 above 小, bolt + 十 right.

story: On the left, Spooled Thread unwinds: Silk Cocoon coiled at its top, Sand Trickle spilling beneath, each grain a passing year. On the right, the Stop Barrier drops — history halted, wound up, finished: a CHRONICLE.
reading_story: Key the locksmith turns once in the archive door — click, "kee" — locking away the CHRONICLE of the century.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'history halted, wound up, finished' and 'each grain a passing year' are abstract narration rather than visible action, slightly diluting an otherwise concrete scene.

story: Spooled Thread trails down the kimono's left seam — Silk Cocoon knotted at its top, Sand Trickle scattering beneath — and the stitched shape they form is our clan's FAMILY CREST.
reading_story: Monn's white skirt billows over the subway grate, flashing a gold FAMILY CREST stitched inside the hem.
issues: Distinctiveness is weak: 'thread on a kimono forms the family crest' is the stock, most-predictable association for 紋 (家紋), so the meaning story risks blending with other 糸-radical mnemonics; no surprising or bizarre hook.
Minor abstraction at the linking step: 'the stitched shape they form' asks the learner to see scattering sand grains as stitching, which is the one blurry moment in an otherwise concrete scene.
The three actors (thread, cocoon, sand trickle) are all fine/small/thread-like and visually similar, so their spatial arrangement (seam / top / beneath) is doing most of the disambiguating work.

Gates all pass: 糸/幺/小 all named, no phantom components (kimono and seam are scenery, not invented actors), no invented cognitive abilities, Monn present in reading_story with an on-persona Marilyn Monroe subway-grate image, keyword at end as declared, no etymology, 29 and 17 words.

story: Spooled Thread unreels on the left — Silk Cocoon knotted on top, Sand Trickle sifting beneath. Its strand stretches over the Stepladder standing inside the Goalpost Frame, piling silk into the empty goal: the day's SUPPLY.
reading_story: Noah stocks the ark for forty days of rain — every deck packed tight with SUPPLY.
issues: Minor (non-gating): first clause is a positional inventory (knotted on top / sifting beneath) rather than action, slightly flattening imageability
Minor (non-gating): the 'Spooled Thread unreels on the left' opening is formulaic across thread-radical kanji; distinctiveness carried entirely by the goal-filling payoff

story: LARGE: a desert Horizon Line stretches endlessly, a Falling Katana plunging above a Sealed Clam-Locket on the right, while left of them a Spooled Thread spills Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle across miles of sand.

issues: Redundant nesting: 糸 is present alongside its own sub-parts 幺 and 小, so three of the six actors are silk/thread variants — the scene carries the same visual idea three times and loses contrast between them.

Keyword is a label, not a payoff: 'LARGE:' is prefixed with a colon and the largeness is then only restated in clichés ('stretches endlessly', 'across miles of sand'), so the meaning is announced rather than earned by the image.

Enumerative rather than narrative: actors are positioned ('plunging above', 'on the right', 'left of them') but never interact causally, so the story reads as a spatial inventory — good spatial fidelity (rubric item 11) but weak coherence.
Repeated setting vocabulary: 'desert' plus 'sand' twice; a generic desert tableau risks interference with other N1 cards using Horizon Line or Sand Trickle.
Minor: 一 (Horizon Line) is the only actor with no explicit position, though in 紘 it belongs to the right-hand 厷 with the katana.

story: The Cleaver swings at Spooled Thread's dangling strand; overhead the Wishbone snaps, one flying leg knocking the blade off-course into Silk Cocoon and the Sand Trickle beneath it — enough to DISTRACT any chop.
reading_story: Fonda drops his hat mid-testimony; the entire courtroom turns to watch him pick it up, the witness forgetting his answer — one small gesture, enough to DISTRACT everybody.
issues: Non-blocking (imageability): Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle are passive impact targets tacked onto the final clause rather than participants in the action - they are the two components most likely to drop out of recall.

Non-blocking (spatial fidelity): 'the Sand Trickle beneath it' has an ambiguous referent (beneath the Silk Cocoon? beneath the blade?), leaving the landing point of the deflected cleaver slightly under-specified.
Non-blocking (distinctiveness): 'something knocks X off-course' is the predictable template for distract/divert senses and risks interference with other N1 kanji sharing 分 or a divert meaning.

story: Lift the Pot Lid: beneath sits a Mound of Soil, and buried in it a Spooled Thread — its Silk Cocoon core unraveling into a Sand Trickle. Stripped down to bare basics: ELEMENTARY.

issues: Minor: 'Silk Cocoon core unraveling into a Sand Trickle' is a silk-to-sand material morph; readable as a thin falling line matching both registry images, but slightly blurs the picture.
Minor interference watch: 'thread buried under a cover' scene family overlaps with 索 (十/冖+糸); the 'bare basics' payoff keeps them separable but curators should check 索's story avoids burial imagery.

story: Against the workshop's left wall, Spooled Thread trails one strand; a Silk Cocoon perches on top, Sand Trickle hisses down below, and the strand twists tighter and tighter — SPINNING.

issues: Spatial anchor is implicit: 'a Silk Cocoon perches on top' and 'Sand Trickle hisses down below' never say on top of / below what, so the internal 幺-over-小 stacking inside 糸 has to be inferred (rubric item 11, spatial fidelity).
The payoff has no agent: 'the strand twists tighter and tighter' happens on its own — none of the three actors causes the spinning, which weakens coherence (rubric item 12).
Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle are decorative placements only; they are named but do nothing narratively, so coverage is satisfied on the letter rather than the spirit of item 1.
High interference risk with neighboring 糸 kanji at N1 (績, 織, 繊): a thread-workshop scene with a twisting strand is the obvious frame for several of them (rubric item 10).
方 (phonetic_extra) is unused, so the whole right-hand half of the glyph is unrepresented — permitted, but it leaves the spatial picture half-empty.
The keyword SPINNING is reused verbatim in the reading_story, so the reading cue leaks the meaning answer during retrieval practice.

story: At the Plus-Sign Crossroads, a Bedsheet Cover drapes over an open manhole; beneath it Spooled Thread lowers its strand — Silk Cocoon knotted at the top, Sand Trickle hissing down the line — twisted into one strong CORD.
reading_story: Sacco the anarchist slips from his prison window at midnight, sliding down a knotted CORD, its rough fibers burning his palms.
issues: Distinctiveness concern: reading story reuses the Sacco prison-escape frame already used by approved neighbor 策 ("Sacco scratches an escape SCHEME into the wall") — same actor, same setting, and 策/索 are same-reading (さく) visual confusables; only the payoff object (CORD vs SCHEME) disambiguates. Consider re-staging Sacco outside the prison-escape narrative.
Minor imageability dip at the climax: "twisted into one strong CORD" leaves the twisting agent vague — the strand + cocoon + sand assembly does not obviously twist into a cord.
Non-issue noted for the record: "manhole" and "prison window" are scene props, not phantom components.

story: A stop sign stands left; right of it the Soup Ladle tips, pouring dye down onto dangling Spooled Thread, its Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle beneath — all soaked glistening PURPLE.
reading_story: The Sheriff barks one clipped order; the dust cloud settles and his star, hat, and horse have all turned shocking PURPLE.
issues: Spatial fidelity (rubric item 11): 幺 sits ABOVE 小 inside 糸, but the story lumps them together as 'its Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle beneath' the Thread — the internal top/bottom stacking is lost.

Imageability drag: 'its Silk Cocoon and Sand Trickle beneath' is an inventory clause, not a scene — 2 of 5 components are named without any action, the top failure mode the rubric flags for coverage-by-listing.
Distinctiveness risk: 'dye poured onto thread' is the most predictable frame for any 糸 + color kanji and could interfere with other 糸 neighbors; the only unique anchor is the PURPLE payoff itself.
止 is carried by the generic prop 'a stop sign' rather than an actor (none supplied in the record) — acceptable, but it is the weakest-imprinting element in the story.
reading_story is thematically a near-repeat of the meaning story (everything turns purple), so it adds a persona but little new imagery.

story: The Rice-Paddy Grid tilts overhead, muddy water dripping onto Spooled Thread below, whose loose strand piles onto the floor in a fat coil, mud-soaked layer over layer — ACCUMULATE.
reading_story: Louie never throws anything away; his hallway is a canyon of stacked boxes he lets ACCUMULATE until the front door won't open.

story: Spooled Thread sits at the ballroom's left edge, unwinding one silk strand rightward that cinches into a gleaming sash across the chest of the bowing SIRE.
reading_story: Shinn the night bartender slides a brandy down the polished counter and bows low: "Your usual, SIRE."
issues: Non-blocking: 申 (phonetic_extra, right side of 紳) is never staged as an image; the right half of the glyph is carried only by the sash/sire. Acceptable since phonetic_extra is optional and the reading actor Shinn covers しん, but spatial fidelity on the right radical is inferred rather than shown.

Non-blocking: 'gleaming sash' overlaps semantically with belt/obi kanji (帯); the sash is legitimately the unwound silk strand (not a phantom actor), but it is a mild interference risk with any belt-keyword neighbour. The ballroom + bowing-SIRE framing mitigates it.
Non-blocking: 'Spooled Thread sits' is slightly flat as an opening verb for a bobbin; the vivid beat is entirely in the second clause.

story: Spooled Thread, left, trails its silk strand rightward into the open Candy Tin, where it winds around the striped candy stick and comes out soaked DARK BLUE.
reading_story: Conn, in a DARK BLUE tuxedo, adjusts his cuffs at the baccarat table and murmurs his name; every rival's face drains pale.

story: On the left, the Spooled Thread — Silk Cocoon balanced on top, Sand Trickle sifting below — whips its loose strand across, lashing the War Helmet down onto the Open Mouth with a tight chin-strap TIE.
reading_story: Ketel loops twine around two frosty vodka bottles, cinching a double knot — a TIE so tight the glass necks clink together.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the mid-sentence aside 'Silk Cocoon balanced on top, Sand Trickle sifting below' is a static component inventory that briefly stalls the action, though it doubles as correct spatial mapping of 糸's sub-parts.

story: On the left, the Spooled Thread — Silk Cocoon perched over its Sand Trickle — flings its loose strand rightward, looping the Crossed Axes where their handles cross beneath the clamped Pot Lid, wringing tighter until the wood shrieks: STRANGLE.
reading_story: Coe rounds the last bend and his gold medal's ribbon whips up in the headwind, cinching his throat — the champion's own prize tries to STRANGLE him.
