Story sits at the ~40-word ceiling (≈38 words); dense em-dash appositive slightly raises parsing load (non-blocking).

story: Spooled Thread lashes the whole scene together: Silk Cocoon knotted above Sand Trickle on the left; on the right, Pot Lid clamps Sealed Clam-Locket onto Wishing-Well Legs. One thread binding everything in place — GOVERNING.
reading_story: Tone seizes the presidential podium, mic in hand, rapping executive orders in one long smooth flow — the whole capital nods on beat. Tone is GOVERNING now.
issues: Non-blocking: six actors in one frame reads as a stroke-map more than a scene; only the lashing thread provides motion (imageability capped at 3).
Non-blocking: record supplies both 糸 and its subcomponents 幺/小, so the left side doubles up actors on the same strokes — inherent to the input, not the candidate.

story: Spooled Thread's loose strand trails rightward until a Lightning Bolt cracks down and severs it; Scattered Rice Grains burst from the break. The strand knots itself onward through the grains — the family line continues: INHERIT.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer hands her feathered headdress to her daughter mid-show: "INHERIT the stage!" The kicking line never misses a beat.

story: Spooled Thread unwinds from the left, lashing Stumpy Sparrow to his wire — the grumpy bird tugs, and every strand he pulls loose frays into FIBER.
reading_story: Mr. Eaton maintains his ancient suit daily, darning every worn FIBER with a sharp "Ee!" whenever the needle pricks him.
issues: Minor: keyword FIBER is mid-sentence in reading_story (placement gate applies to the meaning story, which ends on FIBER — compliant)
Distinctiveness capped at 3: 'thread binds something' is a recurring scene shape across 糸-series kanji, though the fray-into-FIBER payoff differentiates it

story: Spooled Thread whirls on the left, its loose silk strand paying out rightward and doubling back over itself, each twist braiding thicker and thicker, until the frail wisp has become a fist-thick ROPE.
reading_story: Coe trains by skipping with a massive ROPE — the heavy hawser cracks the track at Olympic speed with every turn.
issues: Forward-looking distinctiveness risk: thread-braiding-into-rope is the most natural image for any 糸+rope kanji; when 縄 (straw rope) is authored, steer it away from a braiding/thickening transformation to avoid interference.

Minor: in the reading story the keyword ROPE appears in the opening clause rather than terminal position — acceptable (not buried, and the main story carries the end placement), but terminal payoff would be slightly stronger.

story: The Twin Pillars topple inside the Goalpost Frame — and bounce. From the left, Spooled Thread had strung its dangling silk strand back and forth beneath the crossbar, weaving a springy NETTING that catches them.
reading_story: Moe misses the trapeze, plummets, and boings safely into the circus NETTING, bellowing a long relieved "moooh!"

story: On the left, Spooled Thread dangles one twisting strand. To its right, a Mound of Soil sits atop Wishing-Well Legs, and beneath them a Trailing Footprint trails a slanted mud-streak — thread and streak crossing into TWILL.
reading_story: Lynn drags her thumb across the diagonal ridges running up her jacket sleeve and grins: unmistakable TWILL.

story: The retainer kneels top-left; a yellow Rubber Glove lies at his right; the Spooled Thread below trails one strand up to that glove, which he yanks wire-tight until it hums — TENSE.
reading_story: Martin Luther King leans into the microphone; the packed square goes silent, every shoulder TENSE, waiting for his first word.
issues: Non-blocking prose defect: in 'trails one strand up to that glove, which he yanks wire-tight', the nearest antecedent of 'which' is 'that glove' — a glove cannot be yanked wire-tight. Intent is clearly the strand. Suggest 'trails one strand up to that glove; he yanks the strand wire-tight until it hums'.
The Rubber Glove is purely a positional marker — it does nothing in the scene, which weakens its retrieval hook for 又.
Distinctiveness risk: 'thread pulled taut' is the obvious semantic route for 緊 and may interfere with other 糸 + tension kanji (張, 締, 縛). Only the retainer/glove pairing differentiates it.

story: At the left of the gate, Spooled Thread flings its loose strand across, looping the latch again and again, then reels itself in until the silk creaks taut — TIGHTEN.
reading_story: Before going on stage, Tay cinches her ponytail, her belt, her shoelaces — everything on Tay must TIGHTEN until it squeaks.
issues: Minor: 'the gate' and 'the latch' are scene props evoking 門, which is not in 締. Corpus precedent treats this as non-phantom (shipped 氏 story uses 'clan gate' and the global phantom scan flags actor-persona phrases like 'Castle Gate', not generic words), and the latch aligns with 締's Shut/Lock meanings — but keep an eye on collision with 閉's shipped Castle-Gate scene (n3-mnemonics.json).

Distinctiveness capped at 3: opening gesture nearly duplicates shipped 結 (n1-mnemonics.json: 'whips its loose strand across, lashing ... tight — TIE' vs this candidate's 'flings its loose strand across, looping ... taut — TIGHTEN'), and N2's 絡 already uses the Spooled-Thread strand-wrapping motif. The reel-itself-in-until-taut beat and the latch target are the only differentiators; the TIE/TIGHTEN keywords are themselves adjacent (締's meanings include 'Tie').
Minor: reading story is a three-item list (ponytail, belt, shoelaces) rather than one image; each item is concrete and the 'squeaks' payoff helps, but it is weaker than the main story's single scene.

story: Spooled Thread's silk runs up the left. On the right, top to bottom: a Hawk Talon lifts off its branch, a flat Horizon Line lies beneath, and a friend catches the dropping strand — letting it SLACKEN.
reading_story: Khan halts his warhorse on the empty steppe, unstrings his bow, and lets the taut string SLACKEN across his fist.
issues: Non-blocking: the Horizon Line is inert filler — it 'lies beneath' but takes no part in the action, weakening imageability and making it the component most likely to be dropped on recall.
Non-blocking: 'On the right, top to bottom:' is positional scaffolding rather than narrative; it states the layout instead of showing it, which flattens the mental image.
Non-blocking: the causal link is implicit — the Hawk Talon is never said to be holding the thread, so 'lifts off its branch' does not obviously cause the strand to drop.
Non-blocking: 'a friend' is a generic unnamed figure (友 has actor: null) and will recur identically across other 友-containing kanji, capping distinctiveness.
Minor: in the reading story, 'unstrings his bow, and lets the taut string SLACKEN' is slightly self-contradictory — an unstrung bow's string is already off, so 'taut' reads oddly.

story: Spooled Thread rolls around a giant globe, its loose silk strand winding perfectly horizontal rings across the sphere — every ring a parallel of LATITUDE.
reading_story: Navigator Eaton squints through his sextant, barking a clipped "Ee!" each time he pins down another degree of LATITUDE.
issues: Non-blocking: story phrase 'across the sphere' incidentally uses the keyword of neighbor kanji 圏 (SPHERE, data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json); it sits mid-sentence, not in payoff position, so interference risk is low — 'across its surface' would eliminate it entirely.

story: Spooled Thread dangles one silk strand rightward; Rake Hand, perched atop the Muddy Boar, snags it in curled prongs and knots rake to boar — an unbreakable AFFINITY.
reading_story: Enzo strokes a scarlet hood and sighs: a man and his roaring engine share one pure AFFINITY.
issues: Minor: 'knots rake to boar' is slightly awkward to visualize on first read (a rake tying itself to a boar's back), though permitted as physical motion for a 'grasping hand' actor.
Watch-item: thread-tying motif overlaps with other 糸-family binding kanji (縛/締/緊); the unique Rake-Hand-on-Boar pairing mitigates interference risk.

story: Spooled Thread sits on the left bank, its loose strand trailing right, lashed around a tortoise's shell — the tortoise hauls it taut across the sand, twisting the line into one thick, bristling STRAW ROPE.
reading_story: Average Joe leans back in a tug-of-war, boots skidding, gripping a fraying STRAW ROPE that groans "Joooe" with every heaving pull.
issues: (non-blocking) Payoff spine 'twisting the line into one thick ROPE' closely echoes the existing 綱 story ('each twist braiding thicker and thicker... fist-thick ROPE') and 索 ('twisted into one strong CORD'); the tortoise is the sole discriminator against near-synonym neighbours.
(non-blocking) Slight material incoherence: a silk strand twisting into a STRAW rope; 'bristling' partly covers it.
(non-blocking) Setting is faintly mixed ('left bank' plus 'sand') — harmless but not a crisp single location.

story: Spooled Thread, left, flings its trailing strand rightward, coiling loop after loop around a specialty certificate until nothing moves; a single Ink Droplet hangs glossy at the certificate's centre, sealed under the windings. BIND.
reading_story: Bachar tests his knots at the docks, wrapping rope around a crate twice and yanking hard — nothing slips. That, he says, is how you BIND.
issues: Gate 5 (actor consistency) is technically met but thin for the reading actor: reading_actor.note defines Bachar as 'Bacca-man — voiced/heavier twin of Hacker (はく)', and the story renders him as a generic dockworker testing knots. Nothing evokes the Bacca-man persona or the heavier/voiced relationship to Hacker, so the fixed-persona benefit (§1.2, KanjiDamage model) is lost.

Distinctiveness risk from story overlap: the reading_story re-enacts the meaning story ('wrapping rope around a crate twice… nothing slips' vs 'coiling loop after loop around a specialty certificate until nothing moves'). Two near-identical binding scenes give the learner one hook instead of two and blur which story carries the ばく reading.

Coherence wobble on 丶: 'a single Ink Droplet hangs glossy at the certificate's centre, sealed under the windings' asks the droplet to be simultaneously pendant (hanging, per its registry image) and pinned flat under thread. Pick one — sealed flat under the windings reads better and still matches 'make one tiny dot'.

Minor prop inflation on 専: kanji_keyword is 'specialty' with no actor/image, and the story materialises it as a 'specialty certificate'. Not a phantom component (nothing outside 縛 is named), but the certificate is invented set-dressing that another 専 kanji's mnemonic may contradict — worth pinning a stable concretisation for keyword-only components.

Distinctiveness ceiling: 'thread wraps tightly around an object' is the most predictable possible image for 縛 and collides with other 糸 neighbours (結, 縄, 絞). The specialty certificate is the only thing keeping it separable.

story: Spooled Thread hangs off a rafter's left edge; its loose strand drops in one dead-straight silk line all the way to the floor — a perfect plumb line, absolutely VERTICAL.
reading_story: Juno stands atop her temple column, arms overhead, stretched into one loooong VERTICAL line from crown to sandals.
issues: Non-blocking: reading_story keyword 'VERTICAL' is in the final clause but not the terminal word — acceptable payoff position, flagging for consistency.

Non-blocking: story's vertical dangling strand closely mirrors Spooled Thread's default registry image ('loose strand trailing off and dangling'), a mild interference risk with other 糸-family mnemonics; the plumb-line detail is what differentiates it.
Non-blocking: 'dead-straight' vs registry's 'thin twisting line' — physically consistent (taut plumb line) but a slight deviation from the canonical depiction.

story: Left of the road, Spooled Thread whips its strand rightward while the Conveyor Belt hauls a Tiered Picket along the bottom, a muddy Trailing Footprint stamped just above it. Silk lashes each slat — that's how you SEW.
reading_story: Ho belly-laughs in his workshop, needle flashing, because he must SEW every torn toy sack shut before dawn.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS — all four mandatory actors named verbatim: 'Spooled Thread' (糸), 'Conveyor Belt' (辶), 'Trailing Footprint' (夂), 'Tiered Picket' (丰); components_used lists exactly those four.

Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS — 'road' comes from the 辶 image ('steadily forward down the road'), 'silk' from the 糸 image ('fine silk thread'), 'slat' from the 丰 image ('three stacked horizontal slats'), 'muddy' from the 夂 image. Nothing invented. Phonetic 夆 is correctly left unmentioned.

Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Ho' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor.actor_name; 'belly-laughs' + 'workshop' + 'toy sack' is consistent with the registry note (Santa Claus, ho-ho-ho), no drift toward the clipped twin Hoth.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS — meaning_placement 'end' honored: story terminates on 'that's how you SEW.'; reading_story also carries SEW as its payoff verb.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS — no invented cognitive faculties. 'Conveyor Belt hauls' and 'whips its strand' are ordinary physical motion consistent with a belt and a trailing thread strand; the belt is not made to decide, perceive, or intend anything.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS — purely imaginative; no claim about historical derivation or the 夆 phonetic.
Gate 7 (length) PASS — story is 37 words, under the ~40 cap.
Spatial fidelity is good: 糸 placed left, 辶 running along the bottom, 夂 stamped directly above 丰 — matches the real 夂-over-丰 stack inside the enclosure.

Weakness (graded, not gating): Trailing Footprint is inert — it is only 'stamped just above it', a position report rather than a participant. It contributes no action to the sewing scene and is the element most likely to be dropped on recall.

Weakness (graded): the middle clause leans on layout vocabulary ('rightward', 'along the bottom', 'just above it') instead of scene action, which flattens imageability; only the closing 'Silk lashes each slat' does real depictive work.

Weakness (graded): 'that's how you SEW' is a generic tag ending; the 辶+夂 pairing recurs across many kanji, so distinctiveness rests almost entirely on the Tiered Picket, capping interference resistance.

story: Spooled Thread's loose strand suddenly recoils, whipping back around the bobbin, loop after loop winding tighter — watch the fat spool SHRINK to a wrinkled bead.
reading_story: The Shucker pries at a stubborn oyster; with every twist of his knife the shell seems to SHRINK, clamping smaller until nothing is left to shuck.
issues: Minor: keyword SHRINK sits in the final clause but is not the literal last word ("...SHRINK to a wrinkled bead"); within tolerance for meaning_placement=end.

story: An agile acrobat somersaults nonstop atop the Spooled Thread; each flip whips the dangling strand faster, and it sprouts loops upon loops until the bobbin vanishes under an overgrown tangle — LUXURIANT.
reading_story: Hancock dips his quill and signs with such a LUXURIANT flourish that ink loops overgrow the whole Declaration page like ivy.
issues: Minor: causal link between the acrobat's somersaults and the strand whipping faster is loose — the acrobat isn't holding the thread, so the mechanism must be inferred.

Minor: 'sprouts loops upon loops' imagery sits in a crowded 糸 family (締/縮/練/績 all use loop-multiplication); the overgrown-tangle-burying-the-bobbin payoff and acrobat-on-top differentiate it, but interference risk is nonzero.

Minor: keyword appears mid-sentence in the reading story ('such a LUXURIANT flourish') rather than as terminal payoff — acceptable since placement gating applies to the meaning story (precedent: approved 敏 record).

story: One strand off the Spooled Thread is dragged over the Mound of Soil heaped atop the Toothed Rack, then split against the Barbed Pike's hook arching overhead — into a filament impossibly SLENDER.
reading_story: Senna threads his race car through a gap so SLENDER the mirrors scrape both walls.
issues: Minor spatial deviation: story puts the Barbed Pike's hook 'arching overhead' while the registry image places the hooked side-blade partway down the shaft — not a persona contradiction, but weakens spatial fidelity slightly.
The Mound of Soil is a passive waypoint (strand merely dragged over it); its causal role in producing slenderness is arbitrary, a mild chain-linking weakness.
In the reading story the keyword sits mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable since the main story ends on SLENDER, but worth noting.

story: Left, the Spooled Thread unreels; right, the planted Barbed Pike snags the strand on its hooked spur and rakes it back and forth, each pass plucking out a harp-like sound, strands crossing tighter to WEAVE.
reading_story: Shicker the factory inspector strokes the fresh cloth: "Only my organization can WEAVE this tight," he brags.

story: Beside the Tree, goods stacked high in its branches, Spooled Thread flings its loose strand around the pile and spins, winding goods and Tree into one enormous REEL.
reading_story: Sosa cranks a fishing REEL instead of swinging: with each long turn he reels the pitched ball out of the air before it reaches the plate.
issues: Minor: payoff image asks the Tree itself to become part of the REEL, which is slightly abstract at the final beat (kept imageability at 4, not 5).
Minor: 'thread winds around X' is Spooled Thread's default action across many 糸 kanji; the goods-in-branches staging carries the distinctiveness.

story: The Fishing Net stretched overhead traps a Speech Bubble beneath it; on the right the Guillotine Blade drops, slicing the netted words to ribbons — the PENALTY for saying too much.
reading_story: Batcher processes convicts in batches, stamping the same PENALTY on every forehead as the line shuffles past.

story: The Fishing Net hangs flat overhead, and beneath its mesh a bolt of silk fiber unspools, shimmering threads rolling across the riverbank until every strand lies SPREAD OUT.
reading_story: Rah snaps a picnic blanket into the air; it drops and lands SPREAD OUT across the grass.
issues: Non-blocking: the Fishing Net is inert — it hangs overhead while the silk unspools beneath it, so the two components share a frame without interacting. Giving the net an active role (e.g. the silk unspooling THROUGH the mesh) would tighten the binding and lift imageability.

Non-blocking: 'flat overhead' slightly re-orients the registry image ('cast down over the water to trap whatever swims below'). Legal as ordinary physical repositioning, but a water-facing placement would match the persona more exactly.
Non-blocking: silk/thread imagery risks interference with neighbouring fibre kanji (維, 絹, 糸-family); distinctiveness rests mainly on the riverbank + suspended-net setting.

story: Twin Pillars perch atop the Kings Crown like two stubby horns; beneath the velvet cushion thick wool bulges, four hooves scrabble out, and a bleat escapes. Behold — a crowned SHEEP.
reading_story: Yoyo saws his cello onstage; every long note draws another SHEEP through the curtain, until the hall is packed with woolly, swaying listeners.

story: A Woolly Ram perches on the shoulders of the Pike-Wielding Duelist below, curling horns crowning his boastful stance. He lowers the pike, kneels, and the warm fleece settles over him like RIGHTEOUSNESS.
reading_story: Gee bangs the gavel, bellowing his own short name over the packed courtroom until every bench rises and answers back with RIGHTEOUSNESS.
issues: Non-blocking (imageability): the keyword arrives via simile with an abstract noun -- 'settles over him like RIGHTEOUSNESS' -- rather than a depicted concrete beat; a visible consequence would hit rubric item 9 harder.

Non-blocking (reading story): 'bellowing his own short name' encodes the short vowel meta-textually (naming the mnemonic device) instead of showing it; it satisfies gate 3 but is the weakest sentence for concreteness.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness): gavel/courtroom is a generic justice setting at risk of interference with other justice-adjacent kanji, and this actor pair recurs in 儀/議 which take 義 as a component (phonetic_extra lists 義).
Non-blocking (clarity): pronoun chain 'crowning his boastful stance. He lowers the pike' relies on the reader binding both to the Duelist; naming him once more would remove the momentary ambiguity.

story: Its turn called from the left, the Feather Pair on the right springs up and tumbles end over end, white vanes flashing — FLIP.
reading_story: Honner flicks a coin high — "Hon for heads!" — and watches it FLIP.

story: The Feather Pair lands on top of something utterly different from itself; the different thing bucks beneath them, the white vanes flare wide and start beating — it has grown a WING.
reading_story: The Yorker sprints for the subway doors, snaps open a WING from under his coat, and glides down the platform.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): 'something utterly different from itself' is an unimaged abstraction — the 異 slot has no concrete visual anchor, capping imageability at 3; a curator edit giving the bucking thing one concrete trait (e.g. scales, chrome) would lift it.

story: ENDURING: Chin Whiskers' four grey strands hang rigid on the left, unmoved, while on the right a Tape Measure's quivering inch presses into them all night — not one bristle bends.
reading_story: Ty slides spikes-first into the base, shin torn open, then holds that bag ENDURING nine more innings without a word.
issues: Minor: 'presses into them all night' substitutes duration for a concrete visual beat; a single decisive image (tongue flexing back, whiskers unmoved) would sharpen imageability.
Minor: reading_story repeats the keyword ENDURING mid-sentence — harmless but redundant with the meaning story's payoff position.
Minor risk: 'endurance under pressure' framing could interfere with other N1 endure-family kanji (忍, 堪); currently mitigated only by the distinct actors.

story: A Listening Ear and an Open Mouth hover side by side above the Kings Crown: the Ear catches heaven's faint whisper, the Mouth shouts it down onto the crown — and the crown glows HOLY.
reading_story: The white-bearded Sage lays his hands on the water, stretching one long ēēē-chant until it shimmers HOLY.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'heaven's faint whisper' names heaven as a sound source; it is scene dressing, not a phantom component, but keep an eye on 'heaven' wording near kanji containing 天.
Minor (non-blocking): 'glows HOLY' makes the payoff slightly abstract; a more physical manifestation (e.g., a visible halo ring) would sharpen the final image.

story: A giant Listening Ear leans in from the left; upper right, the public murmurs; lower right, a heart thumps. The ear drinks in both crowd-chatter and heartbeat — instantly WISE.
reading_story: Sosa steps to the plate, hears the pitch coming by sound alone, and crushes it — a swing the whole stadium calls WISE.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (imageability): the payoff clause is auditory, not visual — 'drinks in both crowd-chatter and heartbeat' asks the learner to picture sound. Only the cupped ear itself is a strong image; 'the public murmurs' is an undifferentiated mass with no visual hook (contrast the component image's concrete 'lobe twitching').

NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness): 耳 + 心 + a hearing→wisdom payoff overlaps heavily with 聴 (listen), which also pairs ear and heart; 聖 and 聞 sit in the same semantic neighbourhood. The sole discriminator is 公, and it is rendered in the weakest verb in the story ('murmurs'), so it is the detail most likely to drop out of recall and collapse 聡 into its neighbours.

NON-BLOCKING (coherence): the first sentence is a positional inventory ('left / upper right / lower right') rather than an interaction — components are placed beside each other, not acting on each other. Only the second sentence supplies causality, and it asserts the leap ('instantly WISE') rather than dramatising it.
NOTE (spatial fidelity, positive): placement is exactly correct — 耳 left, 公 upper right over 心 lower right, matching the 忩 stack listed in phonetic_extra. This is the candidate's strongest dimension.

story: LISTEN! Beside the Plus-Sign Crossroads, the Listening Ear cups toward the tarmac as a Fishing Net drops over the junction, trapping a runaway heart beneath its mesh — the heart pounds frantically against the net.
reading_story: Cho the witch presses her wand-tip to her lips — "Chooo…" she breathes, long and low, and the whole classroom leans in to LISTEN.
issues: Minor (non-gating, spatial fidelity): net drops 'over the junction' but in the glyph 罒 sits below 十; net-over-heart and ear-beside-stack are correct.
Keyword is an exclamation prefix rather than the causal payoff of the scene; ear-listening-to-the-pounding-heart link is implied, not explicit.

story: Low on the left, the Full Moon glows close and silver; its two faint surface-stripes shimmer, reflected in the wet crimson sheen of an enormous, quivering LIVER.
reading_story: Khan gallops past, leans from the saddle, and bites into a raw LIVER, blood streaking his chin — warrior's fuel.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in reading_story the keyword LIVER is followed by the tail '— warrior's fuel', slightly diluting the end-placement payoff.

story: Low on the left, the Full Moon bloats until it wedges in the window frame, silver bulk squeezing through the gap, its two surface-stripes stretched to straining seams — a sky gone OBESE.
reading_story: Bowie belts a ballad on the rooftop; with each held note his glitter jumpsuit balloons outward until the star himself is comically OBESE.
issues: Distinctiveness risk: both stories run the identical 'inflates until OBESE' mechanic, and swelling/ballooning is the default image for the whole 肥/脂/太/肪 'fat' neighbourhood — high interference potential with other 月-plus-fat kanji. The window-frame wedge is the only genuinely unique hook; the reading story has no comparable anchor beyond the glitter jumpsuit.
Minor: keyword lands on 'a sky gone OBESE' rather than on the bloated moon itself, so the payoff attaches to the backdrop instead of the acting component — slightly softer than a direct hit.

Minor: 'window frame' and 'gap' are invented scenery. Not phantom components (neither maps to a registry actor), but they are the kind of extraneous prop the length/focus gate discourages; the story is 32 words, so it passes.

story: The Full Moon sinks low on the left of a striped Market Awning; the canvas swells and sags, swells and sags in the night wind — the whole stall breathing like a pair of LUNGS.
reading_story: Mr. Hyde staggers through the fog clutching his ribs — every monstrous, clipped gasp rattles his transformed LUNGS.

story: The Full Moon hangs low, its two faint stripes swelling as bitter green bile fills the silver disc — the night sky's glowing GALL BLADDER.
reading_story: Tanner cures his leather in bile: he squeezes a GALL BLADDER over each hide, boasting nothing bites deeper.
issues: Non-blocking: interference risk with shipped 肝 (liver), which uses near-identical staging (Full Moon low, two faint stripes, paired with a wet organ); candidate is saved by distinct mechanism (moon fills with bile and becomes the organ vs. reflection) and green-vs-crimson color split — keep both details if edited.
Minor coherence strain: 'stripes swelling as bile fills' slightly conflates the stripes with the disc; harmless for recall.

story: Full Moon hangs low on the left, so close its two faint stripes glow right through the mother's taut skin, lighting the curled sleeper inside her WOMB.
reading_story: Ty Cobb slides into home plate and curls up there, refusing to leave — the dugout groans that he's treating the batter's box like a WOMB.
issues: Minor spatial inconsistency in reading_story: Ty slides into home plate but is then said to be treating the batter's box (a different spot) like a womb.
Moon-and-pregnant-belly is a semi-conventional pairing, which caps distinctiveness; the 'two faint stripes glowing through skin' detail is what rescues it.

story: A translucent membrane balloons around the Full Moon, swallowing it whole; the silver disc glows through the wet skin, its two stripes warped, floating like a yolk inside its SAC.
reading_story: Ho pats his sack — it squelches. It's a wet SAC: presents float in fluid inside. "Ho-ho-ho," he booms, delivering each gift slick and newborn.
issues: Minor (non-gating): reading story leans on the sack/SAC homophone; keyword spelling could momentarily blur, though SAC is capitalized and lands clearly.
Minor (non-gating): meaning story layers several visual clauses (glow, warped stripes, yolk simile) — still one scene, but slightly busier than a single snapshot.

story: The Full Moon hangs low; above it a Flexing Bicep cocks back, bulging, knuckles poised an inch from the silver disc — one twitch from smashing it. The moon's stripes tremble. THREATEN.
reading_story: Kyo grabs a front-row fan by the collar mid-song and howls one endless note into his face — that's how rock frontmen THREATEN.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'knuckles' extends the Flexing Bicep actor with a hand/fist; acceptable as ordinary physical motion but drifts slightly from the registry image 'no body attached'.
Minor (non-blocking): 月+力 actor pair recurs across neighbors (脇, 協, 勝) — the pre-impact smash pose mitigates but does not eliminate interference risk.

story: A plane descends past the Full Moon hanging low at the left edge of the runway; its wheels rake two glowing stripes across the disc — sparks showering from the UNDERCARRIAGE.
reading_story: Kyacker stows away in the plane's UNDERCARRIAGE, hugging a wheel strut, screaming as the doors fold shut around him.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in the story, "its wheels" briefly parses as the Moon's wheels before resolving to the plane.

story: The Swap-Meet Haggler, lit by the Full Moon hanging low on his left, shouts a final deal — coins spin skyward as he peels off shirt, trousers, boots, trading the very clothes off his back. UNDRESS!
reading_story: Backstage, Datcher rips his whole costume off in one snap — buttons pinging everywhere — the fastest UNDRESS in showbiz.
issues: Minor: story enumerates three garments (shirt, trousers, boots) plus spinning coins — slightly busy for one flash-image, though within length and coherence limits.

story: Inside the borough, under its wide overhanging roof, a forgotten slab of meat hangs blackened and dripping, and the whole district gags at the stench: ROT.
reading_story: Foo rips a screaming solo, then sniffs his amp: black fuzz creeping over the speaker cone, the whole cabinet furry with ROT.
issues: Non-blocking: "its wide overhanging roof" surfaces 广, a sub-element of 府 rather than a listed component. It is genuinely present in the kanji (so not a phantom per rubric gate 2) and it usefully stages the 府-encloses-肉 relation, but a stricter deterministic verifier keyed only to the supplied component list could flag it.

Non-blocking: "forgotten slab of meat" is the most predictable image for keyword "rot", so the meaning story leans on semantic obviousness rather than a distinctive hook; interference risk with other decay/spoil kanji is the main quality ceiling.
Non-blocking: both stories draw on the same mold/blackening image family, so the reading story reinforces rather than diversifies the retrieval cue.

story: A Full Moon hangs low on the left, its two faint surface-stripes unspooling off the disc and slithering rightward into a steaming, glistening pink heap of INTESTINES.
reading_story: Cho flicks her wand over a cauldron; ropes of glistening INTESTINES leap out and knot themselves into a neat bow around her broomstick.
issues: Non-gating: the 'two faint surface-stripes' device is already load-bearing in shipped siblings 胆 ('two faint stripes swelling') and 脂 ('the two faint stripes that groove its low silver face'), and 腸 sits in a dense 月-organ family (肝, 胆, 胃, 脂, 胸, 肺). The unspooling/slithering motion is what keeps it separable; a future edit should preserve that motion rather than the stripes themselves.

Non-gating: INTESTINES falls mid-sentence in reading_story rather than at an end. Shipped precedent allows this (胞 buries SAC similarly), and the placement gate is scored on `story`, so not a fail — but the reading story would land harder with the keyword as the closing beat.
Non-gating: the reading story does not dramatize the long ō of ちょう; it relies entirely on the Cho persona carrying vowel length. Consistent with shipped 肝 (Khan), so no gate failure.

story: MEMBRANE: a taut, glistening skin stretched across the night sky. The Full Moon, low on the left, presses its silver disc into it from behind, its two surface-stripes bulging through the translucent film.
reading_story: Macker licks his thumb and pokes a hole clean through the drum's MEMBRANE, grinning at the whistling squeal.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the reading story's punctured drumhead slightly clashes with the intact, taut film of the meaning story; separate scenes, so no gate failure, but a non-piercing action would read cleaner.

story: The Full Moon pours light from the left into the War Helmet stacked on the Stemmed Goblet; the whole tower bloats, Comb Streaks of strain raking its right side as it starts to SWELL.
reading_story: Bowie holds one long note — "bōōō…" — and watches his cheeks SWELL in the mirror, ballooning bigger with every second he sustains it.

story: The retainer stands stiff at the left as the Falling Katana slashes down on his right, splitting the pyramid of goods stacked beneath it — every eye turns to LOOK TO him.
reading_story: When the alarm rings, nobody moves — the whole room turns to LOOK TO Lynn, who calmly points the way out.
issues: Soft phantom risk: 'every eye turns' — 'eye' may evoke 目, which is not in 臨; idiom-level bystander description, not a staged component, so not gated
Weak causal link: katana splitting the goods does not motivate why everyone would LOOK TO the retainer — payoff feels bolted on

Interference pressure from 臣-family neighbors (監 'oversee', 覧 'look at') that will likely also pair the retainer with a looking/turning-eyes payoff; the split pyramid of goods is the only strong differentiator
Reading story keyword is one short clause before the end ('LOOK TO Lynn, who calmly points the way out') — acceptable but not the final beat

story: STINKING: high on the ledge you smell oneself, nose crinkling; sprawled on the rock beneath, Starfish bakes in the sun, orange arms flung wide, oozing warm brine.
reading_story: A Shoe left in the locker all summer; the cobbler pries it open on his bench and the whole street gags — STINKING.
issues: Non-blocking (coherence): 'you smell oneself' competes with the starfish as the stench source, so the causal link between the two components is implied rather than stated; 'smell yourself' would also read more naturally while still anchoring 自.
Non-blocking (rubric 4): keyword sits at the start as a label rather than as the payoff; an end placement would make the stench the punchline of the starfish image.

story: From the flat Horizon Line the Sealed Clam-Locket plummets, whistling down through empty sky, and thuds half-buried into the Mound of Soil — the farthest point a fall can ATTAIN.
reading_story: The Sheriff snaps one clipped "shi!" as he pins the tin star to his own chest — the rank he rode a thousand dusty miles to ATTAIN.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the Clam-Locket plummets 'From the flat Horizon Line', but the Horizon Line's registry image places it at ground level (sky meets sand), so a fall originating there is spatially paradoxical — reads fine as the glyph's top stroke, but costs a beat of visualization.

Minor (non-gating): 'the farthest point a fall can ATTAIN' is a slightly strained collocation (one attains ranks/goals more naturally than landing spots), though it aligns with the record's 'Reach/Arrive' meanings.

story: In its smoking crater, the Landed Meteor shudders as the Cracking Whip snaps down on the right, lashing the great rock until it strains and grinds forward, forced to EXERT every ounce of itself.
reading_story: Chee the clipped cheerleader barks one sharp chant — "EXERT!" — pom-poms stabbing the air, drilling the sweating crowd until every last fan strains with effort.

story: Pestle Basin splits into two halves grinding the exact same rhythm, perched on Horizon Line's endless flat stage; beneath it, Wishbone snap-kicks its legs in a can-can, all to ENTERTAIN the empty desert.
reading_story: Kyo the howling rock frontman screams a long "Kyooo!" into the mic — his one job tonight: ENTERTAIN.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 同 'same' is carried adverbially ('grinding the exact same rhythm') rather than as a visual object, slightly weakening its imageable anchor.

story: TONGUE: Open Mouth lies flat below, a square hole in the pavement; up through it Lolling Tongue rears, pink and dripping, curling over the rim like a wet slide.
reading_story: Zetzler dares a spoonful of molten ramen broth, then dances round the shop howling, clutching one scalded TONGUE.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: both supplied actors named verbatim — 'Open Mouth lies flat below' (口) and 'up through it Lolling Tongue rears' (舌).
Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS: 'pavement', 'rim', 'wet slide' are scene staging/simile, not named kanji parts; no unsupplied component is introduced.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: 'Zetzler dares a spoonful of molten ramen broth' opens the reading_story; reading_actor_used matches the registry name for ぜつ.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: 'TONGUE:' is the first token, matching meaning_placement='start'; reading_story also lands on '...clutching one scalded TONGUE.' at the end.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: 口 image says 'a perfect square hole' → story renders 'a square hole in the pavement'; 舌 image says 'long pink tongue lolling out and curling, dripping' → story renders 'pink and dripping, curling'. No invented cognitive ability; 'lies flat', 'rears', 'curling' are ordinary physical motion.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS: no origin/historical claim anywhere.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story 29 words, reading_story 19 words, both under ~40.
Spatial fidelity is correct and load-bearing: 口 is the lower element of 舌, and the story stages the mouth 'below' with the tongue rearing 'up through it'.
Minor (non-gating): the simile 'like a wet slide' stacks a second image on the primary one; trimming it would tighten focus per rubric §3.13 (conciseness / low load).

Minor (non-gating, data artifact not candidate fault): 舌 is listed as its own component, so 'Lolling Tongue' doubles as both a part and the whole; the story handles it cleanly but the pairing is inherently near-tautological.
Distinctiveness risk: 'Lolling Tongue' will recur in 話/活/乱 and 'Open Mouth' in every 口-bearing kanji, so the pavement-hole staging is the only interference guard here — hence a 3, not higher.

story: A Stepladder splays open as a roof over a Mound of Soil; at the base an Open Mouth gapes as the doorway — squint, and the whole stack is a COTTAGE.
reading_story: Shaq folds his seven-foot frame through the tiny door of the COTTAGE, shoulders scraping both walls, head jammed in the thatch.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'squint, and...' is meta-commentary rather than direct image content — could be tightened, but keyword placement and imagery still land.

story: SHOP: a Stepladder balances on a Mound of Soil over the Open Mouth doorway; outside at the Plus-Sign Crossroads, every inch is utilized for displays, and one Ink Droplet dots the freshly painted sign.
reading_story: Hoth barges into the SHOP, slaps a coin down, grabs his bread, and is out before the bell stops — Hoth's shopping trips are as clipped as his name.
issues: 'every inch is utilized for displays' is abstract and low-imagery — unavoidable given 用 has a null actor, but it dilutes the scene (passive construction, nothing concrete shown)
Scene props (doorway, displays, sign) add mild extraneous load on top of six mandatory components, keeping imageability at 3

story: Dwarfed at the waterline, the Dugout Canoe knocks its carved log hull against a wall of white portholes rising twelve decks above its single plank seat: the LINER.
reading_story: A Hacker in a deckchair, laptop on his knees, seizes the LINER's navigation screens; the vast white ship swings around while passengers calmly sip cocktails.

story: A Dugout Canoe drifts at the left bank as the Vaulting Pole bends and carries the Kings Crown over the water in one huge stride — it lands on the plank seat, crowning the craft a royal ROWBOAT.
reading_story: At the regatta, Tay wins the ROWBOAT race by dragging each stroke out looong — just like her name.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): spatial fidelity slightly loose — in the glyph 王 rests on 廴 in the right half, but the story lands the crown on the canoe's seat; the pole-carrying-crown beat still encodes the 廴/王 relationship.

story: Along the harbor's left pier, a Dugout Canoe is sheathed in riveted steel, cannons bolted amidships, until the carved log bristles grey and menacing — relaunched as a WARSHIP.
reading_story: Khan gallops his horse up the gangplank and plants his horsehair banner on the gun deck — from today the steppe conqueror commands a WARSHIP.
issues: Minor: 'bristles grey and menacing' is slightly adjectival rather than pictorial; a fully visual beat would push imageability to 5.
Minor: Khan-commands-a-military-object is a recurring pattern across kan-reading kanji; scene-specific props (gangplank, horsehair banner) mitigate but do not eliminate interference risk.

story: A Pot Lid lies clamped flat on bare ground; a Grass Tuft sprouts thick across its top, knitting into a springy green carpet — peel the lid up and you lift a perfect square of TURF.
reading_story: The Sheriff stalks the courthouse lawn, tin star flashing, barking one clipped "shi!" at trespassers — nobody tramples the Sheriff's TURF.

story: The Grass Tuft crowning the hilltop drips with morning dew; one brush against its two green blades and your sleeve carries PERFUME all day.
reading_story: Ho booms "ho-ho-ho!" down the chimney — no toys in his sack tonight, only little bottles of PERFUME, and the whole house smells of roses.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): mild interference with shipped 杉 CEDAR entry — its meaning story closes on 'the unmistakable perfume of CEDAR' and its reading story also uses Santa + scent; two Santa-plus-fragrance reading stories in the same level could collide at recall time.
Advisory (non-blocking): keyword tail — story ends 'PERFUME all day', a two-word trail after the keyword; acceptable per house style but dead-last placement would be crisper.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the cracked sidewalk, its two blades parting like curtains as something pale shoulders up between them — swelling, glistening, unfurling into one fat green BUD.
reading_story: Garr rolls up growling outside the greenhouse; his engine's hot exhaust blast pops every BUD open at once.
issues: PASS §3.1 component coverage: the sole mandatory component ⺾ is named verbatim as "A Grass Tuft" and its registry image is honoured — "crowns" echoes "plant-crown capping whatever grows below" and "its two blades" echoes "sprouting two blades side by side".

PASS §3.2 no phantom components: "cracked sidewalk" and "curtains" are scenery/simile, not actor personas; "something pale" is the emerging bud itself (the payoff), not an unsupplied component. 牙 sits in phonetic_extra, not components, so its absence is correct.
PASS §3.3 reading actor present: "Garr rolls up growling" opens the reading_story and reading_actor_used="Garr" matches.
PASS §3.4 meaning lands: "...into one fat green BUD." is the final word, matching meaning_placement="end"; keyword also recurs as the payoff of the reading_story.

PASS §3.5 actor consistency: Garr's registry note is "a growling engine, short" — the story uses "growling" and "his engine's hot exhaust blast," ordinary physical/mechanical behaviour with no invented cognitive faculty.
PASS §3.6 no false etymology: the story never claims 牙 or ⺾ explains the character's history.
PASS §3.7 length & focus: story = 28 words, reading_story = 19 words, both well under ~40; single continuous image, no digression.

NON-BLOCKING (§3.11 spatial fidelity, graded): ⺾ caps what grows below, but the bud "shoulders up between" the blades, placing it level with/above the tuft rather than beneath it. Reads naturally, slightly loosens the top-over-bottom staging.

NON-BLOCKING (§3.12 coherence, graded): colour drift — the sprout is "pale" mid-sentence then "fat green" at the payoff. Defensible as unfurling, but it is two different images of one object in eight words.

NON-BLOCKING (§3.10 distinctiveness, graded): "grass pushing a sprout through cracked pavement" is the single most predictable image for a ⺾+bud kanji and is the nearest neighbour of 苗/茎-type stories; the curtain-parting beat is what keeps it above a 2.

NON-BLOCKING — upstream data, not a candidate defect: dominant_reading is kun め, yet a reading actor (が / Garr) is supplied. docs/07 §1.3 states kun'yomi get no reading actor. The candidate used what it was given correctly; flag the record for the registry pass.

story: Above the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid, a Grass Tuft perches on the topmost mud dike, its two green blades trembling over the four square plots below — the paddy's first SEEDLING.
reading_story: Beau wades barefoot through the shallows, cupping one trembling SEEDLING, his deep drawl booming across the water.
issues: Minor: 'trembling' is reused in both the meaning story and the reading story, slightly blurring the two scenes rather than giving each its own texture.

Minor (distinctiveness): the story is close to a literal reading of the kanji's semantics (grass above field = seedling), so it has little narrative hook of its own; it relies on spatial fidelity rather than surprise to be memorable.

Minor: the Grass Tuft effectively IS the seedling, making 'the paddy's first SEEDLING' slightly circular — it still lands the keyword at the end, but the payoff restates the actor rather than resolving into it.

story: A Barbed Pike stands planted in the dirt, a Falling Katana slashing down across its shaft — yet the Grass Tuft crowning them swallows both weapons in sprouting green until nothing shows: OVERGROWN.
reading_story: Mo mows his lawn every morning, yet by noon the OVERGROWN grass towers over his head — only Mo's tuft of hair pokes above the green.

story: VILLA: a lone Grass Tuft roots in a bare hillside plot and swells overnight into a green mansion, its two giant blades arching overhead into a shaded veranda.
reading_story: Sosa retires mid-season, hangs his bat above the VILLA fireplace, and spends August signing baseballs for tourists on the terrace.
issues: Minor: 'bare hillside plot' is free scenery, not a component — harmless but adds a spatial element that could later be mistaken for a radical.
Minor: meaning story (28 words) + reading story (21 words) run close to the length budget when read together.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the scene; beneath it, the Swaddling Wrap curls over, hugging Scattered Rice Grains that fan outward like white petals inside its fold — a perfect CHRYSANTHEMUM.
reading_story: The Kicker lines up a penalty — but the ball is a giant CHRYSANTHEMUM; his kick bursts it into drifting petals.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the gateless Walled Box; sealed inside, one Rice Stalk rots in the dark, its drooping head furred with grey fuzz — every airless corner blooming GERM.
reading_story: King leans over the pulpit, microphone hissing, and one invisible GERM on the polished rail outlasts the whole speech.
issues: Non-blocking: 'every airless corner blooming GERM' is grammatically loose — 'germ' is countable, so the payoff phrase reads as a label rather than an image; 'blooming with GERM' or restructuring so the fuzz itself is the keyword would sharpen the punch.

Non-blocking: the reading story hangs on 'one invisible GERM', and an explicitly invisible object is weak mnemonic material — the concrete anchors ('pulpit', 'hissing microphone', 'polished rail') carry it, but the germ itself cannot be pictured.

Minor: mold/fuzz imagery risks interference with other decay- or fungus-adjacent N1 kanji; the gateless stone box + rice stalk pairing is what keeps it separable, so that structural detail should survive any future edit.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the flat Horizon Line; a Lightning Bolt spears straight down through both, and the strike makes every grass blade blossom in dazzling gold — SPLENDOR.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr slams the brakes, awestruck: the whole avenue glows with gold-leaf SPLENDOR, so extravagant he waives the fare.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in reading_story, SPLENDOR is followed by a short trailing clause ('so extravagant he waives the fare') rather than being the final word; still reads as the payoff and 'extravagant' usefully echoes the 豪華 vocab gloss.

story: BUSH CLOVER: autumn wind combs the Grass Tuft flat, so it grows sideways instead — a shaggy waist-high thicket sprawling across the gravel path, rustling and snagging every passing ankle.
reading_story: The cobbler hammers a Shoe on his bench; wiry BUSH CLOVER stems have shot up through the floorboards and tangled the sole he is nailing.
issues: Non-blocking: story leans on 'autumn wind' — licensed by phonetic_extra 秋, so not a phantom component, but it is the closest thing to a semantic gloss here (grass + autumn = bush clover); it stays a scene rather than a stated derivation, so the no-etymology gate holds.

Non-blocking: dominant_reading is kun はぎ while reading_actor is on-reading しゅう (Shoe). The candidate correctly uses the supplied actor, but the record itself pairs a kun dominant reading with an on-reading actor — worth checking upstream, not a fault of this candidate.

story: Grass Tuft sprouts over a fresh grave; just beneath, the Horizon Line marks ground level. Deeper, Crescent Moon and Soup Ladle lie buried as grave goods, while Cupped Palms cradle them all from below — INTERMENT.
reading_story: Sosa hits his final home run, then digs at home plate and gives his beloved bat a solemn INTERMENT before the roaring crowd.

story: AMASS: the Grass Tuft crowns a secret mound, its two blades sweeping every stray seed down beneath it, packing the hidden heap fatter and fatter until the ground itself bulges.
reading_story: Chicker clucks over his nest, pecking every dropped grain into one towering pile — Chicker lives only to AMASS, hoarding until the coop bursts.
issues: Non-blocking: story frame overlaps 蔵 (n2), whose story also opens with a Grass Tuft crowning a storage scene ('A Grass Tuft crowns the STOREHOUSE roof') — same ⺾-atop-hoard schema, distinguished mainly by the payoff word and the sweeping-seeds mechanism.

Non-blocking: heap/mound/'packing' imagery echoes semantic neighbor 積 PILE UP (n3: 'Cowrie Shells tumble into a heap, a Mound of Soil packs down'), a mild interference risk for the amass/pile-up cluster.
Minor imageability drag: 'secret mound' / 'hidden heap' is inherently unseeable; the closing 'ground itself bulges' mostly compensates.

story: Atop the black pond a Grass Tuft rides like a green crown, its two blades slicing the surface; directly beneath, a pale pink cup opens wide — LOTUS.
reading_story: Wren kneels at the pond's edge, tracing his compass around one floating LOTUS until its petals become the blueprint for his cathedral dome.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the meaning payoff object is the keyword itself — a lotus flower drawn to cue 'lotus'. Near-tautological, so the story carries little independent retrieval value beyond the ⺾ actor.

Non-blocking: nothing in the meaning story encodes the lower element 連; combined with the very common Grass Tuft actor and a generic pond setting, this risks interference with neighbouring ⺾ water-plant kanji (荷, 藻, 菱, 萍). Reading story's Wren (れん) is the only 連 hook.
Minor: 'a pale pink cup opens wide' pre-announces the payoff one clause before '— LOTUS', slightly softening the terminal reveal required by gate 4.

story: A Grass Tuft caps the Cliff Awning's slanted roof; beneath, a Coal Brazier's four coals glow warm along the floor — a shelter this cozy is impossible not to RECOMMEND.
reading_story: Every rookie asks Senna which tires to run; he taps the rain slicks — the only ones he will RECOMMEND at Monaco.
issues: Non-gating: 'rain slicks' is contradictory F1 terminology (slicks are dry tires; rain tires are 'wets') — consider 'the wets' for persona coherence.
Non-gating: reading story keyword is followed by 'at Monaco', so RECOMMEND is terminal payoff but not the literal last word.
Non-gating: moderate interference risk with other 广+灬 kanji (e.g. 庶) — awning+brazier scene recurs; Grass Tuft cap and the review-style payoff are the only differentiators.

story: SEND FORTH FRAGRANCE: a Grass Tuft perched atop a heavy cast-iron bank safe that squats on the Coal Brazier's four glowing coals until its sheer mass bakes white-hot, roasting the blades into smoking perfume.
reading_story: Kuhn burns his outdated paradigm's notes in the faculty fireplace; the smoldering pages SEND FORTH FRAGRANCE so sweet that his rivals drift in and convert.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the 'cast-iron bank safe' is an invented prop standing in for the 重 keyword. 'heavy' is stated explicitly and reinforced by 'sheer mass', so gate 2 (no phantom components) passes -- the safe is not a kanji element -- but there is some risk the learner encodes 'safe' rather than 'heavy' as the middle component.
Minor: 'until its sheer mass bakes white-hot' has a muddled causal link (the coals, not the mass, do the heating); it reads as slightly abstract physics in an otherwise concrete image.
Minor: heat must conduct through the safe to roast the grass on top -- physically plausible once the safe is white-hot, but the chain adds one inferential step.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns it all: the Full Moon hangs left while a Lightning Bolt stabs through the Horizon Line into a Tsunami Wave; the lit spray droops in purple clusters of WISTERIA.
reading_story: Tone grabs the mic under a dripping arbor, purple WISTERIA clusters bobbing on the bassline as he drawls his long, low rhymes.
issues: Minor: 'Full Moon hangs left' is inert set-dressing — the moon never interacts with the scene, weakening cohesion slightly.
Minor: in reading_story the keyword WISTERIA sits mid-clause rather than as the final payoff; gate 4 applies to the meaning story (which ends on WISTERIA), so not blocking.

story: TIGER: stubby Wishing-Well Legs stride out from beneath the Rock Overhang, hoisting the striped Tiger-Hide Cowl so high it snaps the Divining Twig off the cliff lip, the Soup Ladle swinging and clanging from its hooked whisker.
reading_story: In her mirrored Paris staircase Coco freezes: a TIGER is climbing toward her, wearing the pearls she left draped on the banister.
issues: minor (non-blocking): 'hoisting the striped Tiger-Hide Cowl so high it snaps the Divining Twig' has an ambiguous 'it' (cowl vs. the hoisting motion), and legs doing the hoisting is a slight physical stretch — permitted under the motion rule, but a rephrase like 'lifting it on their shoulders' would read cleaner.
minor (non-blocking): 'its hooked whisker' — the possessive points back across two clauses to the Cowl; naming it ('the Cowl's hooked whisker') would tighten spatial fidelity for 匕 sitting under 厂.

story: You don the Tiger-Hide Cowl — Divining Twig spiked on top, Rock Overhang jutting beneath, Soup Ladle clenched inside — then rake the ladle across the Toolbox Tray pinned below, gouging out its every tool: TYRANNIZE.
reading_story: Gyacker stomps into the schoolyard, growling his heavy G, snatching lunches and shoving the small kids in line — day after day, Gyacker lives to TYRANNIZE.
issues: Spatial/scale incoherence (rubric §3 item 11/9): 'Rock Overhang jutting beneath' a cowl worn on the head mixes a cliff-scale object into a garment-scale image; the reader cannot form one consistent picture of the head assembly.

High element load (§3 item 13): four sub-actors are stacked onto/into the Tiger-Hide Cowl in a single clause chain ('spiked on top, jutting beneath, clenched inside'), which reads as a positional checklist rather than a scene.
Redundant nesting: the story names both 虍 (Tiger-Hide Cowl) and its own constituent parts 卜/匕/厂 as separate objects hung on it, which is required by the component list but weakens coherence.

Distinctiveness risk (§3 item 10): the Tiger-Hide Cowl recurs across 虚/虜/虞/慮; only the ladle-raking-the-tray beat separates this from its neighbours, and 'Soup Ladle + Toolbox Tray' is a pairing likely to be reused.
reading_story does not encode the -ku coda flagged in the reading actor note; only the voiced heavy G is dramatized ('growling his heavy G'), and that cue is meta-linguistic rather than imagistic.

Content safety (§3 item 14): schoolyard bullying is on-keyword and mild, but note it is depicted against children ('shoving the small kids'); acceptable here, worth flagging if the corpus accumulates similar scenes.

story: The Tiger-Hide Cowl hangs like a tent: Divining Twig planted on top, Rock Overhang jutting beneath it, Soup Ladle tucked inside — it scoops nothing. At the base, one bare Horizon Line: VOID.
reading_story: Cole leans over the well and shouts; no echo returns. His voice just drops away — Cole is yelling into pure VOID.
issues: Minor: 'hangs like a tent' introduces a tent simile — acceptable staging, but a stricter phantom check could flag it; consider 'hangs like a canopy' to match the registry image exactly.
Minor: meaning story reads slightly listy (planted / jutting / tucked inventory) rather than one action, which costs some imageability.

story: The Tiger-Hide Cowl hangs from a Rock Overhang, a Divining Twig and Soup Ladle tucked into its stripes; beneath it the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid presses a Flexing Bicep down into the mud — a CAPTIVE.
reading_story: Ryo-short jerks the rope taut with one clipped tug; the CAPTIVE stumbles two steps and stops — short leash, short march, short name.
issues: Non-blocking: 卜 (Divining Twig) and 匕 (Soup Ladle) are discharged as inert cargo ('tucked into its stripes') with no motion, contact, or consequence — coverage is satisfied on paper but these two carry near-zero retrieval weight.

Non-blocking: 'the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid presses a Flexing Bicep down into the mud' makes a location the agent; physically defensible (mud/water weight) and not a cognitive-ability violation, but harder to picture as a single action than an explicit agent would be.
Non-blocking: the sentence follows a generic 'A hangs from B, C and D tucked in, beneath it E presses F' template, which caps distinctiveness against neighboring 虍-family kanji (虚, 虐, 慮).

story: On the left a Fat Grub writhes; on the right a Thatched House caps a tilted Soup Ladle, and from its deep bowl pours a glistening, coiling SNAKE.
reading_story: Jacques the sommelier tips his decanter at the table, and instead of wine a hissing SNAKE spills out across the white cloth.

story: The Three-Legged Cauldron rattles on the left, steam hissing from its lid seam; the Fat Grub pressed against its right flank sags in the heat, plump body running into milky syrup — watch it DISSOLVE.
reading_story: Yuna lands a triple jump, but her blades glow so hot the rink starts to DISSOLVE into warm water around her skates.
issues: Minor: reading story keyword not sentence-final — 'DISSOLVE into warm water around her skates' trails four words after the keyword (still the climactic verb, passes gate 4)
Minor: melting-rink imagery in the reading story is a generic hot-object trope; watch for interference with other heat/melt kanji stories (e.g. 溶)

story: A basin of blood tips off a ledge onto Stepladder below — one of countless identical Stepladders packed leg-to-leg, every A-frame dripping red: the MASSES.
reading_story: The cobbler hammers one Shoe while the MASSES crowd his shop window, ten thousand bare feet all demanding that single Shoe.
issues: Minor: in the reading story the keyword MASSES sits mid-sentence rather than at the payoff position; non-gating (meaning story carries the placement gate, matching shipped n2 precedent).
Minor: cobbler-shop setting is shared across all Shoe-family (shuu/shu) reading stories, slight interference risk mitigated by the 'ten thousand bare feet' twist.

story: The Four-Way Junction stretches wide: its crosswalk stripes fuse into endless tree-lined lanes, and the whole city pours down the grand BOULEVARD.
reading_story: Guy rolls his gunpowder barrels straight down the middle of the BOULEVARD, planting fireworks under every streetlight.
issues: Unused phonetic_extra 圭: story never anchors the middle element (stacked-earth filling of the 行 frame), so nothing distinguishes 街 visually from 術/衛/衝/衡 beyond the keyword — caps distinctiveness at 3.
'Tree-lined lanes' is keyword-inherent scenery, not a phantom component, but could faintly suggest a 木 element to a literal reader.
'The whole city pours down' is a vague crowd abstraction — the one non-picturable beat in an otherwise concrete scene.
Keyword appears mid-sentence in the reading story (terminal in the meaning story, which is what the placement gate covers).

story: The Four-Way Junction's traffic parts around its center, where the Circling Sentries pace their endless loop — one treading above the outpost, one below — guarding the crossroads: DEFENSE.
reading_story: At dawn Abe rattles the outpost gate, then nods, satisfied: a DEFENSE this tight won't even let Abe himself slip through.
issues: Minor: main story's em-dash aside ('one treading above the outpost, one below') slightly clutters an otherwise single clear scene, but it faithfully mirrors the Circling Sentries' defined image rather than inventing anything.
Reading story beat of Abe testing a gate he cannot pass is slightly paradoxical but remains ordinary physical action and is memorable, not a gate failure.

story: A heavy iron block sits dead center in the Four-Way Junction; brakes screech too late, and cars from all four crosswalk-lined streets COLLIDE with it, one after another.
reading_story: The top-hatted Showman plants himself mid-road crying "Shoooow!" — gawking drivers COLLIDE behind him, and he bows at every crash.
issues: Minor: reading story places COLLIDE in the penultimate clause ('...drivers COLLIDE behind him, and he bows at every crash') — end placement is softened, though the closing word 'crash' echoes the keyword and keeps it as the payoff.

Minor: 'iron block' brushes the semantic territory of 鉄 (iron); it is a scenery prop concretizing 重 'heavy', not a phantom — registry word-boundary scan across all n*-component-actors.json is clean (the only raw hit, 'Tree', was a substring false positive inside 'streets').

Distinctiveness capped at 4: a multi-car crash at an intersection is a fairly default traffic scene, though no shipped story in any level currently uses collide/pileup imagery and the other Four-Way Junction stories (衛, 術, 行) do not compete.

story: Dead center of the Four-Way Junction, a Swaddling Wrap curls down over a Rice-Paddy Grid, which rests on a Starfish's outspread arms below — traffic circling, nothing tipping: perfect EQUILIBRIUM.
reading_story: Coe rounds the final bend, shoulders level, stride and breath held in flawless EQUILIBRIUM.
issues: Minor: the scene is largely a static vertical stack (wrap over grid over starfish) — the only motion is background traffic, so it reads more as a glyph-layout description than an event.
Minor: 'nothing tipping' is the sole load-bearing link to EQUILIBRIUM; a physical near-tip or wobble would bind keyword to image more forcefully.
Minor: 田 (Rice-Paddy Grid) is present but passive — it is only a thing resting on the starfish, so it is the component most likely to be forgotten on recall.

story: The Hanger Kimono hangs alone in the desert, the Horizon Line slicing straight across its waist; where the line cuts, silk fades to sand-grey thread and the wide sleeves sag lower daily — DECLINE.
reading_story: Every morning Swee marks his stock chart one notch lower — a clipped, steady slide into DECLINE.

story: The Mound of Soil sits atop the Hanger Kimono; from the right the Barbed Pike leans over both, its hooked spur slicing a perfect sleeve pattern from the silk — work of a TAILOR.
reading_story: Between innings, Cy hands his split uniform to the TAILOR, who stitches it up before the next pitch.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in the reading_story the keyword TAILOR sits mid-sentence rather than at start/end; acceptable since the meaning story ends on TAILOR and placement gating targets the meaning story.
Minor (non-blocking): soil mound resting directly on the silk kimono is slightly incongruous, though it accurately encodes the 土-over-衣 layout.

story: Hanger Kimono hangs serene — then its aged silk shrieks, ripping from the collar's soft V straight down to the hem; two ragged halves swing apart on the wooden hanger, utterly SPLIT.
reading_story: Retzler flexes his shoulders; his too-tight jacket gives a deafening SPLIT down the back seam.

story: Beside the Tailor's Lapel, the Twin Ski Slopes pour endless snow: a Wishbone toboggans past the Stepladder straight into the Open Mouth at the valley's pinch, which swallows heap after heap — ABUNDANT.

story: A Speech Bubble drones on the left; to its right a Hawk Talon grips an Antenna Mast whose foot plunges into a Trap Pit, the buried hum booming back as NOH CHANTING.
