story: CONVEY: Pot Lid pops off the top, Wishbone beneath snaps its legs into a chute, and Hanger Kimono glides down it, handed over to Speech Bubble waiting on the left, which prints "mine now."
reading_story: Average Joe signs the deed with a stretched "Joooe," happy to CONVEY his farmhouse to the neighbors and yield the keys.
issues: Minor: 'handed over' is agentless passive — the kimono glides down and is 'handed over' with no visible hander; a self-sliding delivery would be cleaner.
Minor: wishbone legs 'snapping into a chute' requires a beat of interpretation (the split V as a slide), though it stays within the actor's defined physical nature.

story: A solid Speech Bubble walls off the left, words stacked like sandbags. Right, a Grass Tuft crowns the huddled chick — one of a pair, its twin already snatched. Wall and crown SAFEGUARD.
reading_story: Goh throws his coat over the shivering chick and stands in the doorway all night to SAFEGUARD it.
issues: Non-blocking (gate 2): the 'chick' prop coincidentally mirrors the real etymology of 隻 (bird in hand). It is not asserted as origin so gate 6 holds, but it edges toward etymology-by-accident; a non-avian 'one of a pair' object (a single mitten, one boot) would be safer.
Imageability drag: 'its twin already snatched' is off-screen negative space — nothing to actually see — and 'one of a pair' is delivered as a label rather than rendered as an image.

Distinctiveness drag: the payoff 'wall and crown' is generic protection imagery liable to interfere with neighbouring protect/defend kanji (守, 保, 衛, 防); only the crowned lone chick keeps it separable.
Minor coherence tension: the twin was NOT safeguarded, which slightly undercuts the keyword payoff even as it motivates the scene.

story: Balanced on the Twin Pillars, wedged beneath their shared ledge, an Open Mouth gapes upward — through a crack in that ledge rattles a steady, drumming trickle of BEANS.
reading_story: Backstage, Tone shakes his maracas — stuffed with BEANS — and raps a long, drawn-out verse to their rattle.
issues: Minor (non-gating): in the reading story the keyword BEANS sits mid-sentence ('maracas — stuffed with BEANS —') rather than at start/end; meaning story satisfies the placement gate with BEANS as its final word.

story: Left: the Full Moon hangs low and silver. Right: the Muddy Boar wallows beneath it, snorting, curly tail flicking mud across the glowing disc — bristles slicked flat, tusks buried, he's now a fat PIG.
reading_story: Tony leans over the sty rail waving a pepperoni slice, yelling "Ton! Ton!" — and every mud-caked PIG stampedes straight at him.

story: A Pot Lid clamps down on an Open Mouth mid-roar; beneath them a Bedsheet Cover strains over the Muddy Boar bucking below — lid, mouth and sheet all heave skyward on its back. Utterly OVERPOWERING.
reading_story: General Gough charges the hill; enemies scatter before a single shot is fired — Gough's presence alone is OVERPOWERING.
issues: minor (non-gating): four stacked elements add slight cognitive load; the recap clause 'lid, mouth and sheet all heave skyward' is mildly redundant
minor (non-gating): mild interference risk with 家-style 'covered boar' scenes, but the roaring mouth + clamped pot lid stack distinguishes it

story: The Divining Twig hovers above the Cowrie Shell, prong tapping its ridged slit to test whether it has ever opened. The shell clamps tight, sealed like a vow — the twig's verdict: CHASTITY.
reading_story: Tay flashes a silver purity ring at the crowd mid-song, belting an entire album about CHASTITY.
issues: Non-gating: 'tapping its ridged slit to test whether it has ever opened' is mildly suggestive innuendo; acceptable since the slit detail is registry-supplied imagery, but curation may prefer a tamer phrasing (rubric item 14, cultural safety).
Watch-item: 貞 story should stay distinct from future 偵 (亻+貞, 'spy') story since they will share the twig+shell cast.

story: You climb the palace steps hauling one huge Cowrie Shell — your village's last coin-treasure — and set it, ridged slit gleaming, at the foot of the throne: your TRIBUTE.
reading_story: Coe finishes his victory lap and the stands rain coins onto the track — a champion's TRIBUTE piling at his spikes.
issues: Non-blocking: story upsizes the Cowrie Shell to 'huge' while the registry image calls it 'one small clam' — physical exaggeration only, persona (coin-treasure, ridged slit) intact.
Non-blocking: reading story keyword has three trailing words ('piling at his spikes') after TRIBUTE; still the final clause's payoff, counted as end placement.

story: PIERCE: the Iron Padlock hovers over the Cowrie Shell, then drives its shackle straight down through the ridged slit and snaps shut — shell skewered on iron, locked through forever.
reading_story: Dismounted at last, Khan hammers his iron tent-stake down to PIERCE the frozen steppe, pinning the great yurt against the howling winter wind.
issues: Non-blocking: keyword PIERCE is mid-sentence in the reading story (start-placement only in the meaning story); consistent with approved corpus convention but not ideal payoff placement.

Non-blocking: Khan-piercing action overlaps with existing 環 (spears ring with lance) and 慣 (spears sack against cowrie coin) reading stories — mild neighbor-interference risk, mitigated by the distinctive tent-stake/yurt/frozen-steppe anchor.
Non-blocking: 'Dismounted at last' departs from the on-horseback persona note, though dismounting is ordinary physical motion with corpus precedent (完, 管).

story: At the desert's dead middle, the Horizon Line lies perfectly flat; dig beneath it and a Cowrie Shell gleams up — buried treasure, utterly PRECIOUS.
reading_story: Key the locksmith refuses every job but one: locking away whatever is PRECIOUS — a single clipped click, and it's safe forever.
issues: Minor: in the reading story the keyword PRECIOUS is followed by a trailing clause ('and it's safe forever') instead of being the final payoff; meaning-story placement (end) passes cleanly.
Minor: 中 is rendered only as the location tag 'dead middle' — acceptable since it has no actor, but it adds no visual content.

story: CONGRATULATIONS rain down from above onto the Cowrie Shell waiting below: it pops its ridged slit wide and sprays its coin-treasure into the air like confetti.
reading_story: Garr guns her growling engine over the finish line, and the whole grandstand thunders CONGRATULATIONS as she revs back in reply.

story: Boarding the bus, the weight of responsibility presses down from overhead as you drop a Cowrie Shell into the till below — that gleaming shell pays your FARE.
reading_story: Chin the boxer boards the train after a match, black-eyed, counting coins in his glove to pay the FARE.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 'weight of responsibility presses down' is abstract — felt rather than seen — slightly softening imageability.
Minor (non-blocking): shell-as-payment is the obvious move for any 貝 money-kanji; the 任-overhead pressure is what keeps this distinct, so preserve it in any edit.

story: Under the table the polished Cowrie Shell slides rightward into the inspector's open palm; the instant he possesses it, his stamp thumps down — that shell was a BRIBE.
reading_story: Referee Wai blows a shrill "wai!" on his whistle whenever an envelope is slipped to him — the match always goes to whoever paid the BRIBE.
issues: Non-blocking: 有 is covered as the verb 'possesses' rather than a named actor — acceptable since the component has no actor (kanji_keyword 'possess'), and the possession moment is anchored to a concrete action (palm closing).
Non-blocking: 'Referee' is a new characterization for Wai, but this is his corpus debut (no prior usage in any mnemonics file) and the registry note defines no persona, so nothing is contradicted.

story: Under the Thatched House's peak, a Falling Katana slices a Sand Trickle; below gleams the Cowrie Shell — a Watching Eye above a snapping Wishbone — tribute laid out for tonight's V.I.P.
reading_story: Hinn strides onstage, palms raised, and the arena roars — tonight's crusade has one guest of honour seated in the front row: the V.I.P.
issues: Non-blocking: the Watching Eye is named but does nothing — it is only positioned ('a Watching Eye above a snapping Wishbone'), so the appositive reads like a decomposition annotation rather than an event.
Non-blocking: 'gleams' and 'tribute laid out' are weak/abstract for the payoff half of the image; a concrete action on the shell would lift imageability.

Non-blocking: interference risk — 'treasure/shell sheltered under a roof for a guest of honour' is the generic template for the 宀+貝 family, so this may blur with neighbouring kanji using the same two actors.
Note only, not a gate failure: the tribute-for-a-guest framing sits close to the real etymology of 賓, but it is presented as imagery with no origin claim, so item 6 passes.

story: The Cowrie Shell — Watching Eye perched on snapped Wishbone legs — pays out: one coin made to stand up on edge above the Open Mouth, then topple in. COMPENSATION.
reading_story: By crashes his bicycle through your window, then calmly empties his wallet on the sill — full COMPENSATION.
issues: Minor: opening appositive ('Cowrie Shell — Watching Eye perched on snapped Wishbone legs —') is a dense parse before the action; consider letting the shell act first and revealing its eye/wishbone anatomy inline.
Minor: 'one coin made to stand up' is agentless passive — giving the shell the explicit action (e.g. 'stands a coin on edge') would sharpen the mental film.

story: Every month the Cowrie Shell — Watching Eye over Wishbone legs — rolls beside the Goalpost Frame capping the Plus-Sign Crossroads; above, a Lightning Bolt spears the Horizon Line: payment taken, SUBSCRIPTION renewed.
reading_story: Coe delivers your newspaper SUBSCRIPTION personally — the Olympic runner sprints one to your door each dawn, always in record time.
issues: Lightning Bolt / Horizon Line clause ('above, a Lightning Bolt spears the Horizon Line') is pure coverage filler — it does not contribute to the subscription payoff, slightly dragging coherence.
'payment taken' has no visible agent taking the payment; the transaction is implied rather than depicted, weakening the visual payoff.
Seven actors in one tableau is near the cognitive-load ceiling; 'rolls beside' is a weak interaction between the Cowrie Shell and the 冓-cluster structure.

story: PARDON: on the left, RED welts glow across a flogged bare back; on the right, the Cracking Whip snaps down, misses, and its lash coils slack on the flagstones — never striking again.
reading_story: Shaq towers over the referee who ejected him, then just grins and waves the call away — the arena roars as he grants a booming PARDON.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): the strongest imagery in the story — red welts, a flogged back, a cracking whip — all encodes PUNISHMENT; 'pardon' is carried only by a negation ('misses', 'never striking again'). Negated actions are weak retrieval cues, so a learner may recall the scene and produce 'flog/punish' instead of 'pardon'. A positive act of clemency (e.g. the whip's lash coiling into a loop that unties the wrists) would carry the keyword rather than merely withholding the opposite.

Non-blocking (reading actor): reading_actor vowel_length is 'short' (しゃ), but nothing in the reading_story clips or shrinks Shaq to signal brevity per docs/07 §1.2 ('short vowel = clipped/shrunken twin'). 'Towers over' and 'booming' both lean long. Not a gate, but it works against the vowel-length encoding the registry is designed to teach.

Non-blocking (coherence): Shaq pardoning the referee who ejected him inverts the usual authority direction — the ref holds the power, so the clemency reads as sarcasm ('waves the call away', 'grins') rather than genuine pardon.

story: A runner explodes from the low left; the Divining Twig is clamped high in his raised right fist, its short prong stabbing forward down the track — the signal to PROCEED.
reading_story: Foo the Foo Fighter strums one screaming chord, the barricade swings open, and thousands of fans PROCEED toward the stage.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness risk): a runner clutching a stick reads as a relay baton, a generic 走-family image; with many N1 kanji sharing 走 the only separator is 'forked twig / short prong', so interference is plausible.

Non-blocking (imageability): the payoff clause 'the signal to PROCEED' is an abstract label rather than a visual beat -- e.g. the prong itself dropping like a starter's flag would make the keyword land as an image.

Note: component 走 is carried by the inflected form 'runner' rather than the literal kanji_keyword 'run'; judged as covered since the concept is unambiguous, but a stricter literal-keyword check would flag it.

story: A runner sprints the left wall, then curves along the floor through rows of brimming teacups — every stride silent, not one cup rattling, not one drop spilled: ELEGANCE.
reading_story: Master Shu pours tea one-handed, sleeve caught between two fingers, and sets the cup down without a sound — ELEGANCE.
issues: Hand-authored after judge rejection: the candidate front-labelled the keyword and restated it rather than paying it off. Rewritten so the payoff lands at the end of both stories on the demonstrated quality (silent, spill-free motion) rather than an assertion.

story: From the start line at the far left, a lone disembodied leg pushes off, pounding stride after stride until it is only a speck on the horizon — pure LONG-DISTANCE.
reading_story: Cole runs LONG-DISTANCE the clipped way: short, chopped strides — millions of them — eating up entire continents.
issues: Minor: 'speck on the horizon' and 'eating up entire continents' drift abstract at the image's edges
Distinctiveness watch-item: running-leg core scene is a common motif among 足-radical neighbors (跳/躍/踏); the endurance framing mitigates but does not eliminate interference risk

story: A lone bare leg stands planted at the left edge of the frame, coils tight as a spring, then launches — land, coil, launch again, each landing shaking dust from the floorboards: HOP.
reading_story: Cho perches on a shifting Hogwarts staircase; every time it swings away she HOPs to the next step, robes billowing behind her.
issues: Soft phantom risk: 'coils tight as a spring' introduces 'spring' — which is also one of the kanji's own meanings (Spring) — as a near-object. Reads as a simile so it clears gate 2, but a learner could mistake it for a second component. Suggest 'coils tight, then launches'.

Distinctiveness is the weak axis (3/5): 'leg jumps repeatedly' is the generic framing for the whole 足-motion family and risks interference with 躍 (leap up), 踊 (dance), 蹴 (kick). 兆 was available in phonetic_extra and went unused — the free differentiator was left on the table.

Non-gating: reading_story does not reinforce the long ō that distinguishes Cho (ちょう) from the clipped twin Choe (ちょ). Registry note flags vowel length as the #1 reading error (§1.2); a stretched/drawn-out beat would harden it.

story: On the left my leg lifts; on the right a Falling Katana slices down, shearing a Duster Wisp loose and knocking an Ink Droplet onto the floorboards — my bare heel stamps all three flat. TREAD.
reading_story: Senna vaults from his cockpit to TREAD the scorching asphalt, testing each rut with a bare heel.
issues: ADVISORY (non-blocking): 'my bare heel stamps all three flat' is the generic 足-radical action and risks interference with 踏 (step on/tread); the discriminating cue rests entirely on the katana/wisp/droplet trio. Also, stamping a katana 'flat' is the least physically coherent beat of the chain.

story: On the shore a giant leg rises as the Tsunami Wave curls over the setting Sun; the leg stamps the crest flat onto the Sun — one thunderous, spray-bursting STEP.
reading_story: Onstage, Tone raps while stomping his boot on the beat — every STEP shakes the arena floor.
issues: Minor persona drift: Sun's registry image specifies a 'bright round midday sun blazing in a clear sky' but the story stages 'the setting Sun' — physical staging only, not gate-failing, but consider changing 'setting' to 'blazing' for exact persona match.
Reading story keyword placement: 'every STEP shakes the arena floor' leaves STEP one clause before the end rather than as the final payoff word; acceptable but weaker than the main story's ending.

story: A giant leg tenses beside Rake Hand, whose tines pin Stumpy Sparrow flat; too old to fly, the sparrow springs off the leg's knee in one tremendous LEAP.
reading_story: Yakker narrates every LEAP he makes — "And he's airborne, folks!" — talking so fast he lands before finishing the sentence.
issues: Minor spatial tension: sparrow is 'pinned flat' by the tines yet 'springs off the leg's knee' — the escape from the pin is implicit rather than shown (non-gating; slight imageability cost).

story: A Cartwheel grinds through mud, carving a deep groove; to its right, the Curled Cat settles its comma-shaped body snugly into the fresh RUT.
reading_story: Deep in the RUT lies a Key; you pry it from the packed mud and it still turns with one clipped click.
issues: NON-BLOCKING (distinctiveness, rubric §3 item 10): the Cartwheel->RUT link is near-definitional (a wheel carving a groove IS a rut), so the meaning story carries little surprise and could interfere with other track/trace kanji; the Curled Cat nesting in the groove is what saves it. Optional sharpening: give the cat a reason the rut is HERS (e.g. the rut fits her comma shape exactly).

story: On the left the Cartwheel spins wobbling; from the right a stone slab carved "wherefore?" slides its rigid stem through the hub, and the wheel steadies on a perfect AXIS.
reading_story: Jicker leaps onto the merry-go-round's central pole, hugging the AXIS as the whole world blurs around him.
issues: minor (non-blocking): 'stone slab... slides its rigid stem' is a slightly awkward composite object; a plain carved axle-rod would picture more cleanly
minor (non-blocking): in the reading story AXIS is followed by a trailing clause, but this matches the accepted corpus convention (placement gate is on the meaning story, which ends on AXIS)

story: A Cartwheel rolls up beside a wall display: a Pot Lid clamped tight above Crossed Axes. Soft round wood next to cold sharp steel — what a CONTRAST.
reading_story: Fight-night CONTRAST: Knuckles flexes beside a scrawny challenger, and the whole arena gasps at the mismatch.

story: The rolling Cartwheel carries a Mound of Soil heaped on its hub; the Barbed Pike slants overhead from the right, its hooked spur snagging the sprout-marker to hold everything steady for the RIDE.
reading_story: Cy refuses cabs; he pitches himself onto every passing wagon, yelling "Best RIDE in the league!"
issues: Minor: soil heaped on a rolling wheel's hub is slightly awkward physics — vivid but takes a beat to picture
Minor: in the reading story RIDE sits inside the final exclamation rather than as the literal last word, though it is still the payoff
Watch-item: 'Barbed Pike overhead' recurs across the 𢦏 family (栽/裁/哉/戴) — the soil-riding-the-wheel core must carry the distinction

story: Atop the Wishing-Well Legs, Bean Sprouts crane rightward at the Bedsheet Cover draped over a Cartwheel — the wheel's glow burns straight through the cloth, bathing the little sprouts in RADIANCE.
reading_story: Key turns in a midnight lock; the keyhole floods with golden RADIANCE, light spilling out around Key's brass teeth.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): in reading_story, RADIANCE is followed by a trailing elaboration clause rather than being the literal final word; acceptable since the clause only elaborates the radiance image.
Minor (non-blocking): light motif plus the shared ⍌/儿 pair could echo a 光 mnemonic; the sheet-covered glowing Cartwheel is the distinguishing anchor — distinctiveness docked to 4.

story: Down the long muddy road a wooden Cartwheel rolls at your heels, spokes ticking through every turn, never pulling ahead, never lagging behind — the faithful wheel is your COMRADE.
reading_story: Hyde storms out of the lab snarling, but you march beside him through midnight London anyway; by dawn Hyde grudgingly calls you COMRADE.
issues: Distinctiveness rests on a single twist (wheel keeping pace at your heels) over the generic Cartwheel-rolls-on-road frame shared by other 車-family kanji; interference risk with neighbors is non-trivial.
Key meaning link uses a negation pair ('never pulling ahead, never lagging behind'), slightly less picturable than a positive image; non-gating.

story: CONTROL: the Cartwheel stops dead beside the Thatched House, whose roof presses a Pot Lid down onto a Mound of Soil, pinning the Open Mouth beneath — every scream sealed shut.
reading_story: The Cutler pins each knife under his thumb, sharpening in strict rhythm — total CONTROL over every blade on the bench.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS — all five supplied actors named verbatim: 'Cartwheel' (車), 'Thatched House' (宀), 'Pot Lid' (亠), 'Mound of Soil' (土), 'Open Mouth' (口).

Gate 2 (no phantoms) PASS — 'roof' is part of the Thatched House image ('peaked crown and two eaves sloping down to cap and shelter everything beneath it'); 'scream' derives from the Open Mouth image ('lips parted as if mid-shout'). Nothing outside the component list is introduced.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS — 'Cutler' appears in reading_story and matches reading_actor.actor_name for かつ.
Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS — 'CONTROL:' opens the story, matching meaning_placement 'start'; reading_story also closes on 'total CONTROL'.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS — 'Cartwheel stops dead' is ordinary wheel motion; the roof 'presses a Pot Lid down' is a physical extension of the house's defined 'cap and shelter everything beneath it', and 'pinning' echoes the Pot Lid's 'clamped down tight'. No invented cognitive ability.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS — purely imaginative scene, no historical/derivational claim.
Gate 7 (length) PASS — story 30 words, reading_story 22 words, both under ~40.
Bonus: spatial fidelity is good — the vertical stack (House roof / Lid / Soil / Mouth beneath) mirrors 害's actual layout, with the Cartwheel positioned 'beside' it on the left, matching 轄.

Weakness (non-gating): 車 is only spatially adjacent ('stops dead beside'), not causally involved. Since the 害 stack (Lid + Soil + Mouth pinning a scream) will recur in 割/憲/豁-type stories, the Cartwheel is the sole differentiator and it is the least active element — main interference risk. Drives distinctiveness to 3.
Minor: 'pinning the Open Mouth beneath' leaves the mouth's exact position (under the soil mound?) slightly under-specified, softening an otherwise crisp image.

story: Beneath the jutting Rock Overhang, a Hanger Kimono swings in the gorge wind, wide sleeves snapping open like scaled wings, its V-collar gaping as a fanged snout — the hollow's living SIGN OF THE DRAGON.
reading_story: Shinn, the night bartender, tips flaming brandy across the bar; the curling smoke coils above his shaker into a horned SIGN OF THE DRAGON.
issues: Non-blocking: the reading story's 'smoke coils into a dragon' is a stock image and carries little of Shinn's specific bar-scene detail; a more idiosyncratic hook would raise distinctiveness.

story: HUMILIATE: under the Rock Overhang, Razor-Clam Hoe spears the Hanger Kimono and dangles the limp silk in the wind; below, Tape Measure unrolls a single quivering inch — the whole robe, sized at one inch.
reading_story: Jocker grabs the microphone and reads out every one of your old love letters, cackling — a whole routine built to HUMILIATE.
issues: DATA (not candidate) — record integrity: the supplied components list includes 衣 (Hanger Kimono), but 辱 decomposes as 辰 (with its 厂 top-left) over 寸; there is no 衣 in the glyph. Rubric gate 2 ('nothing named that isn't in the kanji') is technically violated by the source record, not by the writer, who correctly covered all four supplied actors per gate 1. Recommend auditing the 辱 component entry upstream — if 衣 is dropped, this story needs a re-run.

Minor — 'meaning lands' is structurally satisfied (HUMILIATE at start, matches meaning_placement 'start') but semantically thin: nothing in the scene is actually humiliated. The shame reading has to be inferred from 'dangles the limp silk' + 'sized at one inch'; a beat naming who is shamed would tighten the payoff.
Minor — the closing clause 'the whole robe, sized at one inch' is a stated fact rather than a picture, which drops the last six words below the imageability of the rest of the scene.

story: URGE — the Conveyor Belt under your heels lurches faster and faster, rubber humming hot, shoving you helplessly forward down the road; you can't step off, can't slow it, only stumble onward.
reading_story: A Hacker hunches over the keyboard, countdown flashing red; every alarm is an URGE to type faster before the system locks.
issues: Distinctiveness borderline: belt-acceleration imagery overlaps 追 (N3 'chase': 'Conveyor Belt speeds up beneath them') and 速 (N3 'quick': belt whips fast down the road); 迫 has no second component actor to anchor it, relying solely on the second-person helpless framing ('can't step off, can't slow it') to differentiate URGE from CHASE/QUICK.
Phonetic 白 is unrepresented in the meaning story (by design, covered via reading actor Hacker/はく), so nothing in the story cues the 白 half of the glyph for recognition.

story: On the Conveyor Belt rolling forward, the Rake Hand claws down from above, the Tsunami Wave crashes below, and caught between them the Fistful of Tail snaps shut on the fleeing beast — APPREHEND.
reading_story: Ty slides for second, spikes high — police storm the diamond and APPREHEND Ty mid-slide, cuffing baseball's dirtiest player.
issues: Minor: scene carries five entities (four actors + beast) because the record supplies both composite 隶 and its sub-parts ヨ/水, making Rake Hand and Tsunami Wave partially redundant with Fistful of Tail's own image — crowds the tableau but coverage is mandatory, so not a candidate defect.
Minor: in reading_story the keyword APPREHEND is the payoff verb but not the literal final word ('cuffing baseball's dirtiest player' trails it); acceptable, meaning story placement is clean.

story: On the Conveyor Belt's road rides the Dodging Hare: a Falling Katana slashes down past its ears, a Swaddling Wrap hugs its ribs, Wishing-Well Legs bracing below — it bounds sideways off the belt to DEVIATE.
reading_story: Mid-concerto, Itzhak's bow slides off the written notes, letting the melody DEVIATE into wild improvisation while the orchestra scrambles after him.
issues: Non-blocking (coherence/imageability): the record supplies 免 alongside its own sub-parts 儿 and 勹, so the candidate hangs 'a Swaddling Wrap hugs its ribs, Wishing-Well Legs bracing below' onto a live hare — stone wishing-well legs under a bounding animal is a visual mismatch. Same input-level doubling already flagged as non-blocking on 統 ('record supplies both 糸 and its subcomponents 幺/小'); not a gate failure, but it caps imageability.

Non-blocking (imageability): the middle of the story is a three-item ornament list (katana past ears / wrap on ribs / legs below) with only the final clause carrying action — the same 'parts list' beat docked on 隔 ('mid-story clause ... reads as a parts list, momentarily lowering scene vividness') and 潟.

Non-blocking (distinctiveness): 辶-family neighbours already occupy the 'leaves/avoids the road' semantic slot — 逃 ESCAPE ('hauls him steadily forward ... a clean ESCAPE'), 避 AVOID ('the belt rolls them just out of reach'), 違 DIFFERENCE ('one tips sideways while the other stays upright'). The Dodging Hare's own registry persona is 'escaping capture', which pushes 逸 further toward 逃; the katana + hare cast is the only real differentiator.

Non-blocking (keyword placement in reading_story): 'letting the melody DEVIATE into wild improvisation while the orchestra scrambles after him' buries the keyword mid-sentence. Gate 4 applies to the main story (meaning_placement 'end' is accurate there), and the corpus already treats this as advisory only (仙: 'keyword HERMIT is followed by a short trailing clause ... still reads as the end payoff'; 潟: 'the placement gate (which applies to the main story ...) passes'). Trimming the trailing clause would land it cleanly.

Non-blocking (reading cue): reading_actor note says いつ is short and 'Ends in -tsu coda', but the reading_story gives no clipped/short-vowel or 'Its' sound cue the way 企 ('one clipped "kee"') or 唆 ('one bare syllable — "sa"') do. Actor presence gate passes; the phonetic hook is just weaker.

story: The Muddy Boar balances the Twin Pillars on its bristly back while the Conveyor Belt carries them steadily down the road to the finish line — a feat no one believed it could ACCOMPLISH.
reading_story: Swee hauls herself onto the mountain summit at dawn and plants her flag — the one dream she swore she would ACCOMPLISH.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): 逐 shares the 辶+豕 pair; the Twin Pillars balanced on the boar's back are the sole differentiator — acceptable since they are physically central to the scene, but curators should keep 逐's future mnemonic visually distant (avoid boar-on-belt framing there).
Minor (non-blocking): 'a feat no one believed it could ACCOMPLISH' is narratorial rather than imagistic; costs imageability a point but the core scene remains vivid.

story: A Conveyor Belt carries strange cargo down the road: a Rice-Paddy Grid balanced atop a Goalpost Frame, a Tucked Haunch crouched inside, tail hooked around a Sealed Clam-Locket — rolling steadily until it and you MEET.
reading_story: The first enemy you ever MEET in World 1-1: a Goomba, waddling stubbornly down the road toward you.
issues: Imageability strained: a flooded Rice-Paddy Grid 'balanced atop' an open Goalpost Frame is physically awkward to visualize (water over an empty frame)
Heavy visual load: five actors stacked in one cargo pile; supplied list's 冂+厶 alongside 禸 (which visually contains them) forces redundancy in mid-scene
Interference risk: Conveyor Belt opener is shared by all 辶 kanji and the 禺 inner stack recurs in 偶/隅/愚; only the 'cargo meets YOU' beat differentiates

story: EVERYWHERE: a Conveyor Belt hauls a tome down an endless road; atop it the Lone Barn Shutter creaks, Draped Cloak slumped inside, the tome's Goalpost Frame split by a Lightning Bolt, crossed by the Horizon Line.
reading_story: Henson tours the world with his puppets — wherever the crowd turns, felt faces are popping up EVERYWHERE.

PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): "FOSTER:" is the first token of the story, matching meaning_placement "start"; reading_story lands FOSTER near the end ("...together FOSTER strong children").

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): the bowl is rendered exactly per its registry image — "domed lid lifted, steam curling up" vs registry "under a domed lid just lifted off, steam curling up". Yoyo is Yo-Yo Ma with his cello ("saws his cello"), persona intact.
PASS gate 6 (no etymology): no historical/derivational claim anywhere.
PASS gate 7 (length): story = 33 words, reading_story = 20 words; both under ~40.
No invented cognitive ability: "meal after meal it raises you" is nourishment producing growth, i.e. the ordinary consequence of a bowl of food being eaten, not a faculty the bowl shouldn't have.

NON-BLOCKING interference risk (drives distinctiveness = 3): data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json already ships a 食-based feeding-to-raise story — "...feeding it daily until it eats calmly: DOMESTICATE" (飼). Both kanji are 食 + repeated feeding + a creature growing/becoming tame. The differentiator here is human child→giant vs animal being tamed, which holds but is thin.

NON-BLOCKING phrasing echo: "steam curling up into your face" is near-verbatim the 餓 STARVE story's "steam curling toward you" in the same file. Consider rewording the steam beat to widen the gap from that neighbor.
NON-BLOCKING style: "saws his cello" and "long, sawing notes" repeat the same verb inside a 20-word reading_story; one of the two could carry more image.

story: The Heaped Rice Bowl sits on the far left of your cell, steam curling toward you; your arm, chained on the right, stops inches short every night — you STARVE.
reading_story: Garr's engine growls in the empty garage, tank bone-dry, revving weaker each hour — even machines STARVE.

story: PACK HORSE: on the left, Galloping Stallion thunders across the dusty plain — while lashed to his right flank a plump, bulging grain sack sways and thumps against his ribs with every stride.
reading_story: Dah slaps the sweating PACK HORSE's rump, and a heavy, voiced "dah!" booms down the valley as the beast plods on under its load.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASSES but 太 is carried only adjectivally: the registry concept is 'plump' and the story uses it as a modifier ('a plump, bulging grain sack') rather than as an actor with agency. It is named, so the gate holds, but it is the weakest possible form of coverage.

Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASSES with a caveat: the 'grain sack' is an invented prop, not a supplied component. It is legitimate as the vehicle for 'plump' and for the PACK HORSE payoff, and it is never presented as a part of the character, so it is not a phantom component — but it is the one element a stricter reading could challenge.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) minor wobble: the meaning story has Galloping Stallion at 'full gallop / thunders across the dusty plain' (matching the registry image verbatim), while the reading story has the same animal 'plods on under its load'. Not a persona violation (the load explains the slowdown), but the two beats contradict each other's tempo within one card.

Distinctiveness risk: 馬 recurs across many kanji (駅・駆・騎・験・驚). The scene here is a near-literal depiction of the keyword 'pack horse' rather than a surprising hook; the only real discriminator from its 馬 neighbours is the plump grain sack thumping the ribs.

story: The Galloping Stallion explodes across the open plain, black mane whipping, four hooves flinging dust skyward — the whole horizon shudders under his thundering GALLOP.
reading_story: Coo the clipped pigeon-keeper clings bareback, pigeons bursting from his coat at every stride, cooing frantically through the GALLOP.
issues: Non-blocking: meaning story nearly restates the Galloping Stallion's stock registry image (mane flying, dust, thundering across open plain), risking interference with other 馬-series kanji; distinctiveness rests almost entirely on the reading story's bareback pigeon-keeper.
Non-blocking: combined length 43 words sits right at the ~40-word soft cap.
Non-blocking: 'the whole horizon shudders' is the lone abstract beat in otherwise concrete imagery.

story: The Galloping Stallion thunders past; riding at his right flank, the Quote Hook curls down and snatches his tiny whinny out of the air — the captured whinny sprouts four legs and trots off as a PONY.
reading_story: Coo the clipped pigeon-keeper whistles one short "coo!" — and instead of a pigeon, a PONY lands clumsily on his outstretched arm.

story: Left of the rail, the Galloping Stallion thunders past. High on the right hangs its laminated racing license; beneath it, a Trailing Footprint drags through mud — the stamped, certified credentials of A GOOD HORSE.
reading_story: Shunsuke the striker races A GOOD HORSE down the pitch, loses by a nose, and shakes its hoof at the whistle.
issues: MINOR (non-blocking): 'Left of the rail' introduces a prop not in the record; it reads as racetrack scenery/spatial divider rather than a claimed component, so it does not trip the phantom-component gate, but a stricter framing (e.g. 'Left of the track') would remove all ambiguity.

MINOR (non-blocking, distinctiveness): the closing payoff 'the stamped, certified credentials of A GOOD HORSE' is administrative/abstract; a concrete consequence (the stallion nosing the license off its hook, the footprint smearing the seal) would sharpen the hook without adding words.
MINOR (non-blocking): racetrack + galloping stallion is high-frequency imagery across 馬 kanji (駅/駆/騎/験); interference risk rests entirely on the license-over-footprint pairing.

story: EQUESTRIAN: you vault onto the Galloping Stallion from its left side, thighs locked mid-stride, dust boiling off its flying hooves, its black mane whipping your face across the open plain.
reading_story: At the stable gate, Key the locksmith turns one clipped lock, and the EQUESTRIAN bursts through onto the track.
issues: Distinctiveness is thin: the story is near-literal (mounting a galloping horse = 'equestrian'), so it carries little beyond the keyword's own meaning. 馬 recurs in many N1 kanji (駆, 騒, 駐, 験), and a generic ride scene risks interference; the left-side vault is the sole discriminating detail.

Short-vowel cue in reading_story is carried only implicitly by 'one clipped lock' — it matches the registry note's wording, but a learner who hasn't internalised the 'clipped' convention gets no explicit き-vs-きゅう contrast.

phonetic_extra 奇 is (correctly) unused since no actor is supplied, but the reading き therefore has no visual anchor in the glyph itself — Key is attached to a stable gate rather than to any part of the character.

story: Left of the fence the Galloping Stallion thunders past; right, a Rubber Glove flaps on the rail above a Fat Grub squirming in the mud — hooves, slapping rubber, wriggling: BOISTEROUS.
reading_story: Sosa swings for the fences; the bleachers erupt so BOISTEROUS the scoreboard rattles loose.
issues: Imageability limiter: the three actors coexist but never interact — a static tableau rather than an event. Nothing the stallion does causes the glove or grub to do anything.
The closing clause 'hooves, slapping rubber, wriggling: BOISTEROUS' is an abstract recap list, not an image; it summarizes the scene instead of extending it.
'a Rubber Glove flaps on the rail' asserts motion with no motivating agent (no wind, no impact) — the weakest of the three visuals despite being persona-consistent.

Distinctiveness docked for template reuse: the 'Left of the fence... right...' spatial scaffold and the 'A, B, C: KEYWORD' cadence are both likely to recur across the corpus and reduce cross-card separation.
Minor cross-story echo: 'fence' in the meaning story and 'swings for the fences' in the reading story reuse the same noun, which can blur which story a recalled fence belongs to.
Combined length (30 + 14 = 44 words) sits just over the ~40 mark if the gate is ever read as applying to both fields together; each field individually passes.

story: The Full Moon glows to the left as the Galloping Stallion springs off the Starfish, up the Stepladder, over the Railway Tracks and Horizon Line, and out between the Twin Pillars — LEAPING UP.
reading_story: Rapper Tone stretches a long booming "tōōō—" over the beat, and the whole crowd answers by LEAPING UP on every bar.

story: The Kneeling Page-Boy bows low atop a Galloping Stallion's saddle; the horse suddenly bolts, and the boy, still frozen mid-bow, streaks across the plain, eyes wide, utterly SURPRISED.
reading_story: Mid-concert, Kyo unleashes a howl so loud his own microphone explodes — even the screaming frontman staggers back, genuinely SURPRISED.
issues: Minor: reading story's 'even the screaming frontman' refers to Kyo but could briefly parse as a second character; non-blocking.

story: MARROW oozes from a cracked bone at the left; right above, the Falling Katana slices the Horizon Line, dropping the Full Moon under a Bedsheet Cover, everything gliding away on the Conveyor Belt.
reading_story: Zwee slurps a hollow bone with a shrill "zwee," drawing the MARROW straight up the straw.
issues: PASS gate 1 (component coverage): all six mandatory components named — 骨 as 'a cracked bone' (kanji_keyword 'bone', no actor defined), ノ 'Falling Katana', 一 'Horizon Line', 月 'Full Moon', 冖 'Bedsheet Cover', 辶 'Conveyor Belt'.

PASS gate 2 (no phantoms): only modifiers ('cracked', 'left') and no extra objects in the story. The reading_story's 'the straw' is the sole quasi-prop — non-blocking (reading stories are outside the component gate) but it is introduced with a definite article having never been established; 'up the hollow bone' would be cleaner.
PASS gate 3 (reading actor): 'Zwee' opens reading_story and the mimetic 'zwee' reinforces ずい; matches reading_actor.actor_name.
PASS gate 4 (meaning lands): MARROW is the capitalized first word, matching meaning_placement 'start'.

PASS gate 5 (actor consistency): every action is ordinary physical motion consistent with the registry personas — katana slices, line is severed, moon drops, sheet covers, belt carries ('carrying whatever sits on it steadily forward'). No invented cognitive faculty.
PASS gate 6 (no false etymology): purely imaginative; no claim about historical derivation.
PASS gate 7 (length): 33 words, under the ~40 cap.

GRADED WEAKNESS — spatial fidelity (rubric item 11, starred): 'right above' reads as 'immediately above', but 骨 is the LEFT radical and the katana/horizon/moon/sheet stack sits to its RIGHT, not above it. 'to its right' would be accurate. Also, the registry places the Conveyor Belt 'along the bottom-left' of its own element, yet the story makes it the terminal carrier of the whole scene — acceptable but loosely sited.
GRADED WEAKNESS — coherence (item 12): the causal link 'slices the Horizon Line, dropping the Full Moon' is asserted rather than shown; why severing the horizon drops the moon is left to the reader.

GRADED WEAKNESS — distinctiveness risk: the right-hand chain (katana + horizon + moon + sheet + belt) is generic enough to recur in neighbours sharing ノ/一/月/辶/冖 (e.g. 随, 堕, 隋 family). Only the marrow-from-cracked-bone opening discriminates 髄; the discriminating beat should ideally be more entangled with the rest of the scene (e.g. the belt carrying the oozing marrow away).

story: GHOST: a Rice-Paddy Grid floats as its blank face, Wishing-Well Legs hang stiffly below, and a Sealed Clam-Locket swings at its lower right, still clamped shut on some grave secret.
reading_story: Key the locksmith jabs one short, clipped key at the crypt door — and the GHOST drifts straight through the wood beside him.
issues: MINOR (non-blocking): slight internal friction between 'Rice-Paddy Grid' and 'blank face' -- a four-square grid is not blank; 'gridded face' would read cleaner.
MINOR (non-blocking): 鬼 is a component of 魂/魔/醜 etc., so ghost/crypt imagery is at interference risk downstream -- keep later 鬼-family stories away from the crypt-and-key scene.

story: On the left a Smoke Swirl corkscrews upward, flattening into two hazy layers; on the right a ghost leans in, breathing that haze back inside itself — reclaiming its SOUL.
reading_story: Sean Connery — Conn — presses a hand to his chest and growls that no man takes his SOUL.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the scene is semantically congruent with the keyword — ghost + wispy haze + 'soul' all live in the same concept cloud, so nothing surprising anchors it; risks interference with other 鬼-radical spirit kanji (e.g. 魄, 魔).
Non-blocking: 'breathing that haze back inside itself' is close enough to the real soul-as-vapor sense that it reads as quasi-explanatory, though it stops short of a §3.6 etymology claim.
Non-blocking: reading_story is generic — hand-to-chest + growl gives Conn no hook specific to 魂, so it could be swapped onto any こん card without loss.

story: A ghost hovers at your left, trailing silver ribbons of mist that wind around your wrists; you cannot look away, cannot blink. That helpless, glowing pull is FASCINATION.
reading_story: Mee whispers her name once, and every head in the café turns, spoons frozen midair, held by pure FASCINATION.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: 鬼/'ghost' is named literally in the first clause ('A ghost hovers at your left'); components_used matches.
Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS: only added nouns are scenery ('silver ribbons of mist', 'wrists', 'café', 'spoons'), none presented as a component. 未 is phonetic_extra and correctly left unused.
Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: 'Mee' opens the reading_story; reading_actor_used matches the registry name.

Gate 4 (meaning lands) PASS: '...is FASCINATION.' is the final word of the story, matching meaning_placement='end'. Note keyword is ALSO the last word of reading_story — harmless but it makes the two stories rhyme semantically and slightly blurs which one is the meaning card.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS: ghost hovering and trailing mist is ordinary physical behaviour for a ghost, no invented cognitive faculty. 'Mee whispers her name once' is consistent with the short/clipped み note.
Gate 6 (no etymology) PASS: nothing claims historical or phonetic derivation.
Gate 7 (length) PASS: story 28 words, reading_story 20 words, both well under ~40.
Spatial fidelity (graded, ★): 'at your left' correctly places 鬼 as the left radical of 魅 — a genuine strength.
Imageability deduction: the back half ('That helpless, glowing pull') is abstract restatement rather than image; only the mist-around-wrists detail does real visual work. Held at 4, not 5.

Distinctiveness deduction: 'ghost hypnotises you with mist' is near-literal paraphrase of 'bewitch' and reuses stock haunting imagery that risks interference with other 鬼-family kanji (魔, 魂, 塊, 醜). The wrist-binding ribbons are the only unique hook — hence 3, not higher.
Minor: reading_story is scenically unrelated to the meaning story (café vs. ghost) and gives Mee nothing physical to do beyond whispering; it is passable but low-imagery on its own.

story: Beneath the cottage floorboards a ghost squats, blowing green smoke up through the cracks until a pointed hat and a cackle take shape above it: a full-grown WITCH.
reading_story: Mah greets the WITCH with one clipped syllable — "ma!" — and every candle in the hallway gutters out.
issues: Gates all pass. Component coverage: the single mandatory component 鬼 is named as "a ghost" (record gives kanji_keyword "ghost"; data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json ships 鬼 with keyword GHOST, so the persona matches). Reading actor "Mah" appears in reading_story and its registry note (data/authored/n5-reading-actors.json: "Mah — clipped bare \"ma\". Short.") is honoured explicitly by "one clipped syllable". Keyword at end ("...a full-grown WITCH."), 28 words / 17 words, no etymology.

Reading-story device already spent on the immediate graphic neighbour: n1 麻 reads "Mah rolls a coil of HEMP rope, testing each strand with a clipped \"ma!\" of approval" — the candidate reuses the identical literal cue ("one clipped syllable — \"ma!\""). Since 麻 is literally the rest of 魔 and shares the same actor (as do 摩 CHAFE and 磨 GRIND), this is the highest-interference pair in the corpus and the one place a fresh device was most needed. Precedent (see the 彫 issues log) treats spent-device reuse as an issue, not a gate failure.

Keyword/actor namespace collision: "witch" is the payoff keyword here, but the reading actor Cho is defined in-corpus as a witch with broom and wand (n1 丁 "Cho glides her broom low down the empty STREET", 彫 "only a witch can CARVE with sound", 聴 "Cho the witch"). A learner meeting WITCH as 魔's meaning will have to keep it separate from a recurring reading persona who is also a witch. Not a gate failure (no registry actor name is used in the story), but it dents distinctiveness.

phonetic_extra 麻 is unused. Permissible per corpus precedent (phonetic_extra carries no mandatory-coverage obligation; e.g. the 加 / 瓜 / 秋 / 金 entries), but note that 麻 does have an authored persona available (n2-component-actors.json: "Hemp-Drying Shed"), and it accounts for the majority of the glyph — so roughly half the character is unanchored. The "cottage floorboards / beneath" staging is a partial rescue: it does put the ghost UNDER a roofed structure, which is spatially faithful to 鬼 sitting below 麻.

"Cottage", "floorboards", "pointed hat", "candles", "hallway" are non-actor scenery, not phantom components — no registry actor name is invoked, matching the precedent set by 彰 ("certificate") and 影. Gate 2 passes.

Minor abstraction at the image's core: "a cackle take shape" asks the reader to see a sound. The pointed hat carries the visual load; the cackle beat is synesthetic and slightly weakens an otherwise concrete picture.

The ghost exhaling smoke that congeals into a form is ordinary supernatural-physical behaviour for a ghost, not an invented cognitive faculty — no gate-5 conflict with 鬼's registry image ("a Rice-Paddy Grid floats as its blank face...").

story: On the fishmonger's marble slab a fish lies gleaming; to its right the Woolly Ram chews placidly, fleece shorn snow-white this dawn. Nothing on this counter is an hour old — FRESH.
reading_story: Senna peels the top strip from his visor mid-corner; grit gone, the track ahead snaps back into colour, the whole race suddenly FRESH.
issues: Gate 1 (component coverage) PASS: the sole mandatory component 魚 (actor null, kanji_keyword "fish") is named as "a fish lies gleaming", matching the shipped kanji-as-actor convention for 魚 — "a silver fish thrashes in the wet spray" (漁, data/authored/n2-mnemonics.json:4358-area entry) and "one fish so mountain-huge" (鯨, data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json). components_used matches.

Gate 2 (no phantom components) PASS: the Woolly Ram encodes 羊, which is in the record's phonetic_extra and is genuinely part of 鮮 — so it is not a phantom. Using it is optional-but-permitted per established precedent in this corpus (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:1139 勘, :1932, :3205 弊). Remaining nouns ("fishmonger's marble slab", "counter") are setting props, not added actors.

Gate 5 (actor consistency) PASS with one non-gating flag: the 羊 registry image is "A woolly ram seen head-on, two curling horns splayed at the top and a fleecy body below, chewing placidly" (data/authored/n4-component-actors.json:78-80). "chews placidly" is verbatim, but "fleece shorn snow-white this dawn" strips the fleece that is the persona's defining visual and the anchor for the glyph's lower body. Softening rather than contradiction, non-gating under the 日-as-dumpling ruling (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:6803) and the midday-sun-staged-at-dawn ruling (:5228). No invented cognitive ability; shearing and chewing are ordinary physical events.

Gate 3 (reading actor) PASS: Senna appears in reading_story and stays in persona — "Ayrton Senna at the wheel" — peeling a visor tear-off mid-corner is ordinary driver behaviour, consistent with all 21 shipped Senna stories (e.g. 旋 "grips the wheel at Monaco", 銭 "screeches to a stop at the toll booth"). The visor motif is unused elsewhere in the Senna set, so no intra-actor collision.

Gates 4 and 7 PASS: FRESH is terminal in both stories (meaning_placement "end" is accurate); 32 words / 23 words, both under ~40, no filler. Gate 6 PASS: "to its right" is spatial staging (rubric item 11), not an etymological claim about fish-and-mutton.
Spatial fidelity is high and correct: 魚 left (slab) / 羊 right ("to its right") reproduces the glyph layout.

Non-gating distinctiveness note: the fish-market motif already appears in 盆's reading story (data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json:7330, "fishmongers scrub eels in a cold stone BASIN"), and 魚's own card already ends "grill your fresh-caught FISH" (data/authored/n4-mnemonics.json), so "fresh + fish" partially echoes an existing card. The marble counter plus the ram keep them separable, but this is what caps distinctiveness at 4 rather than 5.

Weakest link (non-gating): the reading story's payoff is metaphorical — clearing a visor gives visual clarity, and "the whole race suddenly FRESH" leans on freshness-as-renewal rather than a physical instance of freshness. Keyword placement is clean, so it passes, but the meaning story carries the semantic load alone.
components_used records the phonetic 羊 (Woolly Ram), genuinely in the glyph and staged by the story (same class as 鳩/睡).

story: WHALE: on the left, one fish so mountain-huge it beaches itself along the shore; on the right the capital's towers glitter, their whole skyline reflected in its wet grey flank.
reading_story: Gei stands on the harbor wall booming a long, heavy "geeeei" across the water, and the WHALE answers with a spout taller than the lighthouse.
issues: Non-blocking: 'mountain-huge' is a size simile, but 山 is a real kanji component elsewhere — a size word not tied to another radical (e.g. 'island-huge' → also risky; prefer 'so huge') would keep the component set unambiguous.

Non-blocking: the meaning story is close to the literal gloss (whale = enormous fish), so the only true retrieval hook for 京 is the reflected skyline; the fish half carries almost no mnemonic work beyond semantics.

Non-blocking: reading_story leans on the phonetic echo 'Gei ... geeeei' rather than an action Gei performs on the whale scene; acceptable since the persona (voiced, heavy, long ē) is honoured, but the link to the meaning image is loose.

story: The Curled Cat uncoils on the left sill and lunges; the grey bird on the right merely shuffles one step, keeps pecking crumbs, head jerking — nothing on earth is that brazen except a city PIGEON.
reading_story: Cuomo's motorcade halts: a PIGEON squats on the hood. He leans out howling "kyuuuu—", long and stretched, but the bird just coos back, unmoved.
issues: Non-gating (imageability): the payoff clause is abstract and negation-framed — "nothing on earth is that brazen except a city PIGEON" — so the keyword lands via inference about a character trait rather than a concrete visual; the same weakness accepted in 孤 ("and no one comes to the door").

Non-gating (persona strain): the registry image for 九 is a cat "curled into a tidy comma-shaped ball, tail tucked, lazily flicking", and the story opens with it "uncoils... and lunges". This is ordinary physical motion for a cat and therefore passes gate 5, but it discards the comma/curled silhouette that is the actor's visual mnemonic for the stroke shape.

Informational (not a defect): components_used lists only ["鳥"] while the story also stages 九 as Curled Cat. This matches the corpus convention for phonetic_extra components (cf. 勘 components_used ["力"], 嘉 ["吉"] in data/authored/n1-mnemonics.json), so no gate fails — but a deterministic verifier that cross-checks named personas against components_used would flag "Curled Cat" as unaccounted.

Non-gating (distinctiveness): 鳥 is shared across a large N1 bird cluster (鶴, 鳳, 鴻, 鶏); separation rests entirely on the cat, which is unique to 鳩 among them, so the anchor holds — but the generic "grey bird ... pecking crumbs" phrasing does little independent work.
components_used corrected to include the phonetic 九 (Curled Cat), which the story legitimately stages; it is a real component of the glyph (role=phonetic), not a phantom.

story: A Full Moon hangs low on the left, its two faint stripes glowing; against it, on the right, a burning bird spreads wings wider than the night itself — the PHOENIX.
reading_story: Ho belly-laughs on a chimney as the PHOENIX lands beside him, tail-sparks setting his red hat smoking.
issues: Distinctiveness is the weak point (3/5): the keyword PHOENIX is itself a bird, so the 鳥 component is semantically absorbed by the payoff and does no independent retrieval work — the only discriminating element vs. other N1 bird kanji (鶴, 鴻, 鷲) is the Full Moon.
The Full Moon is passive backdrop only ('hangs low', 'against it'); no interaction between Moon and bird, which weakens binding of the left-hand component.
'wings wider than the night itself' is a hyperbolic scale comparison rather than a concrete visual, slightly diluting an otherwise strong image.

story: Under the Thatched House's low eaves squats the Stumpy Sparrow, glaring rightward at the tall white bird stalking outside on stilt legs — that elegant giant is a CRANE.
reading_story: Knuckles balances one-legged in his boxing ring, copying a CRANE's stance — the CRANE itself stalks in and jabs its beak faster than his punch.
issues: Non-blocking: two birds share the meaning-story stage (Stumpy Sparrow and the crane), a mild risk the learner recalls 'sparrow' as the keyword -- mitigated by the explicit end payoff 'that elegant giant is a CRANE' and the size/color contrast.

Non-blocking: reading story keyword sits mid-sentence rather than at an edge, but corpus convention (e.g. approved 丸, 久 in data/authored/n2-mnemonics.json) applies the placement gate only to the meaning story.

story: Under the Cliff Awning, a Scarecrow stands stiff-armed beside grumpy Stumpy Sparrow; below them a huge bird unfolds wings wider than the shelter — a HAWK.
reading_story: Yoyo drags his bow across the cello; the shrieking note calls down a HAWK, which lands on his shoulder and glares.
issues: Non-blocking (distinctiveness): the payoff is near-tautological — 'a huge bird ... — a HAWK'. The 鳥 component and the keyword collapse into the same concept, so the keyword is recoverable from 鳥 alone and nothing in the scene disambiguates HAWK from eagle/falcon/crane/heron. A hawk-specific cue (hooked beak, hunting stoop, falconer's jess) would harden it.

Non-blocking (interference): three avian elements in one scene (Stumpy Sparrow, 'huge bird', HAWK) create intra-scene confusion risk and will read similarly to other 隹+鳥 kanji. The size contrast ('wings wider than the shelter' vs the stumpy sparrow) is the only separator.

Non-blocking (rubric §1.2): reading_story relies entirely on the Yoyo persona to carry the long ō; no stretch/sustain cue in the prose ('drags his bow', 'shrieking note' are neutral). Acceptable per the registry design, but a sustained/drawn-out note would reinforce vowel length.

Note (data, not candidate): dominant_reading is kun たか while reading_actor is よう — the reading_story teaches an on'yomi the record does not mark as dominant. Gate 3 passes as specified, but worth checking upstream.

story: Beneath the Cliff Awning, the Twin Spoon Silhouettes stand stiff as hind legs, propping up a dozing velvet-antlered body — look again: the whole shelter holds one enormous DEER.
reading_story: A Rocker windmills his guitar onstage; a DEER bounds into the spotlight, hooks the mic stand on its antlers, and headbangs through the encore.

story: LOVELY: the flat Horizon Line stretches overhead, a Goalpost Frame stands beneath it, and inside that empty frame a deer poses motionless, antlers gilded by the setting sun.
reading_story: Ray Charles sways at his piano out on the sand, sunglasses flashing, holding one long note so LOVELY the whole desert hushes to listen.
issues: Gate 2 (no phantom components) — borderline pass: 'antlers gilded by the setting sun' names a SUN, which is not a component of 麗 and is itself a high-frequency kanji component (日/夕). It sits in a subordinate participial clause as lighting, not in a structural slot (the three slots are line-overhead / frame-beneath / deer-inside), so it does not read as a fourth building block — but it is the one line a learner could mis-encode as 日. Cheapest fix: 'antlers gilded gold' or 'antlers glinting'.
Gate 7 (length & focus) — 28 words, well under ~40, but 'by the setting sun' is the only clause carrying no component load; per §3.7 'no extraneous detail' it is the first thing to cut.
